players.name: Ryan Waldschmidt
players.note: On my first draft of this sheet I had Waldschmidt as a 4 for one reason only and that's that his prices are up over 200% since I ranked him as a 5 last year. In a world of 'buy low, sell high' it felt wrong to give my highest rating to a player whose autograph price has already tripled in the past year. But then I looked around. 29 of my top 30 ranked hitters have a Bowman autograph. Twelve of them are over $100. Nineteen of them are over $70. Only four of them are under $50, Waldschmidt being one. Although we've already made our money and I admit I've sold all of my shares and currently own nothing of his, if I'm trusting my rankings (which I do) he's honestly still a great value. The scouting report is still the same as it was when I yelled from the rooftops last year in every post about him being one of the most underrated hitters from 2024 Bowman Draft. It's a package of tools we hardly ever see, as he's one of the few hitters whose hit, power, and speed are all legitimately above average. He hit .289 with 18 HR, 29 SB, 16% BB, 17.6% K, .184 ISO, and 142 wRC+ between A+ & AA. Literally a work of art stat sheet. Among all qualified prospects age 22 or younger last year (DSL excluded) there was one prospect who had a BB% over 15%, K% under 18%, and ISO over .180: Ryan Waldschmidt. There was also only one prospect in the 15 HR/25 SB club that had a BB/K over 0.75 and a SwStr% under 10%. Again, Ryan Waldschmidt. He's patient, doesn't chase, makes contact, makes hard contact, and steals bases. It's one of the most flawless offensive profiles you'll find at this level when you consider all aspects. Waldschmidt hasn't generated a ton of buzz yet but if he dominates AAA which I fully expect him to I don't see how it doesn't happen soon. On top of that he's already the team's #1 prospect according to almost all outlets and I'm pretty confident we will see him get called up at some point this season. When that happens I can't imagine this base autograph will be going for less than $100.

players.name: Kayson Cunningham
players.note: is a player that I like but based on his ranking he'll probably need to fall down more into the $20 range before I'm buying so with him it's just about patience. Don't throw tomatoes at me but

players.name: Druw Jones
players.note: at $23 is awfully tempting. He gave us some hope when he looked good in 2024 but regressed last year and saw his price drop another 60%+. Still has yet to show as much promise as we expected but he is an elite athlete whose base autograph was once $400 on the release of 2023 Bowman. He's still not cheap but given how down everyone is on him I'd at least consider a dart throw.

players.name: Slade Caldwell
players.note: I like to joke that the Diamondbacks have a type and if you were to try and clone Corbin Carroll in the 2024 draft class it would have been Slade Caldwell. The 5'9" lefty might not be a big name in the hobby due to his height but don't mistake being short for being small because Caldwell is extremely strong physically. Similar to Carroll he has a mature approach and phenomenal speed which will help him be not only a high OBP guy but also a plus defender. The big question mark for us is going to be the power, and it might grade as a tick below average but given his strength and ability to lift the ball I don't think it getting to average is out of the question. I mean Carroll is all of the sudden a 30 HR guy and I'd argue that at this age he showed less game power than Caldwell has. Last year Slade hit .260 with a 124 wRC+ between A & A+ in his age 19 season but still managed to have an OBP over .400 thanks to a 17.6% walk rate, a number that was up over 20% prior to his promotion to A+. His contact rates at both levels were a fraction under 80% and for the year he had a swinging strike % under 7%. This is fantastic discipline and contact for a player his age and we've already seen him flash the speed (25 SB) and defense. All of this comes while playing at a pretty advanced level for his age, as he was one of only thirteen prospects in all of baseball last year who got 300+ PA above Single-A at age 19 or younger. The hobby has many "if they grow into power their cards will blow up" type prospects and in my opinion Caldwell is one of the safest bets since he already excels in every other aspect of the game. This is a hell of a floor for a teenager.

players.name: Demetrio Crisantes
players.note: Here's a name you probably haven't heard in a minute. Other than Waldschmidt the only other Arizona prospect I gave a 5 to last year was Crisantes, but he was unfortunately shut down less than two months into the season with a shoulder injury that required surgery. His breakout campaign in 2024 had a little bit of everything we like to see. Between CPX & A he batted .341 with 7 HR, 30 SB, 12.5% BB, 15.7% K, .151 ISO, and 143 wRC+. All of that came with a very impressive 82.3% contact rate at age 19. Prior to his injury last year he was hitting .252 with 4 HR, 6 SB, 13.9% BB, 12.6% K, .163 ISO, and a 111 wRC+ in 34 games. Although the average and wRC+ dropped off it's worth noting that his BABIP was 140 points lower than it was in 2024 and he actually increased his contact rates to a wild 87.1%, leading me to believe that the average would have normalized over time had his season not been cut short. It was only 151 PA but he saw his contact rate go up nearly 5% while also improving his ISO by more than 10 points, two things you love to see out of a prospect his age. I know it's a small sample but if you throw out the rookie leagues there were only three prospects in baseball last year age 20 or younger who had 150+ PA with an ISO over .160, more walks than strikeouts, and a swinging strike % under 8%. Are you ready for this? Kevin McGonigle. Max Clark. Demetrio Crisantes. He's bordering on the range where he could be a 5 again, especially since his price is down over 30% since I made him a 5 last year, but I have a hard time going too hard on injured players that I've yet to see post-surgery. With that being said of the "injury stashes" from last year he's one of my favorites so if he looks like his usual self this Spring I wouldn't be surprised if this one moved quickly.

players.name: LuJames Groover
players.note: are both coming off nice seasons and will start the year in AAA where they should have a good chance of getting the call this year. I'd consider them appropriately priced for where I have them ranked but since they could see a call-up bump this season they're not bad players to hold.

players.name: JD Dix
players.note:
Dix didn't make his professional debut in 2024 after he was drafted 35th overall, but of the prep bats from that class who got their first action last season he was one of the sneakier ones to me. Seeing time between the CPX & A, Dix hit .297 with 2 HR, 28 SB, 14.2% BB, 20.8% K, .109 ISO, and 126 wRC+. He also had a 77.9% contact rate and 9% swinging strike %, again, the Diamondbacks seem to have a type. The difference here is the the 6'2" switch-hitting middle infielder was given above average power projections by some evaluators when he was coming out of high school, so although we haven't seen the power yet he's not your typical small frame contact hitter. He's had issues with his shoulder and though he played all four infield positions at the Area Code Games prior to the draft Arizona seems content with him at 2B since he played there almost exclusively last year. While both of his HR's came from the left side of the plate, Dix has a great swing from both sides and makes contact to all fields which he showed in his pro debut when he hit .297 lefty and .299 righty. The thing holding him back in the hobby up to this point is almost certainly that .109 ISO in his first season. Even then it feels like a prep hitter who went at the back of the 1st round and nearly hit .300 in his debut should get a little more attention. Although Slade Caldwell is more dynamic, if you look at the chart above Dix isn't far behind him in any of the rankings and they were actually drafted within six picks of each other back in 2024. We would need to see some more game power this season for this to take off, but I can't help but love the value we're getting now.

You'll notice a trend with these sheets that hardly any prospects who just got their 1st autograph in 2025 Bowman Draft will be a buy because single prices are still high.

players.name: Patrick Forbes
players.note:
I won't give many 4's to players in 2025 Bowman Draft because single prices still seem pretty high but considering he was my 12th ranked pitcher in the product and is inside my top 100 pitchers, $11 ain't too shabby. Forbes was believed by many to be the best prep hitting prospect in the state of Kentucky back in 2022 but things changed in 2024 at Louisville when he was hit by a pitch and broke his non-throwing hand in the first at-bat of the season. Though he had pitched some in the past this really started his shift to focusing on pitching full-time. One month after breaking his hand he returned to the mound and had a 3.72 ERA in 12 appearances (4 starts). After working solely on pitching for one offseason he came back as a pitcher-only in 2025 and had a 4.42 ERA in 15 starts, but his 3.09 FIP suggests he pitched much better than that. What really improved was the stuff. After posting a 9.93 K/9 in 2024 he returned last year and saw that improve to 14.76. That's almost 5 additional strikeouts per game. His overall K% went from 26% to 36.7% in just one season of not hitting. He's still risky because the command has not been great and he doesn't have a true third pitch yet, but for a kid who is essentially brand new to pitching you can't teach the fact that he can already touch 100 mph and struck out nearly 15 college hitters per 9 innings last year. I'd probably still wait because I do think he'll get down under $10 (probably by next week), but on ability alone I'd be willing to sit on something of his and see how what the Diamondbacks can do with him this year.

I had

players.name: Daniel Eagen
players.note: Some of the beauty when it comes to pitchers is how some of them seemingly come out of nowhere and one of my favorites of those stories is Daniel Eagen. Pitching in the Big South at Presbyterian he struggled in 2022 with a 7.63 ERA, 10.31 K/9, and 6.39 BB/9 as he was both hit hard and struggled with command. After only throwing 9.2 innings the following year he was shut down with arm injuries. Who we saw come back in 2024 was almost an entirely different player. He was the Pitcher of the Year in his conference after going 6-2 with a 2.67 ERA, 2.38 FIP, 14.14 K/9, and 3.24 BB/9. I'd argue few have come back from an injury and improved that drastically in the year of their return. My favorite quantifiable leap was seeing that his K-BB% rose by over 20%, as he increased his K rate by nearly 17% while also dropping his BB rate by almost 5%. After opponents hit .330 against him in 2022, they hit just .171 (!) off him in 2024. When he returned his fastball sat about 5 mph higher than it did prior to the injury and he ran it up to 96 with carry from the right side. His curveball is his best pitch and it is filthy, generating an absurd 53% whiff rate his final year in college. His slider was also a big swing-and-miss pitch and gives him three offerings that are above average. He made his professional debut in High-A last year where in 19 starts he went 7-5 with a 2.49 ERA, 2.97 FIP, 12.16 K/9, and 3.78 BB/9. He made a handful of starts at AA after a promotion where he struggled a little more but the season stat line was still great. Among all pitchers who threw 100+ innings in the minors last year at age 22 or younger only two of them had an ERA under 3.00, a K/9 over 11.5, and a BB/9 under 4: Mets phenom Jonah Tong… and Daniel Eagen. I'm really high on his stuff and though he's not a big name prospect yet I expect him to be by the end of this year.

players.name: Mitch Bratt
players.note: I don't want you to get too excited and think every team will be chalked full of 5's but but there are a grand total of four pitchers in my entire top 50 who have a base autograph under $12 and two of them happen to be on the same team. I love going from Eagen to Bratt, two pitchers who I love but have entirely different styles. If you grew up watching 90's pitchers like Greg Maddux toy with hitters you should watch a Mitch Bratt start. Not that the stuff is the same but his willingness to go deep into the repertoire and move which side of the zone he wants to attack is incredible. He makes adjustments during the at-bat and will find out early on what you're expecting and hit you with the opposite. And he does so by having elite command of his pitches. He sits low-90's and touches 95 from the left side so he's not your typical blow you away pitcher that we love but the fastball plays up because his location and ability to mix his pitches are both so good. Bratt throws a fastball, slider, changeup, curveball, and cutter, and while none of their stuff really grades as above average he goes on runs where he's nearly unhittable. He came over from Texas in the Merrill Kelly trade last year and pitched in AA for both organizations. Between the two he threw 122.1 innings with a 3.38 ERA, 3.56 FIP, 2.92 xFIP, 10.89 K/9, and wait for it… my favorite part… a 1.54 BB/9. If it sounds ridiculous it's because it is. Out of every Minor League pitcher age 21 or younger who threw 100+ innings and had a K/9 higher than 10.5, the next lowest BB/9 you'd find after his is 2.58. He not only surrendered the fewest free passes in that group but it was by more than a full walk per 9 innings. Out of curiosity I went to FanGraphs to check the last time a pitching prospect his age had a season of 100+ innings, a K/9 over 10.5, and a BB/9 under 2 at Double-A or higher. Their Minor League data goes all the way back to 2006. It returned no results other than Mitch Bratt. There's disagreement among evaluators if he'll ever be more than a middle of the rotation guy since the stuff isn't elite but one thing is for sure, he's going to be an MLB starter at some point. And that point might be 2026. You many not find another one of those under $10.

players.name: Dean Livingston
players.note: as one of my sleepers in 2025 Bowman Draft and he could almost be a 4 already but I do want to see him pitch professionally before I dive in to his cards. Very new to pitching and didn't even crack his high school's rotation until about a year ago. Athletic delivery and scouts think he'll throw 100 once he fills out. Definitely one worth putting in a pin in for early this year.

players.name: Tate Southisene
players.note: from a hobby perspective and I know the organization thinks highly of him, but his price is rich for my blood. It could come down more as 2025 Bowman Draft singles move further from the release date but until I see a big sample of him playing I'd really want this under $20.

players.name: Diego Tornes
players.note:
For most players a base autograph over $25 with a Hobby Rank outside of the top 100 would put you in a hold range (3), but the statistical component of my rankings gives hardly any credit to DSL stats because, well, they don't mean much to me. Because of this it's almost impossible for DSL prospects to break my top 100, but that has more to do with how scared I am of the floor. Since many of their ceilings are high they're still worthy of a buy if the price is right, you just have to be willing to accept that it's more of a gamble. Enter Diego Tornes. My 9th ranked chase in 2025 Bowman Chrome, the teenager signed out of Cuba for $2.5 million last January. International scouts raved about Tornes during the signing period citing that he was already ahead of most of his peers offensively despite being one of the youngest players in the class. That's right, the extremely physical 6'2" switch-hitter was not just 16-years-old when he signed, but he played almost the entire first half of his debut season in the DSL at 16 before turning 17 in July. In that debut he hit .279 with 0 HR, 24 SB, 15.6% BB, 21.8% K, .123 ISO, and 118 wRC+. Despite failing to go deep he was able to keep a respectable .123 ISO thanks to his 5 triples in 147 PA which could be an indicator of future game power. 

These stats are great but compared to some of the other top DSL guys that we'll see later on these sheets they aren't as gaudy, but we can't forget about what is often the hobby's favorite "tool" and that's age. There were 123 qualified DSL hitters with a higher wRC+ than Tornes's 118, but only 3 of them were younger than him, and only 1 of those had a higher ISO. I think this puts Tornes in a great spot for us because he's young, the tools are fantastic, and while the stats were great they weren't so good that it made people overreact to his cards. I've seen the hit tool projected in the 50-55 range and the power in the 50-60 range, of course there's a lot of development to go but if he is able to reach the top end of those you'd be talking about a hobby star. He's already drawn Anthony Santander comps from international scouts due to his elite bat speed metrics from both sides of the plate along with how physical he is for his age already. There's always risk with DSL guys but Tornes checks a ton of the hobby boxes including being on a franchise with a good fanbase who doesn't have many hitting prospects to be excited about. If he shows out in the CPX/A this year, there's a ton of upside at this price.

players.name: Conor Essenburg
players.note: is probably the one I'll buy sooner. Less hype so the entry price is lower but he's a two-way player who is more than likely a hitter and has potential 20+ HR pop in his bat. He'll be a fun one to watch them develop and if his price gets in the $15 and below range I'll likely grab a couple before the season just in case.

players.name: John Gil
players.note:
My highest ranked hitter in the entire Braves organization in terms of hobby appeal is 19-year-old shortstop John Gil. He joined Tornes getting his 1st Bowman autograph in 2025 Bowman Chrome but his path was a bit different since he originally signed for just $110,000 which was at the bottom end of their international signings from 2023. I'd argue that Gil's stock since signing has gone up more than any other Braves prospect and his production so far in only two professional seasons has been so good that he's almost cracked the Scout the Statline top 100 in terms of peak offensive projections. It's a solid package of tools with average power, plus speed, and above average defense, but the improvements to the hitting approach are what really have me high on him. In 2024 between the CPX & A he had a 0.66 BB/K with a 12.7% BB, 19.2% K, and 74% contact rate. This past season he saw his BB/K shoot up to 0.86 thanks to an almost 5% decrease in his strikeouts (14.5%) and a nearly 4% increase in his overall contact rates (77.4%). 

When your tools are already this good and you drop your K rate 5% at age 19 this is a big green flag, enough of one that the Braves promoted him from Single-A, skipping High-A, and letting him play Double-A for about a week at the end of the year. Now that wasn't necessarily a promotion as teams frequently do this so I'm not expecting him to start the year in Double-A, but getting a taste of a level that high at 19 tells me the Braves believe in him at least a little bit. The only thing holding these cards back is the power. While he does project for average power he hit only 7 HR this year and had a .113 ISO. As a counterpoint though, 5 of those 7 long balls came in his final 150 PA of the season after hitting only 2 in the first 300+, so he really ended the year on a power surge. Though his power hasn't fully shown up yet he'll still be just 19 at the start of this season and the team is optimistic that as he gains strength the power will come with it. While the Braves have much of their starting lineup locked up long-term, shortstop is one of the positions they could need help at in a year or two assuming Ha-Seong Kim doesn't re-sign again. With his bat-to-ball skills, improving approach, fantastic speed (54 SB last year), and good defense, John Gil could move up quickly in this organization. If his power trends up in 2026 he could be a big name to watch for. 

I think the tools are nice here for

players.name: Jose Perdomo
players.note: has struggled quite a bit since he was given a $5 million signing bonus back in 2024 and saw his card price drop over 50% last year. I'm still holding at this price because he's been injured and the tools are still awesome, but until I see it it's hard to buy much. I've actually liked

players.name: Luis Guanipa
players.note: 's tools and production even more but he's another one who can't seem to stay healthy. Not a ton of power but really good speed and defense make him pretty exciting to watch when he's on.

players.name: Cam Caminiti
players.note:
As a Braves fan I always joke watching the draft "which college pitcher coming off of TJ are we going to draft this year?", so when they went with a 17-year-old lefty I sat up in my chair a little more. He's someone I didn't go after cards of when they first came out because he was somewhat pricy considering he was years away from the MLB. Now that I've gotten a good look at him in 2025 I'm sold, and he's now moved all the way up to my 12th ranked non-debuted pitcher for the hobby. This is everything you want in a pitcher for Bowman. The 19-year-old has four pitches which could legitimately all be above average, headlined by a fastball that touches 98 with ride. Aside from that he throws a slider, curveball, and changeup, all of which flashed this past season though he does need a touch more consistency. 

As a former two-way player who played CF he's a fantastic athlete on the mound and his delivery is very repeatable. Last year in what was technically his age 18 season, Caminiti threw 70 innings between CPX & Single-A and had a 3.09 ERA, 3.30 FIP, 2.92 xFIP, 11.57 K/9, and 3.60 BB/9. And again to reiterate, he was pitching as an 18-year-old until August of that year. Unreal. The crazy part is that he was even more dominant after his promotion from the CPX to A, where he made 13 starts with a 2.08 ERA, 11.98 K/9, and held hitters there to a .210 average against him. 18 YEARS OLD. In the last 15 seasons do you know how many pitchers age 18 or younger had an ERA under 2.10 and K/9 over 11.5 in 50+ innings at Single-A? Two. 2021 Eury Perez and 2025 Cam Caminiti. The Braves are great at developing pitchers and they've got a farm full of talented arms. This one is easily my favorite in terms up upside.

players.name: JR Ritchie
players.note:
Back in 2022 the Braves used their first three draft picks on high school pitchers, one of those being JR Ritchie. He looked great in his professional debut that year and again in early 2023 before he was shut down with an elbow injury that required Tommy John surgery. When he returned in 2024 it was in more of a "ramping back up" capacity but the results looked great. In 49.2 innings between A & A+ he had a 2.90 ERA, 10.15 K/9, and 3.08 BB/9 in his return to game action. The expectations entering last year were high for Ritchie in the Braves organization and he did nothing to shake their confidence in him. He threw 140 innings, nearly 100 more than his previous high for a season, and finished with a 2.64 ERA, 9.00 K/9, and 3.47 BB/9. Now his 3.84 FIP and .215 BABIP suggest that maybe he got a little lucky and those numbers are friendlier than they could have been but one thing in particular stood out to me, and that's how aggressive the Braves were with his promotions. He entered last year having never thrown more than 10 innings at High-A and by the time the season ended he found himself in Triple-A. 

This is an Atlanta thing. Spencer Strider went from Single-A to the MLB in a single season (2021). AJ Smith-Shawver went from High-A to the MLB in a single season (2023). Spencer Schwellenbach went from High-A to the MLB in a single season (2024). Didier Fuentes went from High-A to the MLB in a single season (2025). When they have a guy they like they don't waste bullets in the minors, and Ritchie feels like the next one they want to see. His fastball, slider, and changeup all look like above average offerings and his athleticism on the mound gives him a repeatable delivery and solid command. I wish I could say I was blown away by his K numbers and whiff rates but neither really popped last year, however his .174 batting average against across three levels was pretty damn good. This is a proximity play. The day we are waiting for to cash in with most pitchers is their MLB debut. Not only is he believed by many to be the second best pitcher in this system behind Caminiti, he's basically a lock to debut this year health permitting.

players.name: Owen Murphy
players.note:
Murphy was one of the other arms taken in the same draft class as Ritchie, and though he was taken 15 picks higher they had nearly identical signing bonuses and pre-draft rankings. Another thing they have in common is that both of them have already needed elbow surgery, with Murphy's coming a year later in June of 2024. While Murphy seems to get much less love from outlets like MLB Pipeline and Baseball America, I actually thought he looked better than Ritchie at times last year. Now to be fair he only threw 30.1 innings since he wasn't able to return to the mound until late July, but considering it was his first game action since TJ he looked really strong. Oftentimes we see pitchers struggle with their command as they try to shake the rust but that couldn't have been further from the case for Murphy who had 1.78 BB/9 walking just 6 batters in his 7 starts at A+. In those starts he went 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA, 2.29 FIP, and 10.09 K/9. Fastball, curveball, slider is the mix here and though the stuff might not be quite as dynamic as Ritchie's his command is better and it really makes everything play up a notch. 

I think 2026 will be a big year for Murphy because the training wheels will come off and the Braves will let him eat, giving us a larger sample of pitching data. Chris Clegg from Dynasty Dugout has already closed the gap between Ritchie (101st ranked prospect) and Murphy (115th) to 10 ranking spots, and using the Peak Projections from Scout the Statline their career Minor League production ranks almost equally. With Murphy being more of a strike-thrower and Ritchie being on the doorstep of the MLB I do give Ritchie the nod but it's closer than some expect, and with him almost $10 cheaper on the base autograph he's just as good of a buy in my opinion. I can only get so excited about such a tiny sample, but of all pitchers age 21 or younger who threw 30+ innings last year (rookie leagues excluded) Owen Murphy was the only one who had a K% over 30% AND a BB% under 6%. If he can build on that performance this season I think he has the opportunity to be a big time riser in the prospect world.

I'm actually higher on

players.name: Briggs McKenzie
players.note: than most people and despite having never seen him throw against professional bats he's already inside my top 100 pitchers. In a perfect world I'd like to see his pro debut before I stack up too many autos but he's already on the verge of a buy at $16 for me. If this thing gets to $10-12 in the next couple of weeks I'm probably snagging some color of his. It took a $3 million signing bonus to keep him away from LSU (nearly $2.5 million over slot value), and if the Braves love you that much I'm inclined to believe they could be right.

players.name: Nate George
players.note: When I did my rankings for 2025 Bowman Chrome I had Nate George as my #4 overall chase in the product which I quickly learned was higher than many others seemed to be on him. And that makes sense. Bowman Chrome is always the "gamblers release" and most people who buy it are after the international lottery tickets like Josuar Gonzalez, Elian Pena, etc. When they zig I zag though and would much rather put my trust in players I've seen play stateside. Out of that crop it was hard to be more impressive than George was last season, and talk about a deep sleeper from the 2024 draft class. Of every high schooler from that class only five were able to reach High-A in their first full professional season. Three of those were 1st round picks including Konnor Griffin, one was an early 2nd rounder (Caleb Bonemer), and then you had Nate George from the… 16th round!! His FanGraphs page is a run of dominance. 92 PA in the CPX with a 171 wRC+, followed by 186 PA in Single-A with a 163 wRC+, and finally 92 more PA at High-A with a 132 wRC+ in his age 19 season. When you combine every stop the line looks like this: .337 AVG, .413 OBP, 5 HR, 50 SB, 10.3% BB, 16.8% K, .146 ISO, 158 wRC+. Pretty damn good. Now he did run a high BABIP of .405 so look for that average to trend down a bit but the contact rates were solid and much of that "luck" came from his ability to beat out throws with his plus speed. George being a hobby superstar is going to hinge on his power. FanGraphs calls it 55 but MLB Pipeline thinks it 45. Now he did only hit 5 HR last season but he also had 9 triples in fewer than 400 PA and his bat speed and loud contact have me leaning more towards that above average power grade. Since much of the power we saw last year was doubles and triples he may need a tweak of some kind to generate more loft if he's going to put up big HR numbers. 34th is probably the highest you'll see him ranked anywhere but I'm fine with that. There were 431 qualified teenage hitters in the minors last year, only 2 of them stole 50 bases and had an ISO over .145: Konnor Griffin and Nate George. Now he'll never have Konnor's power but he drew walks at a higher clip, struck out less frequently, and had a higher overall contact rate. He'll start this season still being only 19-years-old. If his game power ends up being above average we're talking about a guy who could legitimately be a top 10 prospect by the end of the year.

players.name: Ike Irish
players.note: and think his bat is going to be legit but since he's presently considered a catcher in Bowman and his base autograph is hovering close to $50 I think you can wait. Once he gets into the $25-30 range I think you can probably feel a little safer pulling the trigger.

players.name: Enrique Bradfield Jr.
players.note: is up nearly 50% since last year and that probably has more to do with him knocking on the doorstep of the big league team than anything. I don't think he's a bad buy at this price if you're going for a quick flip when he gets called up. He's an extremely exciting player but with his best tools being his speed and defense I'm not sure how much hype he generates, though I admit Chandler Simpson getting people buzzing may have cleared a path for more players like this to have hobby relevance. My favorite 3 for the price is probably 18-year-old shortstop

players.name: Aron Estrada
players.note:
The first time I mentioned Aron Estrada on my Substack was in June of last year when I wrote an article called "*Bob's Budget Buys*" highlighting my favorite hitting prospects with a base autograph under $10. His price then? $5. I've talked about it in the past on here, it might not seem sexy to be buying the "no-namers" but the opportunities to make money are much easier in my opinion when you dive a little deeper than most people are willing to. Now here we are already up 360% on Estrada's cards and I think we're going to keep going. Part of the reason that people may not have been paying more for his cards originally last year is because he's 5'8" and having such a small frame can be a tough sell in Bowman. Although he had a great year in 2024 with a 129 wRC+ between A & A+ his .129 ISO wasn't that special for his age. This past year he ticked that up quite a bit to a .159 ISO between A+ & AA and it was actually even higher after his promotion to AA where he had a .200 ISO in 110 PA. The switch-hitter makes good contact regularly posting contact rates near 80% and strikeout rates under 17%, while also adding a good amount of speed with a combined 73 SB over the past two seasons. His final line between both levels last year was .288 AVG, 10 HR, 34 SB, 9.9% BB, 16.9% K, .159 ISO, and 135 wRC+. Not bad for a guy that MLB Pipeline calls the Orioles' 22nd best prospect. And honestly I love that for us. While I don't think their prospect rankings should be used for determining whose cards to buy, them being low on guys creates a better buying opportunity for us because when they're late to the party and move someone up 10+ spots in one season we can see big reactions in the hobby (i.e. Esmerlyn Valdez). With many of these smaller guys we tend to see their ISO's trend down as they move up levels because better pitching can expose their lack of raw power. Estrada might end up having below average power but the fact that it seems to increase with each higher level he reaches can only be a green flag. Scout the Statline's Peak Projections uses a model to predict your Major League success based on your Minor League production. They have him as their 18th ranked hitting prospect in all of baseball. There were 11 prospects last year who had 10+ HR/30+ SB at age 20 or younger and only 4 of them did so while seeing time at Double-A. Konnor Griffin, Sebastian Walcott, Josue De Paula, and Aron Estrada. Not a bad list of names to be included with when your autograph is under $25.

Quite a laundry list of 3's for the Orioles as they have a ton of prospects that I like but don't love. I will say that I actually do love

players.name: Wilfri De La Cruz
players.note: I need to see him play in the states before I make a big move but he looked great in the DSL and is pretty cheap already for his tools. After that you're going ceiling hunting. Big hobby ceilings, big power potential, but BIG dice rolls. In that group I'd be looking at

players.name: Luis De León
players.note: Before I looked at pricing I honestly thought that De Leon would be like a $10-15 guy and I was going to be able to slam a 5 rating on him, but it appears that some people out there are sharper than I give them credit for because this is a fun arm that hasn't gotten much public love yet. Talk about a find for the Orioles who signed him for just $30,000 back in 2021. De Leon is absolutely electric. He's a 6'3" lefty that throws an upper-90's bowling ball that has tremendous sink and induces ground ball rates around 60% or higher. The slider was unhittable this year and could grade as a double plus pitch and his changeup has really good fade away from righties giving him an effective third offering. With all of these things I've said you can probably guess that I'm about to say his issue has been control. His delivery and release point can get all over the place and in 2024 he had a 4.62 ERA, 3.70 FIP, 10.88 K/9, and 5.03 BB/9, showing a good ability to miss bats but also struggling with command. The improvements we saw this past season are really what shot him up the list though. In 20 appearances across 87.1 innings he had a 3.30 ERA, 2.59 FIP, 11.03 K/9, and 4.23 BB/9. The Orioles liked what they saw so much that they twice promoted him despite him not even reaching 100 innings and he finished the year in Double-A. In his last two stops at A+ & AA he had a BB/9 under 4 at both of them, marking the first times he had gone under that number at any stint in his career so far. When you look at the numbers side by side from 2024 to 2025 there are tons of other things that make me think he's trending in the right direction too. His K% went from 26.3% to 28.5%, BB% from 12.2% to 10.9%, but the biggest might be that contact rates against him dropped from 72% to 65.1%. He could be a 5 if not for the extreme reliever risk he comes with but even with that I still like him as a buy, especially since he continues to improve in all of the areas that seem to be sort of yellow flags. To give you an idea of how hard his pitches are to square up he pitched in Single-A, High-A, and Double-A this year facing a total of 375 batters and not a single one took him deep. Zero HR's allowed. This stuff is just too good to ignore.

players.name: Joseph Dzierwa
players.note: could be getting close to his buy range as his base autograph is already down to $10 just weeks after the release of 2025 Bowman Draft. Another 6'8" lefty he was dominate last year at Michigan St. though he's more of a strike-thrower than a pure stuff guy which could limit his hobby upside unless some of his pitches tick up. Not a bad play at all but definitely a better floor than ceiling right now. I'm most intrigued by

players.name: Boston Bateman
players.note: You've probably noticed that I love a high ceiling on a cheap player so it's hard not to like Boston Bateman who is a 6'8" lefty that the Orioles acquired at the deadline from the Padres. In the 2024 draft San Diego selected him in the 2nd round out of high school giving him a $2.5 million signing bonus and it's worth noting that while the Padres farm is depleted from trading all of their prospects away they've actually been really good at finding young talent. Apart from his giant stature Bateman was praised by scouts during the pre-draft process for his makeup and way that he approaches the game. He can sit in the mid-90's and touched 97 last year and he pairs that with a really good plus grade slider that is probably his best pitch. He also will randomly throw in a 12-6-ish curve but very rarely and more often will go to a changeup for his third pitch but it definitely needs some work. Bateman moved around a bit last year making 15 starts in Single-A with San Diego where he had a 4.08 ERA, 3.23 FIP, 9.88 K/9, and 3.29 BB/9 prior to the trade. Upon arrival to Baltimore's system he made just two starts at that same level before the Orioles decided they wanted to see him in High-A for the end of the year. All in all his final stat line at three stops was a 4.14 ERA, 3.54 FIP, 9.72 K/9, and 3.93 BB/9. His FIP and xFIP both being lower than his ERA lead me to believe he pitched better than the stats show and his .358 BABIP would probably agree. I'm interested to see what Baltimore does with him in the offseason as far as developing his secondary pitches but starting off with a 55 fastball, 60 curveball, and solid command as a 6'8" left-hander is a heck of a jumping off point for a kid so young. While you won't often hear them labeled as a "pitching factory" like some other teams the Orioles have been sneakily good and now have 6 non-debuted pitching prospects in my top 100 and that's not including Bateman who is 101st. This could be a great fit and there's some really solid potential here for $8.

players.name: Tyson Neighbors
players.note: of the 3's because his numbers last year were incredible. In 44 appearances between A+ & AA he had a 1.53 ERA, 12.66 K/9, and 3.51 BB/9. Great slider, nasty curve, 36.4% K rate. The downside is that some prospects have "reliever risk" and he is… well.. already a reliever. 0 career starts. I do still think there's a path to hobby relevance as a lights out reliever (look at the spike Mason Miller's cards did) but it's not an area I've ever tried to attack in buying. That's not to say it can't be done though if any of you are brave enough to give it a try! It's a very cheap entry point considering how well he's pitched.

players.name: Franklin Arias
players.note: On last year's Boston sheet there were three different non-debut hitting prospects with base autographs over $100. Now that they've all debuted Arias is the top guy for the hitting side, and while his auto hasn't quite gotten up there yet I think it will. Arias started generating buzz in 2024 when he had one of the best stateside debuts of any international prospect. At age 18 between CPX & A he hit .309 with 9 HR, 35 SB, 13.4% BB, 17.5% K, .178 ISO, and 143 wRC+. Last season his stats didn't pop as much. In 526 PA he hit .278 with 8 HR, 12 SB, 7.2% BB, 10.1% K, .111 ISO, and 109 wRC+. The power and wRC+ were both way down and it's absolutely slowing people from going in big on his cards. He is after all projected for below average power which is a huge strike in the hobby, but I don't think it tells the whole story here. For starters Arias is playing at extremely advanced levels for his age. He started the year in Single-A but was twice promoted and finished the year in Double-A where he'll likely begin 2026. After posting a 77% contact rate in his breakout season back in 2024 that number went up to… wait for it… 89.1% last year. It was 87.3% in A, 89.8% in A+, and 87.4% in AA, all at age 19 with a combined swinging strike rate of 5.3%. His contact skills are bananas. And not only that he is the best defensive shortstop in the entire Red Sox system. Though we always joke that defense doesn't matter in the hobby, it does if you're so good at it that a team is willing to fast track you through the Minor Leagues. I mean most 19-year-olds hitting .265 with a 107 wRC+ in High-A aren't seeing an early second promotion, but when your bat-to-ball skills and defense are both this good that's what happens. If you filter FanGraphs to show teenage prospects with 300+ PA and an ISO over .110 for last season you get 57 results. Only 6 of them reached Double-A or higher. Konnor Griffin, Leo De Vries, Sebastian Walcott, Jesus Made, Colt Emerson, and Franklin Arias. The other 5 are ALL in my top 10 non-debuted hitting prospects. Rarely will I recommend buying a prospect with below average power but the other skills here could be elite. On top of that this is one of the best hobby fanbases and he might be their only hitting prospect that will generate any excitement this year. It might not be until 2027 but when his name is called for a debut you better believe the Red Sox fans are going to be paying well over $65 for this card.

players.name: Yophery Rodriguez
players.note: who they acquired from the Brewers. Good contact hitter with great speed who has flashed power but not consistently. 2025 line isn't overly impressive but he was unlucky on the BABIP side and looked great in his two full years with Milwaukee. He's a good dark horse pick to be the best breakout prospect in this system. If you like the buy low spots as with Bleis, the prices for

players.name: Yoeilin Cespedes
players.note: went down about 60% after he struggled in Single-A but he looked dominant in the DSL & CPX. Smaller but good pop (Howie Kendrick-ish), could be a nice bounce back candidate. After those two I've been tempted in the past by

players.name: Miguel Bleis
players.note:
As someone who sadly ripped a lot of 2021 Bowman Chrome I admit that I squinted a little bit when I saw this price to make sure I was reading it right. Now the hard part here is that he only has 1 sale I could find in the past 3 months so I don't know that we can actually find them at this price since someone seems to be hoarding them, but since a PSA 9 of his Refractor Auto just sold for $18 I don't think it's too far off. There was a time not too long ago when outside of Emmanuel Rodriguez (MIN) we thought Bleis would be the one who would have to save the whole product since the checklist flopped so hard. He was a huge chase and I have a screenshot from March of 2023 when the going rate on his 1st Refractor Autograph /499 was $275. That's because when it comes to tools he's the hobby dream. He's electric and that's in the power and speed departments where he's got a 60 grade on both. Unfortunately the tools don't matter if you can't consistently make contact and he's never been able to do so. Last year between A+ & AA, Bleis hit .222 with 14 HR, 27 SB, 9.3% BB, 23.9% K, .164 ISO, and 100 wRC+. Not a BB/K ratio at 0.39 that you ever love to see as he's chase prone and swings for the fences on nearly every cut he takes. But when he does make contact the exit velocities are crazy impressive. And he's got a plus arm in the outfield which helps him be an above average outfielder defensively too. This is 4 legit tools, but when the missing one is the ability to make contact that's a tough sell. And I admit I am a notorious hater of this type of prospect for Bowman. Give me the small contact hitters and let me pray the power comes before you give me a physical freak of nature who struggles to put the bat on the ball. With that said, $7?! This was an $100 autograph two years ago. It was $35 on last year's sheet. It went down 80% again. How much lower could it go?! Dangerous question I know but we've got to be close to the floor I'd think. I mentioned his 14 HR/27 SB line from last year. There were only six hitters in the minors who did that at age 21 or younger and also had a swinging strike % under 12.5%. Konnor Griffin (my #1), Eduardo Quintero (#7), Edward Florentino (#8), Aidan Miller (#11), Jett Williams (#23), and Miguel Bleis (#267). He terrifies me personally but for those of you who don't mind throwing money at a dice roll with a high ceiling, as the saying goes 'you can't teach size and speed'. 

Boston has a boat load of 3's that I like but that's to be expected. When you are a franchise with one of the biggest and most loyal fanbases it causes there to be a tax on the cards of your players because more people are fighting over them. It puts a bunch of guys in the "I like him but he's not cheap enough" bucket. My favorite is

players.name: Allan Castro
players.note:
who despite being a top 20 Sox prospect and nearly cracking the StS top 250 has gotten zero love. 119 wRC+ last year in AA, improving contact, good raw power, and solid speed. Nothing stands out as being a "wow" in the box score but should start the year in AAA and has had an extremely productive career for a guy with an autograph this cheap.

I'm a fan of all three pitchers from 2025 Bowman Draft but I think we still have one more week before prices reach the range where they'll sit for the next month.

players.name: Kyson Witherspoon
players.note: should be an absolute monster after time in the Red Sox pitching lab and he's already inside my top 10 before he even throws a pitch as a professional. Even then $60 is a touch steep considering both of my top 2 pitchers sit around $70-75. I'm probably looking for Kyson in the $50 range and if he gets there I'd feel confident buying.

players.name: Marcus Phillips
players.note: are almost identical in my rankings at the moment barely outside the top 100. For that range with pitchers I'm looking for a $10-12 auto to load up on, we'll see if they get there. Based on my rankings versus the price

players.name: Yordanny Monegro
players.note: made the most sense to me as a buy. Had a 2.84 ERA and 11.18 K/9 in 2024 and looked to be on an even better track last year with a 2.67 ERA and 13.10 K/9 in 8 starts at AA. Unfortunately tore his UCL and will miss all of this season. Keep an eye out though if these continue to dip under $10 while he's out I may grab something to stash away for 2027. If you're surprised by a

players.name: Shane Drohan
players.note: sighting I can tell you so was I. Not the biggest hobby ceiling since he's now 27-years-old but had one of the sneakiest seasons you didn't hear about last year and is now ranked as a top 100 pitcher by StS. Went 5-1 with a 2.27 ERA and 12.65 K/9 in AAA which is damn good. Should get the call this year so not a bad play at $10. Dart throw time.

players.name: Sadbiel Delzine
players.note: The stuff is nasty, he's 6'5", and he just turned 18 last month. Only threw 9.1 innings and it was in the DSL so I need to see more but for $5 this is could be a fun one.

players.name: Ethan Conrad
players.note: For the first 'buy' on the Cubs sheet I'm going to go with their 1st round pick from last year's draft Ethan Conrad. When I did my 2025 Bowman Draft rankings he was my 8th favorite hitter to chase in the entire product which was the highest of any college bat. It's only been a month since then and no games have been played so my feelings are exactly the same. Back in 2024 as a 19-year-old Sophomore at Marist University he hit .389 with 9 HR, 19 SB, 10.4% BB, 12.4% K, .314 ISO, and 183 wRC+ in 55 games. That year he had a .704 SLG because on top of those 9 homers he added an absolutely absurd 13 triples which led all Division I hitters in the country. The stat line was crazy but I'd still need to see two more things before I bought into a player, how he handles a wood bat and how he fares against better competition. After that season at Marist he played in the Cape Cod League where in 30 games he had a .430 OBP, and both his .385 AVG and .920 OPS ranked second in the entire league. Wood bat, check. Conrad then transferred to Wake Forest where in 21 games he hit .372 with 7 HR, 4 SB, 18.6% BB, 14.4% K, .372 ISO, and 167 wRC+. Sadly an injury ended his season after only 97 PA and while that's not enough for me to officially say he dominated that next step up in competition, he had a .495 OBP, .744 SLG, 1.238 OPS, and more walks than strikeouts in his time there so… I'd say that's ok. He's extremely physical, flashes plus run times, has a compact swing with really quick hands, and can hit the ball with power to any part of the field. Conrad checks just about every offensive box that you can coming into your professional debut season. Though he's not exactly cheap I think people are sleeping on him in this new product a bit since he's not a prep and is coming off an injury, but make no mistake about it this is in my opinion the most well-rounded collegiate hitter in this entire draft class. To make things even better this $49 comp is a rolling average but the few most recent sales have gotten down into the $35-40 range. He's already a 4/5 for me under $50 but if this gets to $30-35 before Spring Training he's absolutely a 5/5. Every year there are college guys who are slept on in Bowman Draft that I put a stamp on and say these are THE guys you want. Last year it was Ryan Waldschmidt and Mike Sirota. This year it's Ethan Conrad.

players.name: Jonathon Long
players.note: There may not be a single prospect in baseball who has been slept on more for the past three years than Jonathon Long. It's a little bit funky of a profile in that he's a first baseman who might be hit-over-power and bats righty which isn't the easiest player to fit into a lineup, but this bat is so good that the Cubs are going to have to find a way. And with Owen Caissie now shipped off to Miami the number of players trying to take that roster spot from him has shrunk by one already. After being drafted in the 9th round in 2023 and signing for $180,000, Long made his debut that year hitting .274 with 7 HR and a 169 wRC+ in 102 PA. Yeah whatever, 21-year-old in Single-A, not a huge sample. The next year he started in High-A where he played 68 games before being promoted to Double-A for the final 46 games. His line across both levels was: .283 AVG, 17 HR, 14.1% BB, 20.7% K, .177 ISO, and 148 wRC+. Now I'm listening. What's even more impressive is that he hit .340 with 7 HR, a .189 ISO, and 188 wRC+ AND had more walks than strikeouts in his 200 PA in Double-A after the promotion. Starting to feel like maybe we should pay attention to him. Last year in Triple-A Long hit .305 with 20 HR, 13.0% BB, 19.1% K, .173 ISO, and 131 wRC+. While sacrificing none of his power he raised his contact rate by 3% and finished the AAA season with a 80.7% contact rate and 7.9% swinging strike %. He has an easy, quick swing that generates good raw power and hits the ball hard to all parts of the field while also being selective enough to wait for the pitch he wants. Last year he only pulled 36.4% of his batted balls while hitting 35.7% to the opposite field and 27.9% up the middle. He's a professional hitter. The downside is that Michael Busch had a breakout year and is holding down the 1B spot, and though the Cubs have tried Long at 3B and in LF he's not particularly great at either one, so his path to a call-up is his bat being so good he forces their hand which I think is coming really soon. Here's a simple one, last year there were only 3 prospects in all of baseball age 23 or younger who hit over .300 and had 20+ HR: Konnor Griffin, Sal Stewart, and Jonathon Long. Decent company. The highest walk rate and BB/K of those 3? Long. The lowest SwStr%? Long. Yeah, that'll play.

players.name: Jefferson Rojas
players.note:
Considering he's still only 20-years-old it's already been a wild ride in the hobby for Rojas. He had his moment in 2023 when everyone thought he could be a hobby star and his price shot up over $40 and then after struggling in 2024 it dropped all the way down to $15. It's come up a shade since then but I think this could be the year that we see it start to creep back up more. He was a 4 for me on last year's sheet because despite the down year in 2024 there were actually a ton of underlying metrics that led me to believe that he'd bounce back. And personally I think he did, the card market just didn't take notice as much as they should have. In that off year where everyone jumped ship in 2024, Rojas hit .245 with a 8.4% BB, 15.3% K, .091 ISO, and 88 wRC+ in High-A. Last year the Cubs had him repeat that level and the improvements were real as he hit .278 with a 12.7% BB, 15.7% K, .214 ISO, and 145 wRC+. His pitch selection improved drastically. He swung at 6% fewer pitches which not only led to a 4.3% increase in his walks but it allowed him to hunt the pitches he was looking for, and the hunt was a success. His .214 ISO was more that double what it was the year prior and he did so without sacrificing a shred of his contact skills as they were almost mirror images of each other at 81%. Here's the downside, they promoted him to Double-A and the same thing happened that it did back in High-A in 2024, the contact skills were still really, really good but the power fell off of a cliff and an extremely unlucky BABIP dropped his average and production significantly. I'm not worried for the same reason I wasn't last year. Underlying metrics are good and I have faith that when he comes back to that level in a few months everything will take off again. The swing is gorgeous, he makes great contact, and when he returns a bit stronger this year I think he'll make some noise. It feels weird to be buying a second bounce back on a prospect this young but I'm still a believer.

Bunch of good 3's here in the Cubs system my favorite two at the moment are probably their other two hitters who were in 2025 Bowman Draft along with Ethan Conrad.

players.name: Kane Kepley
players.note: is the other and he's your Sam Antonacci-type. Fantastic bat-to-ball skills and he's allergic to striking out. Hit .299 with a 180 wRC+ in his pro debut with a 19.1% BB, 11.5% K, and 85.9% contact rate. Plus hit and plus speed all day and being inside my top 100 this price is fair for him already, but since I know the power is easily below average I'd need it around $10-12. Love the player but not sure that the hobby will. After that I like

players.name: Josiah Hartshorn
players.note: is a high ceiling prep bat that stands at 6'2" 220 pounds already and projects for plus power. He's a switch-hitter who won the All-Star High School Home Run Derby but I'm unsure on the hit tool. That's partly because he had elbow and back injuries in high school which caused him to only bat righty for full years and then only bat lefty for another. Love the upside but I'm cautious, would probably need him under $15 but he's getting close.

players.name: Juan Cabada
players.note: who had a great DSL debut and $11 is already a solid deal but he's got a smaller frame and I'd like to see if he shows any pop against the better pitching here before I buy in. Great upside for the price though. I'll give you one more and that's

players.name: Cole Mathis
players.note: Was a big sleeper for a lot of people in the 2024 draft after hitting .335 with a .315 ISO and 1.44 BB/K at Charleston. Somewhat of a Jonathon Long-esque profile in that it could be above average hit and power but he's been hurt so we haven't seen much. Good breakout candidate for this year.

players.name: Jaxon Wiggins
players.note: From a hobby standpoint Jaxon Wiggins checks almost all of the boxes you want to see in a pitcher. First, the stuff. Electric. The 6'6" righty can sit in the high-90's and reach back for 100 with movement. Secondary offerings are also filthy as he features a slider that makes hitters look silly and a changeup that he ramps up to the mid-80's with deceiving arm speed that falls off the map. All three of his pitches are above average. The slider is plus. The fastball might even be double plus. It's just a nasty arsenal for a starting pitcher to have. Now let's talk about the proximity. While hitters are different in that we can buy and sell at peaks and valleys over the course of years, with pitchers we're almost always looking for that MLB debut. We've seen it with Jacob Misiorowski. A guy gets called up, has filthy stuff, racks up some K's, his card prices go through the roof. That's the dream. Well, Wiggins reached AAA last year and will start there this year, so when the time comes that the Cubs have an injury in their rotation or need a spot start we're probably going to see him and I think it's before the All-Star break. Not only that but he is THE ONLY pitching prospect in this organization who is exciting at the moment so he should get plenty of buzz leading up to that debut. Now let's talk results. Last year Wiggins was promoted twice, starting the year in High-A and finishing in Triple-A. Between all three levels he threw 78 innings with a 2.19 ERA, 11.19 K/9, and 4.15 BB/9. Walk rates aren't exactly ideal but they were much improved from his 5.43 back in 2024, and the bulk of his starts last year came in Double-A where that number was even lower at 3.64. In his 68.1 innings he threw between High-A and Double-A, opposing hitters had a .146 batting average against Wiggins and his strikeout rate was north of 30%. Don't get me wrong I'm worried about the command but I also stayed away from Jacob Misiorowski cards because I thought he'd end up a reliever. The fact is that certain guys have the stuff that will make the hype explode IF they're on for those first couple of weeks when they get to the show. I think Jaxon Wiggins has that same stuff and we're going to see it this year.

players.name: Brandon Birdsell
players.note: is an interesting name if you like to stash guys away. Probably would have made his MLB debut last year but needed TJ after just 4 starts in AAA. Bad news is that this is his second time since he had it in college prior to the Cubs drafting him. I'd imagine as the season goes on and people aren't seeing him pitch this gets under $5 and while there's more risk now with that second elbow surgery I don't hate it as a dollar bin stash for 2027 if it gets there. Good stuff, great command, funky arm action and has been a really productive minor-leaguer.

players.name: Caleb Bonemer
players.note:
*

My first (and possibly last) buy rating with an asterisk. That's because the spread on Caleb Bonemer's base autograph sales is wild. In his last 5 alone which we use to get our average there is a $59 sale and a $100 sale, both confirmed. If you see Bonemer's autographs at $55-60 he's a slam dunk 5/5 buy in my opinion. When you get closer to what his average is, say $75-80, I still would give him a 4/5. Once these things creep to $100 which it looks like some have he probably goes to a 3.5 where I'm teetering between buy and hold. In most cases if a player's cards have gone up 600% in the last year like Bonemer's have I'm cashing everything out. But he's a rare case because my ranking of him as a top 15 hobby prospect is EXTREMELY aggressive, and given that he's surrounded by guys with $100-200 base autos I still think there's a little room to go up from here. Although I was cautious with him when 2024 Bowman Draft was released, it only took a couple months of watching him before I began beating the drum on him having the skills we're looking for. I think the first few times I tweeted about him his base autograph was still in the $20 range. Now he's gotten a ton of offseason hype including a top 30 ranking by Baseball America and his price continues to climb. And he deserves it. Coming into the draft the reports from evaluators were that he had some of the best speed in the entire class, with big time power to his pull side, but might have some hit tool concerns as he was inconsistent against better competition as a prep. Whatever questions there were about his ability to make contact were erased quickly in his professional debut where at age 19 Bonemer had a 78.3% contact rate and 8.4% swinging strike % between A & A+. His approach which many thought could be too aggressive early on? 15.8% BB to 21.2% K (0.74 BB/K) and just a 38.8% Swing%. Considering that we thought those two things could be a weakness they looked pretty damn good and his power was as advertised for a teenager as he hit 12 HR with a .192 ISO. Oh, and he stole 29 bases. Oh, and he had a 151 wRC+. Not a single player other than maybe Konnor Griffin improved their stock more in the 2025 season for me than Caleb Bonemer. The only prospects age 19 or younger last year who had 400+ PA with an ISO over .190 and SwStr% under 10% were Equardo Quintero and Caleb Bonemer. If you expand the SwStr% to 11.5% you add Konnor Griffin and Leo De Vries to that list. You don't hear Caleb Bonemer ever mentioned in the same conversations as these types of guys but if his 2026 looks anything like his 2025 it's going to happen soon.

players.name: Braden Montgomery
players.note: who I honestly went back and forth on and was very close to giving a 4. Fantastic power potential from the 6'2" switch hitter and he looked the part last year with wRC+ marks of 150 in A, 135 in A+, and 133 in AA. Great upside play but there are certain things that make me pause when I'm paying $60-ish for a base auto and one is that he had a contact rate under 70% at all three levels. Hobby superstar ceiling but I think the swing-and-miss is more questionable than people expect. Hit a HR every 77.2 PA as a RHH in his pro debut and every 18.7 PA as a LHH, might be better off as lefty-only. Fascinated by

players.name: Billy Carlson
players.note: but he's more of a hold for me than anything until I see his bat against professional pitching. If he has 20 HR upside with above average speed I could get in on this profile quickly considering he's one of the best defensive prep shortstops many scouts have ever seen. If it's double plus defense and the bat is just 'eh' this price is going to be too steep for me. Fun player but need to see it.

players.name: Sam Antonacci
players.note: From a guy that I was cautious about in 2024 Bowman Draft in Bonemer to a guy that I screamed from the rooftops how he was undervalued, those who know me know I've always been a big Sam Antonacci fan. That's because from a bat-to-ball perspective he's one of my favorite hitters in the entirety of Minor League Baseball. I don't throw around 60 hit grades. Antonacci has one. It's tough to find many statistics for D-II baseball but as a Freshman and Sophomore at Heartland Community College, Antonacci hit .471 and .515. Those are batting averages by the way not OBP's. Tough to gauge the competition there but he then transferred to Coastal Carolina for a season. The results there? .367 AVG, .523 OBP, 1.027 OPS, 6 HR, 15 SB, 16.3% BB, 13.1% K. Three consecutive years in college with an OBP over .500. After being drafted he was assigned to Single-A for his pro debut where in 102 PA he hit .333 with a 16.7% BB, 12.7% K, .471 OBP, and 170 wRC+. This is when I had him pinned as a deep sleeper given that his base autograph was selling under $5. He did not disappoint last year against a rise in competition and between A+ & AA he hit .291 with 5 HR, 48 SB, 13.3% BB, 14.1% K, .118 ISO, .433 OBP, and 156 wRC+. Across both levels he had a combined 86.8% contact rate and a swinging strike rate of 5.2%. Of course the issue here is how high can your ceiling be in Bowman without power. Seeing that he's already gone from $4 last offseason to almost $20 now tells me that it hasn't been an issue yet. I just don't see how he doesn't fly through this organization. He'll likely start the year in AA but he's already been announced as a non-roster invitee to Spring Training where I suspect that he will turn some heads. I wouldn't say this about probably any other hitter in all of AA but I genuinely believe you could put Sam Antonacci in the White Sox MLB lineup today and he would hit, probably better than half of their current starters. His hobby upside is definitely capped by the fact that he'll have below average power and while I think that's something that will stop him from ever being a $100 base auto guy, I don't think this doubling again and getting to $40-50 by the time he debuts is out of the question. Not counting the rookie levels only two hitters in all of the minors last year had a wRC+ over 155 and a SwStr% under 8%: Kevin McGonigle and Sam Antonacci. Only two had an OBP over .415 and 48+ SB: Konnor Griffin and Sam Antonacci. I'm not suggesting that he has the most exciting parts of either one of their profiles but if there are names in the hobby you want to be on a list with those are the two.

players.name: George Wolkow
players.note: is your roulette wheel spin. The power on the 6'7" lefty is as high as the scale can go but his contact rates are terrifying. I understand the draw of his cards because that power ceiling is elite but you have to make contact and I'm not positive he will. Still very young though just turning 20 last month so your hope is that with a few more years of experience he could be Spencer Jones. Risky for $20 but I get it. My White Sox dart throw of the 3's is

players.name: Kyle Lodise
players.note:
I admit that this isn't one that I expected to love but I did have him as a sleeper in my 2025 Bowman Draft article and I'm pretty surprised that his autographs are already trending towards the $6-7 range. Not a big name coming out of high school Lodise went the D-II route like Antonacci for two years before transferring to a bigger school. His last year at D-II Augusta he hit .369 with 14 HR, 24 SB, and a 1.59 BB/K. In his lone season at Georgia Tech he batted .329 with 16 HR, 13 SB, 12.8% BB, 17.7% K, .338 ISO, and 135 wRC+. I think the approach and contact are both above average and while his run times aren't out of this world he has a really good baseball IQ and is opportunistic on the basepaths which allows him to be a threat there. The big question here is going to be the power which is likely a tick below average and when he played with wood bats in the Cape Cod League he didn't look that great. His professional debut is really what has me more bullish on him than I was coming out of the draft. Though most people are going to look at the stat line and see that he hit .185 in 113 PA at High-A it's worth noting that his .188 BABIP was extremely low, and had it been closer to the league average he would have hit close to 50 points higher. Despite being below the Mendoza line he was still able to get to a 108 wRC+ thanks to a good walk rate (13.3%) and surprisingly good power. Of his 17 hits, 8 of them went for extra bases including 4 HR and a triple which gave him a .185 ISO. It's a bit of a mixed bag of results but I'm not too worried about the average because I know the contact skills and approach are fine, I wanted to see how the power would look and to be honest I think it was quite a bit better than I expected. I won't overreact to a small sample but the rankings from Dynasty Dugout and Rotowire confirm that my eyes did not deceive me in that pro debut. Not many prospects are going to be ranked in the top 500 by both of these publications and have a base autograph under $10. To me that makes Lodise's cards kind of a sneaky play in hopes of a breakout season in 2026.

Samuel Zavala ($5*)

When I started the Hobby Advantage Tool at Scout the Statline I'll never forget how much Samuel Zavala broke the ratings system early on. That's because he debuted at age 16 in the DSL with a 143 wRC+ and carried that over to the states where at age 17 he had a 127 wRC+ and an absolutely absurd .258 ISO between CPX & A. One of the most ridiculous 17-year-old seasons I've seen since I got into Bowman. And to be honest he dominated Single-A again when he started the year there in 2023 at age 18 but following a promotion to High-A that year he struggled quite a bit. I took it as a "ok no need to worry he's still very young for the level", but then he hit .187 when he repeated it in 2024. This led to him dropping off of everybody's map as far as ranking prospects. Now I will say some of the underlying data wasn't so bad for a .187 hitter including a 79% contact rate, 7.3% SwStr%, and 17.8% walk rate. All very good. He almost got caught in this kind of funk we've seen Jaison Chourio fall in at times where they get so selective they're passive to a fault. Walk rates stay high, OBP and wRC+ are fine, but the rest of the stat line is yuck. Well this past year Zavala finally did what I'm always hoping these type of hitters do and that's swing the bat. He increased his Swing% from 34.6% to 41.9% and the results were fantastic. His batting average went up almost 70 points to .254 and he raised his wRC+ by 25 from 97 to 122. Though it feels like he should be dead to us from a Bowman perspective since he was in High-A in three different seasons, it's not actually that bad when you consider he was 18 on his first try. There were only 5 qualified minor leaguers in High-A last year who were 20 or younger and had a wRC+ higher than Zavala's and a few of those names are Josue De Paula, Zyhir Hope, and Colt Emerson. I'm not going to pretend like I love Zavala nearly as much as I did in 2023 but this feels like rock bottom as far as a buy low spot. His base autographs were redemptions and very rarely have posted sales but I watched a PSA 10 1st Refractor Auto /499 of his end at $16.50 the other day. I've seen players who are no longer on rosters sell for more than that. Zavala is still only 21, once had quite a bit of hobby hype and pedigree, looked much improved last year, and should start the year in Double-A. Quite a bit to like as a cheaper sleeper.

Most notable of the 3's is of course

players.name: Javier Mogollon
players.note: Dominated DSL (.267 ISO, 147 wRC+) and the CPX (.266 ISO, 132 wRC+) but had bad contact rates in both. Improved his contact a ton this past year but even then it's still not great. 5'8" but he can swing it, might have legit 55 power 60 speed and is only 20. Pretty fun for $7.

players.name: Hagen Smith
players.note: Both of them fall into the same category for me currently. As you can see I really like them since they're almost side-by-side in my top 30 pitcher rankings, the downside is that neither of them are particularly cheap. The last article I did was the Cubs where Jaxon Wiggins was $50 and I had him as a top 10 hobby arm. The article before that I said I'd like to see Kyson Witherspoon who is also in my top 10 get to that $50 range. Schultz and Smith are both similarly priced but are ranked 15+ spots lower. Still love them I just don't love the value currently. Recently acquired

players.name: Tanner McDougal
players.note:
I bet everyone who got to pitchers was ready to hear me talk about how you should buy Noah Schultz and Hagen Smith right? Well, in the name of value give me some Tanner McDougal cards instead! He's been on my undervalued pitchers lists a few times over the past 6 months or so and even though his prices have more than doubled since then I still don't think he's too expensive here. It was a forgettable year in 2024 for McDougal who went 0-11 in 22 starts with a 6.04 ERA, 11.31 K/9, and 5.65 BB/9. No surprise he didn't start the 2025 season inside my top 100. But what he did last year catapulted him almost into the top half of that list. Making 28 starts between A+ & AA, McDougal had a 3.26 ERA, 3.15 FIP, 10.80 K/9, and 3.89 BB/9. And he got even better after the promotion to AA where his FIP was 2.76 and his BB/9 dropped all the way to 2.75. The stuff coming out of the hand of the 6'5" right hander was never a question, his fastball touches 100 and his high-spin curveball and slider give him three pitches that could legitimately be plus with some more refinement. His issue in the past of course was with command, and when he struggled to find the zone he not only handed out a ton of free passes but him getting behind in counts led to a lot of fastballs down the pipe and a lot of home runs. In 2024 he surrendered 13 HR in 65.2 innings at High-A and had a HR/FB ratio of 23.2%. Last season with the improve command on all of his pitches he gave up 7 in 113.1 innings dropping his HR/FB to 7.8%. If his control backs up on him again he has big time reliever risk and I think that's definitely affecting his ranking, though because of his stuff he could still be an electric reliever. But for now the White Sox are going to continue to develop him as a starter and he hasn't so much as made 1 relief appearance in the last three seasons. If he were to take another step forward in 2026 with the ability to repeat his delivery and locate all of his pitches his stock could go way up, and he's definitely trending in the right direction. In the 15 starts he made from June 1st thru August 31st he had a 2.08 ERA with 72 K's in 60.2 innings. Chris Clegg and James Anderson BOTH have him ranked higher than Schultz and Smith for dynasty which I admit feels extremely aggressive, but it's a testament to just how dominant he looked in the second half of 2025.

The two biggest names when it comes to White Sox arms are

players.name: David Sandlin
players.note: isn't a bad bet at under $10 either but I'd wait to see how the White Sox use him since the Red Sox shifted him primarily to the bullpen when he reached AAA. He's odd because based on all of the stuff readings he's got 4+ pitches that could play but he didn't miss nearly as many bats this past year as you'd expect. Interested to see what the White Sox do with him but could be a good sleeper since he should debut this year.

players.name: Steele Hall
players.note: I think we've officially reached that point where 2025 Bowman Draft singles are starting to hit their bottom and because the product was delayed by a month we're actually seeing some of them creep back up as we approach Spring Training. In my hitter rankings I had Steele Hall as my third favorite autograph on this entire checklist and although $70 is still steep, to me he's the type of player worth taking this chance on. What pulls me back and forth on him a little is that there could definitely be growing pains early on as he adjusts to professional pitching. I expect him to get to average power but his swing isn't currently geared for that presently so I won't be too shocked if we don't see a ton of it early on, but when it comes to Bowman prospects we are looking at two things that could take a player to that elite level of hobby stardom and that's athleticism and age, two things very much working in the favor of Hall who will be 18 for the whole first half of this season. He's the most athletic player in this entire system and has easily 70 grade speed maybe even 80 depending on who you ask. Not only does that make him electric on the base paths but he also has great range on the dirt as well and a plus arm which could make him a 60 grade defender at shortstop. His Junior year of high school Hall hit .484 with 8 HR, 14 2B, 5 3B, and 33 SB in 37 games and because he reclassified prior to this season he was draft eligible as a 17-year-old. There are different ways to approach buying Bowman prospects and I know everybody has their preference. If you want a safe play you could definitely look elsewhere at this price but if you're hunting for ceilings this is the type of guy you want. I thought Konnor Griffin's base auto being $150 before he debuted seemed crazy high because despite his tools he was a bit of a dice roll and look what happened. That's not to say Steele Hall is Konnor Griffin he doesn't have near Konnor's power, but when kids this young have this type of athleticism their ceiling, IF they hit it, puts them in a different tier simply because they can do things on the field that others physically cannot do. I'm not denying there is risk but I like the player, love the tools, love the organizational fit, and if it all clicks the upside is massive.

players.name: Alfredo Duno
players.note: as a 3 and listen I LOVE him. Was high on him last year and even with his price up nearly 200% I still like him. With their pricing being the same it's not that I'm saying Steele Hall is a better prospect than Duno, especially since Duno is more proven, but if I'm buying a $70 base auto it's because I'm hoping it's a guy who is a big enough star to get to $200, something Hall has a better chance at. I'm still holding Duno because he's an absolutely beast but he's a C/DH and for comparison when I was paying $70-80 for Samuel Basallo he was already near my top 10. Big offensive ceiling but I think his cards are now priced about where they should be.

players.name: Cam Collier
players.note: Last week I tweeted that of the Reds hitters I gave a 4 or 5 to on last year's sheet, three of the four were up 100% or more, the one who wasn't was Cam Collier. And I don't think that's entirely his fault since he tore a ligament in his thumb in March of last year and ended up having to miss a significant period of time recovering. He was one of the most popular chases in 2023 Bowman because when he was drafted as a 17-year-old he had huge future power projections. In his first few professional seasons he proved that those were correct. Since he was so advanced at the plate for his age he moved pretty quickly early on and played a full season in High-A at age 19. All he did there was hit 20 HR with a .194 ISO and 128 wRC+ while being more than three years younger than his average competitor. It's not often we see a player not only have that type of power at that age but also be doing it at a more advanced level. This past season the only teenage prospect to hit 20+ HR while getting 200+ PA above Single-A was Konnor Griffin to give you an idea of how impressive it was what Collier did in 2024. After returning from that torn ligament last year he saw a couple of weeks in the CPX followed by about the same time in High-A before the Reds assigned him to Double-A. This also gave me quite a bit of confidence as far as what the organization thinks of him to come off an injury like that at age 20 and put him into Double-A so quickly. Between all three of those levels Collier hit .279 in 396 PA with 4 HR, 14.9% BB, 26.3% K, .105 ISO, and 123 wRC+. Without a doubt the reason that his cards are down slightly from last year is because of how low his power output was last year, but coming back from surgery on your thumb can absolutely mess with your ability to grip the bat. Much like the hamate injury it's not uncommon to see players struggle for a stretch to get their power back after this surgery. If anything his base autograph still being $40 is a testament to how many people still believe that he's going to bounce back in a big way. I'm one of them.
