Anyone who has followed Cam Collier for longer than a year knows that there's no way he repeats that low of an ISO and HR total. On top of being fully healthy entering 2026 he has been added to the Reds roster for Spring Training which will give him an extra chance to generate some early hype this season. I think this could be the year of Cam Collier.

players.name: Tyson Lewis
players.note:
There probably won't be a ton of prospects barely inside my top 100 that I'm saying to buy at $30 but Tyson Lewis really has a lot of the things that make the hobby go. He's someone that everyone seemed to be torn on when 2024 Bowman Draft came out because he had really good tools as a prep but there were questions about his approach, he toyed with a couple of different setups, and because of that he wasn't nearly as consistent as evaluators would have liked. This is the hobby skillset though. Young shortstop with really good power and speed, this is the package we kind of dream on if it all comes together. There were people who originally put an average power grade on him but based on the hard hit rates and exit velocities we saw in his debut season it feels safe to assume it's going to be well above that and he may end up with 60 power 60 speed, FanGraphs actually has it as 70 and 70 which would be wild. The approach is still ehhhh for me. Between the CPX & A he had a 8.3% BB versus a 29.1% K, and that 0.28 BB/K, aggressive swing rate, AND low contact rate (63.2%) are usually the things that have me running away from prospects. But sometimes those things are ignored in the hobby because the tools are so good they can generate their own hype, and I think that will happen with Lewis. Despite all of those scary numbers I gave you he still hit .311 with 9 HR, 27 SB, .175 ISO, and a 124 wRC+. I do still think his batting average will regress, he ran a really high BABIP and there's no way someone with that approach and those contact metrics is going to continue to bat over .300, but as he adds muscle this offseason the power numbers might go crazy. If he has 30 HR/30 SB potential does the hobby turn a blind eye to the fact that he's not an extremely polished hitter? I think so. The only teenage prospects with 300+ PA last year who hit .300, had an ISO over .175, and stole more than 25 bases were Konnor Griffin and Tyson Lewis. He's risky, as was Konnor, but you just can't teach size and speed.

I know it's sad to see my guy

players.name: Sheng-En Lin
players.note: is fascinating as a two-way player from Taiwan which gives a big hobby ceiling but even after a couple of years this is still more of an experiment than anything, it's a fun one though. We can kind of throw

players.name: Adolfo Sanchez
players.note: dominated the DSL last year but he was repeating it as an 18-year-old which is a no-no for me, but the data was so good that he's at least worth monitoring to see how he looks early on in the states. My personal sleeper is

players.name: Carlos Jorge
players.note: and Ricardo (Ricky) Cabrera in the same bucket as guys who had a bunch of hobby love back in 2023 but have slowed down. All still worth a chance with how cheap they are in case they bounce back this year.

players.name: Alfredo Alcantara
players.note: here. Good power and speed, saw a promotion to Single-A last year at 19 and in 139 PA had a .210 ISO and 161 wRC+. Worth putting a pin in for this year.

players.name: Aaron Watson
players.note:
Watson was the first pitcher I named in the "Next Best - High School" segment of my 2025 Bowman Draft pitcher rankings. I'm very intrigued by this profile. It's not uncommon to see big 6'5" prep arms throwing with extreme velocity but not knowing where it's going to go, but Watson is a bit of the opposite in that he's a big strike thrower. Fastball, slider, and changeup is the mix and the stuff really plays up thanks to his ability to locate all of them. I think the pitchability is really good here and is something the Reds have targeted in the past, Rhett Lowder was voted as having the "best pitchability" in the minors a couple years ago by scouts. I said it in my Draft preview but you don't find a ton of pitchers this size who are able to dominate without electric stuff but Watson was able to do so as a high schooler thanks to that plus command. He just turned 19 and is entering his first season as a professional, I wouldn't be surprised if the Reds saw something in his pitch data that led them to believe they can improve those secondaries, and it's pretty likely that the velocity will start to tick up as he fills out that big frame. I think he offers a safer floor than most prep arms because his control is already so refined and if they're able to unlock a couple more notches in velocity on the fastball and spin on the slider I think this ceiling could end up being higher than expected. James Anderson at Rotowire already has him as a top 250 prospect and MLB Pipeline has him as the Reds 10th best prospect before we've even seen him throw a pitch professionally. When you combine that with the fact that his card just came out of a brand new product and is already under $10 I feel like he's a great upside grab.

Third round pick in last year's draft

players.name: Mason Morris
players.note: intrigues me a bit. Former two-way player who hits 99 on the gun and has a low-90's cutter that is devastating, slider is really good too, could have three above average pitches. Was used as a reliever only at Ole Miss so that's hurting his stock but he has a good frame and the Reds are going to try and stretch him into a starter which could make the upside solid.

players.name: Ty Floyd
players.note:
for $1 feels like an easy buy the more I look at it to be honest, 38th overall pick in 2023 but has been unable to stay healthy pitching only 27.2 innings in two years professionally. I still think the stuff is really solid if you want to stash something cheap. If he can make it through a full season he should perform well enough for this to go up (how could it go down?).

Jeral Perez ($10*)

I have a feeling I'm going to blow up somebody's spot here (including my own) but I can't believe how under the radar Jeral Perez flies in Bowman ESPECIALLY given how short printed his 1st Autographs are. If you're wondering how short the print run is the answer is extremely, perhaps one of the smallest sets of autos you're going to find. He currently has ONE 1st Bowman autograph listed on eBay and it's a True Gold with 3 days left on the auction (there goes my chance of winning it). When you search previously sold autographs in the last 90 days you get 6 results. A True Orange /25, an Orange Shimmer /25, a True Gold /50, and three different Yellows /75. This is basically all you can find for Perez. No base. No refractor. There's almost nothing except those few colors. Of those most recent sales the Yellows went for $42-44, the True Gold went for $70, and the True Orange went for $279. Using the updated multipliers that has come up with for those parallels that puts his hypothetical base autograph in the range of about $7-11. Perez came over from the Dodgers in 2024 as part of the Tommy Edman & Michael Kopech deal. Splitting time between both franchises that year he hit .262 with 12 HR, 4 SB, 12.9% BB, 22.9% K, .161 ISO, and 120 wRC+ in Single-A at age 19. This past season he was in High-A at 20 and was noticeably more aggressive at the plate increasing his overall Swing% from 40.3% to 46.5%. While that caused a 4.7% drop in his walk rate the other results are exactly what we like to see. The number of singles and double were almost mirror images of each other from the year prior but he had twice as many triples (2 to 4), and homers (12 to 22), raising his ISO over 40 points to .204. His profile is funky as a stocky 6'0" infielder who isn't great at any of the positions he plays but it's hard for me not to buy this noticeable power increase especially considering he dropped his K rate while doing so. Only 7 prospects in all of the minors had 20+ HR last year at age 20 or younger and all of them are the giant power names you'd expect; Laz Montes, Bryce Eldridge, Konnor Griffin, Ralphy Velazquez, Josue Briceno, Rainiel Rodriguez… and then Jeral Perez. Not only did Perez have the second lowest SwStr% of any player on that list he's the only one other than Konnor who had double digit stolen bases too. I'm not 100% sold on the ceiling but based on his age and production thus far his prices feel insanely low. In a market where players' prices are often blown up exponentially due to a short supply, Perez's are way too cheap when you consider how few of his autographs are in circulation.

players.name: Travis Bazzana
players.note: Nothing against Bazz I like him quite a bit but the top pick in each draft class tends to come with a tax on their cards because their names are more recognizable and I think that's happening here. I don't have any doubts that he'll be a great pro and he'll probably still get a small bump when he gets called up but at $135 I'm not super interested in buying.

players.name: Ralphy Velazquez
players.note: When I saw this price and ranking it almost looked like a mistake so I had to double check my sheet. Of my top 25 non-debuted hitting prospects, 23 of them have a 1st Bowman autograph. The average price for a base autograph among those 23 is $161. There are only two of them with a base autograph under $60 and one is Ralphy Velazquez, who is well under that. I think the market is missing something on Velazquez. Not only is the power projection from the 6'3" lefty big here but this hit tool is much better than most power hitting 1B prospects. Last year between A+ & AA, Velazquez hit .265 with 22 HR, 9.6% BB, 19.1% K, .232 ISO, and 136 wRC+ at age 20. He's also a young 20 and is still going to be that age for the first couple months of the 2026 season. Not only do you hardly see a K rate under 20% from this type of power profile, you also never see a 78% contact rate go with a .232 ISO like this. I actually love this bat and I'm not sure if it's the fact that he plays for the Guardians and their prospects are often overlooked in the hobby but for where I have him ranked this autograph price should easily be double what it is. The argument here is that a masher who doesn't offer any sort of athleticism has a cap on how high his price can go, and it's the argument I used for keeping Alfredo Duno as a 3/5 at $67 in my Reds article. But I've got Velazquez 14 spots higher and he's almost 40% cheaper. He doesn't offer any less versatility than Lazaro Montes whose card price is nearly double that of Velazquez and my hobby rankings value them almost identically. If you exclude the rookie levels only six prospects in baseball last year age 20 or younger hit 20+ HR. His 19.1% strikeout rate is the lowest out of everybody. It's 10% lower than Bryce Eldridge and Laz Montes and his contact rates were over 12% higher than both of them! If you've ever watched those two guys crush baseballs and thought, "I'd take a touch less power if their hit tools weren't so scary", you may not realize you're just talking about Ralphy Velazquez. He deserves to be mentioned in the same breath in my opinion. On top of that he's a non-roster invitee to Spring Training and he's probably one monster swing away from this card price going up 20%+ really quickly.

players.name: Angel Genao
players.note: Genao was a buy for me last year and his price has stayed basically the same but I think much of that had to do with him missing a big chunk of time due to injury. He burst onto some radars in 2024 when between A & A+ he hit .330 with 10 HR, 25 SB, and a 151 wRC+ at age 20 but a shoulder injury kept him sidelined at the start of the 2025 season and he didn't make it back from rehab until June. One thing I like to see with rehab assignments is where the teams will put prospects when they return from injury and often times it's the level they last played at but the Guardians took him straight from his rehab stint in the CPX to Double-A which gives me the idea they like him quite a bit, a notion that was confirmed when they protected him by adding him to their 40-man roster in November. The switch-hitting shortstop ended up hitting .263 with 5 HR, 6 SB, 9.4% BB, 15.5% K, .119 ISO, and 110 wRC+ in 2025 but based on how his power was trending over the previous three seasons prior to the injury I'm not overly concerned about the lack of power last year, especially since AA Akron where he played his home games was a miserable hitters park. He was a bit more selective swinging at fewer pitches, drawing more walks, and running a higher contact rate (82.8%) than he did back in that 2024 breakout season, all things I love to see. After the season was over Genao played 26 games in the Dominican Winter League where he hit .325 in 94 PA. Add him to the long list of switch-hitters with good contact in the Cleveland organization as it's 100% their type but I think there's more here with Genao and he's probably my favorite of those type. It's not just contact skills but the power could be solid, the speed is solid, even the glove at SS are solid, he doesn't have much of a weakness in his game. I mentioned that his power may have suffered last year between the injury and the park, Baseball America's Park Factors had Akron as the third least hitter friendly park in all of AA. At some point this season (probably soon) he'll get to AAA Columbus where the Park Factor for home runs is 118 compared to 47 in Akron. I think this is the year he fully breaks out and if the Guardians need shortstop help down the stretch I think Angel Genao is who they want there.

players.name: Alfonsin Rosario
players.note: has always fascinated me, big time power but couldn't water if he fell out of a boat with the Cubs (contact rate under 60%). Comes to Cleveland and cuts his K rate down, increases contact by 6%. It's still not good but it's better. He's streaky because he's aggressive but this is possibly 70 grade power if the Guardians can get it to click.

players.name: Jaison Chourio
players.note: Ughhhh this is the last time I swear! I can't lie I made Chourio a 3 out of my frustrations with him but for the price I do still like him as a buy. His cards are down over 50% from last year's sheet and while many people will see that as a reason to jump ship it's hard to ignore that it puts him in sort of a buy low spot. The things I've always loved most about Jackson's little brother showed up again in 2025 and that's the OBP and contact skills. Last year in High-A Chourio hit just .235 with 2 HR, 9 SB, and a .049 ISO while missing almost all of May with an injury. Not hype. Even with that though he had a .380 OBP and 103 wRC+ thanks mostly to his 18.7% walk rate. Now I love a good walk rate but it can be good and bad. With a player like Chourio he actually has surprising pop when he's aggressive, and my hope for 2025 was that he'd become more aggressive but the opposite happened. His swing rate dropped for the fourth consecutive year and was down to 34.9%. It's the beef I have with guys like Emmanuel Rodriguez I want to just shake them and be like, "stop trying to walk". Walks are good until you can't post good counting stats because you don't swing and that's kind of where I'm at with Chourio. BUT being able to get on base and having a great ability to make contact is a skillset that really helps your floor as a young player. After struggling for the first few months of the season he finished as hot as we had seen him all year, batting a combined .295 between August and September. His 36 hits in 140 PA were as many as he had in 240 PA from April through July. He carried that momentum into the Venezuelan Winter League where in 46 games Chourio hit .323 with a .408 OBP, 2 HR, 2 3B, 6 2B, and 9 SB in 191 PA. His walk rate in those games was 13.1% which was 5.6% lower than it was during the Minor League season and it goes to show, as I've always thought, that his production could go through the roof if he swung the damn bat. I'll give him one more chance entering this season because I do think the skills are here for a really good hobby player and for the first time in awhile his autograph prices are a great deal.

players.name: Juneiker Caceres
players.note: When I did my 2025 Bowman Chrome chase rankings I was higher than the consensus on Caceres with him being my #3 chase in the product ahead of Nate George, Elian Pena, Kevin Alvarez, etc. and not much has changed for me since then. One of the things that is weighted heavily in my hobby rankings is age versus level and I think it is consistently one of the most overlooked aspects of prospect rankings. If two guys produce similar results in Single-A and one is 18 and the other is 21 you can't view those statistics through an equal lens. That makes what Caceres has done in his professional career so far even more impressive. Debuted at age 16 in the DSL where he hit .340 with a 140 wRC+ and more walks than strikeouts. At 16. Came to the states last year and saw just 160 PA in the CPX before the Guardians somewhat aggressively moved him to Single-A. Across both stops he hit .270 with 4 HR, 7 SB, 12.4% BB, 12.1% K, .139 ISO, and a 123 wRC+. More walks than strikeouts, a 84% contact rate, and a 7.3% SwStr% at age 17 while playing half of the season in Single-A deserves to be getting WAY more credit than it does. People are probably chalking this up to the Guardians having another small contact hitter with no power but I actually don't think that's the case here. Caceres posted really good exit velocities especially for his age and though the 4 HR in 290 PA doesn't exactly pop the .139 ISO for his age is actually really good and that's in part to the 18 doubles and 2 triples he added in 70 games, perhaps an indicator of more future power. You never quite know what these young prospects will turn into as far as how much strength they can add to their frame but his contact metrics are so elite for his age and level I'm not even worried. The only prospect in baseball last year who was 17, got 120+ PA in Single-A, and had a wRC+ over 100 there was Juneiker Caceres. In 2024 it was also only done by one player and that was Leo De Vries. Last season there were only two prospects age 19 or younger who had 250+ PA with an ISO over .135 and more walks than strikeouts. They were Alfredo Duno and Juneiker Caceres. Much of their seasons were played at the same level in Single-A. They're ranked side-by-side in my hobby rankings. Caceres is two full years younger than Duno and his autograph is about 25% of the price. He could be Sam Antonacci but what if he's Kevin McGonigle, another prospect who had a similar skillset as a teenager that everyone thought would have below average power? He's the only prospect in my top 50 non-debuted hitters with a base autograph under $20. This is a no brainer for me. If I could give him a 6 I would.

players.name: Welbyn Francisca
players.note: is the same boat as Chourio for me, loved him but he's just not progressing how I expected. Contact rates still great but power really falling off. Still think there's upside here and I'm holding what I have but if I'm choosing between the two I'm still taking Chourio.

players.name: Kahlil Watson
players.note: Here's a name you may have to dig through those old boxes for. Watson was an elite hobby name back in 2022 Bowman where he was one of, if not the main chase early on in a product that featured Elly De La Cruz, James Wood, and Colson Montgomery. I actually talked about Watson a couple of months ago when I did an article predicting MLB debuts for each team and he was my Guardians pick. After a few average seasons from 2022-24 that saw him post wRC+ marks of 104, 110, and 108 he had his best professional season yet in 2025 hitting 16 homers and stealing 17 bases with a .217 ISO and 129 wRC+ between AA & AAA. He made almost every improvement that you can make offensively from 2024 to 2025. Walk rate up, strikeout rate down, contact rate up, batting average up 30 points, ISO up 30 points, wRC+ up 21. This is more like the Kahlil Watson that we expected to see when we were chasing his cards way back when he was with the Marlins. Since I was a notorious hater of the Marlins development on the hitting side during the old regime and also a lover of how the Guardians operate, it's not a big surprise that they look to have found something here with a player who oozed talent coming out of high school in 2021 and was drafted 16th overall. It's a really good package of hobby tools too with above average power and speed, and that good athleticism allowed Cleveland to move him from the dirt to the grass where he's capable of playing all three outfield positions. Not only did he match his career high HR total with 16 but he was an extra-base machine adding 20 doubles and 6 triples go along with it. To see what kind of company that stat line puts him in the only prospects age 22 or younger last year with 16+ HR, 20+ 2B, 6+ 3B, and 17+ SB were Kahlil Watson, Jett Williams, and Eduardo Quintero. This is a great combination of bat speed and foot speed for $12. Watson has good hobby pedigree as a 1st round pick and former top chase in a Bowman product and the Guardians have already added him to their 40-man roster. Seeing him start hot in 2026 could ping a lightbulb in the heads of people who recognize his name but may have forgotten about him. I think this a good formula for generating hype.

players.name: Cooper Ingle
players.note: Ingle was a buy on last year's sheet at $5 and though he's now officially up 75% this price still feels a touch disrespectful to me. Now don't get me wrong, Ingle is a 5'8" catcher who is about to turn 24 which is not a combination that will lead to hobby stardom. But regardless of the age and position I don't see why anyone who is this productive with a bat should be under $10. Since being drafted out of Clemson in the 4th round in 2023, Ingle has played three professional seasons. His wRC+ in those years were 153, 161, and 139. Last year between AA & AAA he hit .260 with 10 HR, 16.9% BB, 16.7% K, .159 ISO, and 139 wRC+ to go along with a 83.7% contact rate and 5.9% SwStr%. If you like Sam Antonacci like I do, you should like Cooper Ingle as this is a rare 60 grade hit tool in my opinion. The approach and contact skills are fantastic and to be honest with you the ISO's and HR totals are much higher than you'd expect from a guy his size. Excluding rookie levels there were only 16 prospects last year age 23 or younger who had a SwStr% under 6%. Cooper Ingle's .159 ISO was the highest out of everybody and more than 40 points higher than other big names on the list like Franklin Arias and the previously mentioned Antonacci. I know an undersized catching prospect that is considered old by hobby standards isn't exciting but I think people are sleeping on how good this bat has been. He's now a top 200 overall prospect for both Dynasty Dugout and Rotowire. Scout the Statline's Peak Projections which use your minor league analytics to predict major league success has him as a top 150 prospect. He'll be a non-roster invitee to Spring Training this year and following that should open the season as their starting catcher in AAA. Since Cleveland has Bo Naylor and Austin Hedges who are both defense-first catchers it wouldn't be surprising to see them bring in a bat down the stretch that could help the lineup if they need one and when they do Cooper Ingle will be ready.

players.name: Nolan Schubart
players.note: would be my sleeper pick. Only has one tool but it's the one we want, power. Hit 59 HR in 3 seasons at Oklahoma St., made his pro debut in Single-A after being drafted and hit 3 in only 66 PA. Hit tool is not good but taking massive power under $10 can be fun because he'll likely be a streaky hitter who puts some crazy weeks together.

players.name: Juan Brito
players.note: is a name I loved for the Guards back in 2024 when he went 21 HR/13 SB in AAA and appeared to be on the verge of a call-up all season. It never came and then he was hurt most of 2025. The results still looked great but since he missed most of the year and there's not a clear opening on the MLB club he could start in AAA again, a level he'll see time at for the fourth consecutive year. I believe in the bat if you want a cheap snag with upside but since he's not a strong defender I'm starting to worry about where he slides in. Dean Curley is probably the bigger name in 2025 Bowman Draft but for hobby purposes

players.name: Robert Arias
players.note: I'm not sure any MLB franchise has a type more than the Cleveland Guardians. It starts to feel like every prospect is a smaller guy with great bat-to-ball skills. Spoiler alert though, I actually like that profile as well. You probably wouldn't guess it due to the fact that he's a 30+ HR candidate every year now in the MLB but Jose Ramirez hit a TOTAL of 13 HR in over 1,500 PA in the minors. It may not be the highest success rate but getting those guys and hoping the power pops is exactly what they're trying to replicate. Now when you get into the Welbyn Francisca's and Jaison Chourio's you're buying that "well, IF the power pops" but honestly for less than half of the price give me Robert Arias. Signed for nearly $2 million back in 2024 he was considered to have some of the most advanced bat-to-ball skills in the international class. He has an uncanny understanding of the zone and that's something he's shown off in both of his first two professional seasons posting BB/K rates of 1.67 and 1.32 at ages 17 and 18. Last year in the CPX he hit .287 with 2 HR, 29 SB, 14.6% BB, 11.1% K, .116 ISO, and 116 wRC+. His swing is a bit choppy at times almost as if he's trying to hit ground balls and beat them out with his plus speed but the Guardians have been optimistic that as he puts more muscle on his frame and gets better at pulling the ball in the air he could have 15-20 HR potential. It doesn't mean everything but since he's 6'1" instead of 5'8" like many of these guys Cleveland signs I'm a bit more optimistic that the future power could be average, but even if it takes some time to get there the floor is absolutely incredible at $7 for a teenager with his approach and contact skills. There were 61 prospects age 18 or younger who were qualified hitters in the states last year. Robert Arias's 1.32 BB/K was the highest of any of them and it wasn't even particularly close. When you take out the DSL only 3 qualified Bowman hitters had an ISO over .110 and 25+ SB at age 18 last year. Jesus Made, Luis Pena, and Robert Arias. Not bad.

players.name: Nick Mitchell
players.note:
It's tough to crack it as a 'buy' when you're ranked outside of my top 300 hitters but $3?! Again, as with nearly all Guardians prospects an undersized contact-first hitter is not what the hobby wants. I understand that. But I also understand that there aren't many prospects whose base autographs are $3 that will make it to the MLB and Nick Mitchell will probably do that. Add him to the list of guys with above average contact and speed. Much of the reason that I followed Mitchell last year was because when he came back from injury his name kept popping up on the hot sheets and I was fascinated by how somebody who was playing so well could command so little respect from the Bowman world. Last year between A & A+ he hit .273 with 2 HR, 9 2B, 7 3B, 14.8% BB, 14.2% K, .097 ISO, and a 122 wRC+. ISO under .100 feels like a death sentence in Bowman, and it kind of is, but his ISO was .178 in his debut pro season prior to sustaining a hand injury so there is hope that it gets to more of the .150 range this season. Across both levels he had a 84% contact rate and just 6.4% SwStr%. While his .097 ISO feels like nothing there were only 14 prospects in baseball last year age 21 or younger who had more walks than strikeouts. His .097 ISO was actually higher than 9 of the 14. Of the five that had an ISO over .095 only two of them had a SwStr% under 6.5%: Max Clark and Nick Mitchell. I'm not going to pretend like Mitchell has $100 base auto upside, hell I don't even know that he has $50 base auto upside, but with his set of skills it would only take a very minor increase in his power output for this to be in the Sam Antonacci price range of $20. The last sale of his True Orange 1st Auto /25 was $55. I grabbed a True Orange /25 non-auto 1st on COMC for $10. You can go deep color for really cheap here and while the ceiling isn't huge I don't think his prices going up 400-500% from here is a reach at all. Three dollars?!

Biggest name of the 3's is of course former #1 overall pick

players.name: Braylon Doughty
players.note: The last time I mentioned Doughty in an article it was back in November in my article "Pitching prospects to stash for $10 or less", and though he's nearly doubled since then I still think he is extremely undervalued in the Bowman market. Just as a disclaimer there isn't a single pitching prospect that I have more money in than Braylon Doughty so if you're buying and holding him I'm along for the ride with you. As a former two-way player Doughty is very athletic on the mound and I've compared him to Spencer Schwellenbach of the Braves in the past due to this, his repertoire of pitches, and his very high spin rates. You can probably tell from the long list of hitters that I frequently agree with the moves that the Guardians make in terms of their prospects and scooping Doughty with the 36th overall pick in 2024 and signing him for $2.5 million is a move I think will pay off. He doesn't have the biggest frame at 6'1" but as a teenager was already hitting 95+ with armside run but it's the secondary pitches for me. Curveball and slider are easily plus and have recorded spin rates north of 3,000 RPMs. He also has a changeup that grades as average that could use some more refinement but he puts all four of these pitches wherever he wants them. Don't get caught up in the 0-7 record in his professional debut because the stats we care about were lights out. At age 19 in Single-A he had a 3.48 ERA, 2.84 FIP, 2.86 xFIP, 10.44 K/9, and 2.43 BB/9. I used this stat in a past article but it's too good not to bring back. There were 301 different minor league pitchers who made 20+ starts in 2025. Only 5 of those 301 had a K/9 over 10 and a BB/9 under 2.5. None of them were a teenager except for Doughty. In fact the last time that a pitcher age 19 or younger accomplished all of that was back in 2022 when it was done by Andrew Painter who almost immediately became a top 10 prospect. Doughty was my favorite pitcher to watch last year and the way he mixes pitches and freezes hitters with multiple offerings in all parts of the zone just isn't something you see often from pitchers this young. I'm in big time.

players.name: Khal Stephen
players.note:
Since I always seem to be a fan of the draft picks and international signings from this organization it shouldn't really be a surprise that I also like the prospects they trade for, and one of my favorites from last year was Khal Stephen who they acquired from Toronto. Stephen was just ok his first two collegiate seasons at Purdue before transferring to Mississippi St. where he went 8-3 with a 3.28 ERA, 10.03 K/9, and 1.97 BB/K in 16 starts leading to a second round selection by the Blue Jays in 2024. That walk number should stick out to you because this command is fantastic, likely a 60 grade, and he showed that again in his professional debut last year. The lower levels were no match for Stephen with a 2.06 ERA in Single-A and a 1.49 ERA in High-A before earning a second promotion to Double-A. When all was said and done across two organizations and three different levels he went 9-2 with a 2.53 ERA, 2.60 FIP, 9.61 K/9, and 1.75 BB/9. His 27.1% K% and miniscule 4.9% BB% created a K-BB% of 22.2% which was the 9th best of the 288 pitchers who threw 100+ MiLB innings last year. The mix is fastball, slider, curveball, changeup and I think they all flash as above average offerings that play up because his control with all of them is so good. My hope is that with Cleveland they can unlock something to improve his pitches even further because his lack of a true plus pitch is what's stopping him from being a front of the rotation arm. Either way he's almost guaranteed to be a big league pitcher and his floor is really good thanks to a good frame, athletic delivery, and pinpoint accuracy. The only pitchers in the minors last year who had a K/9 over 9.5 and a walk rate under 5% were Mitch Bratt who I already raved about as a 5/5 buy for the Diamondbacks and Khal Stephen. Again, not your usual high octane, big strikeout numbers guy, but he's really solid and I think he could find himself in their MLB rotation by the end of the year.

Most clubs only have 4-5 non-debuted pitchers with Bowman autos but the Guardians list is a bit longer.

players.name: Daniel Espino
players.note: is definitely the most intriguing of the 3's as he was once considered an elite pitching prospect with one of the best fastballs we've ever seen at the minor league level, touching 103 mph. Unfortunately he may also be the most injured pitcher in minor league baseball and due to a number of injuries he didn't pitch in an official MiLB game for a period of three years. He's back now and the stuff still looks like it is legit but he's got quite a bit of rust to shake off. This is a HUGE upside play. He could debut and strikeout 10 and see this thing go up 1,000% but considering I've only seen him pitch a grand total of 5 innings since 2022 I have to see it before I buy anything for myself. After that my favorite 3 is Matt "Tugboat" Wilkinson, 80 grade name. Had a huge year in 2024 but regressed a bit in 2025, still think there's good upside here but opponents' contact rates jumped nearly 10% from the year prior as High-A hitters seemed to have him figured out. 1.90 ERA and 13.20 K/9 the year prior though have me optimistic that he could bounce back this year.

players.name: Charlie Condon
players.note: At 6'6" the obvious calling card here is the power which we saw a ton of at Georgia and is a legit 70 grade. He struggled quite a bit in his pro debut after being drafted but he was battling a hand injury and it wasn't a huge sample so I'm not too worried about that. Last year he looked much better with a 135 wRC+ between A+ & AA with 14 HR and a .175 ISO. My hobby formula uses hitting data from the past three seasons when applicable so although I don't think his 2024 stats paint a clear picture of who he is it is weighing down his ranking a bit, something that should correct itself in 2026. I still think there's some hit tool concern here but his upside is massive. The ceiling is there for this to be a $150+ auto but since he doesn't come without risk I'd want him in the $50-60 range for buying so I'm holding at $85 for now.

players.name: Cristian Arguelles
players.note: is my favorite dart throw here. Absolutely dominated the DSL last year hit .422 with a .230 ISO and 201 wRC+. Video game stuff. Unfortunately he was repeating the DSL which is a big strike in my book. I actually love the upside but without seeing it in the states I'd want him in the $10-15 range given that he struggled his first time through the DSL.

players.name: Jared Thomas
players.note: When 2024 Bowman Draft was released many of you will remember that I was on board the Jared Thomas hype train. His cards felt extremely cheap and I really liked what I saw him from him at Texas prior to the draft. In his Sophomore season he hit .349 with 16 HR and 18 SB and since he was draft eligible following that year he was one of the youngest players in that college draft class. Much of what I liked from him in college was his ability to hit without selling out for power. You'd see him hunt pitches to crush early on in counts but when he got behind he was really good at shortening up, taking the pitches he was given and depositing them for singles. It was an approach I thought would work well professionally and in his first full pro season it did just that. Between A+ & AA Thomas hit .300 with 14 HR, 33 SB, 13.1% BB, 27.2% K, .152 ISO, and 135 wRC+. The contact rates were a bit lower than I expected (71.3%) and the strikeout rate was higher. I'd also like to see him close the gap on that BB/K but other than that I'd say the season was a success. The fact that his base autograph only went up $2 is a bit surprising to me. I know the Rockies aren't the most collectable team of late but this price still feels low for his sneaky combination of power and athleticism. Following the minor league season Thomas went to the AFL where again we saw a lot of good but with some underlying concerns in the approach. He hit .302 with 2 HR, 6 2B, and a 3B in his 17 games but he was even more aggressive than we saw him earlier in the year, with 28 K's to only 3 walks. If his approach and/or contact were to tick up a bit this year I think it could be a breakout campaign, especially if he reaches AAA where Albuquerque is a hitter friendly park. There were only two qualified hitters with Bowman autographs in all of the minors last year who hit .300 with 10+ HR and 30+ SB. They were Konnor Griffin and Jared Thomas. I think we may be sleeping on him a bit still.

players.name: Robert Calaz
players.note: Every team has one of those "if you don't mind rolling the dice for a big ceiling" type prospects and for the Rockies it's 100% Robert Calaz. After a great showing in the DSL for his pro debut he came to the states in 2024 where all he did was win the Triple Crown in the Arizona Complex League at age 18 hitting .349 with 10 HR, 12 SB, and an absurd .302 ISO and 174 wRC+. The power ceiling here is massive and the exit velocities off the bat of the 6'2" righty are big. I think the funniest thing I've read on Calaz is MLB Pipeline saying that he was the best hitter in the CPX "without really having an idea of what he's doing at the plate." Which honestly is true. He dominated the rookie levels purely out of being way more physically gifted than most of the players, but his approach and ability to make contact have a loooong way to go. Last year he was in Single-A and hit .259 with 10 HR, 7 SB, 8.7% BB, 25.9% K, .140 ISO, and 105 wRC+. Not shocking that a guy this raw struggled against a step up in pitching, both his 0.34 BB/K and 69.8% contact rate were red flags. Now both his contact rate and SwStr% did improve from the year prior so that's nice to see but they're still not good by any means. There's a bit of some Emil Morales in here to me, a player I've basically said the same things about in the past. Huge upside because the power for his age is tremendous but betting on guys who struggle to make contact can be scary. The main difference is that one is being developed by the Dodgers and one by the Rockies, two franchises with very different track records. With that being said it's a MUCH cheaper entry point than Morales whose base autograph is nearly quadruple the price of Calaz's. FanGraphs has five years worth of CPX data and Robert Calaz in 2024 is the only player who has ever had an ISO over .300 for 200+ PA. Whether he'll be able to improve his quality of contact enough against better pitching is the gamble, but it could be a fun one at $15.

players.name: Roc Riggio
players.note: came over from the Yankees and quietly had a pretty damn good year with 20 HR/17 SB, a .255 ISO, and 155 wRC+ in AA. He's climbing and could be a name to watch early on. Also don't hate

players.name: Cole Carrigg
players.note:
If the premium for your cards was directly determined by how fun you are to watch Carrigg would be a top 10 prospect for me, one of my favorite minor leaguers there is. That's in part because he played three different positions when he made his professional debut in 2023 and it's a trio of spots you've probably never seen a single professional play. Centerfield, shortstop, and catcher. As you can guess the athleticism is fantastic but honestly the power isn't bad either which makes him a really fun Bowman player. Over the last two seasons he's combined to hit 32 HR and steal 99 bases. After moving all around the field the Rockies seem to have settled on him playing CF which is where he made 97 of his 120 starts in 2025. Due to his great speed and double plus arm I wouldn't be surprised if he ends up being a plus defender there as he gets more reps. After hitting .280 with 17 HR, 53 SB, and a .208 ISO in 2024 those numbers dipped a little bit last year in AA where he batted .237 with 15 HR, 46 SB, and a .157 ISO. One of the reasons I'm not too too worried about the decrease in raw power is that AA Hartford is a notoriously bad environment for hitters and starting the year in AAA Albuquerque could turn those power numbers around this season. My only real yellow flag for Carrigg is that he's never been a patient hitter. He got away with it at lower levels but the step up to AA last year saw his strikeout rate rise by 8%. Despite that I think he's a player whose stats could really pop with a full year in the hitter friendly Pacific Coast League. I wouldn't be surprised if he goes 20 HR/50 SB this year to be honest. I also wouldn't be surprised if he was able to find a spot on the Rockies big league roster later in the year assuming he's playing as well as I expect. We always say the hobby loves power and speed. Guess how many players have 30+ HR and 90+ SB since the start of 2024? One. Cole Carrigg. The way he plays with his hair on fire could definitely generate some buzz in Spring Training too. I think there's a lot to like here for $10. 

The only non-debuted prospect in the entire organization with a base autograph over $20 is the #3 overall pick from 2024's draft

players.name: Sterlin Thompson
players.note: at under $10. Hit .296 with a .223 ISO in AAA last year and probably isn't getting enough respect for it. He's already on the Rockies 40-man roster so I think we'll see him before the All-Star break. Might be a rare player to hold after call-up since he won't get a ton of hype but could get hot hitting in the elevation at Coors Field.

players.name: Brody Brecht
players.note: It's hard being a pitcher in the Rockies system these days and I'm not overly surprised that they don't have a single non-debuted pitching prospect with a Bowman autograph who is ranked as a top 400 prospect by Dynasty Dugout or Rotowire. I think if you're going to buy an arm in this system though this is hands down the one that you want. I'll start off by saying that Brecht does have some serious reliever risk. In his three seasons at Iowa his BB/9 rates were 9.93, 7.13, and 5.63. During his professional debut last year it was 5.16. On the bright side it seems to be improving pretty drastically every year, on the down side it's still not good. What is good is his stuff though and when I say good I mean great. Brecht hits triple digits with his fastball and his slider is in the low-90's with two plane break and is virtually unhittable when he's on. In his final season at Iowa his slider generate whiffs 56% of the time and I'd argue it's one of the best in the minor leagues, potentially 70 or even 80 grade. Due to this he posts some gaudy strikeout numbers. Last year between the CPX & A he had a 2.51 ERA and a 14.02 K/9 striking out an absolutely ridiculous 36.1% of the total batters he faced. Opposing hitters had just a 61.6% contact rate against him and a 17.8% swinging strike % in 61 innings pitched. The caveat here is that you're likely buying a reliever but the upside because of the stuff is fantastic if he continues to improve his control. Last year there were 343 pitchers who threw 60+ innings in the minors. His 36.1% K rate was the 8th best out of those 343. If you limit it to pitchers who had an ERA under 2.60 the only pitchers with a higher K% were Jonah Tong, Johnny King, Thomas White, and Chase Burns. Talk about guys with nasty stuff. You have to temper your expectations because of the reliever risk and fact that Colorado hasn't exactly crushed it with pitcher development, but on pure stuff alone this card should be worth more in my opinion.

players.name: JB Middleton
players.note: is definitely my favorite of the 3's and is already very close to being a 4. I named him as one of my sleepers for pitchers in 2025 Bowman Draft. Really good stuff and command last year where he was dominant at Southern Miss. He's knocked for his frame because he's maybe 6'0" and the track record isn't great for starting pitchers being that undersized. Interested to see how he looks against that step up to professional hitters but I'm actually leaning towards him being better than most people expect.

players.name: Sean Sullivan
players.note: There may not be two more different pitchers on the planet than Brody Brecht and Sean Sullivan. Where Brecht was pure stuff, Sullivan is pure command. He's a lefty who throws from a low slot and had a fastball that averaged 88 mph in 2024. That's not Bowman stuff. He also uses a changeup which is probably his best pitch and a slider, but none of his three offerings really grade as above average. His command is amazing though. And because it's so good and his arm slot is so funky he actually gets more K's than you'd think, but this is more about productivity than swing-and-miss. Last year in 20 starts (18 of them at AA) Sullivan had a 2.94 ERA, 9.00 K/9, and a 2.16 BB/9. Where I raved about Brecht's 36.1% strikeout rate, Sullivan's was only 24.9%, but his 6% walk rate was over 7% lower. This is a pitching profile you simply don't see in today's game anymore but the weird thing is that it's working. While you won't see him ranked on any prospect lists he's actually a top 80 pitcher on Scout the Statline's Peak Projections because the results have been too good to ignore. My disclaimer here is that much like being a 5'6" contact hitter with zero power there is absolutely a cap on how high Sullivan's hobby ceiling can go, but that doesn't mean that it can't go up. I mention it with hitters all the time even going from $5 to $15-20 is a worthwhile investment if you're buying in volume or deeper colors. Since his command is so good and he keeps producing at every level we're going to get to the point where the Rockies have to call him up and it's hard not to take a chance on someone with a $4 autograph who is nearly certain to end up in a big league rotation at some point. He's now had consecutive minor league seasons with 100+ IP and an ERA under 3 which makes him the ONLY pitcher with a Bowman autograph who can say that. Not every play is sexy. Value is value. Sean Sullivan has shown me enough to say this price should be higher.

players.name: Max Clark
players.note: Obviously I love both of them as prospects and I do think McGonigle could be the Opening Day starter at shortstop but to be honest I'll hardly ever give a 4 or 5 to someone with a base auto that's already over $200. They absolutely can still go up but I like to play percentages and find value in guys who could double in price. Love both of the players but I'm holding what I have.

players.name: Bryce Rainer
players.note: Can you believe there was a time when I was flipping a coin between Bryce Rainer and Konnor Griffin for which one I liked more in 2024 Bowman Draft? That was because while Griffin came with the massive ceiling of power and speed, Rainer actually looked like he might be a more polished bat-to-ball hitter coming out of high school. He looked really good in his professional debut before injuring his shoulder but since he was the other big prep name who came out of the same class as Konnor that combined with the injury definitely slowed his hype. But at age 19 in Single-A he hit .288 with 5 HR, 9 SB, 13.4% BB, 22.1% K, .160 ISO, and 134 wRC+. Now that was only 35 games but for your first 149 PA as a professional that's damn good. He added a bit more power his final year of high school which improved his draft stock and I think we saw it here in the debut. It's not going to be your 70 power 70 speed like with Griffin but I think the case can be made for Rainer to have 60 power and maybe even 60 speed, I really like the tools here. Last April at the USA Baseball National High School Invitational the top four exit velocities at the event all came off the bat of Bryce Rainer. And for all of the things Konnor is great at I think Rainer's approach is going to be better. His base autograph did get all the way down to $55-60 when he was shut down with his shoulder surgery so it definitely has come up from there now that we know he should be ready for the start of the 2026 season but when I looked around my hobby rankings he's already 25th and that's with only seeing a handful of PA so far. I don't think that him playing well enough this season to be a consensus top 10 prospect entering 2027 is out of the question, and if that happened I do think that his base auto would get to the $200 range especially with him being a high 1st round pick coming out of high school. McGonigle should graduate, Clark might too, and both of them have base autos over $200. Of the next crop of names in this system that could have their type of hype entering next year Bryce Rainer is definitely my favorite pick. It's tough to say anyone with a $90 base auto is a "buy low" but I do think that had he played all of year last year at the pace he was on this thing would already be $150 easily, so I really like the chance of this card going up this season.

players.name: Josue Briceno
players.note: The Tigers are loaded with big name hitting prospects who have yet to make their debut but based on the prices of their cards Josue Briceno is definitely my favorite one. There was a time the world was sleeping on Briceno but not anymore as Dynasty Dugout and Rotowire both have him as a top 50 overall prospect. Based on his minor league production so far and how it should translate to major league success Scout the Statline has him as their 10th best hitting prospect. In my hobby rankings he's currently 16th for non-debuted hitting prospects and all of these rankings are really high for a guy who hasn't generated a ton of hype up to this point. Now he did hit a left-on-left bomb yesterday off of the reigning AL Cy Young Tarik Skubal and there was some buzz going around Twitter so I really hope his card price didn't spike overnight before you all were able to buy but I love this play. I mentioned it in my Guardians article with Ralphy Velazquez it's not common to see big power hitters post good contact rates and Briceno's underlying data is even more impressive. Last year between A+ & AA Briceno hit .266 with 20 HR, 14.9% BB, 19.7% K, .234 ISO, and 153 wRC+. I know it's easy to get overlooked especially when you keep getting promoted and grouped in with names like Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark but this is crazy production. A .234 ISO with a K rate under 20% and a 77% contact rate is really really good stuff. He was originally signed as a catcher but for the first time in his minor league career last year he saw more starts at first base than catcher, so seeing him at the corner or as a DH will likely be the trend going forward. There is only one hitter in my entire top 20 who has a base autograph under $60 and it's Briceno which makes him a slam dunk in my opinion. I actually have him ranked higher than Laz Montes whose autographs are quite a bit more expensive so I think the hobby is sleeping on Briceno. Excluding stats from the rookie leagues there were only six qualified hitters age 20 or younger last year who had an ISO over .225. The only ones with a SwStr% under 10.5% were Kevin McGonigle and Josue Briceno. I think this bat is legit.

players.name: Cris Rodriguez
players.note: is a player who has a ton of hobby buzz and it is warranted because he has some of the best power projections out of anybody from last year's international class. As I said back in my 2025 Bowman Chrome preview he may have the highest ceiling in that product but he doesn't have the steadiest floor. There could be some big time swing-and-miss issues here but we honestly won't know until he gets to the states and is further along in his development. I'm a notorious hater of DSL stats and while I was willing to go in on guys like Diego Tornes and Kevin Alvarez with base autos closer to $30, I'm personally not going for Rodriguez at $40 until I see him face some better pitching and we see what that hit tool might look like.

players.name: Jordan Yost
players.note: was the Tigers 1st round pick last year and he could be worth a snag. Really good hit tool and advanced approach for his age along with great speed, the tough thing for us is that he's projected for below average power. I do think because the rest of his tools are so good he's worth a flier because if that power shows up as he matures this could be a really fun player but from what I've seen so far he would probably need to fall under $15 before I make a play. The 3 that was the closest to being a 4 for me was probably

players.name: Thayron Liranzo
players.note: The switch-hitting catcher looked great in 2023 and 2024 showing a solid approach and really good power. Hit 24 HR with a .290 ISO at age 19 which is insane. Unfortunately with his move to AA last year he really struggled and almost all of his stats went in the wrong direction. With that being said his base auto is now under $10 so if you want to buy a bounce back candidate who could go on a nice power run this is a good cheap option. Also don't hate

players.name: Franyerber Montilla
players.note: as a stash in that same price range. Improved his contact rates by 5% from 2024 to 2025, seems to have a solid hit tool, good speed (57 combined SB the last two seasons), just need that power to come along which it may.

players.name: Malachi Witherspoon
players.note: who the Tigers selected in the second round, for those who don't know he is the twin brother of Red Sox prospect Kyson Witherspoon. Malachi was actually a higher rated prospect coming out of high school and was drafted in the 12th round but elected to go to college with his brother. Once they got to college Kyson ended up improving more and becoming the better pitcher. Malachi has a really good curveball and slider which may be plus pitches, and his fastball touches 99 but he doesn't locate extremely well. That's what's holding him back at the moment. He's very athletic and deceptive on the mound and get's good extension but he can get all over the place at times with his body and the inability to repeat his delivery really plagued his control in college. Last year at Oklahoma Witherspoon made 15 starts where he went 4-8 with a 5.09 ERA, 5.00 FIP, 11.02 K/9, and 3.87 BB/9. Despite the good strikeout numbers he did get hit hard at times as referenced by the ERA and I think a lot of that had to do with him falling behind in counts and having to come back with a fastball that while the velocity is great it doesn't have a ton of movement. I think the Tigers took him where they did because they recognize that with some tweaks he really does have great upside if he can harness his stuff a little bit better as a professional. I know it's probably silly of me to think he's worth a stash because his twin brother who is his genetic equal is a top 10 hobby pitcher… but for under $10 why not?

players.name: Ethan Schiefelbein
players.note: was a Comp B pick out of high school in 2024 and the 6'2" lefty is a command over stuff pitcher. Tigers went above slot with $1.8 million to pull him away from UCLA. Throws fastball, curveball, slider, changeup. The slider and curveball are probably his best pitches and could both be above average offerings but it's really his plus command that could make him an effective starter as he mixes pitches and locates all of them very well. Only threw in 3 CPX games last year prior to being shut down but he's still only 19-years-old I think for $5 he's an arm worth watching.

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.note: When I did the Tigers buy sheet I gave Cris Rodriguez a 3 because although I loved the power ceiling I think the contact could be shaky. That also could be the case for Neyens but he's actually a few bucks cheaper and I like him quite a bit more overall especially since I prefer draft picks over international signings, so I'm more comfortable buying him. I had him as my 7th ranked hitter in 2025 Bowman Draft which put him right in between Billy Carlson (CHW) and Ethan Conrad (CHC) two players whose base autographs are quite a bit more expensive on average. Most of that comes from the fact that Neyens has the best power projections of any prep hitter in this class and I'm not sure it's that close. Rapsodo was recording MaxEV's at the combine and according to their readings they got a 120.3 mph reading on one of his batted balls which was the highest of any first round pick, high school or college. No need to worry about if he'll adjust to lifting the ball like many prep hitter, launching balls to his pull side is already one of his biggest strengths. The concern here is that he played in a division in Washington that didn't see a ton of high-end competition and when he did hit the showcase circuit he struggled with contact at times causing some evaluators to worry about his hit tool. Part of what intrigues me is that Neyens won Gatorade Player of the Year in his Junior season where he batted .455 with a .615 OBP and 1.327 OPS. He also went 8-0 with a 1.26 ERA on the mound. What's strange is that he only hit 3 HR that year and area scouts said of him that he had "long been seen as a potentially elite hitter from the left side of the plate with an outstanding approach". After some swing adjustments he added loft, the power went through the roof, but now there are swing-and-miss concerns. Entering the draft the player comparison that was thrown around most was a left-handed Austin Riley. This could come down to what the Astros do with him developmentally but because of the power ceiling his cards could go absolutely nuts if he's making consistent contact.

players.name: Kevin Alvarez
players.note: I'm using yesterday's prices so if his stuff went nuts after the video circulated of him going deep twice on the back fields the other day I wouldn't be surprised, but as of Friday his average base was still under $35. When it comes to the DSL stats I always say we should take them with a HUGE grain of salt because there's not a ton of consistency when it comes to how players perform there versus when they come to the states. Again I'll reference Cris Rodriguez who I was unwilling to call a buy at $40 but I actually trust Alvarez quite a bit more. When I did my 2025 Bowman Chrome preview Alvarez was my highest ranked DSL guy in the product other than Josuar Gonzalez and even though I was somewhat alone in this thought, I always liked him more than Elian Pena (NYM) and Cris Rodriguez (DET). In 192 PA in his DSL pro debut Alvarez hit .301 with 2 HR, 11 SB, 12.0% BB, 9.9% K, .154 ISO, and 129 wRC+. You know I love more walks than strikeouts at age 17 and that sub-10% K rate came with a 82.8% contact rate and 8.2% swinging strike %. If you were scouting only the box scores you might think that a guy posting these contact rates with a strikeout rate this low and only 2 HR was a smaller contact-over-power type. Kevin Alvarez is 6'4". The projection in his frame is really really good. I think as he matures physically this is 60 grade power which could be scary on a bat whose approach and contact metrics looks this good early on. Now as with all DSL guys we will have to see if it translates to the states and I know back field HRs don't mean anything but seeing a guy go deep twice in one day after only doing so twice the entire season last year feels like a good start to his time here. I know a lot of people got caught up in how weird his swing looked in those videos but it almost reminded me of a young Kyle Tucker and when he was being evaluated by international scouts that's actually the comp they put him on him over a year ago due to how he brings the barrel through the zone. I don't have any proof that contact rate is the stat that translates from the Dominican to the U.S. but one guy I really liked from the previous year's international class was Luis Pena of the Brewers who obviously broke out in a big way last year. If you look at their pages side-by-side Pena had a 78% contact rate and 14.6% SwStr% when he was in the DSL. Alvarez had a higher contact rate by over 4%, a lower SwStr% by 6% and he's 5 inches taller than Luis Pena. If everything comes together for him we're all really going to regret not buying more.

players.name: Ethan Frey
players.note:
Nobody who read my 2025 Bowman Draft preview is going to be surprised here. I ranked the Astros as having some of the best PYT value in breaks early on because somehow with Neyens and Frey they were being extremely slept on, and I think most of that was Frey. Though he wasn't priced like it out of the gate I had him as my 12th favorite hitter in that product because there's a ton to love here from a hobby standpoint. Not your usual first round bat we are chasing in Bowman, Frey went 95th overall and his $1 million signing bonus was the lowest of any hitter that I put in my top 20 for this product. Frey could barely crack the starting lineup his first two years in college and then was unable to show us anything in summer ball because of a torn labrum. Finally last Spring he got his chance to be a full-time starter and he did not disappoint. In 62 games at LSU he hit .331 with 13 HR, a .309 ISO, and 128 wRC+. Frey is 6'6" so it's no surprise that he's got plus maybe even double plus power projections. He can lift the ball to all fields and has HR power to every part of the park. FanGraphs has his fielding grade as a 30 but I think that's unfair and is probably because he mostly DH'd at LSU, but a lot of that was due to his recovery from his arm injury. Frey clocks above average run times though and was a multi-sport athlete in high school where he was a dual-threat QB for the football team. There is pretty shocking athleticism here for a frame this size. The Astros put him in Single-A following the draft and in his pro debut he hit .330 with 3 HR, 9 SB, 16.4% BB, 20.5% K, and a 166 wRC+ in 122 PA. I don't want to overreact to a 21-year-old's stats in A ball but his 83.4% contact rate and 6.2% SwStr% reallllly caught my eye for a 6'6" hitter. He also stole those 9 bases in 26 games which was more SB's than he had in three years combined at LSU. On top of that Houston played him in CF in all of his starts. It's risky gambling on a college bat with only one productive season but due to his injuries I actually don't think we saw his peak in college, something I also loved about Ryan Waldschmidt which made him a sleeper of mine. If this is 50 Hit, 60 Power, 55 Speed on a 6'6" guy that the Astros think is athletic enough to play CF how could we not take a chance?

This isn't a very deep hobby system but of the 3's I'm definitely intrigued by

players.name: Anthony Huezo
players.note: He projects for above average power and speed which is a combo we love. Last year at age 19 he had a 139 wRC+ and .196 ISO in 252 PA. The crazy part is after that he went and played professionally in the Australian League and hit .340 with 6 bombs in 30 games. We may not know much about that league but oddly enough Junior Caminero played a season there at 18 and dominated and it's what helped put him on my radar early. I'm definitely watching Huezo this season.

players.name: Walker Janek
players.note: could be worth a look as a cheap sleeper. 12 HR/30 SB last year pretty sneaky speed and athleticism for a catcher. Was a first round pick in 2024 so pedigree is good and Astros gave him over $3 million so they saw something. Might be a slow burn though since he debuted in A+ and then played there again all season last year. Tough to get too much attention in the hobby as a 23-year-old catcher but he's worth watching.

players.name: Luis Baez
players.note: is a player I loved as a sleeper in 2024 Bowman but he's really struggled to stay healthy since. Big time power upside and as a streaky hitter who is aggressive he's capable of going on crazy runs that could boost his card value. Also made it to AA at 20 so the Astros must like him at least a little bit. There will always be approach concerns but if he's healthy the power could really bounce back this year. We know the hobby hates catchers but

players.name: Miguel Ullola
players.note: Now the higher ranked of the Astros non-debuted pitching prospects per MLB Pipeline is Miguel Ullola. I do also really like Ullola who is less of a starter and a bit more expensive so I'll go 4 here, but I still like him as a buy for this price. The fastball here is electric. Flat release and a ton of carry and it's more up in that 98 range. Slider is mid-80's and is also nasty when he works it in with that fastball and it made some hitters look silly last year when he was locating well. There's also a curveball and changeup in the mix that he uses less frequently but there's some projection that the curveball could improve to an above average pitch with a little more refinement. We know the hobby loves pitchers with whiff stuff and Ullola has that. In his 2021 pro debut he had a 14.05 K/9. All he did the following year was improve that number to 15.0 K/9 which is bananas. Now the issue of course is that his walk rates in those seasons were 7.77 and 6.88 BB/9 respectively. There is major major reliever risk here. Because he has a hard time keeping the bases clear his ERA can balloon on him at times despite the fact that hitters have hit under .185 against him in consecutive seasons. Last year in AAA Ullola had a 3.88 ERA but his 4.63 FIP and 5.65 xFIP suggest maybe he was a bit lucky in his ability to strand runners. With that being said, there are quite a few pitcher profiles like this and while it may not looking pretty when we're projecting guys to be MLB starters it's hard to deny that being exciting can lead to hobby hype. And Miguel Ullola is electric, much more so than Ethan Pecko. On top of that he's already on the Astros 40-man roster so we probably will see him early in Spring Training. It's kind of a catch-22 though because despite him being on the roster I mentioned above that the Astros already have a 6-man rotation, so if Ullola breaks camp with the team which he very well may he's almost guaranteed to be in the bullpen. For that reason I give Pecko the nod as far as projecting starters but Ullola has a much better chance of creating buzz in Spring Training so I still think he's a good grab while he's selling for $10.

players.name: Ethan Pecko
players.note: One of my favorite sleeper pitchers in Bowman. Had him as my 5th ranked pitcher in 2025 Bowman Chrome. Sixth round pick out of Towson back in 2023 and he's someone that you didn't see on any prospect radars until 2024. In his first full professional season he was twice promoted, starting the year in A and finishing in AA, and between all three levels he had a 3.47 ERA, 11.72 K/9, and 3.47 BB/9. Athletic delivery and his fastball has been graded as high as 70 out of 80 by FanGraphs. It almost has the action of a sinker more than a traditional 4-seam and in college in sat in the low-90's but he's added velocity since then and last season he was in the 95-96 range much more frequently. I know that doesn't sound impressive these days but with the arm angle he throws from and life that he gets on it it's pretty nasty. His sweeper/slider looked great last year and he also throws a curveball and cutter which look like average offerings or better. Last year Pecko threw in AA & AAA and in 80 innings he had a 3.83 ERA but his 3.29 FIP paints a better picture of how well he threw in those starts. He struck out 28.7% of the hitters he faced between both levels with a 10.69 K/9 and again improved his BB/9 to 3.04. After his promotion to AAA we actually saw him look the best he has so far as a professional and in 8 appearances he had a 3.09 ERA, 2.99 FIP, 12.34 K/9, and 3.09 BB/9. In those starts Pecko had a 23.8% K-BB% thanks to a 31.8% strikeout rate and 7.9% walk rate, both the best we've seen from him since he was drafted. Evaluators think he could be a rotation 4 but with the improvements I've seen the last couple of years I actually think he could be a 3 which feels crazy for a $6 base auto, especially on a guy who could very likely debut this year. The strange part here is that the Astros didn't really invite any of their pitchers to Spring Training who weren't already on their 40-man roster so despite him being a guy who seems ready to make the leap to the MLB we won't see him early in Spring which does confuse me a bit. Also between a couple of trades and the signing of Tatsuya Imai the Astros now have a 6-man rotation already which makes Pecko way more blocked than he was a few months ago. Regardless I think he was WAY too good last year to be this cheap. This is probably the most green you'll see on one of my rankings graphics for this price.

players.name: Josh Hammond
players.note: Since there hasn't been any minor league action since I did my 2025 Bowman Draft preview I am going to stick to trusting my rankings and the research that I did on these players back in December. I had Josh Hammond as my 9th ranked hitter in the product and it was truly a toss-up between him and Ethan Conrad (CHC) for that 8th spot, a player I not only labeled as a buy on the Cubs sheet but who is nearly $10 more expensive on the base autograph than Hammond is. When Bobby Witt Jr. finished top 3 in the AL MVP voting the Royals were rewarded with an extra pick via the MLB's Prospect Promotion Incentive. That pick was the 28th overall pick in the 2025 draft and they used it on Josh Hammond, a two-way player out of High Point, North Carolina. Hammond was part of the 2024 USA baseball 18U national team whose roster included Eli Willits, Ethan Holliday, Gavin Fien, and Kayson Cunningham, all of whom were selected in the first round of last year's draft. On that team Hammond was a pitcher, a position many scouts thought he was best fit for. Between his Freshman and Sophomore years of high school he went 14-0 with a 1.28 ERA while striking out 150 batters in 84.2 innings. He looked great and honestly would have been a pitcher that I'd normally target in Bowman. Except Hammond decided he wanted to be a hitter. That move paid off because his offense exploded his Senior year, hitting .471 with a .613 OBP, .882 SLG, and 1.495 OPS. You know I love an approach/hit tool improvement. In his Junior season Hammond had 18 walks and 17 strikeouts. After one offseason where he focused full-time on hitting only he came back his Senior year with 29 walks to just 8 strikeouts. You can guess by that SLG he is projected for plus raw power from many evaluators. He already can take the ball to all fields, has great bat speed, and projects for possibly 25-30 HR if it all clicks. There's disagreement on the hit tool where FanGraphs has it 30 and MLB Pipeline has it 50, but given how much that approach improved in just one season after he gave up pitching I'm siding with Pipeline here. Two things I give slight bumps to in my prospect rankings that often make me like a player more, being a two-way athlete and growing up the son of a coach. Hammond is both. I think this Bowman ceiling could be really good.

players.name: Sean Gamble
players.note: Also coming out of 2025 Bowman Draft was Sean Gamble who was my 13th ranked hitter in the product, and the gap between these two wasn't very big for me. As a price reference he was one spot after Ethan Frey (HOU) in my rankings who I just gave a 4/5 rating to at $21 on the Astros sheet and Gamble is more than two years younger. I also had him one spot ahead of Ike Irish (BAL) whose base autograph is still about $40, so the value at $26 here is nice. I did multiple drafts of my 2025 Bowman Draft rankings and I don't know that I moved a player more frequently than Gamble because there were so many conflicting reports, scout grades, and prospect rankings based on where you looked. As an example FanGraphs had him at 40 Hit, 60 Power, 45 Speed. MLB Pipeline has him at 55 Hit, 50 Power, 60 Speed. Even when you look at my chart above Dynasty Dugout has him as their 332nd best prospect and Rotowire has him at 106th. I think what I learned while diving in to what tape I could find is that all of this disagreement stems on what Sean Gamble's future power is going to look like. At the IMG Academy he hit .413 as a Senior with a 1.324 OPS and in 91 PA he struck out a total of 6 times. A lot of times we are guessing what sort of competition these guys faced in high school but as someone who is very familiar with IMG and lives in that area of Florida I can tell you that his competition was very good. From what I've seen I do agree that presently it's probably below average power and plus speed but I think it has less to do with how strong he is physically and more to do with a swing that isn't geared to lift the ball, but that's something that can be worked on. We love those "if he grows into power" guys and Gamble could be one of the better ones. He's patient and makes fantastic contact to all parts of the field. Due to his speed he's extremely versatile defensively and saw time at CF, SS, and 2B, similar to how we've seen Jett Williams utilized. If you're someone who believes that money talks, the Royals gave Gamble a $4 million signing bonus and not only was it over slot but it was more than they gave Josh Hammond. Hammond may have a higher hobby ceiling but Gamble might have a better floor because of his contact skills and speed. We haven't seen either play professionally so what the 2026 season will look like is a bit of a guessing game, but Gamble has a 6'1" frame that could still add quite a bit of strength to an already really exciting offensive profile.

players.name: Blake Mitchell
players.note: was a name I really liked prior to last season but much of his hobby upside as a catcher is his offensive ability and almost all of his metrics took a step back last year. He's a funky player at the plate similar to Emmanuel Rodriguez where he both walks and strikes out a ton (over 50% combined last year) and when you do that the only way to stay exciting is with power, which Mitchell does have but it fell off an absolute cliff with his ISO going from .192 to .102. He has battled through injuries so I still think the ceiling is really good but with him still hanging around that $25 range after somewhat of an off year I'd be holding, probably not buying more until I see if he can rebound this year.

players.name: Yandel Ricardo
players.note: was reallllly close to a 4 and the upside here for $14 is fun, good tools all around but his hobby hype will hinge on the power. Had a .192 ISO and 151 wRC+ in the CPX last year but struggled after a promotion to Single-A. To be fair though he was only 18, and as a 6'1" switch-hitting SS there is a bit to like here.

players.name: Carson Roccaforte
players.note: wasn't on any radars and really only ended up on mine because of how many 'Hot Sheets' he made last year. Hard to be hobby exciting when you're almost 24 but last year between A+ & AA had a 138 wRC+ and .212 ISO after a 86 wRC+ and .134 ISO the year prior. One of the best single season turnarounds we saw last year but is he so old it doesn't matter for Bowman? We'll find out this year, but at $10 last year's season was pretty damn impressive.

players.name: Asbel Gonzalez
players.note: another 'almost 4' stole 78 bags last year and is the highest ranked prospect on this list by StS. He's electric. But he'll never hit for power. If you're someone who believes that the Chandler Simpson hype we saw last year could continue to be a trend in the hobby then Gonzalez isn't a bad grab considering how cheap he is, I just get really stuck on the fence with guys like this. Don't hate the lottery tickets in

players.name: Ramon Ramirez
players.note:
When 2024 Bowman came out there were a number of cheap sleepers that I chased and luckily one of them was Esmerlyn Valdez because his stock has gone insane ever since then. Another that I liked quite a bit was Ramon Ramirez who the Royals signed for just $57k out of Venezuela back in 2023. Despite not being a big name in the international class he had one of the best professional debuts we saw in the DSL that year where he hit .344 with 8 HR, 6 SB, 14.0% BB, 12.0% K, .270 ISO, and 171 wRC+. I mean, more walks than strikeouts with a .270 ISO, that's an easy way to get on my radar. My expectations were tempered of course since I don't trust DSL stats but when he came to the states in 2024 I still liked what I saw for a guy with a base autograph under $10. In the CPX that year he hit .265 with 7 HR, 12.8% BB, 20.7% K, .194 ISO, and 114 wRC+. The approach didn't look quite as good against the step up in pitching but a walk rate that high with a strikeout rate under 21% is still really solid for a young hitter with plus power projections. His overall production went up last year in Single-A where he hit .244 with 11 HR, 6 SB, 11.7% BB, 21.2% K, .198 ISO, and 120 wRC+ in 307 PA. Against a better level of pitching again he was able to keep that ISO around .200 with a similar BB/K. A couple of things that stood out to me when looking at some of his advanced hitting stats, despite his average dropping from .265 to .244, Ramirez actually increased his overall contact rates from 70.6% in 2024 to 75.5% in 2025. Part of the reason his batting average fell was that he was a bit unlucky compared to the year prior and his BABIP was almost 40 points lower. The 5% increase in contact rates when you already have .200-ish ISO power is a big green flag for me, and there was a lot of talk around the organization about how he showed up last year in much better shape than he was in the year prior. Despite missing some of the season due to injury and never playing above Single-A the Royals brought Ramirez to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee this year which I love to see. There's almost no buzz around Ramon Ramirez, just as there hasn't been for that last two years, but I'll say the same thing I said back in 2024 Bowman and that's that I think this guy is being slept on. Put me down for an offensive breakout campaign from Ramirez this season.

I actually love a lot of these Royals 3's.

players.name: Ramcell Medina
players.note: from last year's international class. Calcano looked great but it was only 35 PA, Medina put together a better body of work throughout the season. Both are solid targets. Of the 3's my favorite dart throw is

players.name: Jhonayker Ugarte
players.note: who doesn't have base autos but you can find his Refractor Autos for like $15. He's actually the Royals player I'm personally most invested in. Can't make him a 4 because the data doesn't really support it, but he's an eye test guy for me. I thought he looked legit when I saw him despite a very underwhelming stat line in his stateside debut. Guess we'll find out this season if my eyes have deceived me!

players.name: Michael Lombardi
players.note: I'm going to be honest I didn't realize how much I liked the value on the Royals for 2025 Bowman Draft until just now as Lombardi makes our third buy from the newest release. This is just a fascinating player to take a chance on for $7 in my opinion.
