Last year at Tulane, Lombardi made 64 appearances in the field and are you ready for this combination? 27 in center field, 21 on the mound, 14 at first base, and 2 at second base. Can't say I see a ton of CF/P at the college level. Offensively he hit .273 with 4 HR, 9 2B, 2 3B, and had more walks than strikeouts in 174 PA. As a pitcher he made 23 appearances (6 starts, 17 relief) where he went 4-1 with a 2.14 ERA, 15.64 K/9, and 4.50 BB/K working primarily as Tulane's closer. Mind you this is a guy who has never been a full-time pitcher. Last year opposing hitters batted .139 against Lombardi, he had a 0.98 WHIP, 12.5% walk rate, and wait for it… wait for it… a 43.5% strikeout rate. He faced 168 batters last year and he struck out 73 of them. What?! Immediately I'm intrigued. What likely improved his draft stock and led to a 2nd round selection from the Royals is that after operating almost solely as a reliever all year Tulane started him in the AAC tournament and he went 7 innings striking out 11 hitters. I'm not going to say there's not reliever risk considering he's basically never been a starter, but something tells me if the Royals went this high for him it might because they think they can make him a starter. His fastball and curveball were two of the most unhittable pitches in all of D-I in terms of in-zone whiff rates. Of course his 4.50 BB/9 isn't ideal coming out of college but that number was 7.78 in 2024, and he was able to drop his walk rates from 19% to 12.5%. On top of that he improved his K-BB% from 9% to 31% which is quite frankly insane, thanks to him also having a 15.5% rise in his strikeout rate from 2024 to 2025. Even if he's a reliever he's one I'm interested in seeing this year, but if the Royals were to try and make him a starter we could see some crazy K numbers early on in his professional career. Given the athleticism as a former CF I don't think him improving his command is a reach either. I haven't really seen him mentioned anywhere and that makes him my favorite type of really cheap stash.

players.name: Drew Beam
players.note: made the hardest push of the 3's to be a buy. Looked good in his debut and has a good mix of pitches but he's always been more of a strike thrower than a swing-and-miss guy, even back to his time at Tennessee. He's a good arm but not overly exciting for the hobby unless his stuff starts to tick up a bit. Watch

players.name: Cameron Millar
players.note:
More 2025 Bowman Draft? If I must. Millar is one that we have much less information on and he's not even ranked as a top 30 Royals prospect by MLB Pipeline but sometimes when we're looking for sleepers that's better for us anyways. Talk about coming out of nowhere, I'm not sure that any player in the MLB draft improved their stock in their Senior year of high school more than Millar who went 7-1 with a 0.11 ERA in 12 starts last Spring. If you're wondering how an ERA gets that low the answer is that Millar threw 64 innings, faced 235 batters, and allowed 1 earned run. Of those 235 batters he faced he struck out 117 of them (49.8%) and walked 18. When you consider that he also hit 6 batters with pitches that means that exactly 60% of the hitters Millar faced last year didn't even put the bat on the ball. The Royals used some of the money they saved signing Michael Lombardi under slot to grab Millar for $1.5 million which was nearly double his slot value in the 3rd round. Part of what caused him to become unhittable is that during the Area Code games the summer prior to his Senior year he was throwing his fastball about 92 mph before seeing a crazy spike in velocity and sitting near 97 in many of his starts last year. According to MLB.com's draft coverage this caused Millar to go from "being a kind of vanilla high school right-hander to one of the hottest prep arms in the west". We don't have much information on the secondary pitches other that he throws a slider and changeup which evaluators have put a 50 (average) grade on, but while I was scouring the internet and reading message boards (as I do) I saw a player who faced Millar in high school say that his changeup has almost screwball-like movement and he threw it to him on a 3-2 count when he faced him and the pitch "just completely disappeared". This is tough because it's so hard for me to hop in on a prospect that I have zero college or professional data on them, but there seem to be some impressive reports on Cameron Millar if you dive deep enough. For $6 I'm probably willing to find out if they're legit or not.

I think

players.name: Justin Lamkin
players.note: this year. I'm not positive his stuff will play professionally but there's always a chance we could see it improve. Funky arm action and deception I actually liked watching him last year at Texas A&M and he's really cheap, floor over ceiling play though.

players.name: Nelson Rada
players.note: which does make sense to me. Part of that is driven by the fact that he has almost no color autos because they were stolen and forged. I believe he has base, refractor, speckle, and then a few others but there's not much out there. Love the hit tool and speed here and he's been moved aggressively, reaching AAA at 19 last year. I think we see him this year and I do think he's a good player but with virtually no power I'm not super in to buying players this expensive.

players.name: Hayden Alvarez
players.note: One of my favorite buys of all the Angels hitters is outfielder Hayden Alvarez who they signed for $685k in the 2024 international class. The teenager is a 6'3" righty with a projectable frame who has shown a really impressive approach and hit tool early in his professional career. In his DSL debut, Alvarez hit .250 with 1 HR, 32 SB, 14.3% BB, 16.1% K, .108 ISO, and a 103 wRC+. Despite the mediocre results he drew rave reviews from people in the Angels organization for his awareness of the zone as he's extremely patient for his age and hardly ever chases. That ability to log advanced at-bats showed up when he came to the states last year and hit .335 with 2 HR, 24 SB, 14.0% BB, 18.6% K, .093 ISO, and 131 wRC+ in 221 PA at the CPX. The Angels liked what they saw so much that they gave the 18-year-old an early promotion to Single-A where he played 20 games to end the year batting .355 with a .459 OBP, 13.2% BB, 10.5% K, and a 156 wRC+. Obviously you can tell by the stats that he hasn't produced much over the fence power yet, with an ISO that hovers around .100 and only 3 career HRs in over 500 PA. However, there is still a ton of strength that he can add to his frame and his bat speed is already good, leading some evaluators to believe that his raw power could eventually be above average. And if it got there, man this would be a legit bat. Last year between the CPX & A, Alvarez had a 81.5% contact rate and 6.9% swinging strike %, but after his promotion to A those actually jumped to 88% contact and 4.2% SwStr% on the 307 pitches he saw there in 62 PA. Naturally there is disagreement on if that power will get there and I've seen his future power grades range anywhere from 40 to 55, and that part of his profile is what is driving a stake between some prospect rankers, with Dynasty Dugout barely having him top 500 but Rotowire having him top 100. As you know by now taking guys with this skillset and hoping the power shows up is my wheelhouse, and sometimes we're doing it with 5'8" prospects but Alvarez's 6'3" frame has me a bit more optimistic. On top of the great approach and contact skills he has 60 grade speed which helps not only on the bases but in the outfield where he is likely to stick as an above average center fielder. I understand it's a small sample but only 45 prospects last year age 18 or younger saw 50+ PA at Single-A. The three highest wRC+ marks were Emil Morales ($53), Dax Kilby ($103), and Hayden Alvarez ($18). The lowest SwStr%? Hayden Alvarez (4.2%). The best walk to strikeout ratio? Hayden Alvarez (1.25). Oddly enough if you put him and Dax Kilby's Single-A stats side-by-side they're almost identical in every category, including power, and people are freaking out about Kilby. Nobody can know for sure if the power will come, but if it did his stock would bang.

players.name: Joswa Lugo
players.note: is a player I like since he may end up having plus power and speed as he grows into his 6'3" frame making for a high hobby ceiling from a 19-year-old shortstop. He has struggled with contact so far and is a bit aggressive for my liking. Great ceiling, not sure the floor is safe enough for this price.

players.name: Gabriel Davalillo
players.note:
Davalillo was signed the year after Hayden Alvarez and he was the top-ranked catcher in the entire international class. This is a spot the Angels target very frequently so they weren't going to let Davalillo go, giving him a $2 million singing bonus last January. Unlike fellow Angels catching prospect Juan Flores whose defense is unreal, Davalillo is bat-first which is great for us in the hobby. It's already been mentioned this Spring that the Angels were giving him reps at third base just to try and find somewhere else to play him in case his bat ends up being so good that they need to move him up faster than his defense can develop behind the dish. And that might be likely. I know I know, I hate DSL stats, but walk with me. Last year in his pro debut at age 17, Davalillo hit .302 with 7 HR, 13.6% BB, 12.4% K, .216 ISO, and a 136 wRC+. His contact rate was 84.4% and his SwStr% was 6.3%. As someone who usually throws DSL stats out the window even I was like 'wait, what?!'. Here's a list of qualified DSL hitters last year age 17 or younger with more walks than strikeouts, an ISO over .200, and a SwStr% under 7%: Gabriel Davalillo. Here's a list of everyone who did it in 2024: Nobody. 2023? Nobody. 2022? Nobody… you get the point. There are two obvious reasons why the hobby is sleeping on him so much. One he's a catcher and two he's a big boy, kind of has that Francisco Alvarez build. That build is what kept people away from Moises Ballesteros cards early on but then we found out as he continued to climb levels that if you're that good at hitting eventually it won't matter and your cards are bound to go up. That's absolutely in play here with Davalillo. It's an awkward body type but when you look into the advanced hitting data I don't know that I've seen a DSL stat line over the past 4 or 5 years that I like more than his. On top of that he just turned 18 in November meaning that he will be 18 all of this season where we will not only see him in the CPX but also very likely Single-A with how aggressive the Angels tend to be with their promotions. If he were to post similarly impressive lines in the states this year I'd go so far as to say he has 55 Hit 60 Power which is crazy impressive. If he is terrible in the CPX I will officially throw out DSL stats entirely moving forward because that's how good his were. I don't expect him to struggle though.

The most expensive of the Angels prospects is

players.name: Raudi Rodriguez
players.note: probably made the strongest push to be a 4. Tools look great and all he did last year was hit .281 with 14 HR and 38 SB. Downside was he was 21 in Single-A. On the plus side he played in the AFL against better competition after the season and hit a ridiculous .433 in 71 PA there. I actually think the ceiling for $10 is veryyy interesting, but he'll turn 23 this July and has never played above Single-A so unless the Angels got real aggressive real fast it may be hard for him to pop as a name.

players.name: Tyler Bremner
players.note: Now Bremner's base autograph is double the price of Klassen's and I do have them ranked almost identically but that's more of a testament to how underrated I think Klassen is, because Bremner is still a buy to me. He was my 5th ranked pitcher in 2025 Bowman Draft and I currently have him ranked one spot after Jamie Arnold (OAK) whose base autograph is closer to $45. It was a bit of a surprise when the Angels passed on Kade Anderson with the second pick but they're known for making these types of moves at the top. This selection marked the sixth time in the last seven years that the Angels used their first pick on a player who signed under the slot value, and Bremner's $2.5 million under slot was the biggest gap of them all. Who knows why they do what they do but a theory I've always had is that they draft the players that they think are the most MLB-ready. My evidence is that their previous first rounders before Bremner were Christian Moore, Nolan Schanuel, and Zach Neto and they were all on a very fast track to the MLB. Maybe they think Bremner is closer to stepping on an MLB mound than Kade Anderson? Who really knows. But back in 2024 at UC Santa Barbara, Bremner went 11-1 with a 2.54 ERA in 88.2 innings where he worked as both a starter and reliever. Last year as a full-time starter he went 5-4 with a 3.49 ERA which may look very blah but his FIP was 2.14 so I think he might have been dealing much more than the stat line shows. On top of that 2.14 FIP he had a 12.92 K/9 and 2.21 BB/9 showing not only a great ability to generate whiffs but he also limited damage by not offering free passes. He throws some of the most effortless 98 mph you'll see with an easy delivery but his changeup is the pitch we're after here, it could be 70 grade and it just disappears late. In college this past season his changeup had a 48% whiff rate. He also has a slider which could be an above average third pitch due to it's impressive spin rates even though he doesn't throw it a ton. Best thing you can do as a pitcher is keep runners off the bases. Bremner did so by having a .178 AVG against him in 2024 and just a 6.1% BB rate in both of his final two seasons. I think it's a somewhat rare combination for the hobby that he has both stuff and command since we're usually trying to decide between one or the other. He's already with the team for Spring Training and it wouldn't surprise me if he was the first player in this class to reach the MLB. It is kind of what the Angels do after all. If he is, I think we still have a good amount of room at this price.

players.name: George Klassen
players.note: When a player's value in the Bowman world is lower than you'd expect you can almost always chalk it up to to something simple. For a hitter, he's too old or has no power. For a pitcher, he has mediocre stuff or is going to be a reliever. But sometimes the market is just wrong. I think it's wrong on George Klassen and it has been for some time. Klassen came over in a trade from Philadelphia and if you love stuff, his is electric. His fastball touches triple digits and rides up in the zone and could be a legitimate 70 grade offering. His slider and curveball are both filthy with high spin rates that make hitters look foolish when he's on and locating them. He also features a changeup as a fourth pitch that is closer to average. Now the thing with Klassen, as is with most guys who have stuff this good, is that his command was bad when he was drafted. He threw 56.2 innings his final year at Minnesota and had a 7.46 BB/9 and 17.9% walk rate. Gross. In his first professional season in 2024 he showed huge improvements to both his pitch shapes and his control while playing for both the Phillies and Angels. He was promoted by both teams in the same season, starting in Single-A with Philly and finishing in Double-A with Los Angeles, and combined across every stop he had a 3.10 ERA, 2.88 FIP, 13.06 K/9, and 4.45 BB/9. The command still wasn't quite where you want it for a starting pitcher but the improvements in his overall walk rates from 17.9% to 12% were a massive single season improvement. During that season the only pitchers age 22 or younger who had a K% over 35% and ground ball rate over 45% in 90+ innings were Jarlin Susana ($44) and George Klassen ($14). I think a lot of the reason people are sleeping on Klassen is because he had a 5.22 ERA last year but when you look closer he was one of the unluckiest pitchers in baseball and his 3.21 FIP and 3.20 xFIP suggest he pitched two full runs better than that. On top of that he improved his control (again) and dropped his walk rate from 12% to 9.7% and his BB/K from 4.45 to 3.89. At the end of the season the Angels moved Klassen to AAA for his final start of the year where he struck out 8 batters over 6 innings and only walked one. Oddly enough I have the Spring Training games on while I'm writing this and Klassen is currently making his first start against the Padres who are playing all of their starters. He just went 3 up 3 down including K's of Manny Machado on a filthy 91 mph slider and Jackson Merrill on an elevated 99 mph fastball. May want to put some eBay offers in before those clips start blowing up on Twitter. People can sleep on him all they want but I'm not. There's a very specific type of pitcher in that Jacob Misiorowski mold who has the stuff to put up big strikeout numbers when they get called up, causing their card prices go nuts. I believe George Klassen is one of them.

players.name: Johnny Slawinski
players.note:
Another 2025 draftee for the Angels was Slawinski, a third round left-handed pitcher who got a signing bonus that was double the slot value thanks to all that money they saved on Tyler Bremner. Two things I love when it comes to players in the draft are when a team likes them enough to go way over slot value (check) and guys who are either two-way players or multi-sport athletes. Well, Slawinski played not one, not two, not three, but FOUR varsity sports in Johnson City, Texas. Ohhhh and he was a two-way player on the diamond. As a hitter, Slawinski batted .478 with 13 HR, 5 2B, and 4 3B in 92 PA putting him at a *checks notes* 1.043 slugging percentage. I suppose that's okay. On the mound he went 9-1 with a 0.37 ERA allowing 4 earned runs in 77 innings while striking out 177 hitters. In case you couldn't have guessed it Slawinski is a great athlete and that shows on the mound where he creates really good extension, has a repeatable delivery, and already has extremely good command for his age. His fastball sits in the low 90's and peaked at around 95 his Senior year but because of its ride and how much extension he gets it plays much quicker. He has a four pitch mix in total. The slider breaks on both planes and could be an above average pitch and the curveball which he used as his third offering looked great as well. While he mostly stuck to those three pitches he did at times mix in a changeup and although it was his fourth and least used pitch scouts loved the fade that it showed against righties and it could end up being another above average pitch as he gets more polished. This pick checks a ton of boxes that I look for in players when I'm buying cards. I've mentioned in the past that I love two-way players who are not only going to be focusing on one side full-time but they're also about to get professional level development for the first time. I also love multi-sport athletes for kind of that same reason. Slawinski was a dominate pitcher as a prep despite the fact that he never played baseball year-round and when he did half of it was spent at another position. Feels like quite a bit of upside for $10 if you ask me.

The Angels seem to have a type recently and sometimes it feels to me like they're just drafting every pitcher who can throw 100 mph and hoping that it works.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: from last year's draft class are prime examples. I'm probably waiting until I see both of them pitch professionally before I'm buying anything but presently I give the nod to Shores who is inside my top 200 pitchers. Lot to like in the 6'8" righty who throws absolute gas but he barely pitched in 2023 before missing all of 2024 and when he returned in 2025 you could definitely see he was trying to shake the rust off. I like the upside but since the results haven't been there he's someone I'd want at around $5 as a dart throw, at $10 I'd much rather just put the money into Slawinski from this class.

players.name: Josue De Paula
players.note: who I've always loved and still do and don't get me wrong if the power show up this year he could move into that tier of top 10 hitters that are selling for $200+, but this feels like the third year in a row I've said that. Weird comps here for JDP who had recent sales over $125, then one that sold in rough condition for $80, now it seems people have accepted offers in that range. If you see him at $80 he's a buy but I'd be surprised at this point if anyone is taking under $100. I wouldn't be too shocked if he keeps going up but he almost certainly won't debut this year. I'm holding what I have of him because I really do believe in the player, but I've got Quintero ranked higher and he's cheaper so it's hard for me to love this price.

players.name: Eduardo Quintero
players.note: Before I even started the Dodgers sheet I suspected that they wouldn't have many 4's since they're such a big market, I mean I had a hard time finding a single buy on the Red Sox. I definitely didn't think they'd have a 5. But man, what are we doing here. When the 2025 Bowman checklist came out I was as loud as I could possibly be about Eduardo Quintero. Early pricing after release had Franklin Arias (BOS) more expensive and I was on here every week being like, "wrong". I'm sure there were some people before me but I'm the first person that I know of who made Quintero the #1 prospect on the Dodgers over Josue De Paula and Zyhir Hope. He is the poster child for the prospect I'm trying to find in Bowman. Every article I do seems to have a "well if this guy grew into power…" and we have the perfect one right here. Back in 2023 in his pro debut in the DSL Quintero hit .359 with 5 HR, 22 SB, 15.1% BB, 16.0% K, .259 ISO, and a 177 wRC+. Dominant but it was the DSL, and I've said in the past that even good hitters with below average raw power can flash power against poor pitching just because they're advanced. What we saw in 2024 was more representative of how Quintero was viewed offensively by most evaluators. Between the CPX & A he hit .285 with 3 HR, 32 SB, 17.1% BB, 19.4% K, .108 ISO, and 123 wRC+. Still a really good season for being 18 but this line was more in line with what we expected from him. Really good approach (0.88 BB/K), good contact (8.3% SwStr%), and good speed (32 SB), but with below average to average power (3 HR, .108 ISO). The improvements that we saw last year were so good that I'm not sure how everyone doesn't have him as a top 10 prospect currently. Across 541 PA in A & A+ this past season Quintero hit .293 with 19 HR, 47 SB, 16.3% BB, 22.7% K, .215 ISO, and 152 wRC+. This is an absolutely insane season. From 3 HR to 19 HR. Doubled his ISO from .108 to .215. Raised his SLG from .394 to .508. Cherry on top which you hardly ever seen when a player this young drastically improves his power output, his contact rates WENT UP from 78.4% to 79.2%. Every single time I do a "here's how many players did X and Y last season", Eduardo Quintero is one of the names it returns. Players age 21 or younger last year who hit 15+ HR and had 45+ SB: Konnor Griffin and Eduardo Quintero. Players age 21 or younger last year (excluding rookie levels) with an ISO over .200 and a SwStr% under 8%: Kevin McGonigle and Eduardo Quintero. Whether you sort lists looking for impressive power/speed combos like Griffin or players with great contact skills like McGonigle, you end up with Eduardo Quintero on it. As a Dodgers prospect I'm shocked his stock hasn't erupted yet. Not that $83 is a cheap base auto but I now have him ranked higher than Colt Emerson, Max Clark, and JJ Wetherholt, all of whom have base autographs over $200. In my interview with Mariners pitcher Ryan Sloan I asked him if he played against anyone that was so good last year he went and bought their cards afterwards. He gave me one name, Eduardo Quintero.

players.name: Emil Morales
players.note: is a big hobby name and I've given the same report on him for years, HUGE hobby ceiling because of his power potential but often terrifying contact numbers though they did look a bit better during his time in Single-A. Due to the upside his price is absolutely warranted at $50+ but if I'm buying a power bat with an unproven hit tool I'm taking Chase Harlan at about 30% of the price.

players.name: Mike Sirota
players.note: Other than Ryan Waldschmidt and Sam Antonacci, Sirota is the name that I personally did the best on in 2024 Bowman Draft. Prior to his trade from Cincinnati I was scooping his cards extremely cheap and when I say extremely cheap I'm talking a $28 refractor auto /499, a $74 true blue auto /150, and a $48 sparkle auto /71 which got a PSA 10. We're up on Sirota. As a disclaimer I sold those last season so I no longer have any inventory but when it comes to Dodgers prospects whose stock still has the most room to grow he's one of my favorites. People around this organization love him and he's one of the first names you hear them rave about when it comes to prospects. Funny enough Sirota was drafted by the Dodgers out of high school but elected to go to college at Northeastern. A few years later he's selected by the Reds, traded to the Dodgers, and now they've got their guy. Following the 2023 college season there were many scouts who thought that Sirota was going to go in the top half of the first round. As a Sophomore he hit .346 with 18 HR, 19 SB, and a 1.149 OPS. Strong. The issue is that in his Junior year he took a step back batting .298 with 7 HR, 19 SB, and a .986 OPS. Still not a terrible year but the HR output dropped significantly along with his SLG of course which fell from .678 to .513. One positive we could take away was that his OBP was still .473 thanks in part to a very impressive 23% walk rate which was up quite a bit from the year prior. During my 2024 Bowman Draft research I looked for information on any injuries he may have had that kind of stunted his power but couldn't find much. Maybe just an off year. Despite that he was a player I was willing to take a chance on because his profile is very hobby friendly. Athletic, strong, good bat-to-ball skills, legit 20/20 potential or even more. That gamble of mine paid off when in his pro debut last year Sirota hit .333 with 13 HR, 5 SB, 17.8% BB, 21.9% K, .282 ISO, and 189 wRC+ between A & A+. The HR/SB total might not pop but that's because he only played 59 games prior to an injury that ended his season. I was only a little excited when he had a 197 wRC+ in A because he is a college bat after all, but his 184 wRC+ and .239 ISO in 155 PA after his promotion to A+ really got my attention. Only three prospects age 22 or younger last year who had 250+ PA had an ISO over .280: Samuel Basallo, Jac Caglianone, and Mike Sirota. The only ones 22 or younger with 250+ PA and a wRC+ over 165? Konnor Griffin, Kevin McGonigle, Jac Caglianone, and Mike Sirota. It may not have been a full season, but it was just about the best three months you can have. At under $50 I think this ceiling could be big if he continues to perform anywhere close to this when he returns.

players.name: Zyhir Hope
players.note: is a player I go back and forth on because he doesn't have a true 1st autograph. While I still think $40 is a touch low for how good he's been the contact rates really backed up last year and when you look at other prospects with non-1st autos the biggest one is Sebastian Walcott and his is $80-90. Because of his tools though he's a top 5 hobby prospect for me and has been for over a year now. If Hope's path to his cards doubling is that he has to generate as much buzz as Walcott and be a top 5-ish name I'm not sure I can get there.

players.name: Chase Harlan
players.note:
We know the name of the game when it comes to Bowman is 'ceiling' and honestly for under $20 there might not be a better one in baseball right now. Now of course that means that the floor isn't super safe but if you're looking for players who have the tools to go up exponentially this is a great roll of the dice. As a disclaimer you'll hardly ever see me selling cards of players I say to buy but I do have a PSA 9 true gold auto currently on eBay. I'm obviously not in a rush to move it but I often list things over comps and wait until the value reaches what I want for it, so if you're wondering why I'm selling… I'm not really but everything has its price. Harlan was taken in the third round of the 2024 draft and signed for $1.75 million which was more than $1 million over the slot value for his pick. Entering the draft the scouting report on him was that he had big time power potential but on the high school circuits he struggled against off-speed stuff. The 6'3" prep had hip surgery following the draft and was therefore unable to make his professional debut until last season. When he did we saw that power that everybody was talking about. Playing in the CPX at age 18 he hit .288 with a 121 wRC+ and had 6 HR in his first 177 PA which put him at a .212 ISO. Perhaps the most impressive part given his scouting report was that his strikeout rate in those games was under 20%. The Dodgers saw all they needed to see and promoted him to Single-A where he struggled a bit more but was still fine, hitting .240 with 3 HR, a .115 ISO, and 103 wRC+ in 123 PA. There were 31 hitters in the minors last year who got 300+ PA at age 18 or younger. Only 7 of those 31 had an ISO over .170. Only 4 of those 7 also had a BB/K over 0.50. Rainiel Rodriguez (STL), Edward Florentino (PIT), Leo De Vries (OAK), and Chase Harlan (LAD). Those first three names are ALL in my top 10 for non-debuted hitters. Harlan has a ways to go developmentally but this still feels like we're getting in at the ground floor with his current price. I've been following him on social media and have seen the videos he's posted on changes he's made to his swing this offseason and it looks great. There's actually a clip I shared last year of him going deep in a Single-A game and the swing and finish look eerily similar to Manny Machado to me. I don't want to make it seem like he's a slam dunk because the contact skills have a long ways to go, but the power gives him an incredible ceiling that isn't too far off from Emil Morales who is considerably more expensive. Really hard to beat the upside at this price.

Out of every team I've done so far this is by far my favorite list of 3's and that's kind of to be expected, the Dodgers are great at finding young talent but their cards are seldom cheap. Biggest name is of course

players.name: Aidan West
players.note: out of 2025 Bowman Draft are both great stashes if you pulled anything of theirs. Have them ranked pretty high but they're in the range where I'd ideally want them under $15. Both are on the fence of being a buy at their current price but could be good breakout candidates for this season. Sometimes the 3's can be guys in buy low spots which might make

players.name: Kellon Lindsey
players.note:
my favorite in this group since his price has been cut in half since last year. One of the best athletes in the 2024 draft he draw a lot of Trea Turner comps coming out. Speed is no doubt but evaluators are torn on future power (as they were with Trea) and he struggled with K's in his debut. Still a great ceiling here and $11 for a guy the Dodgers gave $3.3 million to doesn't feel like the worst idea.

Honestly, both

players.name: Adam Serwinowski
players.note: could be buys. I have put other pitchers ranked in their range with similarly priced base autographs as a 4/5 on other teams. And don't get me wrong I do think both of them should see an increase in price this year so I don't think you can go wrong buying either. With pitchers specifically though it usually comes down to one of two things for me. Will they debut this year or are they drastically undervalued? Most of my favorite buys will fall into one of those categories. Getting ahead of a breakout or chasing that call-up. Not only are Ferris and Serwinowski both valued right about where I'd put a pitcher on the fringe of my top 50, the chances for upward movement in the organization right now give me pause. Injuries have plagued the Dodgers rotation the last few years and because of that we've seen a number of guys get their shot at pitching in the bigs so there's definitely a chance we could see some guys get the call this year. But let's look at the projected rotation. Yamamoto, Glasnow, Ohtani, Sheehan, Sasaki. And that's not including Blake Snell who will miss Opening Day but should be back this season. Ready for the list of pitchers who are already on the Dodgers 40-man roster and expected to begin the year in AAA? River Ryan, Kyle Hurt, Gavin Stone, and Landon Knack. All are expected to throw MLB innings this year. I will probably like Ferris and Serwinowski as buys this time next year and hopefully their cards don't go up too much between now and then but with so many arms in front of them I just don't see how they make a huge splash this season.

players.name: Zach Root
players.note: was also really close to being in the buy range for me at around 80th with a $12 autograph. Would have preferred it under $10 but I still like him as a hold, just need to see him professionally before I jump in. Above average secondary pitches but his fastball is his lowest graded pitch and he only threw it about 35% of the time at Arkansas. I think the Dodgers can get it to play up but low-to-mid-90's with good command and great off-speed isn't exactly the profile that makes the hobby go nuts. With that said, I really like the floor for this price and if the stuff trends up this year he could be worth watching.

players.name: Joe Mack
players.note: and always have but after being a 4/5 on last year's sheet at $5 we're officially up 500% which is the dream. I still think if the Marlins are serious about winning he breaks camp as their Opening Day starting catcher because he's miles better defensively than Agustin Ramirez. Even then I'm not sure how much juice this has left in the next month? I could be wrong and it could double again but his ranking of 74th at $30 puts him in a hold range for me. It's been a fun ride though! I feel like I've been higher than most on

players.name: Andrew Salas
players.note: who I don't think gets enough credit for playing a full season of Single-A at 17. From both an approach and bat-to-ball perspective I do think he'll be a better hitter than both of his brothers. I thought we'd get a buy low spot since the stats didn't pop last year but $20 is a touch higher than I expected for his ranking. Still love the upside though so keep holding if you've got them.

players.name: Deyvison De Los Santos
players.note: is down from last year and it's still pretty shocking he hasn't debuted yet. It feels like we'll for sure see him this year because how could we not? The man had a 40 HR season in the minors in 2024. Huge power upside so when he comes up he could definitely go on a heater. Under $10 range I'm looking at

players.name: Kemp Alderman
players.note: Part of the reason that I love doing the 'Hot Sheet' during the season is that there ends up being a few names that you never hear about who seem to make it over and over and get me thinking, "why aren't we talking about this guy?". One for me last year was Kemp Alderman who the Marlins drafted out of Ole Miss in the 2nd round of the 2023 draft. The scouting report on Alderman is that he mashes. Depending on where you look I've seen him get raw power grades ranging from 60 to 80, with of course 80 being the highest you can get on the 20/80 scale. In his final season at Oxford in 2023 Alderman hit .376 with 19 HR in only 54 games. Not only did his power trend way up with a 100 point rise in his ISO from the year prior, but he improved his contact a ton too dropping his strikeout rate from 24.2% in 2022 to 16.9% in 2023. Unfortunately in a limited pro debut he struggled, and then in his first full professional season in 2024 he struggled again. He did battle some injuries that year and despite the stat lines not looking good the Marlins still promoted him twice and he finished the year in Double-A. This is where it gets fun. After hitting 8 HR in 320 PA that season Alderman went to the Arizona Fall League and hit 6 more in 9 games. I know it's a hitter friendly environment but that's an .833 slugging percentage in 40 PA. Still such a small sample that he still wasn't really a name worth mentioning until that breakout carried over into 2025 in a big way. Last year between AA & AAA, Alderman hit .285 with 22 HR, 22 SB, 7.3% BB, 23.1% K, .197 ISO and a 135 wRC+. That huge power we hadn't see since college came back and on top of that he stole 22 bases in 130 games after stealing a combined 7 of them in three collegiate seasons. I'm not going to lie to you and tell you the approach (0.31 BB/K) or contact skills (72.5%) are what I look for in a player but one way to make your cards go up when you have that profile is by having big time power. In his 82 PA in AAA he was in the 97th percentile for Max EV (114.4 mph), 99th percentile 90th% EV (110.3 mph), 93rd percentile barrel rate (14.5%), and 98th percentile hard hit % (61.8%). There were only four prospects age 22 or younger last year with 20+ HR, 20+ SB, and a wRC+ of 135 or higher. Konnor Griffin, Joshua Baez, Kaelen Culpepper, and Kemp Alderman. Considering you may have never heard of him unless you follow the Marlins this was a pretty impressive season AND he should debut this year. I know the Marlins aren't nearly as exciting as the Yankees but he's not ranked that far behind Spencer Jones in my rankings and his autograph is about 5% of the price.

players.name: Brandon Compton
players.note: It's pretty tough for me to call any prospect who is ranked outside my top 200 a buy but when the ceiling is good and the price point is low that often creates a compelling case. Enter Brandon Compton. This is an extremely intriguing play and honestly I'm surprised that his autographs out of 2025 Bowman Draft are already this cheap. He was very, very close to making my top 20 hitter rankings when I did my Bowman Draft preview but instead he ended up barely on the outside and in the 'High Upside Stashes' category. And that's what he is. The only difference is that every other player I put in that category still has a base autograph near $15 which makes Compton's at half of that price a worthwhile stash to me. His freshman year at Arizona St., Compton hit .354 with 14 HR, 3 SB, 10.8% BB, 25.4% K, .307 ISO, and 152 wRC+. Pretty shaky approach there for a college bat but despite that he was labeled as a potential first rounder to watch for the following season. Unfortunately his stats went backwards in his sophomore year where he hit .271 with 9 HR, 10 SB, 15.3% BB, 21.1% K, .215 ISO, and 99 wRC+. It's hard to take any positives away from a season where we saw a player drop his ISO by 90 points and his wRC+ by more than 50, but as an approach guy myself seeing the BB/K move from 0.43 to 0.73 as he increased his walk rate 5% and dropped his strikeouts nearly the same has me a little intrigued. But we all know what really got me intrigued. And if you don't know look up highlights from the 2025 MLB Draft Combine. Would you believe me if I told you that Brandon Compton broke the record for highest exit velocity with a wood bat since the combine started tracking EV's five years ago? If not then buckle up, because he did it three times. That's right, he is now the sole owner of all three of the hardest hit balls in the event's history. 116.9 mph, 116.6 mph, 116.4 mph. In one round of BP he hit 12 balls over 112 mph and along with owning the three hardest hit ever, he also has five in the top seven. Is it crazy to buy a player who regressed their final year in college just because he can hit a baseball harder than anybody else? Maybe. And I'll be the first to admit it's not the profile I usually go for. But $7 feels like an extremely low entry point given how much noise he could potentially make as a minor leaguer. I once bought cards of Tony Blanco Jr. from the Pirates who I admitted in a write-up had a hole in his swing so big I could drive my car through it but that it didn't matter because the first time Twitter saw a clip of him hitting a ball 120 mph his cards were going to explode. And they did. Sometimes that's all it takes.

players.name: Dillon Head
players.note: For under $5 guys I don't think you could really lose buying

players.name: Carter Johnson
players.note: at $3. To be honest with you this whole Marlins spreadsheet might not be the most exciting crop but I don't hate a single hitter on this list at their current price.

players.name: Esmil Valencia
players.note:
As I said above with Compton, rarely will I give a buy to someone who is outside my top 200 but then again up until now I've yet to have anyone inside my top 300 with a base autograph of… $1. Honestly, if it had been someone who was 24-years-old or had 30 grade power I would have just been like, "yeah, ok whatever", but that's not really the situation here. Valencia came over to the Marlins last year in the trade that sent Jesus Sanchez to the Astros. He was playing in Single-A at the time at age 19 and the Marlins elected to keep him at that level. At the end of the year his Single-A line across both organizations looked like this: .279 AVG, 8 HR, 64 SB, 6.8% BB, 22.4% K, .116 ISO, and 112 wRC+. The only thing that stands out in a negative way is of course the low BB/K and that comes from the fact that Valencia is a very free swinger, taking cuts at over 54% of the pitches he saw throughout the season. Everything else for a teenage prospect though? .279 AVG, 8 HR, 64 SB, 112 wRC+. Nothing screams '$1 auto'. There are guys who haven't been on a roster in years whose autographs still sell for more than that and this kid is 20. What really stands out though is if you split the stats at the date he was traded and compare them to each other. BB/K - 0.27 with Houston, 0.47 with Miami. Strikeout rate - 24.6% with Houston, 15.6% with Miami. ISO - .093 with Houston, .184 with Miami. wRC+ - 103 with Houston, 141 wRC+ with Miami. On these alone my brain was convinced something had to have changed in the amount he swung but nope almost identical, amount he made contact almost identical, even the BABIP was almost identical. I'm not going to applaud Miami and act like they fixed him immediately since it was only 109 PA but the new regime is built on finding guys who the computer models like and the fact that Scout the Statline's Peak Projections have Valencia as almost a top 200 prospect means they see whatever it is too. With these types of players it could always be nothing and they can fade away quickly but for a kid who at age 19 had 112 mph exit velocities and stole 64 bases it feels like it's worth finding out for $1. There were only four teenage prospects last year with 5+ HR and 50+ SB. Konnor Griffin, Nate George, John Gil, and Esmil Valencia. Obviously nobody is in the Konnor Griffin conversation but what if I told you that Valencia not only hit more homers than Gil and George, but also stole more bases than both of them. That's right the 8+ HR/60+ SB club for teenagers last year was Konnor Griffin with a $800 autograph and Esmil Valencia with a $1 autograph. I don't know why but that was hilarious to me. Again, I'm not going to sit here and say he's going to be a player, but $1 is borderline disrespectful. 

This could literally be it's own article so I'll try to keep it short. I absolutely love the Marlins 3's and it's not surprising since they've made a lot of analytics-based moves lately and I tend to like those. We all know I love

players.name: Thomas White
players.note: White is the prime example of how we can all get ahead by following the updated hobby pitcher rankings throughout the season. When I did them last year I would name a handful of players as "best value buys" based on my ranking versus their price and Thomas White was a recurring guest. May 29th at $17.85. June 5th at $17.66. June 19th at $18.48. July 3rd at $19.44. July 18th at $16.56. Months of him moving up my rankings but his price staying stagnant because he wasn't getting public love. We've come a long ways since then and now everyone seems to be familiar with how nasty he is but even at $52 I still think he's lower than he should be, he is in fact my #1 ranked non-debuted pitcher after all. The 6'5" White was the best left-handed prep pitcher in the 2023 draft class and the Marlins took him 35th overall and gave him a bonus north of $4 million. So far in his development this pick looks like it could pay off because White is filthy. One of the few minor league pitchers who legitimately has three pitches that are 60 grade or better. The fastball can sit high 90's with carry, the slider is absolutely devastating and probably his best pitch, and the changeup he uses against right handed hitters has great fade. All of that was on display last year where between three levels (A+, AA, & AAA) he had a 2.31 ERA, 2.27 FIP, 14.55 K/9, and 5.12 BB/9. I have to admit that this BB/9 is not one I love to see out of a starter and would usually ring the "reliever risk" bell but much like Jacob Misiorowski was when he came up Thomas White might be so nasty that it doesn't even matter. It was a shame to see his walk rate increase from 9.2% in 2024 to 13.6% in 2025 but his K-BB% was still able to go up by 5% thanks to an almost 10% increase in his strikeout rates. He may have allowed more free passes but batting averages against White went from .241 to .172 as his stuff ticked up so much he was nearly unhittable. Unfortunately White strained his oblique in his Spring Training start and is expected to miss three to four weeks. It sucks but honestly he wasn't going to debut the first month of the season anyways in my opinion. If the market starts sleeping and this price comes down while he's hurt I'd be buying up any deals you can because when he comes back he may not be in AAA for very long assuming he's healthy. Of the 539 pitchers who threw 80+ minor league innings last year only 4 struck out more than 36% of the hitters they faced. Trey Yesavage, Jonah Tong, Payton Tolle, and Thomas White. The first three all had moments last year where their 1st base autograph got over $200 because that's exactly what can happen when you get called up and make professional hitters look silly. Thomas White could do the same.

players.name: Robby Snelling
players.note: When Snelling was drafted back in 2022 there were many conflicting reports on him from evaluators, but most people saw him as a mid to back of the rotation arm since his command looked much better than his stuff. He also didn't have your prototypical pitcher build since he was a high school linebacker for the football team he was kind of built like… well, a linebacker. That didn't stop him from firing off about as good of a professional debut as you can as Snelling had a 1.82 ERA, 10.24 K/9, and 2.95 BB/9 as a 19-year-old while being promoted twice and reaching Double-A. He was the only pitching prospect in baseball that year who threw 100+ innings and had a K-BB% over 20% as a teenager. Unfortunately in 2024 he came out and got shelled at that same level with a 6.01 ERA, 8.22 K/9, and 4.05 BB/9. His batting average against jumped from .215 to .304, K% down from 28.4% to 20%, and the walks up from 8.2% to 10% in 16 starts. It was then that the Padres traded him to the Marlins as part of the Tanner Scott deal. Talk about a change of scenery. At the same level he made 7 more starts as a member of the Marlins and in those starts had a 10.25 K/9 versus the 8.22 with San Diego, and a 2.75 BB/9 which had previously been 4.05. His FIP dropped by nearly three runs from 5.50 to 2.76. Now it gets fun. Snelling spent most of the offseason prior to the 2025 season working with Sean McLaughlin at Maven Baseball Lab on improving his arm slot and other mechanical issues. Whatever they found was absolute gold. Last year between AA & AAA, Snelling had a 2.51 ERA, 2.77 FIP, 2.72 xFIP, 10.99 K/9, and 2.58 BB/9. Dominance. The improvements to both the command and repertoire were enormous. His fastball was low 90's during the 2024 season and he was hitting 100 last year. Spin rates on his slider/curve way up. Walks way down. Everything you'd want to see. From 2024 to 2025 alone Snelling improved his K-BB% from 13.8% to 23.2%. Here's a comprehensive list of EVERY pitching prospect age 21 or younger last year who threw 100+ innings with a K% over 30% and BB% under 8%: Robby Snelling. He doesn't have the name recognition that Thomas White has but they're basically neck and neck for me, and though Snelling's base auto looks similarly priced it's not because he's also been pumped up but rather because he was a redemption and his autographs are hard to find. In the last 90 days Thomas White has had 58 copies of his base autograph sell, Robby Snelling has had 4. That's a very important distinction when trying to compare the value of autographs. Also, with the news that White will be sidelined with an oblique injury that makes Snelling now the frontrunner to debut first. When you consider the proximity, improvements, and short supply of his autographs I think he's a great buy if you can find them.

players.name: Kevin Defrank
players.note:
I will preface this by saying that you will almost never EVER hear me say to buy an international pitcher who has yet to throw an inning in the states. And for that reason I personally put off buying Kevin Defrank for a couple of months after 2025 Bowman Chrome came out, but it ended up getting to the point where I truly could not help myself. There was a run for a few years where I swore off Marlins hitting prospects under the old regime because they were basically 0-fer on developing bats but they've never had a problem developing pitchers and when it comes to pitching prospects they're usually one of the first organizations I look at prospects for. It's part of the reason why I was so high on Thomas White early on last year. Defrank's ceiling here is absolutely massive just like he is. As a 6'5" right hander he's extremely athletic on the mound for his size giving him a fairly easy delivery with really good extension. He made his professional debut in the DSL last year and what slowed me originally on buying his cards are that it's not a strong level and the sample was tiny. However, in 10 starts spanning 31 innings Defrank had a 3.19 ERA with a 9.87 K/9 and 2.90 BB/9, striking out 24.1% of the hitters he faced and holding opponents to a 68.7% contact rate. Pretty good right? You usually see high walk rates in the DSL since the instruction isn't nearly as good as what they get when they come to the U.S., but a 7.1% walk rate while facing 141 hitters isn't too shabby. Especially when you consider a couple of things that don't show up in the box scores. 1. Kevin Defrank was 16-years-old in all of those appearances. 2. Kevin Defrank was throwing 100 mph. That's right, Kevin Defrank is a 6'5" 17-year-old who won't turn 18 until August and he already throws 100. While we haven't seen a ton of the offspeed stuff yet, those in the organizations have already raved about how good his 92 mph changeup looks at this stage in his development, and he has a slider/sweeper that could be above average as well. A couple of weeks ago he was throwing live BP against other Marlins prospect and he struck out first round pick Aiva Arquette who hit .354 in college last year. Again, Defrank is 17 and just showed up to the states. Luckily his agent shared the pitch data from the outing and though we only got the numbers for 21 pitches from that session they are nutty. He threw 6 fastballs which had an average velocity of 99.9 and a max of 101.4 with more than 15 inches of induced vertical break. 17-YEARS-OLD?! This is a risky play no doubt because DSL success doesn't always translate but Defrank checks nearly every box you'd want in a hobby pitcher and he landed with a team whose pitching lab in Florida has worked miracles on pitchers who were way less genetically gifted than him. The floor could be $5 but the ceiling could be the #1 pitching prospect in baseball, and for that reason alone I think you have to give it a shot here.

If I'm buying a 3 it's definitely

players.name: Noble Meyer
players.note: the 10th overall pick in the 2023 draft. Big upside here as Meyer potentially has three plus pitches but he's struggled to stay healthy early on in his professional career. The 6'5" righty posted videos of himself earlier this spring throwing bullpens where he was around 98 with the fastball which is a great sign that he's fully healthy entering 2026. Other than health the other issue has been walks, something I hope to see the 21-year-old improve on going forward. Since he was a big hobby name in the past and the Marlins have been great with pitchers I'd be willing to take a chance on him, but the results haven't been good enough (yet) for me to want to pay over $10 for a base auto right now.

players.name: Jesús Made
players.note: is the biggest name in this organization and of course I love him but I'll almost never give a 'buy' to someone with a base autograph over $200 so he's almost automatically a hold. I do think he's worth holding onto though if you have him because when Konnor Griffin and Kevin McGonigle graduate there's a real chance that Made could enter the 2027 season as the #1 prospect in baseball and we've all seen what that can do to your hype during Spring Training.

players.name: Luis Pena
players.note: As with Pratt, this is just a play on my numbers. Pena is my highest ranked non-debuted hitter on the Brewers not named Jesus Made. In my hobby rankings he is currently ranked just one spot behind Walker Jenkins of the Twins whose base autograph is currently selling for $100 more than Pena's. Even when you look at him compared to Made, he may be eight spots back in my overall rankings but does that warrant Made being nearly triple the price? I vote no. Pena entered my rankings when he debuted as a 17-year-old in the DSL in 2024 hitting .393 with 1 HR, 39 SB, 8.2% BB, 8.2% K, .190 ISO, and 177 wRC+. Despite only going deep once that ISO was still able to stay near .200 thanks to Pena's 16 doubles and 6 triples in just 184 PA, making him an extra base machine. When he came to the states last year what immediately shot him up my rankings is that we saw that extra base power turn into home run power really quickly, where in 309 PA in Single-A at age 18 he hit .308 with 6 HR, 41 SB, 9.1% BB, 13.3% K, .161 ISO, and 139 wRC+. Of course he's not thought of as having the same type of power as Jesus Made but he actually hit more HR in 70 fewer PA at this level. Now when they got promoted to High-A Made performed much better and I'm not denying that he is overall the better prospect and hobby prospect, but I don't think the gap is as big as everyone may think. Pena's contact skills are so advanced for his age. 78% at age 17 in the DSL and 79.6% in Single-A at 18. He was the only player age 18 or younger to have 300+ PA in Single-A last year with a strikeout rate under 15% and an ISO over .160. You don't see that combination of bat-to-ball skills and power for a player this young at this level. Do you want to know who the last player was prior to Pena to do that? Vladimir Guerrero Jr. back in 2017. I think that Luis Pena has somewhat been cast in the shadow of Jesus Made because they were in the same signing class and seem to get promoted together but if he continues to produce like this it's only a matter of time before people will have to recognize how ridiculously good he's playing. This should already be over $100 in my opinion.

players.name: Jett Williams
players.note: Jett is a prospect that I've long been a fan of going back to his time in the Mets organization and the Brewers acquired him this offseason in the Freddy Peralta deal. Williams was drafted 14th overall out of high school back in 2022 and signed with the Mets for $3.9 million. Since then he has been one of the most productive minor league hitters as confirmed by his ranking of 13th on the Scout the Statline Peak Projections, higher than any other Brewer on this list. Although he has gotten some hobby love in the past I think what is keeping Jett's cards at this price range is the fact that many people look at a 5'7"-5'8" hitter and assume there's no power. It's actually something I talked about when I interviewed Ryan Sloan of the Mariners and his reason for picking Michael Arroyo as a sleeper in their organization. Don't be fooled by the size some guys can just swing it, and Jett can. Last year at age 21 while seeing time between both AA & AAA, Williams hit .261 with 17 HR, 34 SB, 13.3% BB, 22.9% K, .204 ISO, and 136 wRC+. Say all you want about a "small frame", but an ISO over .200 at the two most advanced levels of the minor leagues at age 21 says there's some power. And he did that while also maintaining a contact rate over 76% and a SwStr% under 10% across both levels. This is such a fun set of hobby tools. His speed is a 60 grade or maybe better and thanks to that and his great instincts he can play a number of positions defensively including shortstop, second base, and center field. I personally think his best fit could be CF but it feels like the Brewers want him on the dirt and love these types of players like Sal Frelick that they can move around. Along with the good hit tool, good power, and fantastic speed, Jett plays the game with the sort of swag that makes him extremely likeable by fans and that can help your card market as well. And I mean the name Jett Williams for a guy who flies around the bases is an 80 grade name. The Brewers are extremely sharp when it comes to prospects (as referenced by how long this list of buys is) and them acquiring a prospect in Williams who I've always been higher on than most makes sense to me as a fit. Last year the only prospects age 21 or younger with 500+ minor league PA, 15+ HR, and 30+ SB were Konnor Griffin, Eduardo Quintero, and Jett Williams. He does everything well and we're almost certainly going to see him make his MLB debut this season so from a hobby standpoint I think there's a lot to like here.

players.name: Cooper Pratt
players.note: Now I admit that I currently own zero Cooper Pratt cards, but if we're trusting the process of following the rankings this price is insanely low for where I have him. Pratt is the highest ranked player in my hitter rankings with a base autograph under $40. After him at 31st the next highest ranked with an autograph price this low is Juneiker Caceres at 36th who I already said would be a 6/5 on the buy rating if I was allowed to do that. Pratt was one of my favorite chases back in 2024 Bowman after the Brewers went and gave him an over slot $1.35 million in the sixth round to pull him away from Ole Miss. The 6'4" right hander made his professional debut in 2024 where he hit .277 with 8 HR, 27 SB, 10.3% BB, 20.0% K, .130 ISO, and 123 wRC+ at age 19 while seeing time between A & A+. What was interesting to me in that season was the difference we saw in splits between A & A+. In Single-A he hit .295 with 3 HR, a .100 ISO, and 0.67 BB/K in 311 PA. After his promotion he hit .221 with 5 HR, a .221 ISO, and 0.17 BB/K in 95 PA. It almost gave me a similar sort of vibe that I felt when we saw Roman Anthony get promoted from A to A+, you have this low power, high average, good approach stat line and then he gets a promotion and his contact metrics move backwards but he starts launching baseballs. Immediately this had me in on Pratt. When a player this young exhibits both of those sets of skills the thought of them eventually working together further down the road in his development gives me a ceiling we can dream on. Last year the Brewers moved Pratt to AA at age 20 where he hit .238 with 8 HR, 31 SB, 12.7% BB, 15.2% K, .110 ISO, and 107 wRC+. Some may look at this batting average and ISO and think he took a step back but there are a few things worth noting. One, and most importantly he was 20 all year in AA which is VERY advanced. He was one of only 6 minor leaguers who got enough PA in AA last year at age 20 or younger to be considered a qualified hitter. Two, despite the low average his contact skills were really good for his age and that level at 78.6%, and his .267 BABIP which was nearly 70 points lower than it was the year prior may be to blame for that average being down. Three, the improvements to his approach. After having a 0.52 BB/K in 2024 that number went up to 0.84 as he increased his walk rate by 2.4% and decreased his strikeout rate by 4.8%. The fact that the power hasn't popped yet is what is keeping this card from trading at over $40 but when you consider the frame on this kid and the fact that he's been playing at advanced levels for his age it's not out of the question to think it's coming. And even if it doesn't the floor might be so good by itself that it should continue to support this price. Pratt has an improved approach, great contact skills, great speed (58 SB last two years), and on top of it all won a Minor League Gold Glove in 2024 for his defense at shortstop. Last year the only players age 20 or younger with 8+ HR, 30+ SB, and a SwStr% under 10% were Eduardo Quintero, Edward Florentino, Josue De Paula, and Cooper Pratt. If that power increases even a little bit this year this card should go boom.

players.name: Brady Ebel
players.note: is a name I was after in 2025 Bowman Draft but I'm a bit surprised that his base autographs have remained this high as we've moved further from release. I still think the upside is really good but until I see him play professionally I would need this at about $20 before I bought anything personally.

players.name: Josh Adamczewski
players.note: Another big winner of ours from the 2025 season is Adamczewski who is up over 200% from his $8 base autograph on last year's sheet. When I started the 'Hot Sheets' last year he was one of the ones early on that I said we've got to go out and buy because the market had not adjusted to how well he was playing to start the year and the production did not look like a fluke. I ended up snagging a true blue auto for $50 back then which I turned around and sold for $100 the day that I got it in the mail because his market started going up that quickly. While we've already talked about players that the Brewers acquired via the first round of the draft, international signing, or trade, Adamczewski was a deep sleeper, selected out of high school in the 15th round back in 2023 and signed for about $250k. Can't say enough about how good this organization is at finding talent for cheap. In Adamczewski's first professional season in 2024 at age 19 he hit .322 with 3 HR, 8 SB, 18.0% BB, 19.7% K, .164 ISO, and 155 wRC+. The season was shortened by injuries and he only played 41 games with 183 PA but hard not to have that 18% walk rate from a teenager catch your eye. Since he didn't get in a full season the Brewers elected to have him start in Single-A again last year where in 206 PA he hit .359 with 5 HR, 4 SB, 14.1% BB, 18.0% K, .210 ISO, and 187 wRC+. That earned him a promotion to High-A but unfortunately he got hurt again and had another season cut short with only 308 PA on the year. That made him a prime candidate to appear in the Arizona Fall League where in 82 PA he batted .277 with 4 HR and a .953 OPS there. The injury plagued seasons may be what's providing somewhat of a discount on these cards because every stat that is calculated as a ratio per PA looks outstanding for Adamczewski. Last year there were only two prospects age 20 or younger who had 300+ PA with an ISO over .170 and batting average over .315: Konnor Griffin and Josh Adamczewski. If you drop the average threshold to .300 in expands the list from two to five. Of those five the only ones with a BB/K over 0.50 are Kevin McGonigle (1.28) and Josh Adamczewski (0.81). It feels like if he can stay healthy it should be pretty easy from him to pick up some steam in 2026 given how little buzz you hear about him in most prospect circles.

players.name: Braylon Payne
players.note: For $20 there are few prospects in baseball who are more fun than Braylon Payne in terms of upside. The Brewers selected Payne 17th overall in the first round of the 2024 draft out of high school and signed him for a shade under $3.5 million. The name of the game here is athleticism, and there may not be a prospect in this entire organization with more of it than Braylon. He absolutely flies and flashes 70 grade run times which gives him the potential to be a terror on the base paths and should allow him to be an above average or possibly even plus defender in center field. Now the question for us, and it's a big one, is the power. While most people are going to chalk this up to a speedy hitter who is built to slap the ball and leg out infield singles, there are a few pieces of compelling evidence that Payne may actually get to average power or better. The first piece is the combine. Rapsodo was tracking exit velocities at the 2024 draft combine and according to their readings Payne had an average EV during his session of 101.8 mph and a Max EV of 109.8. That's serious for a prep bat. Out of every top 100 player in that class the only player they had a higher average or higher max from that year was PJ Morlando who was drafted by the Marlins basically because of his freak-ish power potential. Why did Morlando's BP get a ton of coverage and nobody mentioned Payne's, because Morlando's average launch angle on those batted balls was 23.1 degrees and Payne's was 3.7 degrees. Is he hitting ground balls? Yes, but he is absolutely smashing them. He was young for the class and was drafted at just 17 so he was 18 during his first full season last year where he hit .240 with 8 HR, 31 SB, 15.2% BB, 30.1% K, .142 ISO, and 114 wRC+. Am I alarmed by the strikeout rate? A little bit. But I'm much more encouraged by the power. This is a guy we weren't sure could lift the ball and he went deep 8 times in 342 PA as an 18-year-old, a number that was only beaten by three players his age at that level including Rainiel Rodriguez and Edward Florentino who are in my top 10. The swing still needs improvement, when he gets behind he gets choppy trying to just put balls in play because he knows how fast he is. You can't teach this athleticism though and the Brewers have been crushing it with prospect development so I'm inclined to believe that they can fix his swing path and get him to more HR power. Since he already showed more of it last year than I expected in his debut I think we're trending in the right direction. Oh, and the 6'2" lefty will still only be 19 for most almost all of this season.

players.name: Brock Wilken
players.note: fits in sort of the same bucket as Luke Adams in that he posts extremely productive stat lines analytically because he hits for good power and draws a bunch of walks. Similar to Adams his low batting averages and high strikeout rates often keep people from going to heavily into his cards but I still think he'll be a solid player. However, $20 with a hobby rank of 140th is in the hold territory and since Adams is similarly priced and ranked much higher I'd go that route. The 3 that breaks my heart the most is

players.name: Luke Adams
players.note: You know I couldn't make this list without including my favorite baseball anomaly, Luke Adams. If you enjoy analytics you're sure to love Adams, if you hate them shield your eyes. From a purely analytical standpoint Adams is one of the best hitters in all of the minor leagues over the past few seasons. If you don't believe me check the Scout the Statline Peak Projections and you will see that their model has him as the 17th ranked hitting prospect in baseball. For those who don't know about my love/hate (it's way more love) relationship with Luke Adams here's how it goes. In 2023 at age 19 in Single-A he had a .400 OBP with 11 HR, 30 SB, 17.3% BB, 22.5% K, .168 ISO, and 131 wRC+. His contact rates were 76.8% and his SwStr% was 8.2%. That's a STRONG debut. The following year as a 20-year-old in High-A he had a .443 OBP with 11 HR, 28 SB, 18.7% BB, 21.3% K, .169 ISO, and 153 wRC+. Contact rates that year were 79.3% and the SwStr% was just 6.4%. I mean this is consistent dominance no? Could someone who gets so little recognition possibly do it again?! In 2025 between A+ & AA, Adams had a .417 OBP, 11 HR, 10 SB, 16.5% BB, 20.3% K, .205 ISO, and 157 wRC+ in only 72 games. 78.6% contact rate. 7.1% SwStr%. From a production standpoint I could argue that he's been a top 10 hitter in the minor leagues for three years running. Where is the red flag that causes his base autograph to be $18? You'll notice above that I used OBP on the stat line and that's because Luke Adams' batting averages by year are: .233, .227, .231. Despite having wildly low swinging strike percentages, making good contact, hitting for good power, and walking at a crazy high clip he can't bat over .240. It's fascinating. Even more fascinating is that you'd expect these 7%-ish SwStr% and back-to-back 28+ SB seasons to come from a small contact hitter. Luke Adams is all of 6'4" 235 pounds. He's anomaly in the same way that Emmanuel Rodriguez is and that's that the analytics love power and OBP but the hobby has a hard time committing to guys with such low batting averages. I don't care though. Never have. These players are great whether you agree with the sets of skills they have or not. Adams went to the AFL following this season and in 68 PA hit .333 with 3 HR, as many walks as strikeouts, and a 1.039 OPS. I love a good approach. I love a good ability to make contact. I love power bats. The only players in the minor leagues last year age 21 or younger who had 300+ PA with a BB/K over 0.75, a SwStr% under 8%, and an ISO over .200 were Kevin McGonigle and Luke Adams. Batting average be damned, if there's a world where nobody is impressed by this offensive production it means I'm no longer here.

players.name: Marco Dinges
players.note: Have I mentioned that the Brewers may be the best team around at finding great talent without breaking the bank? Well in the 2024 draft they selected Marco Dinges out of Florida St. in the fourth round and signed him at $500k which was under the slot value. Coming into the draft the scouting reports seemed to be that if you were taking him you were buying the power because there were concerns about his hit tool. There is still a bit of concern there because Dinges takes some huge swings and is often fooled by offspeed pitches, something he will most certainly have to work on going forward. If what we saw in his debut though was any indicator of how successful of a hitter he'll be in the minor leagues then I'm down to get in on the action. In his first full season between A & A+, Dinges hit .300 with 13 HR, 5 SB, 15.5% BB, 19.2% K, .214 ISO, and 161 wRC+. I will say as a disclaimer that anyone who played collegiate ball, especially in the ACC, should be able to hit Single-A pitching and he torched it with a 204 wRC+ in 112 PA. After the move to High-A his production came back down to earth but even then the wRC+ was 137 in 205 PA and the ISO remained above .200 showing that the power is certainly no fluke. Back in college he was considered a bat over defense prospect which can never hurt us in Bowman and many evaluators believed he would move off catcher and possibly to a corner outfield spot. Since the start of his professional development the Brewers have actually liked his improvements behind the plate and will keep him there in the near future. This is a play on the bat though at $15. This franchise just keeps stacking undervalued players in the hobby who at some point will be forced to get recognition if they continue producing the way they have. It will be interesting to see Dinges against that next step up in AA competition since his numbers trended down slightly in the move from A to A+ but at this price point I'd be willing to bet on him based on what we've seen so far. If you throw out rookie level stats the only hitters in the minors last year age 21 or younger who had 300+ PA where they batted .300 with a .200+ ISO were Sal Stewart, Kevin McGonigle, and Marco Dinges. I feel like he should get a little respect for that.

players.name: Jeferson Quero
players.note: who honestly at $13 with a hobby ranking of 70 should be a buy. The only issue is that with hitters you have to have a period of time that you can create buzz and his may be gone. Arguably the best defensive catcher in the minor leagues and I think the bat is sneaky but with William Contreras locked in the Brewers lineup I'm not sure where he fits. A couple of months ago I would have made him a 4 just because it looked pretty obvious that he'd make the Opening Day roster as the backup catcher but now the Brewers have given money to Gary Sanchez to fill that spot. Love the player, love the price, I'm just not sure the path to him gaining steam before he debuts is there anymore. If you want an even deeper sleeper of a dart throw than Eric Bitonti I'd be looking at

players.name: Eric Bitonti
players.note:
Every team needs their low-floor high-ceiling dart throw and for the Brewers it has to be Eric Bitonti. Leading up to the 2023 MLB draft Bitonti put on an absolute clinic during some of his live BP's showcasing his massive power potential as a 6'5" 17-year-old. Milwaukee liked what they saw enough to select Bitonti in the third round and give him $1.75 million which was more than double his slot value. In his first full professional season we saw that huge power on display as he hit .282 with 16 HR, 12 SB, 16.5% BB, 27.9% K, .262 ISO, and 146 wRC+ between the CPX & A. I'm not going to lie to you and tell you there was something fluky about the high strikeout rate because there was not. Bitonti had a 65.4% contact rate that season in which the rest of the stat line looks incredible. As you can imagine players who are 6'5" and have such long levers that generate that kind of power are often very prone to this issue. Lazaro Montes has contact rates this low. Bryce Eldridge has contact rates this low. It's the price you pay for being a power bat with an enormous frame. I asked FanGraphs to give me the last time prior to Bitonti's 2024 season that a minor leaguer had 300+ PA with an ISO over .260 in their age 18 season and it gave me 2008 Mike Stanton as the most recent result. Some of you may know him as Giancarlo. The issue is that the Brewers had Bitonti in Single-A again last year at age 19 and the contact didn't really improve. His average went up from .221 to .238 but his contact rates stayed basically the same (65.4% vs. 65.8%) and his strikeout rate went up from 27.9% to 33.5%. He still had a 117 wRC+ along with 19 HR and 17 SB showing sneaky speed for a player his size which isn't surprising since he was drafted as a shortstop, but I can't say I love that the contact didn't improve. It may be time to just accept that this is who Bitonti is, and honestly for $11 I think that's fine. The only teenage prospects last year with 19+ HR, 17+ SB, and a wRC+ over 115 were Konnor Griffin, Eduardo Quintero, and Eric Bitonti. If the contact were to improve his ceiling would be massive, but I'll also go on record as saying I don't think it matters if it does. You aren't finding any other players with this power potential this cheap. The hobby is notorious for turning a blind eye when it comes to alarming contact or strikeout rates if a guy is hitting long homers. Bitonti is one viral clip on Twitter of him hitting a 450 foot HR away from this card price doubling and I think when you have that going for you you can never really be a bad buy at this price.

Obviously

players.name: Bryce Meccage
players.note: I guess I didn't realize how much I liked Milwaukee's 2024 draft but this makes the third player from this class along with Braylon Payne and Marco Dinges that I'm a fan of buying in Bowman. Meccage has two things about him that pulled me in opposite directions originally. In the wrong direction he's a cold weather pitcher, something that is always tough when it comes to a player's development. Not to get into the science behind it but the track record for prep pitchers who come from cold weather states is not great, and when it is great the time it takes for them to reach their full potential is often longer. That didn't stop the Brewers from giving Meccage $2.5 million in the second round which was nearly $1 million over the slot value. Now what pulls me in a good direction is the bloodline. Kids who grow up around the game and have a dad who was a player or coach is something I love to see because they usually come in with a good baseball IQ, understanding of the game, work ethic, etc. Meccage's dad Jeremy was a 6'4" starting pitcher at Iowa who was drafted by the Dodgers (twice) and went on to coach collegiately. His uncle, Justin, was a 6'5" pitcher at Oklahoma St. who was drafted by the Yankees and currently serves as the pitching coach for the San Francisco Giants. Love that for him. Now what got him drafted. Meccage is a big righty who sat mid-90's as a prep with a really good slider that could grade as a plus pitch. He also throws a curveball and a changeup, but the curveball is much better and serves as the third option. Last year in his professional debut at age 19 he was running that fastball up to 98 mph but wasn't extremely consistent. Making 19 starts at Single-A he had a 4.35 ERA but his 3.67 FIP and 3.82 xFIP were more encouraging along with a 8.83 K/9 and 3.33 BB/9. His delivery gets out of sync at time but the raw tools and ability are really good and I think the longer he is under the instruction of the Brewers system he will only go up. There were some concerns that he could have reliever risk when he was drafted but I would say his 8.9% walk rate over 70.1 innings as a teenager in pro ball is encouraging. He's still only 19-years-old and should start the year in High-A, I think for $7 there's sneaky upside here.

players.name: Shane Drohan
players.note: sighting I can tell you so was I. Not the biggest hobby ceiling since he's now 27-years-old but had one of the sneakiest seasons you didn't hear about last year and is now ranked as a top 100 pitcher by StS. Went 5-1 with a 2.27 ERA and 12.65 K/9 in AAA which is damn good. Should get the call this year so not a bad play at $10. Dart throw time.

players.name: J.D. Thompson
players.note:
I wrote up Thompson in my 2025 Bowman Draft preview and had him in my 'Stash 'Em' category just barely missing my top 12. Considering that he was that close to breaking into that tier I'm pretty surprised that he's already trading this cheap and I even saw an accepted price under $4 on one of his base autographs. It might not be a flashy play but this feels like a great buy. Of course in the hobby we'd prefer the pitchers who are overly physical but sometimes guys just know how to pitch and that's J.D. Thompson. While many of the pitchers we cover in Bowman Draft were relievers turned starters their final season in college, Thompson was a starter in Vanderbilt's rotation in back-to-back years. In 2024 he had a 4.15 ERA, 12.81 K/9, and 3.12 BB/9 before returning in 2025 with a 4.00 ERA, 12.20 K/9, and 3.00 B/9.
