I'm always a fan of checking in on the FIP or xFIP for a pitcher since those often paint a better picture than ERA in terms of how well someone is throwing and in those seasons his were 3.03 and 3.34. Thompson is a smaller lefty but his pitchability is fantastic. With a fastball in the low-90's you wouldn't expect it to grade as an above average offering but it does thanks to fantastic metrics including a great IVB. The secondary pitches are also good with a big sweeping slider, a good curve, and a fading changeup that he utilizes nicely against righties. As I mentioned in my preview most of the reason that we get excited about these big imposing arms throwing 100 mph is because we love the high swing-and-miss rates, but Thompson gets a pretty impressive amount of strikeouts given how his stuff grades out, thanks to it's movement and how well he locates. This is a really safe floor at $6 and I don't see a scenario where he's so bad this year that it goes down, and with some time in this system he could really pop especially if he adds a couple of notches to the velocity. I'm in on J.D. Thompson at $6 all day.

I already wrote up

players.name: Jaron DeBerry
players.note: who was extremely productive in his professional debut last year earning two promotions and reaching Double-A. The stats are good but the whiff numbers aren't crazy and he probably profiles as a command over stuff pitcher. Don't have any issues with buying him he's probably a safe arm at this price but not sure if the ceiling is what I'm looking for.

players.name: Walker Jenkins
players.note: is the big name here for the Twins. Love the player and think he'll be a great major leaguer but once a base autograph gets up towards $200 I'm almost always going to be in hold territory since I'm looking for guys whose prices could 2x in a perfect world.

players.name: Emmanuel Rodriguez
players.note: How fortunate for us that Milwaukee and Minnesota are back-to-back alphabetically because I just told you about the prospect anomaly that is Luke Adams and now I get to talk about his predecessor and creator of the "what am I looking at?" stat line and that's Emmanuel Rodriguez. If you haven't heard my story on how I came to be an E-Rod fan I was at a Twins Single-A game back in 2022. I liked to sit behind the on-deck circle and look players up on the roster by their jersey number, then check their FanGraphs stats to see if they were a player worth keeping an eye on. A then 19-year-old Rodriguez stood in front of me and to that point all I could see for stats was that he hit .214 with a 36.6% strikeout rate at age 18 in the CPX. Not ideal. Later in that game he hit two HRs which are still to this day the loudest batted balls I've ever personally heard live at a minor league game. He was 19. Later as I dove into analytics more I realized that that .215 AVG with 36.6% K line that I was grossed out by actually had a 132 wRC+ and .310 ISO. This started my fascination with his game. Rodriguez has now had 1,283 PA as a minor leaguer, he has walked in 21.7% of those and struck out in 30.3% of them. That's 52% of his career trips to the plate that have ended with him walking to first base or back to the dugout. If you're someone who gets frustrated watching Juan Soto because you feel like he's trying to walk instead of hit, don't watch E-Rod because he's even worse about it, swinging at only about one third of the total pitches he sees. Here's the issue, when he does swing his contact rates aren't good, but when he makes contact the raw power is legit. Now most guys who have big power but struggle to make contact like Spencer Jones see their struggles compounded because they expand out of the zone. Rodriguez doesn't do that. He may be in the 9th percentile for in-zone contact rates but he's also in the 96th percentile for chase rate. With that extremely strange split also comes a 98th percentile 90th% EV. Rodriguez tattoos baseballs. In 2024 his season was shortened by injuries but he got 200+ PA between AA & AAA. In those he had a .287 ISO, .459 OBP, and 180 wRC+ at age 21. FanGraphs has minor league stats back to 2006 and the only player ever at age 21 or younger to have 200+ PA above rookie levels in a season with an ISO over .280 and OBP over .450 was Emmanuel Rodriguez. Along with the great raw power E-Rod has good speed too and plays flashy defense in CF which adds another element of excitement to his game. Nobody is quite sure how to feel about his wonky stat lines but if you like analytics here are his career wRC+ marks by year: 132, 197, 147, 180, 135. Scout the Statline has him as their 8th best hitting prospect when it comes to projecting major league production. If not for injuries he probably would have debuted last year and given their lack of outfield depth and the fact that he's already on the 40-man roster I wouldn't be surprised if he's an Opening Day starter for the Twins. He's always been strange, but because of the loud tools and proximity to the MLB I still think he has a great chance to make some more noise.

players.name: Kaelen Culpepper
players.note: When 2024 Bowman Draft came out I admit that Culpepper was not a player that I was extremely high on. He was taken in the first round out of Kansas St. at pick 21 and signed for just shy of $4 million. Culpepper was extremely consistent in college hitting .325 and .328 with wRC+'s of 126 and 127 his last two years. He had a good approach and made good contact to all fields but despite his great bat speed his power never really popped. Even during the draft process there were evaluators who said that a good scenario for him would be getting to 12-15 HR power. Though his professional debut in his draft year wasn't a huge sample he hit 3 HR in 112 PA with a strikeout rate under 14% and I kinda thought yeah, this is who I expected. But then something beautiful happened. Last year Culpepper hit 20 HR in 113 games. Now I'm interested. When you look at the contact rates they slipped a little bit but were still fine. His strikeout rate went up from 13.4% to 17.4% and his overall contact rates dropped from 82.1% to 76.8%. Of course I'm never rooting for a player's contact skills to go down but when you're a guy with great bat-to-ball skills and average power, I am always in favor of sacrificing some of it for more power because ultimately it is much better for your cards. Culpepper finished the year hitting .289 with 20 HR, 25 SB, 9.7% BB, 17.4% K, .181 ISO, and 138 wRC+ between A+ & AA. He had shown a good approach, good contact ability, good speed, and good defense, the only thing we really hadn't seen from Culpepper prior to 2025 was the ability to hit 20+ HR and then he did it. This is all of the sudden a package of tools that I'm very interested in. Last year there were only five players age 22 or younger that had 20+ HR and 25+ SB in the minors. Culpepper had the lowest strikeout percentage on that list by more than 3%. The two highest batting averages in that group? Konnor Griffin and Kaelen Culpepper. I may have had him pegged as kind of a boring hobby play back in 2024 Bowman Draft but with the increase in power he's shot way up my rankings and is now inside my top 50 non-debuted hitters. After Walker Jenkins he's the second highest ranked Twins prospect by MLB Pipeline on their updated team top 30. He should have plenty of opportunities to see his hobby stock rise even further this year and given the state of their major league roster I wouldn't say that him playing well enough to debut later in the season is impossible either.

players.name: Gabriel Gonzalez
players.note: had a fantastic year and he's a player I really like in real life. Should debut this year, does everything right. My issue with him has always been the tools. He's a really good hitter. He makes great contact and should continue to hit for a good average, but both of the power and speed are close to average. His base auto price started last year under $10 and even if it had doubled to $20 after his great year I'd probably give him a buy, but without a ton of power or speed I'm not in love with the upside of a $30 base auto.

players.name: Eduardo Tait
players.note: Tait came over from the Phillies last year in the Jhoan Duran trade and he's a left handed hitting catcher with an extremely strong arm and massive power projections. Philadelphia signed him out of Panama for only $90,000 and he immediately turned heads in his DSL debut in 2023 for his big exit velocities. Tait presents one of the most difficult questions when it comes to choosing players in Bowman: 'would you rather have great power or a great approach?'. I'm going to give you the bad first. Last year he had a 0.36 BB/K and the reason that he rarely draws walks is because he swung at more than 55% of the pitches he saw. He's extremely aggressive and last year he had a chase rate on pitches outside of the strike zone that was over 40%. The weird part is that he actually doesn't have a problem making contact (for now) and has regularly had contact rates around 78% and strikeout rates around 20%, neither of which really worry me. What worries me is that when you're that aggressive eventually you're likely to run into better pitching that will expose you. You can swing at every pitch at the lower levels and be good enough to put balls in play but if you get to the upper levels swinging nearly 60% of the time the pitchers will eat you up. I know that all sounded bad but I had to give the warnings before I give the good, and boy is it good. Eduardo Tait was playing in High-A at age 18 last year. He was one of only two prospects who got 150+ PA at that level, the other being Leo De Vries. I've always given a huge bump to younger kids playing at advanced levels and/or showing power early on and Tait more than excels at both of those. In 2024 at age 17, he hit .302 with a .184 ISO and 126 wRC+ between CPX & A. If you only look at the at-bats in Single-A he had a .192 ISO in 114 PA. The only age 17 players that year with 100+ PA in Single-A and an ISO over .190 were Leo De Vries and Eduardo Tait. Last year he started the year in A again but was promoted to A+ prior to the trade to Minnesota and stayed there afterwards. On the season he hit .253 with 14 HR and a .174 ISO. There were only three player last year who got 100+ PA in High-A at age 18 and had an ISO over .150. Jesus Made, Leo De Vries, and Eduardo Tait. Anytime you keep ending up on lists this short in consecutive years with Leo De Vries you're doing something right. At some point his approach will need an adjustment to help him be more patient but this is 70 grade power on a prospect who is still a teenager at $30. On that alone I'm in.

players.name: Quentin Young
players.note: is someone I talked quite a bit about in my 2025 Bowman Draft preview. If you want to hold a dart throw for the Twins he's 100% it. HUGE power projections for a prep shortstop which creates a massive hobby ceiling, but the hit tool really scares me. The issue here is that waiting to see if his contact is good this year runs the risk of this price going crazy before you have time to buy, but I'm not confident enough in the contact to go in yet. Can't blame anyone who wants to go for it though!

players.name: Hendry Mendez
players.note:
Another bat that the Twins acquired via trade last year was Hendry Mendez who they got from Philadelphia in exchange for Harrison Bader. You'll notice that the sheet above says that Mendez was a $2 base autograph entering last year and that's not a typo, he's been slept on for forever and I have always been a fan of his bat. Here's what's changed. Back in 2024 Mendez hit .284 with 3 HR, 3 SB, 13.9% BB, 13.9% K, .107 ISO, and 130 wRC+ in High-A at age 20. Along with having as many walks as strikeouts he had an 82.8% contact rate and 7.8% swinging strike %. My issue with Mendez from a hobby standpoint was that despite having incredible bat-to-ball skills and approach he didn't offer much power or speed. Tough to get the people going with 3 HR and 3 SB over 90 games. This past year everything, and I mean everything, went up for Mendez. Between A+ & AA he hit .299 with 11 HR, 10 SB, 13.6% BB, 13.2% K, .140 ISO, and 138 wRC+. While more than tripling both his HR and SB outputs, he raised his ISO by over 30 points, his contact rates went up from 82.8% to 86%, and his SwStr% dropped from 7.8% to 5.9%. This is a crazy impressive stat line for a prospect who gets virtually zero recognition. Here's a list of every prospect last year age 21 or younger who had 300+ PA with more walks than strikeouts, 10+ HR and 10+ SB: Kevin McGonigle, Max Clark, Hendry Mendez. That's it. He's always been a great hitter who controls the zone well but what changed most for him was the ability to drive the ball in the air. He still needs some work in that area but from 2024 to 2025 he improved his GB/FB from 3.08 to 2.40, his ground ball rate from 60.4% to 54%, and his HR/FB from 5.9% to 14.1%. It was his first time as a professional having a ground ball rate under 60% and we saw that raw power that was being used for hard ground balls start lifting balls out of the park. If he were to improve this again for 2026 I think he could big a helium name. I tweeted out a comparison yesterday of two players with very similar approach and contact skills last year but very different autograph prices.

Player A is Sam Antonacci who we know I love, and Player B is Hendry Mendez. Antonacci has more speed with his 48 SB last year but his power was quite a bit lower, hitting half as many HRs as Mendez. Both played at the same levels and Mendez is a year younger. The reason I've always loved Antonacci is that when you're that good of a hitter and not hitting HR's nobody pays attention to your stats, but all it takes is a few HR's for people to be like, "wow I didn't realize he was this good", which is exactly what has happened to Antonacci this spring and has caused his base autograph price to go from $19 when I did the White Sox buy sheet a few weeks ago to now $54 on average. Mendez might not have the speed, but he's got better raw power, he's a year younger, oh, and he's 6'3". Antonacci finally got the buzz we've been waiting for. Hendry Mendez could be one more small swing adjustment away from having the same happen to him.

players.name: Brandon Winokur
players.note: It's hard for me to give a strong buy rating to a player coming off a disappointing year but I am willing to go out on a limb and say that Brandon Winokur has the best combination of tools and athleticism that you'll find for $6 at any minor league level. So much so that I could make the argument for him being a 5/5 based on his ceiling versus this entry price, especially considering him and Mendez are ranked back-to-back and he's a little more than half of the price. Minnesota took Winokur in the third round back in 2023 and signed him for $1.5 million which was second round money and the same amount that they gave to Luke Keaschall in that round before him. Entering the draft Winokur was described as a unicorn because he's 6'6" with plus power, plus speed, and possibly even plus defense at shortstop. He's literally a freak athlete and I tell you this as someone who saw him play live quite frequently in 2024. The issue of course is that you can have four plus tools but if the one you're missing is the ability to make contact it's tough to make it anywhere. And usually I avoid those types of players but that's because their loud tools lead to inflated prices, but at $6 you almost have to take a stab here for the ceiling. I already mentioned the bad. Approach and contact both. He had a 0.30 BB/K and 63.4% contact rate in 2024 followed by a 0.34 BB/K and 67.8% contact rate last year. Not good. However, in 2024 he went 14 HR/23 SB with a .185 ISO in just 94 Single-A games at age 19, making him one of only two prospects to hit those marks at any level for that age. Last year in High-A he played a full season and went 17 HR/26 SB making him one of only three minor leaguers to hit those marks at age 20 or younger. Ready for the other two? Konnor Griffin and Eduardo Quintero. Pretty good company. I'm not going to pretend like they were comparable seasons since they both cleared Winokur by 50+ in wRC+, the point is that as they always say you can't teach size and speed, and he has plenty of both. This is going to sound crazy but I don't think Winokur's tools are all that different from Spencer Jones's and Winokur is a legit defender at a few different positions including shortstop and center field. We act like Spencer Jones deserves a $300 autograph because you don't see many guys with 30/30 potential who are 6'6" but the Twins have one who is nearly four years younger trading at $6. It could be a long road developmentally and there's absolutely a chance that it never all clicks, but for this cheap you almost have to find out.

players.name: Eduardo Beltre
players.note: is definitely the most tempting of the 3's for me and honestly with a hobby ranking near 250 and base autograph around $5 the case can be made for him to be a 4/5. Great power/speed combo for a teenage prospect and in his DSL debut he burst onto some radars when he hit .326 with 11 HR, 10 SB, .292 ISO, and 177 wRC+ in 43 games in 2024. Last year in the states he hit .186 with a .140 ISO and 84 wRC+ and saw his autos drop from $22 to $6. The tools are really good and I think he is a sneaky buy low candidate for a bounce back, but I was burned by Yasser Mercedes so I'm reluctant to jump into a tools-y international guy since the Twins track record with those types of guys hasn't been the best recently. Love the tools for $6 though. Similar to Beltre, I had

players.name: Kyle DeBarge
players.note: bordering between 3 and 4 and like him for very different reasons. Great hit tool, fantastic speed (66 SB last year), and great defense (MiLB Gold Glove winner at 2B), but not a ton of power. Still a really fun hold for $5 because he's an extremely exciting player and his 8 HR last year were actually more than I expected out of him. I have a few autos of his personally that I'm holding but this one would hinge on the power and it's almost certainly below average. Still fun. One of my "eye test" picks is

players.name: Enrique Jimenez
players.note: who came over from the Tigers last year. He got 102 PA in Single-A with the Twins and he looked legit when I saw him. Hit 6 HR with a .282 ISO, 22.5% BB, and 172 wRC+. He's a short and stocky catcher so no surprise his cards are cheap but he's someone to keep an eye on in 2026 to see if the improvements we saw in A were real because he looked like one of their best hitters for over a month when I was there. After that my favorite sleeper 3's for the price are probably

players.name: Kendry Rojas
players.note: Yet another trade target of the Twins in 2025, they acquired Rojas from the Blue Jays at the deadline and he's a 6'2" lefty with good stuff. He has a mid-90's fastball with good life along with a slider, splitter, and changeup that all have the makings of being above average pitches. Although his prices have started to creep up this spring it feels like a good buy low spot here getting a solid arm coming off somewhat of a rough ending to last year. Rojas has had a string of injuries including a shoulder in 2024 that caused him to miss some time. Despite that he was able to make 11 appearances in High-A where he had a 2.43 ERA, 9.86 K/9, and 1.94 BB/9. He was one of only four pitchers that year in the minor leagues who at age 21 or younger threw 60+ innings with a K-BB% over 21% and a walk rate of 5.5% or lower. He missed the start of last year with an abdominal strain and when he was finished rehabbing the Blue Jays assigned him to Double-A. He made a grand total of four starts at that level before they promoted him to Triple-A and that's because in those starts Rojas had a 1.79 FIP, 1.08 xFIP, 14.46 K/9, and 0.96 BB/9. In 18.2 innings he faced the Double-A squads for the Red Sox, Yankees, Mets, and Rockies, all of whom have legit bats, and struck out 30 of the 75 batters he faced while walking only 2 of them. Filthy. Here's where it gets weird. Rojas is promoted to AAA, makes one start, and is traded to the Twins. The Twins kept him in AAA and in 8 starts over 27.1 innings he had a 6.59 ERA, 9.22 K/9, and 7.57 BB/9. He could not find the zone. Now Rojas was pretty outspoken about the fact that they use a different ball in AAA and for whatever reason he could not figure it out and it was messing up the spin on all of his pitches causing him to get erratic. I was interested to see how he looked this year after an offseason to get it right. It's a tiny sample but he's looked like his old self again so far this spring, striking out seven and walking only one in 6.2 innings. I sat front row when he threw against the Braves starters and watched him go 6-up 6-down against Ozzie Albies, Michael Harris, etc. while striking out Austin Riley on a nasty changeup down and away and throwing Ronald Acuna Jr. a 3-2 slider that he swung through. He also topped 98 a couple of times. I know people are down on him because no way around it the AAA numbers were bad, but it seems like there were some external factors at play. I thought he looked phenomenal when I saw him and this winter the Twins moved him to their 40-man roster. We should see him get his shot this season.

players.name: Charlee Soto
players.note: Soto is pretty easily my favorite buy in this entire organization. I would argue that he may have one of the best ceilings of any pitching prospect with an autograph around $10. All he has to do is stay healthy which has been the only issue so far in his professional career. The Twins selected Soto out of high school at pick 34 overall in the 2023 draft and signed him for $2.48 million. He's pretty much the youngest you can be for a draft class without reclassifying because his birthday is August 31st which is the last day of the cutoff for most schools here. That means that he was still 17 when the Twins called his named in July of 2023. As I mentioned, since the Twins facilities are nearby not only do I see their Single-A players often but I also see players like Walker Jenkins and Charlee Soto when they're down here rehabbing their injuries. Soto blew me away the first time I watched him live as an 18-year-old. This stuff is really, really good. He throws both a 4-seam and 2-seam fastball, a slider, and a changeup, and I think all of them have a legit chance of being 55-60 grade the way they move. If you love velocity it was reported by those around the team that early in camp Soto was throwing 95-96 mph while supposedly only going at about 80% effort. Aside from the age and the velocity another thing I like about Soto is that there aren't many miles on his arm, not only has he had a couple of shortened seasons in the minors but he also barely pitched in high school. This is still all pretty new to him. In his pro debut at 18 he had a 5.23 ERA but the 3.88 FIP and 3.60 xFIP were much more encouraging, with a 10.58 K/9 and 4.01 BB/9. Single-A hitters had a 68.8% contact rate against him and he was four years younger than his average competitor at that level. He was primed for a breakout year last year but after only three starts in High-A he was shut down with what they thought was just a triceps strain. In those starts he had a 1.38 ERA, surrendering 2 ER in 13 innings with 15 strikeouts (28.3% K) and only 4 walks (7.5% BB) while topping at 101 mph on the radar gun. During his rehab it turned out that he actually had bone spurs in his elbow which required a surgery and stopped him from coming back. While this sounds like an injury ridden career none of them have actually been very serious and he should be 100% healthy entering this season. It almost feels like there's some prospect fatigue here but since he was so young for his class Soto is still only 20, and will be for this entire season, where we could likely see him end up in Double-A if he remains healthy. When it comes to buying pitchers in the Bowman the dream ceiling is a young, big frame, that throws 100 mph with good secondary pitches and solid command. It's why people are enamored with Marlins pitcher Kevin Defrank. And while I admit that I am too, I actually have Soto ranked a couple of spots higher and he's nearly half the price. We can never assume health but if he makes it through the full season Charlee Soto has a chance to be one of the biggest risers of any prospect in baseball this year in my opinion.

players.name: Riley Quick
players.note: Quick was selected by Minnesota with the 34th overall pick in last year's draft and signed for $2.69 million. In my 2025 Bowman Draft preview I was pretty aggressive with Quick and ranked him as my 11th favorite pitcher in the entire product. Given that his autograph is already $7 it feels as though that should make him an easy buy and stash for me. Quick is a 6'6" 255 pound righty that is built like an offensive lineman, which is fitting considering he was an offensive line recruit as a football player when he was in high school. He opted to go the baseball route and as a freshman coming out of the bullpen at Alabama he had a 3.86 ERA and 10.64 K/9. Good. But his FIP was 4.70 and his BB/9 was 8.59. Bad. The following year he had a spot lined up in the rotation but in his first collegiate start he blew out his elbow after only three innings and had to get Tommy John. It was a pretty quick (no pun intended) turnaround from a torn UCL as Quick was available at the start of the following season for 2025. He made 14 starts last year where he went 8-3 with a 3.92 ERA, 3.49 FIP, 10.16 K/9, and 3.48 BB/9. Less than a year removed from TJ and he dropped his walk rate from 18.9% the last time we saw him fully in 2023 to 8.9% last year. Velocity is not an issue here as Quick's best pitch is maybe his sinking fastball which he throws 99 mph. He also throws a 95 mph cutter, a wipeout slider with great two plane break, and an upper-80's changeup which has flashed as a plus offering at times as well. Despite having stuff that grades off the charts I wouldn't say he missed as many bats as I expected in college and that could be because although his walk rates improved his control was better than his command. He also threw a lot of fastballs, more than 50% of the time. Already in spring workouts the Twins have been working with him on his fastball usage, mixing when he throws the 4-seam and when he throws the sinker, along with getting him to use his nasty secondary pitches more. I think this is a fantastic upside play. He has the frame. He has the stuff. But he threw less than 90 innings total in his three college seasons. With some professional instruction this could end up being a legit arm. I think people may be sleeping on this pick by the Twins.

players.name: Andrew Morris
players.note: both have had productive minor league careers and it's hard to hate either of them at around $5 given that both should debut this year but Raya has struggled with walks and will almost certainly be a reliever at this point. I prefer Morris a bit more and think he could be a sold back of the rotation arm but he's profiled as more of a command pitcher in his few minor league seasons and hasn't shown much of an ability to miss bats so he's not super exciting to me.

players.name: Carson Benge
players.note: is a great player but as I mentioned with Walker Jenkins in yesterday's Twins article, I'm hardly ever buying an autograph this high especially since I feel pretty confident that Benge will be an Opening Day starter. That leaves a pretty small window for buying this and then trying to sell when that news comes and even then you're probably looking at a $50-ish gain. Not sure it's worth it now. Keep holding if you have him though.

players.name: A.J. Ewing
players.note: is a player I liked a lot last year and got some really cheap stuff of and he's now up over 1,000% which is wild. He's now priced pretty appropriately for where I have him ranked and though he might be more exciting than Reimer overall because of his speed (70 SB last year), Reimer's power ceiling is much higher. I have them almost as equal in terms of hobby upside and it's not that I hate Ewing as a buy here it's just that Reimer is $10 cheaper.

players.name: Jacob Reimer
players.note: Although I said that Ryan Clifford shouldn't be cheaper than Jacob Reimer in my opinion, that was much more an endorsement of Clifford than a slight of Reimer because I love this guy too. His price is now up 650% since he was on last year's sheet as a $6 base autograph. Crazy. I've been a supporter for a while and mentioned him in multiple articles last year as a buy including ranking him second behind Caleb Bonemer (CHW) on my 'Top 10 High Upside Buys Under $20' article last July. Safe to say both of those went up. Reimer is an extremely well-rounded hitter and what kept him from blowing up prior to last year is that we hadn't seen much of him. Back in 2023 at age 19 he reached High-A and finished the year with a 121 wRC+, showing a good approach and contact skills but not a ton of power. Then he missed almost all of 2024 and only logged 95 PA where he failed to go deep. Whether it was rust or something else, whatever it may have been was fixed when he showed up in 2025 and he looked noticeably stronger. We saw that good approach and contact we had seen from him as a teenager now be paired with above average power and he took off. Starting in High-A he hit .284 with 8 HR, a .218 ISO, and 163 wRC+ in 61 games while playing in Brooklyn which is not a hitter friendly environment at all. The Mets then promoted him to Double-A where he played the exact same amount of games (61) and the results did not suffer. Combined between both levels Reimer hit .282 last year with 17 HR, 15 SB, 11.1% BB, 21.5% K, .209 ISO, and 157 wRC+. I mentioned how well-rounded of a hitter he is. Throwing out rookie level stats there were four prospects age 21 or younger last year who hit .280 or better with 15+ HR, 15+ SB, and had a wRC+ over 150. They were Konnor Griffin, Sal Stewart, Eduardo Quintero, and Jacob Reimer. This year Reimer should see plenty of time in AAA Syracuse which according to Baseball America's Park Factors from last year is the only Mets minor league park at any level that is more hitter friendly than pitcher friendly. I think this could be a big year for him and with Benge likely to graduate and Clifford having a shot to debut, he could be the next Mets hitting prospect we see get pumped up as he gets closer to the league.

players.name: Ryan Clifford
players.note: Sometimes you have to trust the numbers and the fact is that Ryan Clifford is pretty easily my highest ranked non-debuted hitter with a base autograph under $40. For context I currently have him ranked one spot ahead of Bryce Rainer (DET) who has an average base autograph currently at $97. I can't say that Clifford gets NO love because his price is up 50% from last year but when you see him surrounded by guys like A.J. Ewing and Jacob Reimer who went up over 500% it feels wrong to me that Clifford is still cheaper than both of them. I have him ranked only five spots behind teammate Carson Benge whose base autograph is more than quadruple the price. When MLB Pipeline updates their top 100 prospects the first thing I do is look at who my highest ranked prospects are that didn't make the cut for them, and this year it's Clifford by a very comfortable margin. The Astros took him as an 11th rounder out of high school back in 2022 and it proved to be a great find by them but they ended up sending him over to the Mets in the trade that sent Justin Verlander to Houston. I can remember this trade happening in 2023 and both MLB and ESPN covering it as "Mets acquire Astros #1 prospect Drew Gilbert" and thinking… Drew Gilbert is not the piece they're after, Ryan Clifford is. He's a 6'3" power hitter who splits time between first base and corner outfield and to be honest I think I know the reason why he might be slept on in Bowman and it's because his approach isn't that different from Emmanuel Rodriguez's and it baffles people. He hits for low average, walks a lot, strikes out a lot, but has great power. Here's the difference, Clifford makes much better contact than E-Rod when he swings, with a 74.9% contact rate last year and an in-zone contact rate of 88.4% in AAA. Yes he's selective, yes he's going to strikeout, but having this kind of power while being a Mets prospect should be the hobby dream. Last year between AA & AAA at age 21, Clifford hit .237 with a .356 OBP, 29 HR, 7 SB, 14.7% BB, 25.6% K, .233 ISO, and 137 wRC+. His wRC+ the last three years: 130, 135, 137. His ISO the last three years: .217, .193, .233. This is how you become the 11th ranked hitting prospect in all of baseball by Scout the Statline's Peak Projections. This is unreal production. There were ten prospects in baseball last year age 21 or younger who had 300+ PA with a wRC+ over 135 and ISO over .230. Basallo, McGonigle, Montes, etc. etc. Every single player on the list has a more expensive base autograph than Clifford. Only two of the ten reached AAA: Samuel Basallo and Ryan Clifford. Aside from that only two hitters at all age 21 or younger hit 28+ minor league homers last year: Laz Montes and Ryan Clifford. When you look at their standard stats next to each other (AVG, OBP, RBI, etc.) they are almost mirror images. Except Clifford's walk rate is higher, his strikeout rate is lower, his contact rates are more than 10% higher, and his SwStr% is 7% better. AND he plays for a top 3 hobby franchise. Yet Montes often sells for double the price. Considering how much the market overreacts to Mets prospects when they play well this one boggles my mind. Maybe it's the lack of love from MLB's rankings but from a purely hobby standpoint Ryan Clifford is the best hitting prospect on the Mets not named Carson Benge. I'd go so far as to say I would personally take him over Spencer Jones in a one-for-one trade. One of their prices is not like the other.

players.name: Mitch Voit
players.note: is a player I felt I was higher on than most when 2025 Bowman Draft rankings came out but even then I'm a bit surprised his base autograph is staying at $20. Great breakout pick for this year but I need to see more and based on where I currently have him ranked that's usually where I'm looking for $10-ish autos. If I have to give my personal dark horse pick to climb the charts in this organization this year it's

players.name: Eli Serrano III
players.note: You don't see many guys who are 6'5" and hit over power, but that's kind of how he's profiled so far in his career. With his frame though I wouldn't be surprised if he ended up with more power than we expect and he's already shown some of it on the back fields this spring. Definitely a name to be watching.

players.name: Edward Lantigua
players.note: Buying a player who is not on a single top 400 prospect list or in the team's top 30 by MLB Pipeline? Sign me up. It's not like I would ever do that with a player whose autograph was over $10 but at $6 I am actually very, very intrigued by the upside of Edward Lantigua and I can tell you that personally he is the Mets prospect that I own the most cards of. In that "Top 10 High Upside Buys Under $20" article last July I gave a handful of names whose stock has exploded since then including Caleb Bonemer, Jacob Reimer, Ralphy Velazquez, Joshua Baez, and Aron Estrada. Lantigua was the last player I wrote up as sort of a deep cut so why not him next? One of the major differences is that all of the other guys had more time to see their card values go up in the second half of the season while Lantigua who was playing in the CPX hasn't played a game since, so there hasn't been any way to create buzz. He's a 19-year-old outfielder with a wiry 6'1" frame that should add more muscle as he matures, in fact many of the international scouts said that due to his projectable frame his power might end up being his best offensive tool. Last year he was an All-Star selection in the FCL and finished the year batting .288 with 3 HR, 13 SB, 17.0% BB, 14.9% K, .111 ISO, and 144 wRC+ at 18. We all know I love to see more walks than strikeouts as a teenager but it's not just that, he made some pretty drastic improvements after his debut season. In the DSL at 17 he hit .263 with an 11.1% BB, 19.6% K, 56.5% contact rate, and 25.6% SwStr%. Last year in his first year in the states his contact rate went up to 71.7% (+15.2%), SwStr% dropped to 12.1% (-13.5%), and he improved his BB/K from 0.57 to 1.14. Talk about a way to get on my radar. As a disclaimer DSL contact rates are consistently inconsistent so we have to take them with a grain of salt, but that approach improvement was very real, with about a 6% increase in walks and an almost 5% decrease in strikeouts. Though he only hit 3 HR last year he's not anywhere near being physically maxed out and after failing to go deep in his first 184 PA in the CPX he hit all 3 of those homers in the final two weeks, including in back-to-back games to end the season. This feels like quite a few boxes I like to see checked when predicting a breakout. Scouts see future power but it hasn't shown up yet, massive approach and contact improvements from age 17 to age 18 season, playing for a franchise whose fans will make your card go up 500% if you show any signs of promise. Count me in.

players.name: Jonathan Santucci
players.note: In the second round of the 2024 MLB draft the Mets took Santucci a LHP out of Duke and signed him for a little over $2 million. Though he battled through some injuries in college what we saw for the most part in three seasons was really good strikeout stuff but not the best command. In 2024 he had a 3.41 ERA, 3.06 FIP, 13.97 K/9, and 5.59 BB/9, and despite striking out 35% of the hitters he faced the fact that he also walked 14% of them probably slid him out of the first round. He usually sits in the low-to-mid-90's but can run it up to 97 and he does so with a really high arm slot and carry that makes it really tough to hit. His best pitch though is his slider which feels pretty easily 60 grade. Not only are the spin rates and two plane break both really good but the tunneling on these two pitches is what makes the slider so untouchable. Maybe one day Santucci will be a big enough name for the Pitching Ninja to do one of his overlays because it's impressive how late that slider looks like a fastball before it snaps off. He also has a changeup as a third offering but it's been nothing more than average and he features the other two much more. What really vaulted Santucci up the rankings though is the improvement to the command as a professional. After posting that 14% walk rate his final year at Duke he walked only 8.5% of hitters last season, dropping his BB/9 by nearly 2.5 walks per game. After his promotion from A+ to AA he was fantastic going 4-0 in 10 starts with a 2.52 ERA. All together across both levels he had a 3.06 ERA, 2.98 xFIP, 10.56 K/9, and 3.14 BB/9 over 117.2 innings while holding hitters to a 66.4% contact rate against him. Hell of a professional debut. Among all pitchers last year age 22 or younger who threw 100+ minor league innings only two had a K-BB% over 20% and induced a swinging strike rate over 16%. They were both Mets. Jonah Tong and Jonathan Santucci. Considering that we usually see the price tag on Mets prospects go crazy this feels pretty reasonably priced since he's inside my top 35 pitchers and all. We've seen how cracking MLB Pipeline's top 100 prospects can cause a price hike with these fans. I wouldn't be surprised if he makes his first appearance there this year.

players.name: Zach Thornton
players.note: really borders on being a 4/5 but usually outside of top 100 for pitchers is the under $10 auto range for me when I'm buying, but he's close and he'll probably get there pretty quickly if he keeps pitching the way he has. One of the best command pitchers in the minors gives him a really safe floor as he'll almost definitely make it to the MLB at some point as a back end of the rotation arm. Has a really good pitch mix but nothing grades higher than average really and he often sits in the low-90's which isn't super exciting for cards. You can't argue with results though and last year Thornton had a 1.98 ERA, 9.66 K/9, and 1.36 BB/9 between A+ & AA. Saw huge improvements to the whiff rates from 2024 to 2025, if he were to do that again and maybe add a touch more velocity his stock could move quickly in 2026 so he's a name to watch early on.

players.name: Peter Kussow
players.note: was one of my favorite high school pitcher sleepers in 2025 Bowman Draft. 6'5" righty who tops 97, tons of spin on the slider and creates great extension. Dominant in high school but the track record for cold weather prep arms is not fantastic. The Mets have done as good of a job as anybody developing pitchers lately so I lean towards this being a good stash, but since it could take some time with him his price at over $10 isn't screaming my name yet.

players.name: George Lombard Jr.
players.note: was a nice buy but this is the second year in a row that he's shown up in a big way during Spring Training and seen his cards get pumped. He's a great player but with a $140+ base auto I'd need him to be in my top 10 to even consider him as a buy and while he's good, I don't think he's that good.

players.name: Dax Kilby
players.note: I'm almost always going into the Yankees sheet with the understanding that nobody who is a solid name is going to be a buy but if I'm being honest I think the market may be sleeping on Dax Kilby? Which feels borderline impossible since he is a prep shortstop from the newest Bowman product and was a top 3 chase in it for most people. For those who are new I always put as a disclaimer to take the hobby rankings for players from new draft classes with a grain of salt because the performance portion of the rankings can move pretty drastically when a player has a limited number of plate appearances. He's currently ranked as a top 50 prospect in that area but since it's only been 81 PA it could slide pretty far as he accumulates at-bats if he were to struggle. Even then I think there's value in this price. We've seen how this fanbase overreacts to prospects. Anthony Volpe was once one of the hottest hobby names. Now with how well he's playing in Spring Training for the second year in a row we've seen George Lombard Jr.'s base autos get back up to the $150 range. Here's the thing. I like Kilby more than Lombard. In the real world Lombard might be a better overall prospect because of his defense, but even in the less than 100 PA I've seen of Kilby professionally I'd take his bat. The 6'2" first round pick was considered to be one of the most polished hitters in last year's prep class and he excelled when it came to facing the top competition on circuits. There's some disagreement on his projected tools but right now I'd put him at above average hit, above average speed, and average power. If that power also got to 55 as he matured you're talking about a potential Bowman monster with that combination of offensive tools and the fact that he's wearing pinstripes. I mentioned it was only an 81 PA debut but it was in Single-A at age 18 where he hit .353 with a .457 OBP and 159 wRC+ while going 16 for 17 on stolen base attempts. He had a 16.0% walk rate, 13.6% strikeout rate, 86.9% contact rate, and a miniscule 4.5% swinging strike rate. I'd like to see 200 PA before I stamped this as a great draft pick but that's a pretty ridiculous debut. Of the 33 prospects who got 80+ PA in Single-A last year at age 18 or younger, Kilby had the highest BB/K and the lowest SwStr% out of anybody. My negative on him is that of the 16 prep bats taken in the first round last year, Rapsodo had Kilby's Max EV as the second lowest that they measured during the combine, and despite the impressive debut he hit more than three times as many ground balls as fly balls. This could take some time on the developmental side for that power to show in games but honestly even if it takes longer than expected, or doesn't come at all, I still don't think this is a bad buy. Even if he posts a .120 ISO this year, hitting .280-ish with a great approach, great contact, and great SB numbers at age 19 on the Yankees could probably support this card price alone. These fans once made Volpe a top tier hobby name despite his lack of a plus tool. I don't think it's out of the question that they will do the same for Kilby if he plays well this year.

players.name: Richard Matic
players.note: is probably the most fun high upside play of the 3's but he's truly a two outcome player, I think it's either going to click or it's not. Hit .336 with 5 HR, 11 SB, 20.9% BB, .231 ISO, and 167 wRC+ in the DSL last year. The bad news is that he was repeating the DSL which is usually a death sentence for me. The good news is that his first time playing there he was only 16 so even being stuck there for two seasons it's not like he was too old to be there. That pulls me in two directions. If he comes to the states and the approach and contact improvements look real he'll probably end up as a buy very early on since he has great power upside, so if you want to stash him now I wouldn't blame you, but $10+ is a bit high given the questions I still have.

players.name: Jace Avina
players.note: When looking at $5-ish breakout picks in this organization my eyes immediately went to Jace Avina. He was drafted as a 14th rounder out of high school back in 2021 by the Brewers who are notorious for finding sneaky talent outside of the 10th round. All he did in his professional debut was win the MVP of the Arizona Complex League when he hit .294 with 10 HR in 36 games, giving him a .336 ISO and 181 wRC+. Pretty unreal numbers there. However, despite absolutely demolishing baseballs he had a 34.2% strikeout rate and 39.6% contact rate. That contact rate seems impossible. It almost feels like a bad number you'd get from inconsistent DSL data. I'm not sure I'd whiff on 60% of my swings in the Complex League. I'm going to go ahead and assume that CPX data in 2022 wasn't honed in yet. We saw that power again the following year where Avina had a .209 ISO in Single-A but this time his strikeout rate dropped to 29.6% and he also saw his BB/K go from 0.29 to 0.47. Then in 2024 he improved his strikeout rate and contact rate again, but the ISO slipped to .154. Here's the thing with Avina, you never want to see power outputs go down but when your contact skills are bad and your K rate is over 30% you have to do something, and that something is to work on your approach and pitch selection and stop swinging out of your shoes. In my opinion the Avina we saw in 2025 was the most well-rounded version that we've seen yet. Between A+ & AA he hit .260 with 11 HR, 5 SB, 11.8% BB, 25.1% K, .165 ISO, and 136 wRC+ in 98 games. This is statistically a really solid season for someone with a $6 autograph. Lowest strikeout rate in his career, highest contact rate in his career (73.6%), and he's keeping the ISO at a good level thanks to 24 doubles and 11 homers. Was he more fun when his ISO .336? Sure, but his contact skills were so bad he may have been out of baseball if he kept swinging like that. These feel like tangible improvements every year. There were twenty non-debuted prospects in baseball last year age 22 or younger who had 400+ PA with an ISO over .165 and wRC+ over 135 while reaching Double-A or better. Twenty sounds like a lot until you realize it's a list with Konnor Griffin, JJ Wetherholt, Aidan Miller, Carson Benge, Lazaro Montes, Ryan Waldschmidt, etc. etc. and eighteen of the twenty have a base autograph over $30. The only two who don't are Chris Suero (NYM) at $18 who I named as a buy in my last Mets article and Jace Avina at… $6. Obviously he's barely in my top 300 so I don't hold him in the same regard as those guys, but for a Yankees prospect who is starting the year in Double-A coming off that good of a season this feels low.

players.name: Stiven Marinez
players.note: feels like a solid sleeper as well, I'm not sure he'll ever get to average power which could hurt his ceiling but he's got a really good approach, drew 41 walks in 160 PA in the DSL (20% BB), and has plus speed (22 SB). There's plenty to like for $5.

players.name: Enmanuel Tejeda
players.note:
Tejeda was actually the only Yankess buy for me last year as a 4/5 and his price has basically stayed the same, but he also missed the start of the year and didn't return from his rehab assignment until late July. Tejada really got on my radar back in 2023 when at age 18 in the CPX he hit .307 with 5 HR, 24 SB, 20.3% BB, 20.3% K, .151 ISO, and 147 wRC+. That'll play. He was one of my favorite sleepers when 2024 Bowman came out but unfortunately he was injured for much of that following season and only got 203 PA between CPX & A. He did however bat .326 with a 121 wRC+ in those games but both his approach and power kind of slid back. When he returned at the end of July in 2025 from another injury he hit .252 with 3 HR, 14 SB, 16.6% BB, 14.9% K, .102 ISO, and 120 wRC+. In the 35 games he played at Single-A Tejeda had an 82.2% contact rate, 7.9% swinging strike rate, and 1.30 walk to strikeout ratio. I still feel, as I've felt for what feels like three years now, that we've seen very solid offensive production from Tejeda it just comes in very small doses since he hasn't gotten more than 217 PA in a season since he signed back in 2022. His wRC+ marks in each year since he's debuted are 149, 147, 121, and 120. He's a 5'9" infielder who projects for average power and speed which isn't the most exciting profile but I don't think any Yankees hitter with his bat-to-ball skills should be under $5, and the only reason it's this low is because of his inability to stay on the field recently. He'll likely start the year in High-A and he's now 21 so the clock is ticking on his ability to get some hobby love but since he's going into the season healthy (knock on wood) I really like his chances. He's definitely a floor over ceiling player but even then it doesn't feel out of the question that this could go from $4 to $15-20 with a strong showing. Tejeda appeared in the AFL at the end of last season and had a 5-hit 3-stolen base game and the thought of him doing that in a High-A or hopefully Double-A game this year makes me want to take a chance on him. Not every play is sexy, sometimes you buy a $40 gold auto of a player because you think it can get to $100+. If Enmanuel Tejeda were to put together 400+ PA matching ANY level of production he's had in his first four professional seasons so far I think his cards go up. 

There was a time that

players.name: Carlos Lagrange
players.note: that I haven't already? Love him and he's electric but a $93 base auto for a pitcher prior to making his debut is crazy.

players.name: Ben Hess
players.note: is probably the closest of the 3's to being a buy ranked 35th at $35. His secondary pitches have looked unreal this spring, he's up there throwing frisbees. I do think there's upside here but this range is typically a $20-25 auto as we saw the other day with Mets Jonathan Santucci who is ranked barely ahead of Hess. Being $10 higher barely puts him into a hold range but not by much.

players.name: Bryce Cunningham
players.note: looked great last year and earned his way into my top 100 pitchers but with a ranking of 90th I'd be looking for about a $10 base auto and he's basically double that. Classic Yankees tax.

players.name: Chase Hampton
players.note:
Probably not the name that we were expecting to see here and I'll say it again, it really is tough to find value when it comes to Yankees prospects. The three arms that I have inside my top 100 are all priced high compared to where I have them ranked. As we saw with the hitters the best buys in an organization like this are almost always the cheap guys who get no love that still have a good chance to break out. For that reason I'd be throwing my pitcher dart at Chase Hampton. The issue here is that there is massive risk because we've only seen Hampton throw a total of 18.2 innings since the end of 2023. In 2024 he had a groin strain and elbow discomfort that limited him to only 7 starts and then while getting ready for the 2025 season it was discovered that he was going to need Tommy John. Hampton wasn't a huge name coming out of Texas Tech but he improved his draft stock at the end of his sophomore year by breaking his own personal single game strikeout record in each of his final four starts while topping 99 mph. The combination of that upside and him being a draft-eligible sophomore led to the Yankees selecting him in the sixth round in 2022 but signing him at almost double his slot value. In his only full professional season in 2023 he threw 106.2 innings between A+ & AA with a 3.63 ERA, 3.38 FIP, 12.23 K/9, and 3.12 BB/9 over 20 starts. In that season we saw what looked like three plus grade pitches: the fastball which was around 97 with carry, a nasty curveball, and perhaps his best pitch a high spin slider. Along with those he also threw a cutter which showed some promise and a changeup which seemed like his clear fifth pitch. He mixed them all extremely well and he comes from a release point and angle that are very tough on hitters. In that season opposing batters hit .212 off Hampton, with a 67.9% contact rate, and 33.1% strikeout rate. In the 9 starts he made in A+ before the promotion his K/9 was 14.74 and he struck out 77 of the 190 hitters he faced (40.5%). It was about as dominant of a professional debut as you could hope to see. In that 2023 season among pitchers age 21 or younger who threw 100+ innings his 24.7% K-BB% was THE BEST in all of the minor leagues. The issue here of course is that I'm citing 2023 stats which is terrifying because that's pretty much the last time we saw him healthy. There are no guarantees that his stuff or his location will be as good as they were back then. But he's healthy entering this year and was assigned to Double-A Somerset the other day where he will begin this season. Hampton is very risky but he's also so cheap that his price might go up just from him stepping on the mound in his return to the minors. For those reasons I would consider him to be the Yankees pitcher who has the best chance to see exponential growth this season. Fingers crossed that we see that 2023 version of him because if we do this could be fun.

What can I say about

players.name: Pico Kohn
players.note: is tempting under $10 his strikeout stuff and command looked better in 2025 than it did in 2024 at Miss St., unfortunately he was also hit harder. Need to see some things corrected but he's a nice sleeper arm.

players.name: Leo De Vries
players.note: I know I've said in the past that it's nearly impossible for me to recommend buying someone whose base autograph is already $200 but I'm making an exception for De Vries because outside of Konnor Griffin he is my highest ranked non-debuted hitting prospect for the hobby. Even at around $200 (was $160 a few weeks ago) he's cheaper than Kevin McGonigle, Jesus Made, Max Clark, Colt Emerson, JJ Wetherholt, and others who I have ranked lower than LDV. We know that De Vries came over from the Padres in the Mason Miller deal and while you have to respect teams going for it all instead of hugging their prospects, this was a wild move and one I think San Diego will probably regret in the long run. The switch-hitting shortstop projects for a 50-55 grade hit tool, 50-55 speed, and plus power. He checks every box you could possibly want in terms of being a hobby superstar and while Jesus Made seems to be the one that gets more love publicly from prospect outlets and the hobby, I am going to respectfully disagree and say that De Vries is a more exciting prospect. I often cite a player's age compared to the level he plays at as a factor that drives my prospect rankings more than most people's and he is the poster child for it. He was the only player to get 100+ PA in Double-A at age 18 last year. He was the only player to get 200+ PA in Single-A at age 17 the year prior. When it comes to performing at a higher level than players your age he quite literally sets the bar. I can remember Sebastian Walcott getting #1 prospect rankings from some people in 2024 and many people's thoughts were, "his stats aren't that great". But I can't say enough about how impressive it is to be an above league average hitter when you're five years younger than your average competitor. When I talked to Jim Callis it's one of the reason he gave for why the clear #1 pick in this year's draft Roch Cholowsky might be ranked behind Made and De Vries for him on his end of the year prospect list. Sure he's dominating college but he'll be 21 when he gets drafted and these guys will have already been tearing up Double-A as teenagers. Last year between A+ & AA at age 18 De Vries hit .255 with 15 HR, 11 SB, 12.3% BB, 20% K, .196 ISO, and 125 wRC+. There were only nine prospects in baseball last year who at age 18 played all of their time above the rookie levels. His .196 ISO was not only the highest but it was more than 20 points higher than the next best and almost 70 points higher than Jesus Made's. Only five teenage prospects even got 80+ PA in Double-A last year, the only two who had an ISO over .200 were Leo De Vries and Konnor Griffin. De Vries' was 65 points higher and he's half a year younger than Konnor. In 2024 Leo had a .204 ISO in 360 PA at Single-A. Sorting FanGraphs minor league data back to 2006 he is the only prospect to ever have an ISO over .200 in 300+ PA above the rookie levels at age 17. Last year after his promotion to Double-A he hit 5 HR in 103 PA and had a .270 ISO there. He became the first 18-year-old prospect to have multiple homers in a Double-A season since Bryce Harper in 2011. I could do these all day. This kid is a freak. I had him as a buy on last year's Padres sheet at $118 and he's nearly doubled. He still feels to me like a guy who could get to $400 by the start of next season and while I'd argue Made could also, De Vries is 15% cheaper and I have him ranked higher.

players.name: Henry Bolte
players.note: is definitely the most exciting name of my 3's and honestly one of the better power/speed combinations in the minor leagues. With 15 HR/46 SB in 2024 followed by 9 HR/44 SB in 2025 I think he's probably the most exciting non-debuted hitter in this organization not named Leo De Vries. The issue is that he's very chase prone and has never had a single professional season with a contact rate over 70%. He also was a redemption autograph and is very short printed which is kind of a catch-22 because holding a player with short supply is never bad, but it also makes him pricy. Right now his average is at $40 but they don't sell often and the last one sold for $75. Really, really exciting kid because of the athleticism but not a price point I love for such a shaky hit tool. I also like

players.name: Tommy White
players.note: aka Tommy Tanks who has been on a tear this spring with 4 HR in 31 PA. Was a big power bat at LSU (75 HR in 3 seasons) but he didn't hit for much power in either of his first two pro seasons. He did however hit for good average and post contact rates over 80%. This honestly makes him very intriguing. His card prices aren't super high and it might be because we haven't seen a ton of homers since he was drafted but if he's improved the contact skills and the power outburst comes this year he could be really fun. For $25 he's in a hold range for me but I do like the upside. The high ceiling stash for the A's is

players.name: Devin Taylor
players.note: I was higher than most on Devin Taylor when 2025 Bowman Draft came out and he was my 10th ranked hitter in the entire product when I did my chase rankings. He was my highest ranked college bat after Ethan Conrad (CHC) who is currently selling for $45 so him going for one third of the price being ranked only two spots behind him in the product feels like a no brainer. A hobby ranking of 172 might not sound high but remember I said that with guys from the newest draft classes I need about 200 PA of professional stats for the "production" portion of their ranking to normalize and despite a solid debut, him being 21 in Single-A is pushing that part of his score down. However, my guess is that he'll end up closer to the top 100 early on this season if he plays as well as I expect. He was arguably the best offensive high schooler in Ohio in 2022 and committed to Indiana where he was a First Team All Big Ten selection in all three of his college seasons. I'll give you some of the stats I pulled in my Bowman Draft preview. Taylor's batting average each season at IU: .315, .357, .374. His wRC+: 143, 150, 160. His ISO: .335, .303, .332. The Big Ten may not be the biggest baseball conference but he has an 800 PA sample of him doing nothing but hit. He has the Indiana school record for homers at 54 and in his college career had an OBP over .450 with more walks than strikeouts. His last year at IU he had a 19.3% walk rate and 11.2% strikeout rate. That's a 1.73 BB/K ratio. This could be 55 hit 60 power. In between his 2024 and 2025 seasons we also saw him do it with a wood bat in the Cape Cod League as hit .296 with a .907 OPS and 5 HR in 116 PA. Last year in his pro debut he hit 6 HR in 129 and had a .217 ISO but I mentioned that was a 21-year-old in A ball so it's hard to get too excited about that. However his batted ball data section is a work of art. On balls he put in play he pulled 32.9% of them, hit 32.9% up the middle, and took 34.3% to the opposite field. I love this offensive profile. The issue is of course the defense, which he doesn't play well and will limit him to corner outfield if anything and he may likely be a DH. That could hurt his value but honestly in Bowman if you're going to have a bad tool we want it to be your defense. I think the bat is legit. I think he has the most hobby friendly offensive profile of any college hitter in this Bowman Draft class aside from maybe Ethan Conrad or Ethan Frey, two players he's less than half the price of. I think he'll hit and if he does I don't see how this price doesn't move.

players.name: Ayden Johnson
players.note: who was the 12th ranked international prospect in last year's class and signed for $1.5 million out of the Bahamas. International scouts put 60 Hit 55 Power potential grades on him which as a 6'2" teenage shortstop would be incredible for the Bowman world. They couldn't say enough about his physicality for his age and said he may be the most polished bat entering pro ball from the Bahamas, a country which produced Jazz Chisholm and Sebastian Walcott. However he had a very low ISO in his DSL debut, failed to go deep, and his strikeout rate was higher than you'd like to see. If you trust all of the international scouts who raved about him he's a fantastic target, but I need to see it in games first. Cheap fun stash is

players.name: Junior Perez
players.note: I know it's very hard to be a relevant name in Bowman when you're 24-years-old but the rankings and production for Junior Perez are pretty wild for a $5 base auto. I'd have to go back and look to be sure but off the top of my head I would guess that he is my highest ranked hobby prospect with an autograph this cheap. Perez isn't a name you hear about often but when I did the 'Hot Sheets' last year he was a guy who would regularly show up at high levels of the minors and sort of put my brain in a blender. In my August 18th Hot Sheet I said of him, "I challenge you to find a prospect with Junior Perez's AAA stats that you can still buy for under $5". Since that article his price has skyrocketed from $2.46 to $5. Joking of course. But the more I kind of look at this profile and hitting data I feel like it's hard not to like what Perez is doing for such a cheap autograph. From 2024 to 2025 he had one of the biggest single season offensive breakouts that you probably didn't even hear about. Back in 2024 in Double-A he hit .220 with 8 HR, 28 SB, 10.8% BB, 35.4% K, .152 ISO, and 90 wRC+. The A's had him start last year at the same level and he played so well that he earned himself a promotion to Triple-A. Between both levels his stat line was… are you ready… .231 with 26 HR, 27 SB, 14.8% BB, 28.1% K, .243 ISO, and 114 wRC+. He added 18 more HRs, increased his walks by 4%, and dropped his strikeouts by 7%? I'm listening. In fact if you look at his stats after his promotion to AAA they're insane. In 182 PA he hit .298 with 12 HR, 11 SB, 16.5% BB, 26.9% K, .344 ISO, and 143 wRC+. Yes, that's a .344 ISO. Now you could argue that the PCL is a hitter's league and may actually be easier to hit in than AA, but still, to do that much damage and see your autograph go up $2 feels crazy? I'm not going to lie to you and say the hit tool is good. You see the batting averages and strikeout rates. The contact rates aren't good either (69.3% last year). But this is above average power, it's above average speed, oh and he plays a plus defense in CF that some in the organization have said is on par with their current CF'er Denzel Clarke. We love loud tools and we love a player getting called up to the MLB. There were only two prospects in baseball last year age 24 or younger who had 25+ HR, 25+ SB, AND reached Triple-A. They were Spencer Jones and Junior Perez. He'll never hit for average but he does go on crazy hot stretches and if he runs into a few of those this season I feel like he could get some buzz. If not, it's $5.

players.name: Dylan Fien
players.note: brother of last year's first round pick Gavin Fien. Haven't seen much and it was hard to even find scouting reports on him when the A's took him out of high school in the 7th round in 2024, but he's a 6'3" switch-hitting catcher who barrels baseballs pretty regularly and could have power upside. Could be a name to watch in 2026.

players.name: Clark Elliott
players.note: It had to be done. For the first time on any sheet I'm giving a buy to a player who is not on the team's top 30 from MLB Pipeline and isn't inside my top 400 hobby rankings. You will notice though on the table above that he is ranked as the 390th prospect on Dynasty Dugout and I have to give them the assist on this one because I wouldn't have even looked up Elliott's stats had I not seen that. I mean he's not even top 500 on Scout the Statline, but any time I see someone with absolutely zero buzz get ranked by a singular outlet it gives me a reason to go look and try to find out what they're seeing. Elliott was selected by the A's with the 69th overall pick in the 2022 draft where he signed out of Michigan for $900k. His first full season in 2023 was forgettable as he hit .218 with a 73 wRC+ in 374 PA. No bueno. He was injured entering the 2024 season and when he returned the A's put him back in Single-A. There are ways to get on radars, playing in Single-A at age 23 is not one of them. That year he only got 256 PA and he hit .300 with 6 HR, 7 SB, .175 ISO, and 144 wRC+. Really good stat line no doubt but comparing the age to the level you can't really put much weight into the stats. This past year Elliott started in High-A but played so well in the first two months he was promoted to Double-A where he continued to perform. Across both levels he hit .251 with 12 HR, 16 SB, 16.8% BB, 20.1% K, .171 ISO, and 130 wRC+. It was the first time in his professional career he stayed healthy for 400+ PA and he honestly looked great. From to 2024 to 2025 Elliott improved his contact rates from 72.1% to 76.3% while dropping his swinging strike rate from 10.7% to 8.7%. Here's the thing. Even if you're performing well in AA you're too old at 24 to be exciting to us. But this is kind of where I go back to finding value. Should he have a $20 base autograph? No. Should it be $1? Also, no. That stat line from last season is extremely well-rounded and it came with a 36.5% swing rate which is very selective. He's controlling the zone much better than he has in the past and it looks like he has enough power and speed to be a solid player. I was curious what kind of company that HR/SB and approach combination put him in so I went and looked. There were seven players in the minors last year age 24 or younger who had 12+ HR, 15+ SB, and a walk to strikeout ratio of 0.80 or better. Two of those players are now in the MLB in Jakob Marsee (MIA) and Dylan Beavers (BAL) and look like they'll be productive big leaguers. The five who have yet to debut are JJ Wetherholt, Max Clark, Josue De Paula, Ryan Waldschmidt, and Clark Elliott. What a list. I don't want people to freak out and think I'm saying that Clark Elliott is about to be a huge name, but if this production continues into AAA even at age 25 it would hard for him to continue getting zero recognition. Even going from $1 to $10 would be fun if you had some color. No guarantees that it goes up but as a counterpoint, how does it go down?

players.name: Jamie Arnold
players.note: as a 3 and to be fair he's probably more like a 3.5 and I almost put him as a 4. I raved about him in my 2025 Bowman Draft rankings and expect big things from him as a professional. He's an awkward lefty who comes from an almost Chris Sale arm slot and could have three pitches that are above average or plus. Had consecutive seasons at Florida St. with an ERA under 3.00, a K/9 over 12.0, and a BB/9 under 3.0. Fantastic stuff. My only concern here is price. I have him and fellow 2025 draftee Tyler Bremner (LAA) ranked back-to-back and when I did the Angels sheet he was $30. Kyson Witherspoon (BOS) is a top 10 hobby pitcher for me and he's also in the $30-35 range. When you get near $50 as a non-debuted pitcher you pretty much have to be in my top 10 for me to think there's buying value. I love Jamie Arnold and he could definitely go up this year, I just wish we had a cheaper entry point. My favorite sleeper arm is

players.name: Henry Baez
players.note:
Top 150 in the hobby pitcher rankings with a $3 autograph? Ok then. Baez was another piece who came to the A's with Leo De Vries in the Mason Miller deal and he's had an interesting career so far. He signed with the Padres for $125k back in 2019 as a 16-year-old but because of the season cancellations due to COVID his professional debut was pushed back two years. His fastball sits in the mid-90's but touches 99 and because of it's sink he generates ground ball rates that have typically hovered in the 50-55% range for his career. Earlier in his career he threw a curveball that flashed as an above average pitch but has since switched to a slider as his second pitch which he also gets good results out of. Changeup is the third pitch but is merely average and he's worked on a cutter but we haven't seen it a ton. Last year in Double-A the 6'3" righty had a 2.39 ERA with a 8.26 K/9 and 2.89 BB/9 over 109 innings. He's not generating the huge swing-and-miss stuff that makes the hobby go and that's why he doesn't get a ton of love but let's be real results also matter. Here's a list of every pitcher age 23 or younger who has a Bowman card and has thrown 105+ innings with an ERA under 3.00 in both of the past two seasons. Henry Baez. The end. Prior to the trade last season Baez had a 1.96 ERA in 20 Double-A starts with the Padres where he led the Texas League in both WHIP and batting average against (.195). Since the 2023 season he has dropped his walk rate per 9 innings from 4.21 BB/9 to 2.89 BB/9 and his ability to keep runners off the bases and handle a starter's workload has improved his stock drastically in my opinion. The issue is that without those big 7-8 strikeout games it's tough to get people super hype about your cards but when you're locating your pitches as well as Baez does and creating ground balls it gives you an extremely high floor for $3. Despite hitters having 78-79% contact rates against him the last two years he's held his opponent's average under .210 in both of them. In that same age group only two Bowman pitchers held hitters to an average under .210 over 100+ innings in consecutive seasons for 2024 & 2025. They were Jonah Tong and Henry Baez. Again, the ceiling isn't huge since he doesn't miss a ton of bats but he's effective enough to make his way into the major league rotation which feels like it's worth $3.

Breaks my heart to put

players.name: Steven Echavarria
players.note: who they drafted out of high school in the third round back in 2023. The results have just been okay so far but he was also playing in High-A as a 19-year-old which is a pretty aggressive assignment for a pitcher. The stuff is electric though for a pitcher his age so at a $3 base auto he's a really high upside stash.

players.name: Justin Crawford
players.note: was my #2 pick. I've always felt like Crawford was a better player than he got credit for and the inability to command a triple digit price during his minor league career was due to a lack of game power. I for one think he'll have more power than people expect and I don't doubt that his cards could continue to go up if that's the case, but I'm not one to hold past the debut. He's gone from $75-ish this offseason to now $100+ but his days of being a non-debuted prospect are numbered. Outside of Crawford my highest ranked 3 is 2024 first round pick

players.name: Aidan Miller
players.note:
- Hobby Ranking: 11

Always tough to make it as a buy when you're creeping up towards $100 but I've got Aidan Miller ranked directly in between Max Clark and Walker Jenkins who are both $170-200 so the path to his cards doubling doesn't feel like a reach. Especially when you consider that Konnor Griffin, Kevin McGonigle, JJ Wetherholt, and Colt Emerson should likely graduate this year putting Miller into a potential range for next year where the prospects currently occupying those spots are $250+. I know that Justin Crawford has been a buzzy name this spring since he should have a good chance of being the Phillies starting CF but in terms of hobby upside these two aren't particularly close to me and are currently separated by 30 ranking spots while being the same price. When I talked to Jim Callis we did a "Rapid Fire" segment where I gave him two prospects ranked similarly and asked whose autograph he'd rather have and I thought that Aidan Miller vs. Luis Pena would be a tough one. He snap answered Miller and said he believed he was the best prep bat he saw in the 2023 draft class and the only reason his draft stock slid was due to a hamate injury. Miller is an extremely well-rounded hitter and depending on where you look you can find evaluators who have him at 55 Hit, 60 Power, 55 Speed which is pretty insane. All of those tools were on display last year where between AA & AAA he hit .264 with 14 HR, 59 SB, 15.6% BB, 23.4% K, .169 ISO, and 137 wRC+ at age 21. All of that came with a 77.5% contact rate and 8.9% swinging strike rate. That season becomes even more ridiculous when you learn that Miller made an adjustment at the plate in the middle of the season and from August 1st until the end of the season had 6 HR, 22 SB, more walks than strikeouts, and a 1.099 OPS in 36 games. Despite being one of the most productive minor leaguers since he was drafted it feels like he's somehow still slept on. You rarely ever hear his name mentioned in the conversation when it comes to top 10 prospects and based on what I've seen I think he deserves to be in that talk. There were only two prospects in baseball last year age 21 or younger who had an ISO over .160 and 50+ SB. They were Konnor Griffin and Aidan Miller. Miller's walk rate was nearly double Konnor's and he had a better overall contact percentage. Jesus Made and Leo De Vries are of course the front runners to be the #1 prospect in baseball in 2027. Aidan Miller is on a very, very short list of players I think could give them a run for their money.

players.name: Dante Nori
players.note: He's a really good contact hitter with double plus speed who stole 52 bases last year but his 4 HR in 577 PA makes it tough to generate a ton of hobby hype. Nori is a Bowman collector himself which is awesome but his prices have spiked recently with him going deep twice in the WBC for Italy while batting over .400. If his base auto was around $15-20 I'd be on board, which it was prior to the WBC, but at $30 I'd probably let it come back down after the tournament ends before buying anything. I named

players.name: Aroon Escobar
players.note:
Signing for $450k back in 2022 Aroon Escobar is one of the few players that has beaten the odds on my "don't buy guys who repeated the DSL" rule because he was stuck there for two summers, and without very spectacular results. Playing in the DSL in both his age 17 and 18 seasons he had a career .694 OPS in more than 300 PA there when he headed to the states in 2024. If he had cards back then he would have been a very clear stay away. What I'm not sure anyone saw coming was his stateside debut. In the CPX in 2024 he hit .338 with with 3 HR, 9 SB, 20.2% BB, 9.6% K, .143 ISO, and 172 wRC+ in 104 PA. An 82.4% contact rate, 6.4% SwStr%, and a 2.10 (!!!) BB/K. What in the world. The only issue is that since he repeated the DSL he was 19 in the CPX which is older than I'd want anybody to be at that level if I'm buying their cards. He would have to move levels quickly in the next season for him to be able to climb my rankings, and that he did. Last year Escobar was promoted from A to A+ after 69 games and then again from A+ to AA after 46 more. Across all three levels he hit .270 with 15 HR, 24 SB, 10.4% BB, 18.2% K, .143 ISO, and 121 wRC+. That's a pretty strong age 20 season especially since he earned the chance to finish the year in AA. While he always made good contact, even back to his time in the DSL, the reason he never produced results was because he wasn't barreling the ball very often. That has now changed and despite being 5'9" everything we saw last year looks like he's going to project for above average power. When you pair that with his advanced approach and ability to control the strike zone he all of the sudden has an offensive profile that is very hobby friendly, and he's moved himself inside my top 75 non-debut hitters. There were only six hitters last year in the minors who had 15+ HR and 20+ SB at age 20 or younger. Escobar's 18.1% strikeout rate was more than 3.5% lower than the next closest person, who happened to be Konnor Griffin. Naturally when I saw this I was curious who the last player was prior to Escobar to have a 15 HR/20 SB season with a sub-19% K rate at age 20 or younger. The answer was 2023 Jackson Chourio. Though Escobar may not have a true plus tool there are almost no flaws in his batted ball data and if the power were to improve again this year he could get some serious helium. Not a bad play at all for $20.

When I did a podcast episode naming the ten non-debuted prospects that I felt were the most likely to make their team's Opening Day roster,

players.name: Gabriel Rincones Jr.
players.note: as a sneaky stash a few months ago in an article about players who should debut this year but he was $7 then and has doubled since. Still love the power upside and he's a sneaky good athlete too with 10+ HR and 20+ SB in three consecutive seasons.
