I do still think his stock could boom but he's now 25-years-old and priced over $15 so he's a hold for me. Best dart throw in this organization is without a doubt

players.name: Griffin Burkholder
players.note: He has struggled but when he arrived after being drafted in 2024 he drew rave reviews from those inside the organization for his freak-ish athleticism. This is a lottery ticket since he hasn't produced much in his young career but he's also been injured for most of it. This could legit be 60 power 70 speed. Think Jonny Farmelo athleticism with a much, much lower floor since his approach and contact aren't nearly as good. Needs to clean up the swing and work on some things offensively. Still has a ways to go developmentally but fun dice roll for $6 due to the ceiling in case it clicks. I haven't abandoned all hope when it comes to

players.name: Carson DeMartini
players.note: who I loved as a cheap stash in 2024 Bowman Draft. Dominated A+ but really struggled after the move up to AA. Still was one of only thirteen prospects last year with 10 HR/45 SB. Could be a sneaky breakout pick for 2026.

players.name: Gage Wood
players.note: is literally right on the dividing line of being a buy. He's $5 more expensive than Jonathan Santucci (NYM) who I gave a 4/5 to and Santucci is only ranked three spots higher. The difference is that I've seen him do it. I love Gage Wood. He is electric. Touches 98 with the fastball paired with a power curve giving him two legitimate plus pitches. His 16.49 K/9 and 1.67 BB/9 were video game stuff last year at Arkansas. Of all the pitching stats I've looked at I'm not sure I've seen another 41.3% K-BB%. Here are my issues. While he did mix in some other offerings in his professional debut he really only threw those two pitches in college. Can't blame him because they're nasty but if he wants to be a starter he'll have to improve his repertoire. Also, not a huge frame at 6'0". He missed time last year due to a shoulder injury and in three collegiate seasons he's never threw more than 40.1 innings in a single year. I'm not saying he can't handle a starter's workload but we haven't seen it. I love the upside here but $30 is pretty steep for a pitcher with these concerns. If he comes out and has a third and/or fourth pitch that look good and proves that he can throw 100+ innings I'd be in, but right now at this price he's a hold for me. Hate to do this to my boy

players.name: Yoniel Curet
players.note: who I was always a fan of in the Rays organization, and with a rank of 73rd and an autograph selling for $8 he's definitely in the buying zone. He has electric stuff and struck out 303 hitters between 2023 and 2024 which was the most in minor league baseball during that span. Unfortunately his command which at one point looked to be improving backed up on him in a big way and then he was hurt for most of 2025. Tampa Bay said their goodbyes and though he looked like he could find a spot in Philly's bullpen he hasn't been able to find the zone at all this spring, walking 4 of the 14 batters he's faced and allowing 8 earned runs in less than 2 innings. I still think he has the stuff to be an electric reliever but his stock is trending the wrong way so I can't say I still love the value as much as I used to. Other than Gage Wood the next closest 3 to being a buy for me is probably

players.name: Matthew Fisher
players.note: This could be a fun one here. When I did my 2025 Bowman Draft preview I had Fisher in the 'Stash 'Em' category which was directly after my top 12 pitchers. Philly took him in the seventh round but gave him almost five times the slot value and signed him for $1.25 million. He was a multi-sport athlete in high school which you all know is something I'm a big fan of. As his school's starting quarterback he threw for 2,779 yards with 34 touchdowns and only 1 interception with a QBR of 140.8, adding 191 rushing yards and 8 more touchdowns on the ground. I would have taken that on my fantasy team for sure. On the diamond he had a 1.51 ERA with more than four times as many strikeouts as walks, punching out 91 hitters in 60.1 innings. His dominance in both sports led to him being named the Gatorade Player of the Year for the state of Indiana. There is a ton of projection in his frame and he already creates really good extension. It's also not much of a surprise based on what I just said that his delivery is very athletic. For someone who didn't play baseball year-round his stuff looked pretty damn impressive his senior year. He spins everything extremely well. Fastball sat in the low-90's but played really well due to its action with good carry and cut. There are also above average projections on both his curveball and slider which have extremely high spin rates for a prep arm. We'll see what the Phillies do in terms of developing a fourth pitch but he did have a changeup he used at times that he has shown some feel for. Fisher checks a lot of the boxes that I like. As he adds strength to his frame I expect him to gain a few ticks on that fastball velocity which already has above average grades from scouts. It's always tough investing in prep arms but when the entry point is under $10 it softens the blow in case it doesn't work out. Thanks to that repeatable delivery he should have no issues with his command as a professional, the stuff is good, the frame is good, there's honestly not much to not like here for $7.

players.name: Cade Obermueller
players.note: who was in my 'Next Best - College' section of my 2025 Bowman Draft rankings. Looked fantastic at Iowa but he's an undersized lefty so there are concerns about workload, although he did make it through consecutive college seasons as a starter without issues. Fastball and slider are both really nice but lacks a good third pitch. There are things to like for sure but I'm still a little on the fence. Pitcher dart throw could be

players.name: Wen-Hui Pan
players.note: who looked dominant last we saw him with a 2.15 ERA, 10.74 K/9, and 2.76 BB/9. Unfortunately that was less than 30 innings and also in 2024 because he didn't pitch last year due to Tommy John. Still reallyyy good stuff. Nasty fastball and splitter. Need to see him post-surgery though.

players.name: Esmerlyn Valdez
players.note: One of the OG finds from our 'Hot Sheets', the first time I put the stamp of approval on people buying Valdez last year came when his base autograph was selling for $7. In that same calendar year that card peaked with a sale of $94. Wild. Valdez is a big power-hitting corner outfielder who made massive improvements in all facets of the game last year. The power has always been there but in 2025 he showed up in much better shape physically, his defense was noticeably better, and his swing decisions improved pretty dramatically which made his overall stock as a prospect boom. Back in 2024 as a 20-year-old in Single-A he hit .226 with 22 HR, 13.6% BB, 30.6% K, .237 ISO, and 131 wRC+. He was a power bat who swung and missed a bunch. And that's fine for a $7 base auto. Last year however between High-A and Double-A he hit .286 with 26 HR, 10.6% BB, 24.6% K, .234 ISO, and 155 wRC+. While keeping his ISO output virtually the same we saw Valdez improve his batting average by 60 points and drop his strikeout rate by 6%. This is now a much better offensive package then it looked to be in the past. There were only four hitters age 21 or younger last year who hit 25+ HR. Bryce Eldridge, Lazaro Montes, Ryan Clifford, and Esmerlyn Valdez. Of those 4 Valdez was the only one who had a strikeout rate under 25%. To prove it wasn't a fluke he then went on to the AFL where he absolutely dominated batting .368 with 8 HR and more walks than strikeouts in 80 PA, slugging .842 with a 1.355 OPS. He would have been the MVP if not for a guy named Kevin McGonigle but between us Valdez should have won. That's when we saw those crazy price spikes. I mentioned his $94 base auto sale, he was averaging in the mid $70's range towards the end of the fall and that peak sale came in November. Now he's half of that price. For what? He didn't start struggling, there just haven't been games. There's always an offseason dip but this one makes no sense to lose half of your value. Maybe people think his 500+ PA season AND AFL output were a fluke but I'm not sure how you could. On top of that he was invited to Spring Training where he's hitting .294 with a homer, more walks than strikeouts, .235 ISO, and 171 wRC+ in 11 games. He's a top 50 hitter for me and all of his improvements seem legit. We've already seen this thing go over $80 when he's hot, I don't know why it wouldn't again.

players.name: Termarr Johnson
players.note: Drafted fourth overall back in the 2022 MLB draft Termarr Johnson was a huge hobby name coming out of high school when the Pirates selected him. He was one of those players who had a very unfortunate 1st Bowman autograph situation. When he got his 1st in 2022 Bowman Draft his autograph was a redemption and compared to other redemptions we've seen in draft products it took them forever to send out his live autos. On top of that he got a second prospect autograph in 2023 Bowman and those autographs actually went out before his redemptions had been even redeemed, making his first live autograph his second autograph. Pretty crazy they let that happen. Regarded by many as being the best pure hitter in that prep class, a class which included Jackson Holliday by the way, Johnson has shown off those skills pretty regularly as a professional. In his first full professional season at age 19 he hit .244 with 18 HR, 10 SB, 21.9% BB, 26% K, .195 ISO, and 139 wRC+. Aside from the batting average this is like if I could build a stat line in a lab for a teenage hitter. An ISO over .190 and a walk rate over 20%? Be still my heart. If you search all FanGraphs minor league data which goes back to 2006, that 2023 Termarr Johnson season is the only time a teenage prospect has ever had an ISO over .190 and walk rate over 20% for 300+ PA. Wild. Unfortunately his ISO and HR totals have dropped in consecutive years since then. Last year he hit .272 with 9 HR, 20 SB, 11.7% BB, 18.5% K, .111 ISO, and 118 wRC+ in Double-A. Still a good season. While it's discouraging to see his power seem to be dropping there's something else happening that is very good. Since 2023 his ISO's by season are .195, .149, and .111. However, his strikeout rates are 26%, 21.3%, and 18.5%. Along with that his contact rates are 68.8%, 71%, and 75.1%. You don't hear much about him because the power numbers are sliding but he's now a much better contact hitter than he has ever been. This is kind of a tricky game but I actually love when players I know can hit for power, and I've seen hit for power, start sacrificing power to work on their contact because it makes people bail on them. I mentioned his base autograph was a redemption so it's pretty short printed and you won't find eBay flooded with them. Due to this these were always sought after when he was a popular prospect name and they were consistently $60+ up until last year. This price at $24 feels too low for me all things considered. I've mentioned it before with guys like Kahlil Watson when you were once a big hobby name, especially if you were a high 1st round pick, people recognize your name even if they've momentarily forgotten about you. When he heats up in AAA this year and gets close to making his MLB debut all of the sudden you're going to hear a lot of, "oh wow I forgot about Termarr Johnson", and those prices will go back up. I'm still a believer in the skills here.

players.name: Tony Blanco Jr.
players.note: but to be honest I already made my money on him and got out, but that's not to say he couldn't pop again. At 6'7" he has a hole in his swing I could drive my car through and will almost certainly always have a strikeout rate over 30%. With that being said he also hits baseballs harder than anybody else in the minor leagues and those video clips are the ones that go viral on Twitter and can make his cards skyrocket, it's happened for him a few times before. Then he does nothing for a while, they fall back down to earth, he hits a ball 120 mph and they take off again, so because of this he's kind of a never ending buy and sell. Very fun upside if you want to try and ride those waves.

players.name: Johan De Los Santos
players.note:
is probably the Pirates 3 I'm most intrigued by. Card prices are being held down by the fact that he's not projected for much power but had one of the best DSL debuts you'll find. Hit .353 with 0 HR, 34 SB, 15.5% BB, 7.5% K, .108 ISO, and 143 wRC+. Approach and contact looked good and he's got potentially 80 grade speed so he's a very fun hold as he comes to the states. Not sure there will be any power but if some showed up he could move up my rankings quickly.

Don't mean to offend anybody who is buying

players.name: Axiel Plaz
players.note:
Plaz is a fun one for me because he was one of those guys who ended up on a number of 'Hot Sheets' but there was a string of three to four weeks where he was a repeat offender and his price was staying around $5 until it finally blew up one week. It has since come back down but being ranked near my top 200 and having a base autograph under $5 is definitely a good buy and hold range. Plaz was a year ahead of most when his pro career started, playing in the DSL at 16 and CPX at 17. That meant in his age 18 season he got 280+ PA in Single-A which was only accomplished by twelve prospects that year, and his 107 wRC+ was the fifth highest of them all. While he struggled with contact batting .207 with a 29.2% K rate that year, he hit 15 HR with a .231 ISO which is ridiculous for an 18-year-old playing there. The Pirates elected to bring him back to A where he hit .262 with 9 HR and a 122 wRC+ in 233 PA last year, dropping his strikeout rate from 29.2% to 20.2%. This caused his cards to spike and we started seeing base autos in the $15+ range. Unfortunately after he was promoted to High-A he hit .086 there in 11 games and his prices crashed back down to nothing. Here's why I'm not concerned. First off, it was 42 PA which is such a small sample it doesn't matter. Second, in those High-A games his contact rate was 79.2% which was actually 7% higher than it was in Single-A. Despite batting .086 he walked in 11.9% of his PA and only struck out in 14.3%. How do you have a 14.3% K rate and 79.2% contact rate and hit .086? Only one way, with a .069 BABIP which is hilariously low. People can drop their cards of him all they want but the underlying data might be the best it could possibly be for a guy who hit under .100 and on top of that it was a less than 50 PA sample by a 19-year-old playing in High-A. Not only do I think he's going to be fine but I would argue that the huge improvements to the strikeout rate and his increased ability to make contact actually make me like him more now than I did at the start of last year. While most levels under AAA don't have Statcast data due to the lack of ABS the Florida State League in Single-A is one of the random ones that does which happened to be where Plaz played his biggest chunk of games last year. 98th percentile Max EV (113.9 mph), 91st percentile barrel rate (12.8%), and 94th percentile hard hit rate (52.7%). He needs to improve his chase rate because he's still too aggressive, but given the power potential we've seen at a young age he's not a bad grab at $5.

Have always been fascinated by

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: but $145 for a base autograph of a high school pitcher is craaaaazy. Now, as a counterpoint, there's an argument to be made that Hernandez has a higher ceiling than any pitching prospect in baseball right now. According to Prospect Pulse he is not only the highest priced non-debuted pitching prospect but it's not even really that close, with the next highest being Kade Anderson at $104. I love Seth and think the stuff is definitely good enough for him to be the future #1 prospect in baseball, but given the track record of prep arms there's no way I could pay this before he throws a pitch professionally. Could be wrong here and he could be another Konnor Griffin where I expect some growing pains and a chance to buy low and it never happens, but my gut tells me we'll get a better price on this in the next few years before he debuts. One guy you don't hear much about that I'm watching for this season is

players.name: Khristian Curtis
players.note: Was nearly forced to medically retire back in 2021, ends up recovering from a strange surgery mishap and gets drafted out of Arizona St. in 2023. Watched him this spring and his stuff is unreal, some of the best in the system. He's 6'5" with a five pitch mix including a cutter, slider, and changeup which all produced 40% or higher whiff rates last year. Great under the radar breakout pick for the Pirates in 2026.

players.name: Ethan Salas
players.note:
When 2023 Bowman Chrome came out he was one of the biggest chases we've seen in a recent product and that's because some outlets were ranking him as a top 10 prospect at age 17 causing his base autograph to sell for $400 during release week. Not that I was ever a hater but I'm not sure he ever cracked my top 25 at that time which I got a lot of hate for, but now I feel like I'm on the right side of history. I actually still really like Salas and I don't know that anyone has had this much prospect fatigue while still a teenager. It feels like he's been around forever but he's only 19. Part of what caused his massive hype in 2023 was that the Padres moved him to Double-A at age 17, something you never see. Unfortunately, he played the same number of games in AA at age 19 that he did at 17 and he's still a work in progress. While his stock is down that's still a very advanced level to play at as a teenager and his combination of plus defense behind the plate and plus raw power is very exciting. He had some back issues but is reportedly fully healthy entering 2026 where this could be the bounce back year we're hoping for. If he plays well I do think there's a great chance these cards go up since he did have so much hype a couple years ago, but considering he's still outside my top 100 hitters $50 on a base autograph is too steep for me.

Shout out to friend of the program and new Padre

players.name: Jase Bowen
players.note:
who has been lighting it up this spring hitting .304 with 4 HR, 6 SB, and a 151 wRC+. He's tearing the cover off the ball and is one of only a few players in all of baseball with 20+ batted balls over 95 mph in Spring Training. I mentioned him in an offseason article predicting sneaky call-ups as he was my pick for the Padres and his prices have gone up since then. He's coming off his best professional season and could start the year in AAA El Paso which is a hitter friendly park in a very hitter friendly league in the PCL. I think we'll see Jase make his MLB debut this year and we'll all be rooting for him when that day comes! Who knows maybe he'll be a guest on a podcast episode between now and then… 

It pinged my attention that

players.name: Ryan Wideman
players.note:
was the only Padres hitter not named Ethan Salas ranked by either Dynasty Dugout or Rotowire so I looked a little deeper and he seems like a fun hobby lottery ticket. Played two years in junior college before transferring to Western Kentucky where he hit .398 with 10 HR, 45 SB, and a 160 wRC+. He became the first D-I player in the last 25 years to have 35+ extra-base hits and 45+ steals in a season and he did so in just 60 games. He's an extremely athletic 6'5" outfielder who could have good power and double plus speed. Wideman is a dice roll since his hitting mechanics and approach looked shaky at WKU despite the great stats. Will need to improve that stuff but not a bad upside hold because of the athleticism.

Coming out of the 2024 MLB draft one of the players I was most frequently asked, "will he have a card in Bowman Draft", about was

players.name: Kale Fountain
players.note: Another 6'5" prospect with really good tools. Struggled in his debut between CPX & A hitting .226 with a 87 wRC+ but he did go 21 for 22 on stolen base attempts showing off that good speed. He's extremely physical for his age and could grow into 60+ power making him a great high ceiling stash but his development could take some time so I think we have time to wait and see how those numbers look early on in 2026.

players.name: Jhoan De La Cruz
players.note:
is really only a 3/5 because I'm so picky when it comes to DSL prospects and wanting to see them in the states first, but he's really close. He's a 5'9" switch-hitter whose defense at shortstop and second base are solid but his Bowman value will come down to how much power we see as he matures. Though he only hit 1 HR in his DSL debut he had a 135 wRC+ thanks to a 23.2% walk rate. I know the pitching is bad in that league but showing the patience at age 17 to control the zone and draw 46 walks in 51 games is really impressive. Hopefully we see it translate this year in the CPX.

The last hold that I wanted to give some love to is

players.name: Ty Harvey
players.note: a high school catcher who the Padres took in the fifth round last year but signed for $1.5 million which was more than triple the slot value at his pick. Looked great on the circuits and at the combine where he hit three balls over 400 ft. with a Max EV of 110.5. Great raw power and doesn't chase much though there is some disagreement on where the hit tool will land. Still think he's a great player to keep an eye on for this season.

players.name: Kash Mayfield
players.note:
Well, if your team is only going to have one player as a 'buy' you might as well make it count! I actually love this play. Based on the ranking and price Mayfield is almost identical in both to Charlee Soto (MIN) who I already raved about as a 5/5, so as much as I liked him is how much I like Kash. Drafted in the first round at 24th overall in 2024 Mayfield is a big 6'4" lefty who signed for a touch under $3.5 million out of high school. He was a repeat winner of the Gatorade Player of the Year award in the state of Oklahoma taking in home in both 2023 and 2024. It wasn't just on the mound where he excelled, Kash also hit .476 with 13 doubles, 11 triples, 21 stolen bases, and a 1.593 OPS in 33 games his senior year. But that's nothing in comparison to the pitching numbers which were so good they almost don't look real. That season Mayfield went 8-0 with a 0.16 ERA. He gave up a grand total of 4 hits and 1 earned run in 44 innings. In those 44 innings he struck out 115 hitters while walking only 8 (14.38 K/BB???), holding opponents to a .030 batting average. If you're doing the math on those 115 K's in 44 innings that means he averaged 2.61 strikeouts PER INNING. Silly. The lefty sits low-to-mid-90's touching 97 but it's his changeup that is his best pitch, with a 70 grade from some evaluators, which he throws with deceptively similar arm speed as his fastball before it dives off a cliff late. He also throws a slider/curveball "slurve" if you will that is his third pitch and has been effective as well. In his professional debut last year in Single-A he had a 2.97 ERA in 19 starts with a 13.05 K/9 and 4.15 BB/9. Mayfield had a 23.3% K-BB% and struck out 88 of the 258 batters he faced (34.1%) while holding opponents to a .203 average against him. There were only three pitchers age 20 or younger last year who pitched 60+ minor league innings with a K/9 over 13. They were Johnny King (TOR), Thomas White (MIA), and Kash Mayfield, and Mayfield's walk percentage was 3% lower than both of the others. He also has the cheapest Bowman autograph of the three by quite a bit. His velocity was down a little last year due to a shoulder issue but I've actually heard reports that not only is it back to normal but that this spring it's been up over 3 mph from where he was prior. I'm not sure how much you can read into this but I do find it interesting that while selling all of their prospects at the 2024 and 2025 MLB trade deadlines Kash Mayfield is really the only one of the Padres top prospects other than Ethan Salas that they've held onto both times. I think there could be something special here. I don't think we saw the best version of Mayfield in his MLB debut and even then the results were very, very good. Put me down as one of the conductors of the Kash Mayfield hype train this year.

I can't lie I'm a little tempted by

players.name: Humberto Cruz
players.note: and seeing Dynasty Dugout rank him near their top 300 definitely gave me consideration to buy at this price. Signed in the same international class as Leo De Vries, Cruz pitched in the CPX & Single-A last year as an 18-year-old. The stat lines aren't impressive and the results were inconsistent but he did flash some stuff that makes him a name worth watching. Easy delivery that's athletic and should allow him to have at least average command. His fastball sat mid-90's while reaching higher but it was actually his slider and changeup which looked like his best pitches. I think both could be 55-60 grade and the slider had a 58% whiff rate last year, and again he was the age of your typical high school senior. Unfortunately he had internal brace surgery in August so I'm not sure what the timeline looks like or when we'll see him again. Since the results didn't really pop and he's injured I'm not sure now is the time to buy but based on how he looks when he returns he could be a sneaky name.

players.name: Colt Emerson
players.note:
I've obviously loved him as a prospect for quite some time now and I still think most prospect outlets underrate him. The improvements he made in the second half last year after some swing adjustments look to be for real and he should be ranked as a top 10 prospect by everybody in my opinion. Unfortunately with a short printed auto he's already well above $200 and since he should debut in the first half of the season it feels like the window to generate more hype prior to that is closing. 

This could be a big year for Felnin Celesten and I would venture to say that he has the most upside of any of my 3's. Extremely high hobby ceiling as a switch-hitting shortstop with good power but between injuries and having to correct an extreme ground ball rate we have yet to see him at his best. He's a name to watch early on though because if we see all of the tools on display he could get some helium quickly, and since his base autograph was selling for $75 one year ago the path to it doubling from $45 honestly isn't a crazy one. Just tough for me to buy at this price with how little I've seen but for those of you who don't mind rolling the dice a little this is a nice target.

I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw recent sales for

players.name: Lazaro Montes
players.note:
When you consider that nothing makes the hobby buzz quite like baseballs being hit a country mile, it feels odd that Montes' stock seems to be going down. On last year's sheet he had a $76 base autograph following a season where at age 19 he hit .288 with 21 HR and a 137 wRC+. All he did last year as a follow-up was launch 32 homers while batting .241 with a 136 wRC+ between A+ & AA. Is it the batting average drop that caused his card price to come down? I don't know how it could be, nobody who watches Laz could ever mistake him for someone who was going to bat .290 at higher levels. The tool we want here is power and it is BIG. He took an already impressive .196 ISO and increased it to a ridiculous .263 last year at age 20 while playing much of his time at an advanced level for his age. There were only five hitters in the minors last year who hit 30+ HR. Three of the five were age 25 or older. Then you had Spencer Jones at 24 and Laz Montes at… 20. He's putting up power numbers that are only being matched by players that are more than four years older than him. It's outrageous. 

Of course the issues with Laz, as with most other hitters who have similar profiles, are that his contact rates are always below 70% and his strikeout rates are always over 25%, but make up your mind Bowman people. If you'll pay top dollar for top of the scale power even if it comes with contact questions (which you always have in the past), then I'm not sure how Montes isn't a $100+ base autograph guy. One way you can offset high strikeout rates is by also being patient enough to draw walks. I get much more worried about players who are striking out 30% of the time if they're also walking under 10% of the time, but Laz has had a walk rate over 14% in all four of his professional seasons. Over the last four minor league seasons here is each instance of a player hitting 30+ HR with a wRC+ over 135 at age 20 or younger. 2025 Lazaro Montes, 2023 Junior Caminero. The end. I almost feel like there might be some prospect fatigue with Montes as we've been watching him hit moonshots since he was 17 and now it's so expected that we aren't excited anymore? But we should be. He hit 14 HR with a .221 ISO last year at AA playing in a home park in Arkansas which ranked DEAD LAST among all 30 AA parks in terms of how hitter friendly it is per Baseball American's Park Factors. When he gets to the PCL this year his HR total might go crazy. I think he breaks the 30 HR mark again and if he does so while reaching AAA I don't know how his card could possibly not go up.

players.name: Michael Arroyo
players.note:
I've said in years past that in my opinion Michael Arroyo is the most slept on hitting prospect in baseball, so when I talked to Ryan Sloan and asked him who was a sneaky bat in this system I loved that this is who he chose. Now I will say that Arroyo did finally get some of the recognition that he's been deserving. I made him a 5/5 rated buy last year at $28 and his card prices are now up 100% so that goal is accomplished. Call me crazy though I don't think he's done. According to Scout the Statline's Peak Projections which use minor league production to predict major league success, they have Arroyo as their 19th best hitting prospect which actually puts him ahead of Colt Emerson. And when you look at the results it is tough to argue. Since his professional debut in the DSL back in 2022 here is Michael Arroyo's wRC+ each year: 162, 129, 147, 139. Back in 2024 at age 19 Arroyo hit 23 HR while adding 18 SB. Not only was he the only teenage prospect to hit both of those marks that season, it wasn't accomplished by a single player last year, not even Konnor Griffin. As a shorter middle infielder I don't think he's ever gotten the respect he deserves for how much power he's capable of hitting for, but don't mistake being short for being small.

Although I mentioned that Laz was still able to drop bombs while playing at the least hitter friendly park in AA, Arroyo did see his power numbers fall off when he made the move from Everett to Arkansas. Despite that he finished the year hitting .262 with 17 HR, 12 SB, 12.4% BB, 18.7% K, and .171 ISO between A+ & AA. He also improved his contact rates for the fourth consecutive season and the 79.6% he posted in AA is the highest he's had at any stop in his career so far. Since Laz can hit bombs anywhere, the move up to AAA which they'll both likely see this year will be an even bigger help for Arroyo who should see his HR numbers bounce back nicely. Last year there were only five prospects who had a 15+HR/10+SB season at age 20 or younger while finishing with a wRC+ over 135. Only three of those five did so while reaching Double-A. Konnor Griffin, Kevin McGonigle, and Michael Arroyo. It's not too often I'll go to bat for a guy and double down on him being a buy even after he's gone up 100%, but I've always believed in the skills here so there's no reason to stop now.

players.name: Jonny Farmelo
players.note:
If I'm being totally honest this is the pick that gave me the most pause of anybody in this entire franchise. Based on the autograph price and my ranking he's actually pretty close to being a 3, teetering on a 4, but due to his ceiling he could also be a 5. That's because it's been a bit of a mixed bag as far as what we've seen from Farmelo since he was drafted but among all of the questions you could have about him one thing that can't be argued is that he's one of the best athletes in all of the minor leagues. Even before he made his professional debut the fascination with Konnor Griffin was that despite the tools being raw, the combination of power and speed was so good that he'd be a unicorn IF he reached his full potential. Now nobody is on Konnor's level but if you were to make a list of the minor league players with the next best combinations of power and speed you might not be more than one or two names in before you got to Jonny Farmelo. Drafted in 2023 he was one of the three prep bats the Mariners used top 30 picks on along with Colt Emerson and Tai Peete, and they went over slot to sign Farmelo for $3.2 million.

Since being drafted we haven't seen much of Farmelo because a string of injuries has kept him off the field. He was not able to play in his draft year and was limited to 46 games the following year where he had a 127 wRC+ in Single-A at age 19 in his professional debut. Entering last season there were high hopes in the organization for him but again he missed a significant portion of time with an injury. He ended up playing in only 29 games where he hit .230 with a 102 wRC+ in High-A but if you split the stats around the injury they tell two entirely different stories. In the first 8 games of the season Farmelo hit 5 HR and started the year with a 1.111 OPS in April and .931 OPS in May. Unfortunately he then missed nearly two and a half months and when he returned he struggled, hitting .167 in 54 PA to end the year. Farmelo was patient and made good contact in his debut season but looked much more aggressive last year in A+. The concerns are that the approach and contact need some refinement but he hasn't been able to stay on the field long enough to get the reps needed to improve them. As I said, from a purely numbers and ranking standpoint I may have made him a 3, but it's hard not to take a chance on players who are so genetically gifted they could have #1 prospect type hype if it all clicks. To me that is a ceiling that's often worth chasing.

players.name: Yorger Bautista
players.note:
Now I will preface this by saying Bautista was believed by many to have the best package of tools of any prospect in the 2025 international signing class. Prior to signing there were international scouts who said his bat speed was the best they had seen at that level in the past five years. Along with that he clocks plus run times and has a rifle for a throwing arm. Unfortunately his DSL debut wasn't very strong (91 wRC+, 29.8% K). He was selling for closer to $20-25 until last Friday's Spring Breakout game when he went 2-3 with three batted balls that were 100+ mph including a triple and a homer. Very, very exciting young player but I haven't seen nearly enough to go in that this price yet.

Obviously we all know about

players.name: Nick Becker
players.note:
My cheapest buy of the Mariners hitters might be a bit of a sneaky pick but I really like everything that I heard and saw when I looked into Seattle's second round pick from last year Nick Becker. He was actually in strong consideration for my top 20 hitters when I did my 2025 Bowman Draft preview but was the first man out and instead ended up as the top selection for the follow up section, 'High Upside Stashes'. Becker is a 6'4" high school shortstop who is a really good athlete. His tools were on display when he performed well against top competition on the showcase circuits and he's often praised for being a "student of the game". That should come as no surprise given that his dad Jeff played both collegiately and at the minor league level, and his older brother Eric is currently the starting shortstop at University of Virginia where he's batting .340 this season. Growing up around the game has given Nick an advanced feel for it along with great instincts and ability to make adjustments.

Depending on where you look you'll see a variety of different scout grades but I think a realistic expectation could be 50 Hit, 50 Power, 60 Speed, and that's with above average defense at shortstop. If you consider that he's still growing into his 6'4" frame and FanGraphs has his projected raw power as a 55, this could wind up being a very, very nice hobby prospect. I'm not going to say that I like him as much but I think that the bones are here for a Cooper Pratt type prospect, another player I'm higher on than the consensus. Pratt is a similar story in that we've seen all of the tools flash except the power but his big frame gives us something to dream on. I think when it comes to chasing high school hitters in Bowman there is a lot of guess work and the best you can do is look for boxes that you like to see checked and find players who check the majority of them. Becker is one of those for me. For what it's worth too the Mariners are pretty sharp when it comes to finding high school talent that slips out of the first round that they can sign over slot. In the second round in 2024 they took Ryan Sloan at pick 55 and gave him $3 million, nearly double the slot value. In the second round in 2025 they took Nick Becker at pick 57 and gave him $2.75 million, more than 1.5x the slot value. Good tools, good makeup, good baseball background, and the Mariners have been developing well. Good stuff for under $20.

Not much to say about

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note:
and how great of a talent he is but there's so much value that can be found with pitchers and most of them come with a much cheaper entry point. It's all personal preference but I'm almost never going to buy a non-debuted arm with a base autograph that's already $100 even if they are in my top 3.

My gap between Anderson and friend of the program

players.name: Ryan Sloan
players.note:
is much smaller than some may think with them only two spots apart. At their current price points I do think that Sloan is a better buy than Kade but he's also now in a hold range for me. Prior to the start of Spring Training Ryan's base autograph was selling for a little over $30 and I mentioned him multiple times in pitching articles last year as being a "Best Buy" or "Most Slept On" of all my top pitchers. That price has since doubled with how great he's looked all spring and while it could keep moving if he's dominant again this year it's already pretty up there so I'm probably waiting until next offseason to try and buy a dip to add more. If I had to guess I would say that this time next year Sloan will be my #1 pitching prospect in baseball.

When talking cards with Ryan I asked him for a sneaky deep, deep sleeper that I could throw out in my futures Mariners article. The first name he gave me was

players.name: Teddy McGraw
players.note:
who has absolutely electric stuff but has missed quite a bit of time with injuries. Seattle is moving him to the bullpen this year and though he's never thrown an inning above High-A, Sloan said he could be a dark horse candidate to make it to the MLB this year as a reliever telling me that McGraw has, in his opinion, the best slider in baseball. I'm always down for a fun cheap chase. 

I'll start at the top with the only Padres prospect with a Bowman autograph over $15 and that's

players.name: Josuar Gonzalez
players.note:
refractor auto after I talked with Jim Callis and he kind of raved about him and Luis Hernandez. From a numbers perspective though I'm not sure I can get there. I do think that he deserves to be ranked quite a bit higher than any other prospects from last year's international class but even then this price is steep. There's two ways to spin this. He might be so good this year that he's a top 10 prospect next year and this base autograph is over $100, but also I always temper my expectations on guys coming from the DSL and $70 for a base autograph of a player who is barely inside my top 50 is steep. Again, I bought one but only because he's a player I'm personally willing to roll the dice on, in the name of finding value versus my rankings he's in a hold range.

Nothing against

players.name: Bo Davidson
players.note:
Nothing I love more then a good prospect story and Bo Davidson is one of those. He was signed as an undrafted free agent out of Caldwell Community College and Technical Institute where he slashed .412/.508/.876 with 16 homers as a sophomore. After that he went on to play in the Coastal Plains league but it was only for a span of 10 games and he struggled there batting just .182. However, there was a Giants scout who watched him play and liked what he saw enough to give him a shot and boy does that guy deserve a raise because what a find. In 2024 at Single-A Davidson hit .328 with 9 HR, a .280 ISO, and 173 wRC+ in 226 PA. While that's dominant it wasn't quite enough to get him on my radar since he was 21-years-old playing in A ball. What he did last year however shot him way up my list. Davidson split time between A+ & AA where across both levels he hit .281 with 18 HR, 19 SB, 13% BB, 22.8% K, .187 ISO, and 137 wRC+. If you compare that to other players age 22 or younger last year, only five matched those 18 HR/19 SB marks and had a strikeout rate under 23%. They were Konnor Griffin, Eduardo Quintero, Ryan Waldschmidt, Joshua Baez, and Kaelen Culpepper. The last three are the same age as Bo and they're all more expensive than him.

There aren't a ton of red flags when it comes to the approach or contact numbers with Davidson and in just two years he's gone from virtually unknown in the world of baseball to "one of the best pure hitters in the Giants system" per MLB Pipeline. He's a bit old for a hobby prospect now that he's 23 but his great combination of power and speed should help continue to improve his hobby value this season. I think both of those tools are at least above average and I wouldn't at all be surprised if we saw a 20/20 season out of him this year. I still do have some concerns about whether all of this production will continue to translate as he climbs to the upper levels of the minors because it feels hard to believe that somebody this talented can seemingly appear out of nowhere, but I have a hard time doubting him. I mean how could you? He was at Caldwell Community College and Technical Institute just three years ago. Two years ago he was a 21-year-old who started the year in the Complex League. Today he's inside my top 50 non-debuted hobby hitters. I don't put any personal emotion into my rankings but you just don't see jumps like this often in the world of baseball and it makes it really hard not to root for him at every stop.

players.name: Jhonny Level
players.note:
During the 2024 international signing period Jhonny Level drew comps to Rafael Furcal from scouts and was thought to be a strong defensive SS with good speed. From what we've seen early on though it sure looks like people were sleeping on his bat when he signed for under $1 million. In his professional debut in the DSL, Level hit .275 with 10 HR, 18 SB, 14% BB, 16.7% K, .242 ISO, and 143 wRC+. As someone who is a hater of DSL stats even I saw the line and was like, "well, damn". That year the only qualified DSL hitters with an ISO over .220, strikeout rate under 18%, and 10+ SB were Jesus Made and Jhonny Level. It's not uncommon to see good bat-to-ball hitters who don't project for good power show some early on against poor pitching so there were still questions about how legitimate that power was when he came to the states. Last year in the CPX at 18 he hit .288 with 9 HR an 17 SB in just 58 games. In those 261 PA he had a 12.6% BB, 15.3% K, .205 ISO, and 121 wRC+. That .205 ISO was the highest among all 18-year-old prospects in the CPX who had 200+ PA, even ahead of Emil Morales (LAD) at .197 who happens to have double plus power projections. Level looked so good there that the Giants opted to promote him to Single-A where he helped San Jose win the California League title.

The switch-hitting Level is probably still somewhat slept on in Bowman due to his 5'8" frame as many people will see smaller hitters and assume there's no power, something that delayed the hobby breakout of Seattle's Michael Arroyo in my opinion. But Level can swing it. I think all five of the tools are really strong here. Great feel for the barrel, controls the zone well, plays good defense, has good speed, and there's surprising pop which could translate to 20+ HR one day. This is a fantastic hobby profile for a player who will still be 19 for all of this season and has a base autograph that isn't even over $30. There were only two prospects last year in all of the minors who were members of the 10 HR/20 SB club at age 18 or younger. They were Edward Florentino (PIT) who sadly does not have a Bowman card but was so dominant last year he catapulted his way into my top 10 hobby hitters, and Jhonny Level. If you expand it to include 19-year-olds the list grows to nine names with some big time additions like Konnor Griffin, Sebastian Walcott, Eduardo Quintero, and Caleb Bonemer. The lowest strikeout rate in the entire group? Jhonny Level's 17.2%. If you keep ending up on lists with names like this then you're doing something right. Teammate Josuar Gonzalez is the more exciting prospect of the two for sure, but he's double the price and I don't think the gap is quite that big.

players.name: Dakota Jordan
players.note: as a buy because he is a freak athlete. FanGraphs has him at possible 70 power and 70 speed which is Konnor Griffin territory. Last year he hit 14 HR with 27 SB and a 135 wRC+. Sounds crazy good. On the flip side he was 22-years-old and in Single-A. He also had a 0.39 BB/K because he's extremely aggressive. There's big time upside here no doubt but there is still a lot of refinement needed in this hit tool and when you consider that and his age I can't get there at $20.

players.name: Gavin Kilen
players.note:
has been selling pretty well in 2025 Bowman Draft and he has two great things going for him outside of his play on the field and that's that he was a top 15 pick and that he played at University of Tennessee, a college with arguably the best hobby fanbase that tends to prop its players up. Unfortunately I think Kilen falls into the category of being a better real life baseball player than hobby name. Good hit tool, good speed, but he's going to have below average power and that limits his upside for us. At $10 I'd be in but he's double that and I'm not sure I love it.

Not many Giants prospects of late have had the hobby buzz that

players.name: Rayner Arias
players.note:
had back when 2023 Bowman Chrome was released as he posted one of the craziest 76 PA samples in the DSL we've seen (.379 ISO, 233 wRC+). Unfortunately he's played a combined 79 games over the past two years. His stats are trending in the wrong direction, and maybe that's because he hasn't been healthy, but at $15 he would need to show some signs of life before I bought anything.

If I had to give a 3 to put a pin in and say you need to watch him early this year it's probably

players.name: Jesus Rodriguez
players.note:
How could I make a Giants list and leave off one of my OG underrated prospects and that's Jesus Rodriguez. Back to his time on the Yankees I've always been fascinated by the offensive profile here. He's a C/3B/DH and you wouldn't know it by looking at him but he's quietly one of the best contact hitters that you're going to find at the minor league level. Signing for just $10,000 out of Venezuela back in 2019, Rodriguez got a late start to stateside baseball since the 2020 season was cancelled due to COVID forcing him to play in the DSL at age 19 the following year. The production we've seen since then will make you wonder why you've never heard him talked about by anyone (except probably me). In his six professional seasons he's never hit below .294, with a string of now four straight years where he's hit over .305. It's strange for a catcher or corner infielder to be hit-over-power but that's what makes him so different. That doesn't mean there's no power though, back in 2024 between A+ & AA Rodriguez hit .302 with 10 HR, 9 SB, 9.9% BB, 14.7% K, .180 ISO, and 146 wRC+ in 79 games. If you throw out the rookie levels only three prospects age 22 or younger that year hit over .300 with an ISO of .180 or higher. They were Kristian Campbell, Luke Keaschall, and Jesus Rodriguez, the first two of course were much more highly regarded prospects. Of those three Rodriguez had the lowest strikeout rate by more than 2.5%. 

This past season while playing in both AA & AAA for the Yankees and AAA for the Giants, he hit .307 with 7 HR, 21 SB, 11.7% BB, 13.8% K, .096 ISO, and 118 wRC+. You hate to see the power go down but on the plus side he stole over 20 bases while posting a contact rate of 85.6% and a 6.9% swinging strike %, both career bests. In his 500+ PA in AAA he was in the 91st percentile for in-zone contact rate with a 91.1%. If you throw Rodriguez a strike he's not going to miss it, and he rarely expands the zone. Of course the argument is that a 23-year-old contact first catcher is not an exciting hobby profile and I understand that, but I think this bat is going to play at the MLB level which is something you can't say confidently about many guys with $10 autographs. The position is unclear. Many in the Yankees organization thought he was best suited for the third base but the Giants plan on getting him more reps at catcher. Eventually though he'll get into a spot that the Cubs are in with Moises Ballesteros where even if his glove isn't ready his bat is too good to be in the minors and they'll call him up. When they do, he's the type of player worth holding past a debut since he won't generate a ton of hype but should be able to produce enough offensively to get some buzz. He's currently hitting .351 this spring with 2 HR and 4 2B in 41 PA (.270 ISO) and a 165 wRC+. It's not a sexy profile but I still think his bat deserves more love and I'm excited to see him potentially make some noise in the Bay Area this year.

I admit that I personally bought a

players.name: Trevor Cohen
players.note:
their third round pick from last year. Had a 5.5% K rate at Rutgers last year. Not a typo. Played 28 games at Single-A in his pro debut and hit .327 with more walks than strikeouts. Very, very solid floor under $10 because of his advanced hit tool and contact skills but similar to Sam Antonacci you'd be crossing your fingers for some power to pop if you're expecting big time gains. Wouldn't be too crazy though…

My favorite dart throw for the price in this organization is

players.name: Lisbel Diaz
players.note: Really good tools for a 20-year-old with an autograph under $5 but the hit tool is shaky. Too aggressive at the plate and often swings at pitches he has no business offering at, but he crushes fastballs with really good exit velocities. Still able to put the bat on a lot of bad pitches when he chases (77.5% contact) but drew walks in less than 6% of his PA last year. With that said, he had 10 HR/29 SB at age 19 so if he improves the plate discipline he could be a steal for $4, but that's always a risky profile to mess with.

players.name: Diego Velasquez
players.note:
are both very sneaky for $2-3. They're not ranked high but I don't see how you lose money on either of them. Not super exciting but good enough that their cards should go up.

Of the Giants pitchers the one I'm definitely the most interested in is

players.name: Jacob Bresnahan
players.note: Big 6'3" lefty who came over in a trade from the Guardians and may have two plus pitches in his fastball and changeup. Won pitcher of the year in the ACL in 2024 and again in the California League in Single-A last year. 2.61 ERA and 12.00 K/9 last season were both really strong. Will be watching early this year to see if he adds velocity (low-90's last year) to a fastball that already plays up due to great IVB. Needs to improve his command and also needs to develop a good third pitch if he's going to stick as a starter but I think the upside is definitely there. Would have really liked this under $10.

players.name: JJ Wetherholt
players.note: Love the player and am very excited to watch him play at the MLB level but unfortunately I unload almost everything I own when a player makes it to the show and now that his time has come to be an Opening Day starter he will be removed from my lists. Wishing him nothing but the best and I expect him to have a great major league career! (He just went deep for his first career hit while I was editing this which was pretty damn cool.)

players.name: Rainiel Rodriguez
players.note:
You know that at $75 and inside my top 10 I was tempted to go 5/5 on Rainiel but him being a catcher and me not having a huge sample of data to work with makes me want to stick him at 4, but it's certainly close, and I wouldn't blame people at all for going hard on his cards. Rodriguez signed for $300k back in 2023 and has had arguably the best first two seasons I've seen from an international prospect since I began collecting Bowman cards. In his DSL debut in 2024 he hit .345 with 10 HR, 16.3% BB, 13.6% K, .338 ISO, and 185 wRC+. Pretty outrageous. Across every minor league level that year there were 1,773 prospects who got 180+ PA. Only 1 of those 1,773 had an ISO over .300 and more walks than strikeouts. Rainiel Rodriguez. "But it's the DSL!", they cried, and they're right, I'm a noted DSL hater. What we saw last year when Rodriguez came to the states though was arguably more impressive when you consider the step up in pitching he faced. At age 18 he hit .276 with 20 HR, 4 SB, 14.7% BB, 17.7% K, .279 ISO, and 162 wRC+. This isn't just the CPX either. The Cardinals only kept him there for 20 games before he was so dominant with a .458 ISO and 238 wRC+ that they had to promote him early to Single-A. All he did there was have a .249 ISO and 145 wRC+ in 271 PA leading St. Louis to move him up again to play the final week of the season in High-A at age 18. 

This is outrageous power production for an 18-year-old especially when you consider how much of the damage he did at a level that should be advanced for him. Luckily for us the Florida League where he played in Single-A is the only league at that level with ABS so we have Statcast data from his games there. 94th percentile xSLG, 90th percentile MaxEV, 87th percentile Barrel %, 95th percentile Pull Air %. 18-years-old… wild. Because he generates so much bat speed and has such great upper body strength there is almost zero wasted movement in the lower half and it allows him to make contact pretty consistently. Last year in Single-A he had a 78.3% contact rate and swung and missed only 9.6% of the time. Running an ISO that high while striking out in less than 18% of your PA is crazy impressive. The more I write the more I'm almost convinced I should ignore what I said earlier and make him a 5/5. While the hobby doesn't love catchers I do think there's a scenario where his bat is so good that it's not worth keeping him down to work on his defense and they'll just teach him 1B or let him DH. FanGraphs has minor league data back to 2006. If you sort it looking for any single season where a prospect age 18 or younger had 300+ PA with an ISO over .275 you get two results in twenty years: 2008 Giancarlo Stanton and 2025 Rainiel Rodriguez. This kid might just mash.

players.name: Joshua Baez
players.note:
Baez is definitely defying the odds here. Is it possible that a player could go up 1,000% in a calendar year and still be undervalued? Logic says no way, but my rankings would say yes. I can't say that I was on Baez prior to last season but I definitely caught on pretty quickly to his huge improvements at the plate. In my July 2025 article, "Top 10 High Upside Buys Under $20" he was on the list with a $16 base autograph, so while I didn't get in at the bottom we're still up over 250% since then. There aren't many paths to having a meteoric climb like we've seen with Baez but one way is to be a genetic freak who drastically improves their hit tool. Now I've said hundreds of times in the past you always take the Kevin McGonigle/Sam Antonacci type and hope they grow into power because guys with big time power who can't make contact aren't going to magically learn how to, but one of the VERY few exceptions to that is Joshua Baez. Here are the strikeout rates for Baez in his first four professional seasons. 29.5%, 36.1%, 34.1%, 35.5%. His contact rates those years? 41%, 52.9%, 65%, 65%. Yuck. This is how you end up with a $5 base autograph. What I don't think anyone saw coming was that last year at age 22 between A+ & AA, Baez had a 20.6% K rate and 76% contact rate. After not being able to make contact for YEARS he improved his strikeouts by 15% and his overall contact by 11%. File this under things you never see.

Of course when your tools are already really loud and you improve your quality of contact as much as Baez did then all of your good HR/SB totals that nobody cared about before because you were batting .220 are now exciting. Not only did those upward trends in his contact cause his batting average to rise by 40 points but his improved bat path led to more consistent hard contact and he also saw a 50 point jump in his ISO. When all was said and done across both levels last year Baez hit .287 with 20 HR, 54 SB, 11.8% BB, 20.6%, .213 ISO, and 145 wRC+. I know a $58 base autograph might not seem cheap but given this production he's not nearly given the credit he deserves. Do you know how many prospects had a 20 HR/50 SB season last year? Two. Konnor Griffin and Joshua Baez. He moves extremely well for his size (6'3", 220), has double plus raw power, a plus arm, and now seemingly out of nowhere might have an average hit tool to go with it all. Assuming all of the improvements we saw are real, which I don't doubt, I think his card price going up 1,000% was actually light as crazy as that sounds. The hobby loves a power/speed combo and there are very few minor leaguers capable of going 20/50. He has the high end power to put balls into orbit which is helpful because those video clips that go viral on social media can do wonders for your prices. It looks like Baez will start the year in AAA and given the state of their current MLB depth chart I'm not sure how long he's there if he hits like he did last year.

players.name: Ryan Mitchell
players.note:
are an interesting trio in that all of their base autographs are priced similarly and all of them are ranked within about 15 spots of each other in my rankings. I still like Blaze as a player but he really started to break out last year and though his prices went up at times he never really was able to see a huge jump. As a player who was a main chase in 2021 Bowman I think there's some prospect fatigue here. He's been a hobby name for too long, was in the same class as Coby Mayo and even he feels like his hobby peak was years ago. Really made strides with his contact skills which I love to see and will likely debut this year so you have that in your back pocket if you're holding his cards, but I think the buying window in closing. He's another player I'll be watching closely as a pro and rooting for though! Bernal is a switch-hitting catcher who is sneaky good offensively. Had 13 HR and a K rate under 17% last year and you don't often see catchers with near 80% contact rates but that's exactly what he does. Will need to see a jump in the power for this price to gain some steam. I thought he would be closer to a $10 guy and we'd have a nice under the radar buy but the Cards fans are pretty sharp and have boosted him up to $20. He deserves it but not sure I'm buying there unless I see some more pop this year. Of the trio Mitchell is the most exciting and is closest to a buy. Second round pick last year out of high school and he may have 55 Hit, 50 Power, and 60 speed. Really good bat speed and exit velocities but has more of a line drive swing. If he can generate some more loft and that bat speed can produce above average game power he'll be a really good grab, but I need to see him play professionally.

Neither of them did much in their professional debuts but under $5 I'd keep tabs on

players.name: Tai Peete
players.note:
Peete is a perfect example when it comes to one of my favorite sayings that applies in the hobby, "you can't teach size and speed". I mentioned in the Mariners article that Jonny Farmelo is a buy for me because he's just such a good athlete that you have to factor in that ceiling. Of course most players won't actually reach their ceiling but the ones that often pop and go up 1,000% are usually able to do so because they have a unique blend of raw tools that come together. Funny enough the Mariners took Farmelo and Peete with back-to-back picks in the 2023 draft at 29th and 30th, but Peete was moved this offseason to the Cardinals in the Brendan Donovan deal. Though he's not as highly regarded of a prospect as Farmelo he does also have the plus power and speed, only with a shakier hit tool. He's still very raw developmentally but given the improvements we just saw Joshua Baez make I wouldn't say anything is impossible and hopefully the Cardinals have a plan here. Peete is fooled often by offspeed pitches and swings over the top of them, and since he can get aggressive he doesn't walk a ton. This creates a fairly large gap between this walks and strikeouts (8.7% BB, 30.6% K last year).

I could give you a laundry list of red flags in his hitting data. He batted .217 last year, I told you the BB/K split, his contact rate was 69.9%, his wRC+ was 79. There are two things working very heavily in his favor though for ranking hobby prospects, his athleticism is fantastic and he's been young for every level he's played at. As an August birthday he was still 17 when he got drafted by the Mariners. All of those stats above may have been bad last year but he played the entire season in High-A at age 19 and he put together a 19 HR/25 SB season with a .187 ISO. There were only three teenage prospects last year who hit both of those HR and SB totals at any level. Konnor Griffin, Eduardo Quintero, and Tai Peete. Peete also had more PA above Single-A than either one of them. You hold your nose when you see his .217 average and 30% K rate next to those other guys but again, size and speed can't be taught. I just said about Baez that there aren't many prospects who are capable of putting up a 20/50 season but if the Cardinals are able to make similar improvements to Peete's approach and contact skills he could be one of them. If he was a $30 guy he's probably a 3 because the floor is too low but I'd argue that there is not a better combination of power and speed in all of minor league baseball for under $20 right now. This is a high risk play but many of the fun gains are.

players.name: Yairo Padilla
players.note:
Back in 2024 the Cardinals signed Padilla for $760k and he wasn't ranked in MLB Pipeline's top 50 for his international class. This turned out to be a sneaky find for St. Louis as the switch-hitting shortstop hit .287 with a 120 wRC+ in his professional debut in the DSL. Last year playing in the states for the first time he posted similar results batting .283 with a 119 wRC+. One of the biggest green flags when it comes to Padilla was the improvement we saw to his approach. Back in the DSL he swung at 58.5% of the total pitches he saw. He made contact 61.9% of the time and had a swinging strike % of 22.3%. Last year he swung at almost 15% fewer pitches in general (43.9%), his contact rate on those swings went up nearly 20% (80.1%), and his SwStr% dropped from 22.3% to 8.7%. These are huge for an 18-year-old. Due to the more selective approach and better contact he improved his BB/K from 0.59 to 0.86, increasing his walks and dropping his strikeout rate from 17.9% to just 14.2%. He also showed off great speed going 24/28 on stolen base attempts in only 38 games.

If he's a young, switch-hitting shortstop who makes great contact, has a solid approach, and good speed, why are his autographs so cheap? The only way they can be, he hasn't shown any game power yet. In his 300+ PA since becoming a professional Padilla has hit just 1 HR, and that one was in the DSL. Last year he didn't hit any and had just a .083 ISO. Despite this FanGraphs still has a 60 grade potential raw power on him, though MLB Pipeline has it at 45. His lack of power so far is not from a lack of bat speed though as much as it is a launch angle issue. Padilla had a 102.1 mph 90th percentile EV in the CPX last year which is pretty impressive so it's not that he can't hit it hard, he's just hitting too many ground balls. I still really like the athleticism though and this feels like a really good price point for a player with his hobby ceiling. Padilla is going to need to learn how to drive the ball in the air if he's going to produce enough HR power to become a big Bowman name but considering we've already seen every other tool pop and he enters this season still only 18-years-old, it has to make you bullish on him.

players.name: Jesus Baez
players.note:
Another prospect that came over in a trade last season was Baez who they acquired in the Ryan Helsley deal with the Mets. It's tough being an undervalued prospect in the Mets system because once you show signs of promise your cards kind of go nuts, but Baez was one I was always a fan of. Being that I usually like the moves that he makes when it comes to prospects, I felt even better about Baez when Chaim Bloom traded for him. Baez is a shortstop who may be better suited for third base due to his plus arm but fringy range. He has good bat speed and posts above average exit velocities and should have power that falls in the 55-60 range, but how much he'll be able to get to will come down to his quality of contact, and I think it's going to be better than people expect. One of the things I'm big on when it comes to the offense of young players is seeing year-to-year improvements and that's what originally put Baez on my radar back when he was with the Mets. From 2022 through 2024 these were Baez's contact rates: 55.3%, 69.1%, 77.4%. These were his strikeout rates: 21.2%, 17.5%, 16.1%. I don't know that I could ask for more from a teenage prospect and along with those improvements he raised his ISO from .123 in 2023 to .184 in 2024.

Unfortunately, in the midst of a heater in 2024 which saw him get promoted to High-A at 19, Baez tore his meniscus and missed the rest of the season. That year there ended up being 101 teenage prospects who got 300+ PA. Only 19 of those had an ISO over .180. Of those 19 Baez not only had the lowest strikeout rate at 16.1%, but nobody else was even within 3.5% of him. When he came back in 2025 there was a bit of rust as he hit just .187 in April before hitting .341 with 4 HR, a .993 OPS, and a 1.4 BB/K in May. Prior to the trade, even with that bad first month, he had a 126 wRC+, .161 ISO, and 16.7% strikeout rate in High-A, once again improving his contact rate to 80.1%. He did struggle for a little after the trade but it wasn't a huge sample and players up and moving can sometimes take a mental toll. This feels to me like a player who is sneakily improving his approach and contact skills while working around some injury bumps in the road and I still don't think we've seen the best of this bat. I actually really like this get by Bloom. Sometimes when I think a player looks undervalued I will go over and check their Scout the Statline Peak Projections because they do a pretty good job of using advanced analytics to find players who are sneakily good. They have Baez as their 139th ranked prospect which is the highest of any Cardinals hitter with an autograph under $24, and he's way under that at $8. I think he's a good breakout candidate for 2026 and there's some solid value here with such a cheap entry point.

Of course I have nothing negative to say about

players.name: Jack Gurevitch
players.note: this year. Both joined the Cardinals in the 2025 draft class and among the many things that Chaim Bloom did well at Boston one of them was finding talent outside of the first two rounds.

players.name: Liam Doyle
players.note:
who I really like but his price is already pretty steep over $45. Very exciting player but there are definitely concerns, one being that he threw a fastball 65% of the time last year in college. I'm sure the Cardinals are working on his expanding his repertoire but he might only have two above average pitches right now and his delivery is the opposite of effortless, he's bringing everything he's got on every pitch. I know that the Cardinals didn't draft a player with the fifth overall pick that they thought was a reliever but there feels to be a reliever-ish profile to the way Doyle threw in college. University of Tennessee players always do well in Bowman and it's a tax that often crushes their value for me. He's priced the same that Robby Snelling was when I did my Marlins sheet and he's my #2 ranked pitcher. I like the upside because this is an absolutely electric arm, but for this price you'd have to be in my top 10 for me to rate you a buy and Doyle's not there.

There seems to be a trend of the Cardinals having both hitting and pitching prospects I like but their cards are already appropriately priced. Must be a stronger hobby fanbase than I've given them credit for in the past! I like

players.name: Quinn Mathews
players.note:
If I'm buying a Cardinals pitcher prior to this season give me Quinn Mathews who is my 32nd ranked non-debuted pitcher. He's right on the line of a 3 to 4 based on his price at $30 but I think there are more things leaning in his favor for us then there are against us. Mathews was a fourth round pick back in 2023 out of Stanford and you won't see many players climb the prospect ladder in their professional debut quite like he did. That's because he started the year in Single-A before earning THREE promotions in one season and finishing in Triple-A. His final line that year across four levels was a 2.76 ERA, 2.59 FIP, 12.68 K/9, and 3.08 BB/9. He struck out 202 batters in 143.1 innings and was named MLB Pipeline's Pitching Prospect of the Year. Hard to argue with them there. Mathews had a 26.8% K-BB% in 26 starts and not a single one of the 216 qualified pitchers in the minors last year topped that just to give you an idea of how dominant his 2024 was. While it seemed like that season went off without a hitch there was one tiny little detail and that's that after his third promotion to AAA he had a 7.56 BB/9 in his four starts. Big deal, only four starts right?

What we found out last year is that Quinn Mathews has a problem with the ball that they use in AAA and the MLB, something that I also mentioned with Kendry Rojas of the Twins. For whatever reason some guys just struggle with it. It's wound tighter and while some players adjust after a few games it messes with others for longer. Mathews said in an interview while in AAA last year that the IVB on his fastball went from 17 inches to 14-15 with the new ball and while it doesn't sound like a big difference it could be the difference in having an above average fastball versus just an average one. He battled this all year last year and finished the season with a 3.93 ERA, 10.24 K/9, and 7.09 BB/9, seeing his walk percentage rise from 8.6% in 2024 to 16.8% in 2025. It's not ideal but I'm kind of in the camp where I refuse to believe he won't adjust. Mathews is a 6'5" lefty who throws mid-90's from a low release point with good ride. His changeup is the true gem though and has really good separation from his fastball in terms of velocity and grades as a 60-65 pitch. He also mixes in an above average slider and a curveball. Considering he was arguably the most dominant pitcher in the minors the year prior I want to believe that he will recapture that. We saw a glimpse of it earlier this spring when he turned in a performance where he struck out 7 batters in 2.2 innings while only allowing one hit and walking zero. Most notably the IVB on that fastball has been more in the 17-18" range where it was prior to his struggles. On top of all of this the Cardinals pitching rotation is gross and we're almost guaranteed to see some of their AAA staff get called up this year. Given that we're in sort of a buy low spot with Mathews and we'll likely see him this year I feel like he's a great pitcher to target in Bowman.

Tough spot here with

players.name: Tanner Franklin
players.note:
who they drafted last year is a nice sleeper, but both are priced higher than my window I'm looking to buy in. With Hence at 77th I'd want his base autograph at $12-15 and for Franklin at 164th I'm a buyer under $10. Both are trading quite a good percentage over that already.

The best value of the 3's based on my rankings is definitely

players.name: Tekoah Roby
players.note:
who I have as my 82nd ranked pitching prospect and his base autograph is currently only $5. Only issue is that Roby had TJ last July and is probably going to miss all of this season. Very best case scenario is that we see him at the end of this year. That's kind of a dagger to his buying value. If you like buying players low while they're out and holding them for when they return he's not a bad option since he's so cheap and has already reached AAA, but at this point you're probably holding until 2027 so I'm not sure how much money I'd tie up in his cards.

Super sleeper arm to watch in this organization is

players.name: Nate Dohm
players.note: who came over from the Mets with Jesus Baez in the Ryan Helsley trade. Third round pick by the Mets out of Mississippi St. in 2024, he went 4-0 with a 1.23 ERA his final year in college. Last year in his pro debut had a 3.24 ERA, 10.80 K/9, and 3.84 BB/9 between A & A+. Really good fastball and slider but will need a reliable third pitch. He's a name I'm keeping an eye on this year and is probably a sneaky one to hold at under $5.

players.name: Xavier Isaac
players.note:
At the time Isaac was around $20 so that paid off. Very exciting power bat for the Rays with potentially 80 grade raw power, but he's going to strike out. Luckily he draws enough walks to where that BB/K doesn't get too out of control but he ran a 33.3% strikeout rate in 2024. Last July he needed life-saving brain surgery which was crazy and I'm glad he's okay now but he missed much of last season. However in the 175 PA he did have he had a 19.4% BB, 29.7% K, .245 ISO, and 144 wRC+, all of which were improvements from the year prior. Excited to see him fully healthy this year but all things considered he's priced about where he should be for my rankings.

You'll notice the asterisk next to

players.name: Theo Gillen
players.note:
In a system loaded with young talent that I like there is not a non-debuted Bowman hitter that is ranked higher for me than Theo Gillen, their first round pick from the 2024 draft. Gillen struggled to stay healthy in high school missing most of his sophomore and junior years due to injuries. In his senior year he hit .415 with 7 HR and 29 SB at Westlake High and was considered by many to be the best high school hitter in the state of Texas, showing a combination of fantastic contact skills and bat speed. Though he played shortstop in high school some teams were worried about his ability to stick there and the Rays announced him as an outfielder on draft day, deciding from day one that his plus athleticism could play in CF where he's made almost every one of his professional starts. Injuries hurt Gillen again last year as his start to the year was delayed by a calf strain and then in August a wrist injury from sliding into a base ended his season early. What we did see though has me extremely high on him for 2026.

In 73 Single-A games last year Gillen hit .267 with 5 HR, 36 SB, 19.8% BB, 23.1% K, .119 ISO, and 151 wRC+. He controls the zone very well as referenced by that nearly 20% walk rate, swinging at only 34.6% of the pitches he saw. Though he was almost too passive he didn't seem to have an issue putting the bat on the ball when he did swing, with a swinging strike % of just 8.8%. No surprise there since Gillen is praised for his bat-to-ball skills and has a hit tool that is projected as high as 60. He also has 60 speed which he showed off going 36/39 on stolen base attempts. The 6'2" Gillen has shown great gap-to-gap power that has translated to extra base hits and the dream is that as he fills out his frame that turns into home run power. I think it will happen. There were only nine teenage prospects last year who had 300+ PA and a wRC+ over 150. All of the big names you'd expect in Griffin, Quintero, Rainiel, Bonemer, etc. etc. Of the seven of those nine who have a Bowman autograph every one of them except for Theo Gillen has a base auto over $60. And here he sits at half the price. I think if he had a played a full year he'd be in more of these top prospect conversations and if his power trends up at all this year I think it could happen very quickly.

players.name: Brailer Guerrero
players.note:
and that's because neither have base autographs so I used a multiplier from their refractor auto sales to give us an idea of where they'd be priced if they did have base autos. Morgan has a very rare set of tools because he's an incredible defender with a fantastic hit tool but he doesn't hit for much power and he plays primarily first base. In his first full season in 2024 he had a 158 wRC+ while climbing three levels and he only struck out in 11% of his PA. You just don't see a K rate that low anymore especially from a first baseman. Unfortunately he's never had an ISO over .160. I actually love his bat because you don't see pure hitters like this very often anymore. I do think there's still a good ceiling and because the Rays value analytics I do think he'll end up in their MLB lineup this season but his cards already sell pretty well for being outside my top 100. Guerrero on the other hand does have big power, he's extremely physical and was posting 110 mph exit velocities as a teenager. The issue is he hasn't been able to stay healthy. He's about to start his fourth professional season and he's never gotten more than 225 PA in any of them. Here's the crazy part though, he's still only 19 which feels insane when you put it in perspective. I actually think he has one of the highest ceilings in this organization but he needs to improve his contact and him missing so much time early on has not helped. Still a really fun stash because if all of his offensive potential clicked his cards could go nuts, but similar to Morgan he's not exactly cheap.

As a player I really like

players.name: Aidan Smith
players.note:
When you believe in a player's ability and they struggle there are two things you can do, bail or double down. With Aidan Smith's card prices dropping over 50% in the last year I'm going to go with the double down here since he was one of my favorite prospects last offseason. As I've said many times before, "you can't teach size and speed", and like many other high variance prospects in this price range I feel like you have to take a chance on the athleticism here. This is above average power and plus speed all day he just needs to improve his contact skills a bit.
