Back in 2024 Smith was traded from the Mariners to the Rays and between both organizations as a 19-year-old he hit .288 with 11 HR, 41 SB, 14.4% BB, 23.2% K, .185 ISO, and 143 wRC+. Not only did his approach and contact improve drastically from the year prior but they also both trended up in a big way after the trade to Tampa Bay. My feelings were that with a full season in the Rays system everything would keep going in the right direction.

However, last year Smith's production took a step back in High-A at age 20 where he hit .237 with 14 HR, 41 SB, 11.5% BB, 31.2% K, .151 ISO, and 114 wRC+. His BB/K dropped from 0.62 to 0.37 as his walks decreased by 3% and his strikeouts increased by 8%. With that his overall contact rates went down by 5%. These are not things I love to see. Still I can't deny that power/speed sells and having what is considered to be a disappointing year by almost everyone and still going 14 HR/41 SB is kind of amazing. There were only three prospects age 20 or younger who reached both of those marks. Konnor Griffin, Eduardo Quintero, and Aidan Smith. Even if you expand the maximum age to 22 the only player in minor league baseball to go 10 HR/40 SB in consecutive years is Aidan Smith. Though his offense backed up a little his defense improved a ton and while the Rays originally had him pegged as a corner outfield there's now feeling in the organization that he's going to be able to stick in CF where his speed and plus arm will make him an above average defender there. In my last article for the Cardinals I said Tai Peete was worth taking a chance on at $16 for his ceiling alone. Not only is Aidan Smith's ceiling similar but I think his floor is much better. I have him ranked more than 60 spots higher and their autographs are the same price. We missed on the big breakout season last year but I still think it's coming and I know people inside this organization share that sentiment.

players.name: Nathan Flewelling
players.note:
I know I just said in the Cardinals article that I was keeping Rainiel Rodriguez as a 4 instead of a 5 because he's a catcher, but even with that deduction Flewelling is still a 5 for me at $12 given that he is my highest ranked prospect under $20 and even still he's about half of that price. Those of you who follow me on Twitter know I've been a Flewelling fan from day one. The Rays selected him in the third round out of a high school in Alberta, Canada, a province that has produced zero major league hitters. In fact Flewelling said when he was drafted that much of what he had learned defensively behind the plate came from YouTube videos. There was very little available as far as data on him when he was drafted and all I had for stats was a season of summer ball in the Western Canadian Baseball League. Though I admit I have no idea what the competition there is like, he hit .329 with a 1.063 OPS, 5 HR, 15 walks, and 10 strikeouts in 87 PA at age 17. He then showed up to the draft combine and posted the second highest Max EV there. The Rays took him at 94th overall despite him being the 236th ranked draft prospect, and signed him at the full slot value. What we knew before he played an MiLB game: 6'2" frame with great exit velocities, still only 17 when he was drafted, and the Rays loved him. That would have been good enough for me.

When it came to his professional debut it wouldn't be out of the ordinary to see an 18-year-old who has never played in the states go to the CPX, but the Rays immediately assigned him to Single-A which I found interesting. Last year he hit .230 with 6 HR, 9 SB, 20.4% BB, 27.5% K, .111 ISO, and 127 wRC+. Here's why I love that stat line more than you'd expect at first glance. FanGraphs has minor league stats back to 2006. I asked it to show me every prospect who had 300+ PA above rookie levels with a walk rate over 20% at age 18 or younger. It returned one result in 20 years. 2025 Nathan Flewelling. I think his cards are slept on because he hit .230 and the ISO was only .111 but he was 18 until November of last year so he's extremely young for the level AND the Rays let him play the final week of the season in High-A at 18 making him one of only five players with a Bowman card who got 20+ PA at that level at age 18. Of course Leo De Vries, Jesus Made, and Luis Pena are on the list of others. Though we didn't see much power last year we saw it at the combine and on top of that there were tweets from this spring saying that Flewelling was putting on a show in BP, hitting balls over the batters eye in CF and may have hit the furthest ball of any Rays player. DON'T TAKE THIS AS A DIRECT COMPARISON but this is almost exactly what I saw in Roman Anthony. We knew there was power in the tank but at 19 in Single-A he was overly patient (35.8% Swing%), drew a bunch of walks (18.8%), and didn't do much damage (.089 ISO, .228 AVG). Those are basically Flewelling's stats mirrored and he's a year younger. I'm not sure if it will be this year or next since he's still very young, but it feels like him putting it all together and rocketing up prospect lists is going to happen at some point.

players.name: Taitn Gray
players.note:
When the checklist for 2025 Bowman Draft was released I know that many Rays fans were disappointed that neither of their first two picks (Daniel Pierce and Brendan Summerhill) got a card in the release. What did happen though is it made them a sleeper team in the product because all five of the picks they made in the first three rounds were prep bats and the other three names all made it in. Of those I think that Taitn Gray has the most fun hobby upside. He's a 6'4" switch-hitting catcher from Iowa, which isn't exactly a prep baseball hot bed but he won Gatorade Player of the Year in the state after batting .538 with 14 HR in 39 games. He had a .709 OBP, 1.165 SLG, and 1.874 OPS. Again, may have not been the best competition but that's still crazy. At the Super 60 showcase last February he had the highest average (83 mph) and max (87 mph) bat speed recorded. Later that year he put on a show at the MLB draft combine with three of the seven highest EV's in his group, hitting four homers over 400 with one at 416 ft. which was the longest of the day. Along with this big time power Gray has sneaky athleticism flashing plus run times in the 60-yard dash too. And of course my favorite part, he did all of that age 17 and was still only 17 when the Rays selected him.

While he's presently a catcher his offensive profile is one that could play at first base or corner outfield if the Rays felt inclined to move him. After being drafted he played some games in the bridge league which high schoolers will often see time in prior to them debuting and Gray crushed balls from both sides maxing out at a 115 mph exit velocity. Needless to say this power upside is massive. What we don't know yet is what this hit tool will look like since he didn't face a ton of great competition in high school, however he's praised for his work ethic and how coachable he is which could be a great fit in this organization. Not that they'll end up being similar players there's a bit of what I loved about Nathan Flewelling here with Gray. Played in high school somewhere without a lot of eyeballs, impressed with big exit velocities at the combine, 17-years-old at the time of the draft, and now lands with a great developmental franchise who is known for finding under the radar talent. Always tough to rank players like this but I feel like there are a lot of hobby boxes checked in his favor for this price.

players.name: Caden Bodine
players.note: who they acquired from the Orioles but I'm on the fence about a 22-year-old catcher who is hit-over-power for the hobby. I will say that his hit tool is legit, maybe 60 grade, as Bodine had a 15% BB rate and 7.7% K rate last year at Coastal Carolina. Extremely polished switch-hitter who has an uncanny feel for the strike zone but he's someone who is trying to hit line drives not home runs. That could change though, and this is a really nice floor for $10 because I do think the bat-to-ball skills are legit, but unless we see some homers fly early this year I'd be worried about the upside.

players.name: Jadher Areinamo
players.note:
Most of the time when the Rays trade for a prospect that is not a big name it's someone I've identified as a sleeper in the past, and that was true for Areinamo who they acquired last year from Milwaukee for catcher Danny Jansen. He's a 5'9" infielder who can move around the dirt thanks to his quick hands and solid arm which allow him to play second base, third base, and shortstop, though second base probably makes the most sense long term. The bat is what intrigues me most at this price though. Areinamo has a 55-60 grade hit tool, consistently hitting for good average, posting contact rates over 80%, and being allergic to strikeouts. Back in 2024 in High-A at age 20 he hit .301 with 10 HR, 32 SB, 7.1% BB, 11.1% K, .141 ISO, and 124 wRC+. Though he didn't get much recognition for that strong season there were only seven prospects that year who had 10+ HR and 30+ SB at age 20 or younger. Areinamo's 11.1% strikeout rate was 10.3% LOWER THAN THE NEXT BEST. Lowest SwStr% on the list was Areinamo. Best BB/K on the list Areinamo. Despite that he was still going to need to improve his power a little more to be hobby relevant.

Last year the Brewers kept Areinamo in High-A for most of the season but after he was traded to the Rays they immediately promoted him to Double-A. Across both stops and organizations he hit .285 with 15 HR, 21 SB, 8.0% BB, 11.7% K, .159 ISO, and 122 wRC+. While improving his contact rates and keeping his strikeout rate sub-12%, Areinamo increased his ISO by nearly 20 points and his HR output by 36%. He was one of only nine prospects age 21 or younger who had 15+ HR and 20+ SB. Again, his strikeout rate was the lowest by 6.5%. Where it really got fun was this offseason in the Venezuelan Winter League. In 36 games he hit .364 with 13 HR in only 162 PA. His SLG was .692 and his OPS was 1.112. He nearly matched his 2025 HR total in 400 fewer PA. I still think that the power will be below average, but if it were to increase again this year it feels like his stock could blow up since pretty much nobody is matching his HR/SB totals the last two years while making as good of contact. Worst case scenario the power stays the same but if he were to produce similar results in AA/AAA I'm not sure how he doesn't get at least a little love. Even if he doesn't his floor is extremely high for under $10. 

*Note: if you're searching for his autographs they are non-1st's. He does have true 1st chrome and color but they aren't autographs. Don't think you can go wrong with either set.

players.name: Cooper Flemming
players.note:
Another high school hitter from last year's class the Rays took Flemming in the second round and signed him for $1.8 million which was about double what they paid Taitn Gray. The profile is quite a bit different. Flemming was a two-way player in high school and although the Rays announced him as a shortstop Topps used a picture of him pitching on his 1st Bowman card which is a bit confusing. As a pitcher his senior year he went 7-1 with a 0.69 ERA, striking out 66 batters and allowing only 8 walks. On the hitting side he batted .407 with 6 HR, 7 2B, 3 3B, and 10 SB in 28 games. Flemming had a .523 OBP, .767 SLG, 1.290 OPS, and drew 21 walks while striking out only 6 times in 111 PA. He has good hands and an above average arm thanks to his time on the mound where he threw in the 90's as a prep. Evaluators have put a hit grade as high as 55 on him as the lefty has a simple setup with really good swing mechanics and a strong approach. His hobby ceiling however is going to come down to the power.

Though MLB Pipeline currently has Flemming at 45 power I think there are reasons to believe that he could end up having more pop than we expect. His raw power is pretty solid, but his below average game power projections coming into the draft had to do with a combination of him having a wiry frame and not generating a ton of loft. Listed at 6'3" 190 pounds on the day of the draft there have been reports that between then and now (8 months) Flemming has grown an inch and put on 25 pounds. We'll see if that added strength changes how much impact he makes in his professional debut but it's definitely encouraging. While I think that presently Taitn Gray is a more exciting hobby prospect because of his big power projections, I do have Flemming ranked a bit higher due to the fact that I think his bat is a bit more polished and he's going to play a premium defensive position assuming he can stick at shortstop. He was given plus marks during the pre-draft process for his work ethic and willingness to learn more about the game. I think Flemming could be a sneaky player this year especially given that his base autograph is under $10. It may take time for him to add more game power as he learns to drive the ball in the air but already coming in with a good hit tool and adding 25 pounds to his frame feels like a great start.

players.name: Dean Moss
players.note:
who they drafted last year barely missed the cut and I do think he's a great hold. Really good bat speed and he seems to barrel everything, controls the zone well, could have an above average hit tool coming out of high school which is a really nice floor for $6 no doubt. The question will be the power. We saw a player as a prep who had no problem hitting the ball to all fields but he rarely looked like he was trying to hit for power and since his speed is no better than average we are going to need that power for him to generate some buzz. Coming in with a hit tool as good as his is a strong starting point though.

Your Rays dart throws are definitely

players.name: Warel Solano
players.note: from last year's international class. I could almost just say any teenage prospect this cheap in the Rays system is probably a buy but I'd like to see them in the states first. Solano probably had a slightly more well-rounded debut but Coret was the bigger name during that signing period as the 9th ranked international prospect and is definitely the more exciting hobby prospect. He's 6'4", had a 94th percentile Max EV in his class, and ran a 6.6 60-yard. If you've ever wanted to put your trust in the Rays development this is a worthy target to try it on.

players.name: Adrian Santana
players.note:
Every now and then you just gotta show a little love to the players who are solid but get absolutely zero respect and my favorite one for the Rays is Adrian Santana. Now I'll preface this by saying that Santana has below average power and I'm not suggesting he should be a player that is selling for a ton, but in my opinion he's much better than this price. The Rays took Santana 31st overall in 2023 and signed him for $2 million. Coming into the draft he was praised for his athleticism as a twitchy athlete, with some of the fastest 60-yard dash times of any player on the showcase circuit that year. That combined with his defense is what attracted the Rays as Santana has a great arm, range, hands, and footwork, everything you need to make it as an everyday shortstop. While he didn't make a ton of impact with the bat he did look like he'd be able to hit for average with a great swing from both sides of the plate, and there were evaluators who thought he could grown into more power as he added strength.

What we've seen offensively is not very hobby exciting as Santana has failed to eclipse a 95 wRC+ in either of this first two professional seasons. Here's the thing though, my favorite adjustment in my rankings is often age versus level and because of his great defense the Rays have been assigning him rather aggressively. Last year at age 19 he played the entire season in High-A where he hit .263 with 2 HR, 47 SB, 8.6% BB, 12.0% K, .063 ISO, and 94 wRC+. Not overly impressive I'll give you that, but he was one of only six prospects in all of the minor leagues last year who got 400+ PA in High-A at age 19 or younger. On that list his strikeout rate was 4.5% lower than the next best and his wildly low 5.8% swinging strike % was nearly 2% better than anybody else. The runner-up in both of those categories was Colt Emerson by the way. His 47 SB were also 22 more than anybody else in that group. Santana's contact rate last year was 88.8% and his swinging strike % was 5.8% in a level where he was more than three years younger than his average competitor. Unless he were to add enough strength that his HR totals jumped way up he'll likely never be a huge hobby name, but his contact skills, speed, and defense at SS give him a hell of a floor for $2 especially considering that Rays are moving him quickly for his age.

After 2023 Bowman had been out for a month I tweeted about a few players I bought the most of in that release, and two of them were Roman Anthony and

players.name: Brody Hopkins
players.note:
To give you an idea of how much buying value I think there is on Brody Hopkins, his rank as my 15th best non-debuted pitcher would normally fall in line with where I'd still be buying a player at $40-45, in fact he's only three spots behind Cam Caminiti (ATL) who I made a buy at $47. This card feels like it should already be double the price that it is. Hopkins is now ranked as the 3rd best Rays prospect per MLB Pipeline and they acquired him with the previously mentioned Aidan Smith from Seattle in the Randy Arozarena deal. The 6'4" right-hander was a two-way player at Winthrop where he hit .288 with 9 HR which may have been even better than he looked on the other side, with a 5.83 ERA in 15 appearances as a pitcher. The Mariners still liked the upside enough on the mound to take him in the sixth round and what a great call that was. In his professional debut he had a 2.90 ERA, 10.22 K/9, and 4.30 BB/9 in 18 Single-A starts with the Mariners prior to the trade. When the Rays acquired him they sent him straight to High-A where he had a 3.45 ERA, 10.91 K/9, and 3.73 BB/9 in seven more starts. Mind you, Hopkins didn't even start really pitching until his final year of college.

He's an incredible athlete and his stuff is absolutely disgusting. Fastball touches triple digits from a low release, curveball and slider have fantastic spin rates, and his low-90's cutter has been graded as high as 70 among evaluators. He throws a changeup as his fifth offering but it's not currently any better than average but even still he has legitimately four above average pitches and I think you could make the argument that three of them are already plus. Considering he didn't start taking pitching seriously until the spring of his 2023 collegiate season it's insane how good he is already. Last year in Double-A he started 25 games and had a 2.72 ERA, 10.94 K/9, and 4.66 BB/9 and his 28.7% strikeout rate was the second highest of any qualified pitcher at that level. The issue of course is that he struggles a bit with control and walked 12.2% of the hitters he faced last year. We saw that again this past weekend when he made his AAA debut and looked electric in four innings striking out five and only allowing two hits, but he also walked three guys. Here's the thing though, I was very close to saying the Brewers should make Jacob Misiorowski a reliever because he struggled to find the zone even more, with walk rates north of 14% at many of his minor league stops. But the fact is that your command doesn't have to be elite if your stuff is so good that people can't hit it. With four above average pitches, good athleticism, the fact that he's still new to pitching, and being that he landed in one of the best pitching labs in the MLB, it's hard not to be in on Brody Hopkins.

players.name: Anderson Brito
players.note:
Another pitcher acquired via trade last year was Anderson Brito who came to the Rays from the Astros in the three-way trade that sent Brandon Lowe to Pittsburgh. From a value perspective this might one of the best buys of any pitching prospect in my opinion. He is currently my 34th ranked non-debuted pitcher and his base autograph is under $10. Brito is only two spots lower than Cardinals pitchers Quinn Mathews who I just said I'd buy at $30. This is a severe misprice in the Bowman market as far as I'm concerned. Now two things are likely keeping Brito's stock from being higher at this moment and it's that he's undersized at 5'11" and his control isn't that great, but the stuff is REAL. Electric fastball that sits mid-to-upper 90's with carry, a slider with huge horizontal break, and a nasty curveball with really good depth. I think all three of them could be plus pitches. He also throws a changeup but it's not any better than average right now. Brito did something you don't see often and that's get promoted during the DSL season. After allowing only one earned run in 22.1 innings (0.40 ERA) the Astros brought him stateside in the middle of the season, put him in the CPX for one start where he was unhittable, and then promoted him again to Single-A. When all was said and done across three levels he had a 1.51 ERA, 13.75 K/9, and 3.52 BB/9 at age 19 in his first season. Filth.

Next year would prove to be a tougher test as the Rays moved him up to High-A but he was still very impressive with a 3.28 ERA, 2.91 FIP, 11.86 K/9, and 5.11 BB/9. Walks were an issue but he was also dealing with a shoulder issue that shut him down for a couple of months. In those 12 games he started prior to injury he had a 31.1% strikeout rate over 49.1 innings. That was the highest out of any High-A pitcher who threw 40+ innings at age 20 or younger. After not pitching in games from the end of June through the start of October, Brito was added to the roster for the Arizona Fall League. Mind you this is the most hitter friendly environment you'll probably find at any minor league level. Hitters put up insane stats and pitchers usually get rocked. In 4 appearances Brito went 2-0 with a 3.97 ERA but here's the crazy part, he struck out 22 of the 47 batters he faced (46.8%). These AFL rosters are no joke either and are usually better than most teams' Spring Breakout rosters so he wasn't facing nobody. Again though, he failed to locate well and also walked 7 of those hitters (14.9%). It's much of what I said with Hopkins, the stuff is unreal he just needs to improve the command. I understand the worry that a 5'11" pitcher may not hold up as a starter but from a pure arm talent perspective I don't know that anybody with an autograph under $10 is even close.

players.name: Trevor Harrison
players.note:
Harrison is a cool story as a kid who grew up right down the road from Tropicana Field and frequented Rays games as a kid, he was then selected by them in the fifth round in 2023 and signed for double his slot value. That was enough to pull him away from his commitment to Florida St. and made him the second player from his high school team drafted that year with the first being Aidan Miller (PHI). Standing at 6'4" 225 pounds, Harrison has a great frame for a potential starting pitcher. He was young for the class as a 17-year-old draftee and when he made his professional debut the following year he was still just 18. Between the CPX and A he had a 3.34 ERA, 3.30 FIP, 10.78 K/9, and 3.22 BB/9. He held opponents to a sub-70% contact rate and struck out 29.4% of the hitters he faced. That year only eight pitchers who were 18 or younger threw 70+ innings and his 20.6% K-BB% was the highest by more than 2.5%. Harrison uses mostly a three pitch mix including an above average fastball that sits mid-90's, a changeup that may be a plus pitch with crazy high whiff rates against it, and a slider that looks to be about average.

The downside is that Harrison's swing-and-miss took a step back last year and his K/9 dropped from 10.78 to 8.41. His command also backed up a little and he saw his overall walk rate rise from 8.8% to 11.1%. Despite this, he was still just as effective finishing the year with an 8-2 record and 2.78 ERA in 22 starts while reaching High-A at age 19. I actually think his card came out at the perfect time. If he had been in previous releases his prices would have come out hot after an impressive debut. With him not getting his 1st autograph until 2025 Bowman Chrome which was at the tail end of a not so exciting season for him he never really generated much hobby buzz. If you still believe in the skills though this is a fantastic price point for a pitcher who is just now entering his age 20 season and I know that the Rays organization is very high on him. There were 42 pitchers age 19 or younger who threw enough innings last year to be considered a qualified pitcher. Only 16 of those 42 had an ERA under 3.00. 15 of those 16 were either in the DSL or CPX. The only one who did it at a higher level was Trevor Harrison, and he did it without his best stuff working. Seems like there's plenty of upside at this price. 

The closest 3 to being a 4 is without a doubt

players.name: Gary Gill Hill
players.note:
who is right on the border for me as my 200th ranked pitcher. Has a good pitch mix with a fastball, cutter, slider, and changeup which are all average or above average pitches. He has plus command with BB/9 rates of 2.24 in 2024 and 1.98 last year. With his release point and ability to locate and mix pitches, he generates quite a bit of weak contact and also a lot of ground balls. Because of this he is an extremely effective pitcher with an ERA under 4 in consecutive years. My only concern for the hobby is that I don't know if he has a plus pitch, and though his pitching style is effective he struck out just 7.05 batters per 9 innings last year in High-A. He's still only 21 so I think there's still hope that his stuff will trend up enough to see his strikeout rates increase, but I'm holding what I have until I see that. Really good arm, good upside, but hard to be exciting when your striking out fewer than 20% of the hitters you face.

Prior to last season I was a fan of

players.name: Jackson Baumeister
players.note: in the under $5 autograph range because I really liked the stuff and he finished his professional debut season with a 2.53 ERA and 12.19 K/9 in High-A combined between Baltimore and Tampa Bay. In 7 appearances with the Rays after the trade he had a 1.24 ERA, 13.66 K/9, and 1.55 BB/9 and I thought maybe they found a gem. Last year he struggled in AA though and saw his strikeout rate nearly cut in half as opponent contact rates jumped 5% against him. His ERA also nearly doubled to 4.62. Not nearly as high on him as I was to end the 2024 season but still think he's a name worth watching in a system that can usually work some magic with pitchers.

players.name: Sebastian Walcott
players.note:
is the gem of the Rangers system and from a hobby tools standpoint he is a potential monster, which is why he's my #3 hitter. Sadly, not only does he have a non-1st autograph but he's now injured. With that elbow surgery there is a chance that we could see him return at the end of this season (likely as a DH) but it also wouldn't surprise me if the Rangers opted to play it safe and wait for next year. Even with that non-1st auto there was an argument to be made at $80 that he's a buy because realistically it still should be over $100 in my opinion, but now that he's set to miss significant time you can probably wait and see if it comes down more over the next couple of months.

I like

players.name: Elorky Rodriguez
players.note:
Rodriguez was an undersized international prospect but he showcased his great offensive ability as an amateur leading the Rangers to sign him for a touch over $1 million. Although he was just 5'7" when he signed and is still listed at that height on FanGraphs and MLB Pipeline there is confirmation that he's now 5'10" which is where the Rangers have him on their rosters. Still not a huge guy, but better. Rodriguez has one of the most advanced bats that we saw in his signing class, he's patient and can hit the ball to all fields with a compact swing from the left side. In the field he saw time at both center field and second base but because he's not a burner I think second base probably makes the most sense since his range and arm are both just okay. This is a play on the bat however. While he had already been regarded as an advanced hitter when he signed there were questions about if he would ever hit for power, however with him growing a few inches we actually saw a bit more game power in his professional debut than was expected.

In 46 games in the DSL, Rodriguez hit .337 with 6 HR, 9 SB, 17.3% BB, 16.8% K, .169 ISO, and 158 wRC+ on his way to being named an all-star there. He showed off that patience with a 38.7% Swing% and a great ability to find the barrel with just a 9.0% swinging strike % as a 17-year-old. Based on the scouting reports those two things were kind of to be expected, what wasn't was the power. Rodriguez was an extra base machine going deep six times and adding ten doubles and a triple in 226 PA. Of the 163 qualified DSL prospects who were age 17 or younger last year only sixteen of them hit six or more HR. In that group the only two prospects with a SwStr% of 9% or lower were Gabriel Davalillo (LAA) who I already stamped as a buy, and Elorky Rodriguez. The two highest walk to strikeout ratios on that list of names, also Gabriel Davalillo and Elorky Rodriguez. I mentioned that from an approach, contact, and power perspective Davilillo had one of my favorite DSL stat lines in the past few years but Elorky Rodriguez's wasn't that far behind. His 158 wRC+ was higher than Josuar Gonzalez, Elian Pena, and Cris Rodriguez, the three biggest hobby names in that signing class. I'm still worried about the power as the exit velocities aren't crazy impressive and the concern is that as an advanced hitter he demolished bad pitching but that power will drop off in the states. While that's definitely possible I still think he's worth taking a chance on under $15 because the floor feels more solid than most DSL prospects.

players.name: Josh Owens
players.note:
When I did my 2025 Bowman Draft rankings I had Owens as my 15th ranked hitter chase which was above some bigger first round picks including Kayson Cunningham (ARI) and Gavin Kilen (SF). It seems the market disagrees with me as he has not been a hot name in Bowman but I'm trusting my process because I think the ceiling for this price is hard to pass up on. Owens was taken 84th overall in the third round signing over slot for $1.1 million out of high school and when Texas announced him as a two-way player it immediately pinged my attention. As a lefty hitter and righty pitcher he was a member of the 2024 18U USA National team which had a roster full of first round picks in last year's class and during the World Cup qualifier Owens picked up two wins for the team on the mound. Not only is he a two-way player which helps his standing with me but he's also the son of a former professional baseball player. His dad Jeremy played in the minor leagues for ten seasons where he was known as a burner, collecting 272 stolen bases including two straight years with 50+. Like his dad, Josh can move and at 6'3" has clocked run times that would fall in the 70 grade range out of 80. 

Thanks to that speed and his obviously plus arm as a pitcher Owens is capable of playing a solid shortstop but could also shift to center field pretty easily thanks to that plus athleticism. Offensively there are some scouts who think he could grow into above average power as he fills out his frame since he already has shown an ability to hit the ball in the air. After being drafted the Rangers threw him right into Single-A at 18 and as a hitter he struggled batting .083 with a 45.8% strikeout rate. Without a doubt this is affecting his card price. Realistically though it was only 24 PA which means nothing to me and his .154 BABIP and 73.8% contact rate suggest he may have been unlucky in those at-bats as well. On the other side he also made two starts as a pitcher but the Rangers limited him to just two innings in each of them. In those four innings he allowed one hit and zero runs, walking three batters and striking out six. He was sitting 93-96 and topping 98 with heavy sink and a good slider. Though the pitching side looked better most evaluators preferred him as a hitter entering the draft. For now it looks like the Rangers are willing to let him play both ways which creates some really fun hobby upside. Son of a former player, 6'3" teenager with a projectable frame, plays middle infield and pitches, might have plus speed and above average power. I mean, even if this is a developmental project it's one I'm interested in.

We all know that

players.name: Cameron Cauley
players.note:
who are not only priced about the same but are ranked nearly identically for me. Castillo has more hobby upside probably because he's a 19-year-old shortstop who projects for above average hit and speed. He didn't light up the stat sheet last year but to be fair he was 18 in Single-A and had a 86.5% contact rate there which is very, very impressive. Back in his DSL debut he had an almost hilarious 2.75 BB/K thanks to a 22.7% walk rate and 8.2% strikeout rate. Really good bat-to-ball skills, has shown good speed, think he could be a sneaky stash in case some more power shows up as he matures. Cauley on the other hand is 23 and 5'9" but I still think he's extremely slept on. Went 15 HR/27 SB in 2024 and then ran it back with 15 HR/28 SB last year. Very good tools and looked great in Spring Training this year, unfortunately he's running out of time to make himself a prospect name because he'll probably debut this year. Not a bad short-term flip though if you want to hold him for a couple months because I have a sneaking suspicion he might crush AAA pitching.

Under $10 range I'm most tempted by

players.name: Dylan Dreiling
players.note: I hate myself for saying Gutierrez because he's a player many of us were burned by after a great DSL and stateside debut, but he kind of fell of a cliff after that. Shockingly still only 21 because we saw him make it to the states at 17 so it feels like he's been around forever. Hit .258 with 48 steals last year in High-A he's got plus speed and plays such good defense in center field he could potentially win a Gold Glove there, but the offense will need to improve. Has suffered countless injuries since becoming a pro which has hurt his development but at 6'3" he still posts extremely high exit velocities, he's just so impatient it hasn't translated to HR power. It's a shame he hasn't put it all together but it feels like there's still good upside for around $5. Dreiling on the other hand makes plenty of contact with an 89% contact rate in his debut season and 85.5% last year, both with swinging strike rates under 6%. Quietly turned in a nice 12 HR/15 SB season last year in High-A. I don't hate the tools offensively as there could be at least average hit, power, and speed, but he's about to turn 23 and the Rangers have now had him play both of his pro seasons with nearly 600 PA combined in High-A. To be hobby relevant he needs to get moving this year but I think it's possible.

players.name: AJ Russell
players.note:
The Rangers were one of my favorite targets for PYT in 2025 Bowman Draft because I seemed to be higher than the consensus on all three of Gavin Fien, Josh Owens, and AJ Russell. I had Russell as my 10th ranked pitcher in the product so the value here under $10 when he's a borderline top 80 hobby arm for me feels really solid. When I rank my pitchers there is no doubt a penalty for having reliever risk and I think there's a chance that Russell could end up as a reliever so let's just get that out of the way. But he also has what was considered by many to be the best fastball in the entire draft class last year, often receiving a 70 grade. In 2023 at Tennessee as a freshman he was a reliever who worked 30.1 innings with a 0.89 ERA, 1.22 FIP, 13.95 K/9, and 2.08 BB/9. Granted this was as a reliever but the advanced pitching section of these numbers on FanGraphs looks like a video game. Pitching in the SEC as a freshman he struck out 47 of the 105 batters he faced (44.8%) while walking only 7 (6.7%). I often cite K-BB% in my hobby pitcher rankings and in the minors over 20% is strong. Russell's that year was 38.1%. He surrendered 9 hits in 24 appearances and opponents had a .092 batting average against him. Unreal. Sadly he was shut down after 14.1 innings as a sophomore and needed internal brace surgery. Last year he returned for part of the year making 6 starts plus 6 more appearances in relief where he had a 3.55 ERA, 3.32 FIP, 12.79 K/9, and 3.91 BB/9.

Given the one year layoff that's pretty solid, and while they weren't as ridiculous as they were his freshman year, his 32.4% strikeout rate and 9.9% walk rate were both pretty strong, and the Rangers went ahead and grabbed him in the second round. He throws from a low release point that was about 4.8 feet in college and his fastball which sits in the mid-90's and tops 98 looks like it's rising, with a vertical approach angle of -3.91 degrees. This pitch was unhittable prior to his injury generating a 42% whiff rate and 33% chase rate. The biggest concern here is that he never threw more than 30.1 innings in a college season but standing at 6'6" he's definitely got a workhorse frame. His sweeping slider looked like a plus pitch prior to the injury but was less consistent last year leading to the second worry and that's that the repertoire isn't deep enough to be a starter. The Rangers have been working with him on improving his secondary pitches and are also going to give him every opportunity to be a starter. I think his floor is probably a high leverage reliever but his ceiling, if that slider and changeup improve and he's able to stay healthy, could be huge.

players.name: Winston Santos
players.note:
Santos is a name I'm very intrigued by with such a low entry point. Back in 2023 he struggled quite a bit in High-A posting a 6.29 ERA and had consecutive seasons with a K/9 under 9. When he returned to the mound in 2024 he looked like an entirely different pitcher than we had seen in previous years. Making 12 starts at the same level he went 6-3 with a 2.80 ERA, 2.67 FIP, 11.33 K/9, and 2.80 BB/9. Thanks to a massive improvement to his stuff that he made during the offseason he saw his K-BB% jump from 14% to 22.9%. Where batters hit .293 off of him in 2023 they hit just .217 the following year. Santos was then promoted to Double-A where his ERA was 4.89 in 10 starts but his 3.63 xFIP was more encouraging and most importantly his high K-BB% carried over, with a 29.5% strikeout rate and a 7.3% walk rate. Santos is a really good athlete but one concern with him is that he's about 6 feet tall and that's kind of in the range where you worry that a pitcher won't be able to handle a starter's workload. This concern came to life when it was revealed he was being shut down with a stress reaction in his back after his first start in 2025.

While this was disappointing I'd be lying if I said it didn't create a better buying opportunity for us since he got his 1st autograph in 2025 Bowman less than a month after being shut down and didn't return to the mound until the end of August when people were starting to sell their cards entering the offseason. His return to action didn't look pretty in the stat line which isn't surprising given the four and a half month layoff, but the advanced numbers suggest he was pitching well and what I found most encouraging is that after starting only three games the Rangers promoted Santos to AAA and let him make a start there to end the year. In his six starts for the year he had a 6.75 ERA but his 1.77 FIP and 2.71 xFIP say he was dealing, something that is backed up by his 13.50 K/9 as he struck out 33.3% of the 78 batters he faced. Despite not being a big guy he sits 95-97 mph and touches 100 with movement and has a slider and changeup that weren't as consistent last year but both looked like above average pitches prior to the injury. He wasn't able to pitch in Spring Training because during BP he took a line drive off the wrist on his non-throwing hand and fractured it. Despite that he stayed in to finish off Wyatt Langford and Corey Seager and after it was revealed later he was pitching with it broken Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said, "that's the stuff I can't teach, those are the guys you want on the mound during a season". We should see Santos again in AAA soon and I wouldn't put him making his MLB debut in 2026 out of the question either.

players.name: JoJo Parker
players.note:
This is a tough price. Last year I put Konnor Griffin in a hold range at $150 because it seemed too steep for a player who hadn't made his debut yet but the more I watch of Parker the more I'm convinced he is the bat that we want in 2025 Bowman Draft. And considering that I liked Bryce Rainer as a buy at this same price and I have Parker ranked higher than him makes me feel as though this is justified. He was after all my second ranked chase in the most recent Bowman product and the scouting report is the same now as it was then. Parker won Gatorade Player of the Year for the state of Mississippi after putting up a .665 OBP in 37 games as a senior where he drew 45 walks and only struck out FOUR TIMES. Along with that approach he flashed the plus power too, hitting 13 HR in 158 PA and slugging over 1.000. Not a one year fluke either, as a sophomore he had a .657 OBP, 44 walks to 8 K's, and again slugged over 1.000 with 15 HR. His patience is incredible for somebody who can hit for his kind of power, with EV's over 115 mph as a high schooler according to Rapsodo. He rarely expands outside of the zone and when you throw him strikes he makes you pay, something we've already seen this spring. 

There have been a couple videos circulating of him on Twitter and while we can only get so excited about back field HRs he hit one that was 111 mph off the bat and a couple of days later hit a double off the wall on a ball that broke his bat. This is going to sound crazy but I think 55-60 hit with 55-60 power is on the table, a combination possessed by Walker Jenkins that has made him a big hobby name. Parker's swing from the left side is gorgeous and he finds the barrel with ease. When I did my deep dive for 2025 Bowman Draft there wasn't a single player on the checklist that impressed me more. Eli Willits was my number one chase but much of that had to do with knowing that his cards would carry a premium as the #1 pick and also that he was more than a full year younger than JoJo Parker. If you're letting me pick a package of tools though, Parker's are the best of any hitter in that entire product for the hobby in my opinion. 6'2" prep shortstops with this combination of raw power and approach don't grow on trees and something tells me he is a name that could explode this year.

players.name: Arjun Nimmala
players.note:
I'm going to preface this entire scouting report by saying that there is still extreme risk involved in buying Nimmala's cards. Although they have improved, his approach and contact skills have been scary at times early on in his professional career. Now that I got that out of the way I'll go into the fun part. I think that Arjun Nimmala has a higher hobby ceiling than any prospect in baseball. Let's start on the field. Last year in High-A, Nimmala hit .224 with 13 HR, 17 SB, 10.1% BB, 21.4% K, .156 ISO, and 92 wRC+. Though it's not overly impressive I go back to my favorite factor when ranking prospects and that's age versus level. There wasn't a single prospect in baseball who got more plate appearances in High-A as a teenager than Nimmala. The list of prospects age 19 or younger with 10+ HR and a strikeout rate under 25% last year in A+ is Leo De Vries, Colt Emerson, and Arjun Nimmala. What's wild is that while that sounds impressive we saw him hit 17 HR and post a .250 ISO as an 18-year-old the year prior. The raw power here is massive, but there's hit tool concerns. With that being said Nimmala seemed to be working on that last year and though his power output dropped he also reduced his strikeout rate from 30.7% to 21.4% while moving up to a higher level. Since I know the power is there but wanted to see contact improvements I actually think last year's season was a positive.

Here's the crazy part about Nimmala for those who don't know. He didn't stop playing cricket to focus on baseball until he was 12. Started baseball at 12, got drafted in the first round at 17, played a full season of High-A baseball at 19. That is outrageous. He's playing at advanced levels and all of this is still somewhat new to him compared to most baseball players. On top of that he was the first first-generation Indian-American to be drafted in the first round of any major U.S. sport. We see how the hobby reacts to Japanese baseball players, their market is crazy because they have a massive reach outside of the states. Now baseball isn't a big sport in India, but there are over a billion people there. Is it crazy to think that if Nimmala ended up being a star in the MLB that his global reach wouldn't be exponentially higher than most players? The thought of it has always fascinated me. Honestly though that doesn't factor into my rankings and he's still a buy because of his massive upside on the field as a power-hitting shortstop. If his hit tool continues to improve I think he has the ceiling of a top 10 prospect in baseball. That combined with the potential for him to bring so many new sets of eyeballs to baseball is something you can't really account for in his prices, but the thought of it happening is a hobby dream.

players.name: Tim Piasentin
players.note:
who the Jays selected in the fifth round of last year's draft. There are hit tool concerns and evaluators are worried about how much swing-and-miss there could be but the 6'3" teenager puts up very impressive exit velocities. He even did so with wood bats which is encouraging for a prospect this age. The Canadian-born slugger didn't get a ton of pre-draft coverage and the fact that we weren't able to see him against good prep competition here makes him a bit of a gamble, but based on the reports it's one that could pay off in the hobby due to his high power ceiling.

Of the players who have already debuted the Jays have two prospects who are slept on a bit for their age that I think could be sneaky and that's

players.name: RJ Schreck
players.note:
It's probably safe to say that at 25.7 years of age, Schreck is going to be the oldest player that I mark as a buy, and while I always harp on how important age is to me just know that he has a massive deduction in my score for how old he is and he's still this high. Schreck was a ninth round pick by the Mariners back in 2023 out of Vanderbilt and signed for just $75,000. All he has done since then is put together two of the most productive minor league seasons that you've probably heard nothing about. Back in 2024 he was traded to the Jays and between both organizations and two different levels he hit .251 with 17 HR, 13 SB, 15.7% BB, 16.5% K, .211 ISO, and 138 wRC+. He did this with a 82.3% contact rate and a swinging strike % of 7.6%. That year there were 1,021 qualified minor league hitters age 25 or younger. The ONLY one who had an ISO over .200 and a SwStr% under 8% was RJ Schreck. Do you know who the player was in that group with next best SwStr% after Schreck? Roman Anthony. Maybe you've heard of him.

Last year between AA & AAA Schreck did it all again, hitting .249 with 18 HR, 9 SB, 16.4% BB, 21.3% K, .211 ISO, and 143 wRC+. Here's a list of Bowman prospects who didn't debut last year but had 15+ HR, an ISO over .200, and a SwStr% under 9% at age 25 or younger in the minors. Kevin McGonigle, JJ Wetherholt, Eduardo Quintero, and RJ Schreck. It's like I know he's old as dirt to Bowman people but these seasons are kind of ridiculous. He has a very good hitting approach, makes really good contact, and just keeps sneakily posting .200+ ISO's without anybody talking about him. While the Jays aren't considered one of the strongest hobby fanbases it's actually very easy to become a player that they love. We saw it last year with Ernie Clement during their World Series run. A prospect who had never been exciting his whole minor league career who didn't debut until he was 25 all of the sudden gets hot in the postseason and his cards go nuts. There aren't many players I'd continue to hold after they're called up but Schreck could be a fun one to hold because he likely won't get a ton of hype when he does get the call but I do think his bat will play and he'll go on one of those, "where did this guy come from?" type runs. Since he should debut this year and it could be a nice short-term flip I'd take a chance on it for this cheap.

players.name: Charles McAdoo
players.note: Keys showed up on some 'Hot Sheets' last year and that's how he got on my radar. Plus power projections and he showed those off by hitting 19 HR with a .191 ISO last year. What you might not expect from his .217 average is that he also made good contact (78.2% contact, 8.4% SwStr%) but was a bit unlucky with a BABIP about 50 points below average. Could be a nice hold and see if that average normalizes this year because the underlying data looks pretty solid. For McAdoo he's even older at 24 and that's why the hobby doesn't care about him but I still think there's potential for him due to his plus power and underrated speed. 17 HR/21 SB with a .200 ISO in 2024 followed by 16 HR/34 SB last year in AA. Age is a killer but for $5 he's a pretty solid bat.

players.name: Yohendrick Pinango
players.note:
Pinango is another player who fits in the same type of description that I just gave for Schreck. Though I like Schreck's overall package of tools a little bit better, Pinango is ranked higher because he's two years younger. That combined with the fact that he's half the price makes him another player in this organization who has just been way too productive to have an autograph this cheap. When Pinango came over from the Cubs in the Nate Pearson deal he had done nothing spectacular in his career up to that point and between both organizations at two different levels had 10 HR, 11 SB, and a 111 wRC+ in 2024. Now he did have a 80.9% contact rate and an 8.6% swinging strike rate, and he does have plus grade raw power, the issue for Pinango has always been that he hits the ball on the ground too much. If you look at every stop he's made in his minor league career he had ground ball rates over 50% in more than half of them but the improvements to them each year have led to him getting to more of that HR power.

Last year between AA & AAA, Pinango improved his ground ball rate, overall contact rates, and swinging strike rate compared to the year prior. What came of it was his best offensive season yet where he hit .258 with 15 HR, 6 SB, 13.1% BB, 20.1% K, .172 ISO, and 122 wRC+. Highest single season HR total of his career, highest ISO, highest walk rate, highest contact rate, and highest wRC+. He's a bit of a late bloomer breaking out at age 23 but he also missed his age 18 season due to COVID. Among all prospects age 23 or younger last year who hit 15 or more HR the lowest SwStr% by a player who didn't debut that year was a tie at 7.5% between Edward Florentino, who is in my top 10, and Yohendrick Pinango. The next two names on that list at 7.7% and 7.8% were Kevin McGonigle and Eduardo Quintero. He's an older prospect, especially for the hobby, but I'll say the same thing I said about Schreck. This is a sneaky fan base and when you get called up if you're productive with the bat your card prices will go up. He's another one I think you stash a couple of dollar bin autographs of and hold them through the call-up just in case.

players.name: Adrian Pinto
players.note:
Not many teams have them but every now and then I get to a player and ask myself, "how is this $1?". Usually these aren't players that I think have massive ceilings but if you're a productive minor league hitter who hasn't been released your autograph should sell for more than $1, and I would venture to say that out of any prospect with this price tag Pinto has been by far the most productive. The issue with Pinto is health. Since making his stateside debut in 2022 he has never gotten more than 200 PA in a single year. Pretty brutal. What's not brutal though are the results. Back in 2024 Pinto split time between A & A+ but only made it through a total of 26 games. However in those 112 PA, he hit .330 with 4 HR, 2 SB, 5.4% BB, 14.3% K, .243 ISO, and 162 wRC+. Really good, but again only 112 PA. Last year he returned to High-A and this time got hurt even sooner into the season, only playing 19 games. BUT in those games he hit .284 with 7 HR. Those 7 homers along with 3 doubles in just 19 games came out to a .324 ISO and his wRC+ was 166.

Pinto is a 5'6" infielder who has plus speed and can play multiple positions defensively. He is a favorite in the organization. Plays with his hair on fire, coaches and players love him, and I think the Jays fans would too… if he could stay on the field. It's tough to really know what his upside is since we've never seen him make it through a full season but we've seen short bursts of what looks like a really solid player. Just last year he was a $3 base auto guy and he showed up on a couple rounds of my 'Hot Sheets' and saw his autograph price more than double and get in the $10 range before crashing back down when he got injured again. Again, I don't know what his ceiling is because you can't get a great read off of samples this small, but I've seen him perform well enough for 100 PA stretches to see his base autograph get up to $10 so there's no reason to think that if he stays healthy for once that it couldn't normalize in that range. That's what kind of makes these $1 plays so fun. Maybe he goes up 10x or maybe he doesn't, but how does he go down? What he's never done is given us an idea that he can't hit the ball because he's done so every time he's been on the field. If this is the first year he stays healthy (I'm going to will it into existence) and we see him go 10+HR/20+SB, which feels modest, I don't see how this price could stay a dollar.

One of the 3's I'm watching this year is

players.name: Ricky Tiedemann
players.note:
This is tough because obviously Tiedemann and King are ranked almost side-by-side and their autograph prices are nearly identical so Ricky should be a 5/5, but that would require him to stay on the mound and prove he's healthy which he has not done in forever. When he is though he's electric which makes his upside phenomenal. The 6'4" 235 pound lefty has some of the best pure stuff that you'll see come out of the hand of a minor league pitcher. His fastball, slider, and changeup all could legitimately be 60 grade and like King he posted some pretty silly strikeout numbers back when he was a younger prospect. In 2022 at age 19 Tiedemann made 18 starts where he had a 2.17 ERA, 13.39 K/9, and 3.32 BB/9 while reaching Double-A. In his 4 AA starts opponents had a 66.7% contact rate against him and he induced a 14.7% SwStr% while being FIVE AND A HALF years younger than the average player at that level. He immediately shot up to being a top 10 prospect many places and he deserved every bit of it. Some of you know where this is going. We've now played three full minor league seasons since then and Tiedemann has never made it through more than 44 innings in any of them, throwing just 17.1 in 2024, and zero last year.

Between having Tommy John and getting bone chips removed in his elbow along with other injuries, Tiedemann has lost a few valuable years already. Everything was pointing towards 2026 being they year of his resurgence as he entered spring healthy and with a new slider he's been working on. As he returned to the mound and we saw the clips going around of him throwing gas that whole, "oh wow I forgot how nasty he was" started popping into people's brains and his base autograph was selling for over $40 this February. Unfortunately while he was ramping back up he reported elbow soreness and they moved him to the 7-day IL. Luckily everything looks clean and there's no damage and he began throwing again so we'll hopefully see him very soon in AAA. When that elbow soreness was reported people jumped ship and this price came crashing back down to about $25. Assuming that he's coming back off the shelf soon it's hard not to like this price. This is a guy who in 2023 had a 1.68 FIP and struck out 44.1% of the hitters he faced. During that season PSA 10's of his base autograph were selling for over $200. It's a bit of a dice roll but if he steps back on the mound in AAA this year and makes it through a handful of starts with his usual strikeout stuff, I think this thing would go up from $25 in a hurry.

players.name: Johnny King
players.note:
I swear there's no bias here given that Johnny King is from my hometown and he's a fellow ginger which does not get you extra points in my rankings (but it should). This is just a play on the fact that we may have never seen more dominant stuff in the minor leagues from a player this young ever. Down here in Naples, Florida, King was not only a two-way player at Naples High School but he was the best hitter on his team. As a senior King batted .500 in 116 PA while only striking out 7 times all season. If he had chosen to go that route I think he could have been an MLB hitting prospect as well. On the mound is where he got more attention from scouts though, going 8-1 with a 0.73 ERA in 11 starts, racking up 110 strikeouts in just 47.2 innings. He struck out a ridiculous 60.8% of the total batters he faced. I actually posted a clip of him on Twitter back in December of 2024 talking about how he was a sneaky cheap stash in 2024 Bowman Draft and included clips of him throwing at the 2023 Perfect Game National against some of the best hitters in that class including Bryce Rainer (DET). King was only 16 at the time and not a single hitter, including future top 10 picks and D-I commits, looked like they were comfortable at the plate.

He has filled out considerably since then and the way that he attacks hitters from a funky arm slot with a mid-90's fastball and nasty curveball made him nearly impossible to square up last year. King was young for his grade and was drafted at age 17 and made his professional debut last year at 18. Between the CPX & A he threw 61.2 innings where he had a 2.48 ERA, 15.32 K/9, and 5.40 BB/9. To say he kept hitters off balance would be an understatement. Opponents had just a 61.9% contact rate against King, batting a combined .199, and he struck out 39.5% of the batters he faced. This is outrageous. Now the downside, there's quite a bit of effort in his delivery and he gets out of control at times as referenced by that BB/9 over 5. He's going to need to clean that up but since he's such a great athlete I have faith it will improve. Even if it doesn't though, we've seen guys like Thomas White and Jacob Misiorowski post walk rates that high and still have success because when they are in the zone they're unhittable. King has a ways to go to be in that conversation but I think he's on the right track. FanGraphs has minor league stats back to 2006. He is the only player in that database over 20+ years who threw 60+ innings at age 18 or younger with a K% over 38%. The only one. And since nothing sells more in the world of pitching than guys who can post high strikeout rates, it makes him one of the best young pitchers you can hold.

players.name: Eli Willits
players.note:
you don't get picked #1 overall as a 17-year-old on accident. Very exciting young prospect that I'm pumped to watch play this year and climb the ranks but as with many 1st overall picks this autograph was just too expensive for me on day one and I may never get a good buying opportunity on him.

Very intrigued by

players.name: Gavin Fien
players.note:
No surprise here since I had Fien as the fourth best hitter in my 2025 Bowman Draft rankings ahead of Dax Kilby who is more than double the price. Fien was the biggest piece in the five-for-one trade this offseason that sent MacKenzie Gore to the Rangers. Texas took Fien with the 12th pick in the first round of last year's draft and he's the younger brother of A's catcher Dylan Fien who happened to be one my deep sleepers in 2025 Bowman. The younger Fien is a big 6'3" righty with a quick swing that leads to consistent hard contact. FanGraphs has his hit tool at 40 but I've seen it other places at 55 and average is about where I lean initially. After hitting .410 his sophomore year of high school he hit .411 as a junior before seeing his production drop a little as a senior where he batted .358. Between his junior and senior seasons he drew 21 walks and struck out 20 times in 216 PA, putting the ball in play in over 80% of his trips to the plate. Having walk rates that low could be an indicator that he's too aggressive but it also could just be that he's not being tested enough. Hard to be patient when you think you can hit everything, and it's hard to blame him for thinking that since he excelled against the best competition prior to his senior year.

Fien was a member of the 2024 USA 18U national team whose roster had multiple first round picks including Ethan Holliday, Kayson Cunningham, Josh Hammond, and his new teammate Eli Willits. At the World Cup qualifier he led all hitters there with a .727 SLG in a field that featured #1 ranked international prospect Josuar Gonzalez among others. Following his time with Team USA, Fien was named to the High School All-American Game where he drove in two runs on two hits, with three batted balls over 100 mph, on his way to being named the MVP. According to Rapsodo they had him measured as high as 118.79 mph on his max exit velocity which was the second highest they got on any prep hitter in last year's class behind Xavier Neyens (HOU). Although his stats taking a step back as a senior seem odd it's hard to be too worried about them considering how well he played against the best amateur competition every time he faced it. He's had a slow start to his professional career but there aren't nearly enough plate appearances to jump to any conclusions. His cards are in a nice spot right now because Rangers fans who were collecting him are probably selling and he hasn't done anything of note as a professional so his stock hasn't really had a chance to pop. I think it will.

players.name: Seaver King
players.note:
who didn't do much offensively last season to excite me in a hobby sense but then went to the AFL and looked fantastic. I know it's a good hitting environment but the approach actually looked much better than what we saw during the minor league season. He hasn't done much hitting in his first few AA games this year but he has drawn 7 walks in 3 games which is again a great sign that he's worked on his approach which was an issue in 2025. I've got my eye on him for this season.

It's easy to get lost in the shuffle with all of the great names the Nats had in 2025 Bowman Draft but don't sleep on their second round pick

players.name: Ethan Petry
players.note:
out of South Carolina. 6'4" right hander who put up big power production in college (54 career HR) and improved his strikeouts quite a bit his final year there. In my most recent rankings update he moved from outside my top 300 to now inside my top 200. Could be a sneaky name to watch.

My favorite sleeper of any hitter in this organization who isn't a buy has to be

players.name: Devin Fitz-Gerald
players.note:
Another piece that came over in that Gore trade was Fitz-Gerald who I've been a fan of since we saw him play professionally for the first time. He was a fifth round pick by the Rangers in 2024 out of high school and he's a switch-hitter with a really good feel the barrel. Fitz-Gerald is the son of a baseball coach and drew rave reviews for his baseball IQ during the pre-draft process which is something I love. Now if you're someone who trusts analytics this is probably the best target for you on this entire team because prior to his injury last year Fitz-Gerald was the 46th ranked hitter in all of baseball according to Scout the Statline's Peak Projections. Making his professional debut last year in the CPX, he hit .318 with 6 HR, 5 SB, 13.1% BB, 11.5% K, .224 ISO, and 147 wRC+. Quite a start to your career. In those 31 games he had a 81.8% contact rate and 8.3% SwStr%. Texas decided they had seen enough and promoted him to Single-A. In his first ten games there he hit .250 but still had a 133 wRC+ due to his 25.6% walk rate in 43 PA. After only two weeks there he injured his shoulder while diving for a ball in the field and wasn't able to return last season.

While we were robbed of seeing him compile more at-bats in Single-A I actually think it was the best case scenario for us buying his cards because his season getting cut short stopped his hobby popularity from growing and his cards are still pretty cheap. Due to the abundance of middle infielders in the Nationals system after the trade they decided to assign Fitz-Gerald to High-A to start this year so him missing all of that time last year ended up not slowing his movement at all. He's only played three games there so far but he's looked the part, collecting three hits in his first A+ game and already has a pair of steals. He was inside my top 15 chases for 2025 Bowman Chrome and the story is still the same, I think because we haven't seen him for any extended period nobody really knows his name, but if he ends up being anything like what we saw prior to his injury I'm very interested at jumping in at this price. Not including the DSL there there were only three prospects last year age 20 or younger who had 100+ PA with more walks than strikeouts and an ISO over .180. Kevin McGonigle, Alfredo Duno, and Devin Fitz-Gerald. It was a small sample and it was the CPX so I can only get so excited, but I think he's worth the shot.

players.name: Abimelec Ortiz
players.note:
One of my personal favorite prospects to watch hit the baseball is Abi Ortiz who has never really gotten much hobby love up to this point. He's had a pretty fascinating road to the show thus far. Ortiz went to the Carlos Beltran Baseball Academy in Puerto Rico for high school and then came to the states and attended Florida Southwestern State College in Fort Myers, FL where he played baseball as a 19-year-old freshman. My favorite part about that is that I live in Fort Myers and I didn't know that FSW even had a baseball team until my first deep dive into Ortiz a couple of years ago. After his lone junior college season where he hit .349 with 9 HR he was signed by the Rangers in 2021 for $20,000. Since then all he's done is mash the ball. His prospect breakout came two years later in 2023 where between A & A+ he hit .294 with 33 HR, a .325 ISO and 163 wRC+ in 109 games. Pretty ridiculous. The following year in AA his stats fell off a bit as he hit .243 but he was still able to hit 18 HR with a .189 ISO and 112 wRC+ while raising his contact rates by over 4% and dropping his strikeouts by 6%. Last year we saw that big power from 2023 and increased bat-to-ball skills from 2024 come together and between AA & AAA Ortiz hit .257 with 25 HR, 11.7% BB, 22.1% K, .222 ISO, and 124 wRC+. 

He's a big guy at 230 pounds so the power is no surprise but the contact skills are actually pretty strong for a player with his offensive profile. Last year in AAA he had a 78.8% contact rate and 88.6% in-zone contact rate which for someone putting up these kind of power numbers is impressive. He hits the ball to all fields instead of selling out for power and the improvements he's made have turned this bat into one that I think is extremely slept on. The issue is the defense and he doesn't play much of it. The Rangers tried him in corner outfield but he's not athletic enough, he plays first but he's not great, so he's likely a DH. But now that he's in an organization where the MLB lineup has many holes I don't know how we don't see him soon because they could definitely use his bat. Of the 1,104 qualified hitters at every minor league level last year only 18 of them hit 25+ HRs. Of those 18, only seven were age 23 or younger. Obviously some big names on that list in Bryce Eldridge, Laz Montes, Esmerlyn Valdez, Ryan Clifford, etc. Only one of them had a contact rate over 75%. Only one of them had a strikeout rate under 24%. Both were the same player and it was Abimelec Ortiz. I think this man deserves more respect for what he's done.

players.name: Ronny Cruz
players.note: who they acquired from the Cubs. 6'2" shortstop who was taken in the third round in 2023 that puts up really good exit velocities for his age. It hadn't shown up as HR power yet last year at age 18 but he still had a .161 ISO thanks to 6 triples in 189 PA. Approach looked shaky last season but this year he's already looked much more passive at the plate early on and went deep again last night. Don't have any stats to back up him being a buy but he could be a great stash for this year.

players.name: Angel Feliz
players.note:
Back in January of 2024 Feliz was ranked as the 24th best prospect in the international class leading to the Nationals signing him for $1.8 million. In his professional debut he was named as an All-Star in the DSL after hitting .310 with 4 HR, 27 SB, 10.8% BB, 18.6% K, .158 ISO, and 125 wRC+. Last year he came stateside and had a 110 wRC+ in the CPX before the Nats gave him an early promotion to Single-A. After the promotion he was just ok, hitting .230 with 3 HR, 5 SB, 10.3% BB, 23.3% K, .140 ISO, and 96 wRC+. What about that stat line makes me like Feliz? As usual, it's the things that don't show up in the box scores. First off, he's a 6'3" shortstop with room to fill out and has not yet gotten to all of his power. Second, and most important, is that he was 18-years-old last year in Single-A. There were only 30 prospects age 18 or younger who got 100+ PA at that level last year, that already puts him in some really strong prospect company. Out of those 30 players Feliz's .140 ISO was the eighth highest behind names like Rainiel Rodrigez, Edward Florentino, Emil Morales, Eduardo Tait, Luis Pena, and Braylon Payne. I mean these are pretty big time hobby guys.

It would have been very easy for the Nats to have Feliz repeat Single-A given that he is still extremely young, was advanced for that level last year, and produced average results, but as they did with Fitz-Gerald they opted to promote him to High-A to free up space for Willits, Fien, and Dickerson. When I did my minor league roster cheat sheets last week Feliz caught my eye because he is 2.86 years younger than the average hitter in High-A, tying him with Nathan Flewelling (TB) and Luis Pena (MIL) for the second youngest Bowman hitters to start the year there (Rainiel Rodriguez is #1). Of course I'm never going to pull data from three games and act like a player is on fire, but there are certain things that are good to see early on with young players especially when they are going up against advanced competition. One is that they aren't pressing. In his first 14 PA Feliz has drawn six walks (42.9%) while striking out just once. He's also stolen three bases in three games. I think the big think with Feliz will be power. Maybe it's 45 grade, maybe it's 50, maybe it's 55. Too soon for me to really get a read but for under $10 I'm willing to find out, especially since the Nationals believe in him enough to continue to put him on the field against players so much older than him.

players.name: Luke Dickerson
players.note:
Another player in that same 2025 Bowman Chrome release as Devin Fitz-Gerald was Luke Dickerson who was my 13th ranked hitter chase in that product, two spots higher than Fitz-Gerald. He was a player that I really went back and forth on and I had him as high as 10th and as low as 16th in my first drafts because I honestly have never been able to get a great read on Dickerson. Many things about him pull me in opposite directions but the fact that his base autograph is under $10 is enough for me to take a chance on the good that I've seen. I'll start with the bad. Last year in Single-A he hit .204 with 5 HR, 21 SB, 12.3% BB, 25.2% K, .116 ISO, and 88 wRC+. Not only is that not encouraging but he's now 20-years-old and starting the year in Single-A again this year so he's going to have to turn it on very quickly and get moving to be a big hobby name. As you can see in the rankings above there's some disagreement on if that will happen with Chris Clegg ranking him as his 114th best prospect but James Anderson putting him at 281st. I admit that sometimes when I'm torn on a player I will look to see where some of the sharper dynasty guys have them ranked and those two being so far apart does not help me one bit.

With that being said, the good is very good because the ceiling for Dickerson could be huge. The Nationals took him in the second round in 2024 and signed him for $3.8 million which was the slot value of the 22nd overall pick in the first round, and was the highest signing bonus ever given to a player outside of the first round in the bonus pool era. When I talk about multi-sport athletes in high school the most common one is football and with some of the more athletic guys you see some basketball. Luke Dickerson was a hockey player and led his team to a state championship, not sure what you know about hockey but it isn't easy. This state title run actually cut into baseball season and made him miss the start of the year but despite that he tied Mike Trout's HR record for the state of New Jersey. As you can guess the hobby tools are fantastic. Not only does he have above average power but he flies and his 60-yard dash times suggest he could have 70 grade speed. The results haven't exactly popped yet on the field but I think because of the tools his hobby ceiling could be big. It's still a developmental project but for under $10 I would take a stab at it.

players.name: Yeremi Cabrera
players.note:
Rounding out the hitter buys I'm going with the fourth and final hitter that came over in the same trade from Texas and that's Cabrera. Different set of skills here but he falls in kind of the same boat as Feliz in that at around rank 200 for hitters if your autograph is under $10 I think it's worth a buy. After signing with the Rangers for only $10,000 back in 2022 he struggled in his professional debut in the DSL and most times when a player has to repeat that level I'm immediately out on their cards because you shouldn't struggle against the pitching there. However, after posting an 83 wRC+ there in his debut he returned as an entirely different player, hitting .327 and raising his wRC+ to 153. Now I will say the only thing that can keep you somewhat in my good graces if you had to repeat the DSL is if you were 16-years-old the first time around which Cabrera was. Since he was so young that meant that even after being held there, his stateside debut still came at age 18 and seeing him play in the CPX is what really got my attention. In his first 211 PA in the states Cabrera hit .301 with 9 HR, 17 SB, 19.0% BB, 20.0% K, .270 ISO, and 149 wRC+ as an 18-year-old. Whoa. 

If you look at players who were age 18 or younger with 200+ PA at any single level that year, he is the only one who hit .300 with an ISO over .250 and had a strikeout rate under 22%. Not only did nobody do that at any level in 2025 but the only person who did it the year prior to Cabrera in 2023 was Eduardo Quintero (now in my top 10 prospects) back when he was in the DSL. Since he couldn't be contained the Rangers promoted him to Single-A for the final few weeks and he struggled with a 79 wRC+ but was only 18 so that wasn't really a concern to me. Last year he saw Single-A again at 19 and hit .256 with 8 HR, 43 SB, 11.5% BB, 19.5% K, .110 ISO, and 120 wRC+. Here's the thing with Cabrera, his tools are phenomenal for the hobby. Above average power and plus speed. He's also a plus defender in CF. BUT his hit tool needs work. Even in his dominant 2024 season in the CPX he had a 66.8% contact rate. Though his power fell way down last year I will say that him increasing his contact rate from 67.3% in 2024 to 75.9% last year is a massive improvement. The main issue is his splits as he he had a .566 OPS against lefties last year and really struggles in left-on-left at-bats. The hobby clock might be ticking because despite reaching Single-A at 18 he's starting the year there again this year at 20. I don't know for sure that he'll ever iron out the hit tool but since the other tools are so loud and you can regularly find his autographs for $5 I definitely like the upside as a flier, so long as your comfortable with his great ceiling coming with a low floor.

Of course I have nothing bad to say about

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.note: both fall in the same range for me outside the top 300, I don't love either but since both should see their MLB debut this year they're not bad holds. I thought that Morales would be a huge power bat coming out of Miami but the HR and ISO numbers just aren't at all what I was expecting. The raw power itself is still there but because of his swing decisions he hasn't been able to get to all of it. Franklin I think I trust a little bit more as a hitter and he's got a little bit of speed which makes him more exciting, unfortunately he's 26 which is a hobby death sentence. You can hold both and hope that their MLB careers start hot and they see a bump.

players.name: Miguel Sime Jr.
players.note: is massive but this price tag is already a little too crazy for me. I mean I know a big teenager who throws 100 mph is the hobby dream but he's priced higher than Kevin Defrank so I think maybe we need to pump the brakes a bit. We don't know much about the secondary pitches. I'm still not sure the command is very good. I need a few more starts to make any decisions on Sime and by the time I do it feels as though I'll be priced out of his cards.

players.name: Travis Sykora
players.note:
buys it's just tough for me given the injuries. The Nationals have really been decimated by pitching injuries in their system but even with my newest rankings update that will come out tomorrow I still have both Susana and Sykora as top 10 hobby pitchers. Two things really drive the market when it comes to pitchers in Bowman and that's having electric stuff and posting absurdly high strikeout rates, and there aren't many pitchers in the minor leagues who excel in both of those areas more than these guys. Unfortunately, Susana is going to miss at least the first half of this year recovering from a torn lat muscle and Sykora will likely lose the entire season due to Tommy John. Neither of these things change my positions on them but when I'm buying pitchers I'm usually looking for one of two things, a player who has not yet broken out that has the potential to or a guy who has a chance of making his MLB debut this year. Since neither of those apply to Susana or Sykora now that their timeline has been pushed back it feels like we could wait until the offseason entering next year and see if we can't get a better price on them.

The hobby ceiling for

players.name: Alex Clemmey
players.note:
