is one of the youngest pitchers to start the year in Double-A at 20 and he's extremely projectable as a 6'6" lefty but my ranking for him is right about where I'd put an autograph that's this price. He tiptoes the line between a 3 and 4 and probably could have been a 4. Really good stuff but way too many walks I'd like to see that improve this year before moving him into the buy range. I think he's somebody who if we see real improvements this year we should have a period of a month or two to buy before he starts getting recognition in the market because he's never been a very buzzy name, but the bones are there for him to make a big jump if that command gets better.

I would be slam dunking a 5/5 on

players.name: Landon Harmon
players.note:
It's always tough for me to take a chance on prep pitchers in Bowman because it can often be a long road where somewhere along the way you'll be able to get a player's cards for cheaper than they are right out of the gate. And that's exactly what kept me from making Seth Hernandez a buy because while I do agree that he has Skenes-esque buzz a part of me wants to believe that some time between now and when he debuts that price will go down some. Based on his professional debut I may be wrong but we'll see. Landon Harmon however did not get much hobby love when 2025 Bowman Draft was released and that was a bit surprising to me since I had him as my eighth ranked pitcher chase in the entire product behind Gage Wood whose base autograph is about 4x this price currently. Harmon is a 6'5" righty who the Nats drafted in the third round and signed for $2.5 million which was $1.5 million over his slot value. As a varsity starter for all four years in high school he didn't have an ERA over 1.39 in any single season. As a junior he only appeared in seven games but went 3-1 with a 1.07 and four times as many strikeouts as walks. When he came back for his senior campaign he went 6-0 with a 1.17 ERA and FIVE times as many strikeouts as walks this time around.

Harmon is a very athletic 6'5" and that showed on the other side of the field where he hit .554 with 7 HR and a SLG over 1.000 his senior year. On the mound he uses his frame really well to create incredible extension and touches 99 mph pretty regularly as a teenager. He also showed a slider that should be an above average pitch but he will need to develop a good third offering. Luckily he has plenty of time. This is an incredible ceiling for around $10. It's not often at this price you get a big teenage arm who is going to throw triple digits and as he fills out his frame his velocity might get outrageous. Since he has an athletic delivery I don't anticipate him having control issues and the command should be good enough for him to stick as a starter as long as he sharpens those secondary pitches to go with the electric fastball. In his professional debut the other night he showed some of that swing-and-miss stuff striking out three and only allowing one hit over 2.1 innings, but he did also walk three. First ever start at age 19 I'm not worried yet about walks I'm sure there were jitters. For all of the hype that Miguel Sime Jr. has gotten early on this year, I have Harmon ranked higher and he's a third of the price. Really looking forward to seeing how he progresses throughout the year and I love the upside here.

players.name: Luis Perales
players.note:
This one was extremely difficult for me but I just can't get over how low this price is knowing how high Perales's ceiling is. Now he did get knocked in my rankings update but it only dropped him from 24th to 34th so at under $10 I could argue that he still should be a 5/5 but because he's struggled recently I'm less confident then I would have been a year ago. With that said, I still think he's a buy. Perales came over in a trade from the Red Sox for Jake Bennett this offseason and Bennett has looked great early on while I can't say the same for Perales. Here's the thing, you don't become a top 50 pitcher on Scout the Statline's Peak Projections on accident and that's because prior to getting Tommy John, Perales was one of the most electric arms in all of the minor leagues. In 2024 between A+ & AA at age 21 he had a 2.94 ERA, 1.19 FIP, 2.09 xFIP, 14.97 K/9, and 3.21 BB/9. Opposing hitters had a 60.7% contact rate against him. Quite literally insane. He always had reliever risk due to his below average command but he dropped his BB/9 in three consecutive seasons and his 8.3% walk rate that year was an extreme improvement from what we had seen in the past. Unfortunately as the story goes he tore his UCL and had to get TJ.

Perales missed basically all of last season recovering except for three appearances in September at the end of the season that the Red Sox brought him back for. After only one inning in AA they moved him to AAA where in his first appearance he threw one inning, striking out all three batters he faced, and landing 10 of his 11 pitches for strikes. Since he missed so much time Boston sent him to pitch in the AFL when the season ended. That's where he really showed struggles with the command, walking 11 hitters in just 11.1 innings. On the positive side he struck out 19 of the 60 batters he faced (31.7%), and of the 43 pitches in the entire AFL season that were thrown 100+ mph Perales was responsible for 20 of them. Sadly he struggled again in his first two starts this year and it feels like people are bailing on him but here's the thing, the stuff is so good. Last month Perales appeared in Spring Training where TJ Stats had the stuff grade on his slider at 116 and his 4-seam at 124. Those are basically two double plus pitches. Even in his first AAA start his year where he struggled his fastball averaged 99 mph with 19.2 inches of IVB. Elite. Might have one of the best fastballs in all of minor league baseball. Maybe I'm crazy but that pitch data keeps pulling back in. He's still thrown fewer than 20 competitive innings since returning from TJ and the fact that his stuff looks just as live as it did before makes me want to believe he'll find it all again. Since the last few months have been rough I would have stayed away at around $20-25 which is where this price was when he returned for the Red Sox last September, but at under $10 it's hard not to take a chance on his upside.

As much as I want to make

players.name: Alejandro Rosario
players.note: based on his price and ranking if these were normal circumstances but they are far from that. It was revealed back in February of 2025 by the Rangers that Rosario would need Tommy John but after that there were no updates which is common with minor leaguers. Turns out he never got the surgery. Can't find any stories on why, all we know is that after he was traded to the Nationals this offseason we learned that he only recently got the surgery so on top of missing all of 2025 he'll now also miss all of 2026. Still a name I'm watching because the last time we saw him he looked like a potential top 10 pitching prospect but with such a long layoff I'm going to need to see him after he returns. Now that he's under $10 I may snag a couple and sit on them but tough to call anybody a buy that is missing this much time.

players.name: Jhonny Level
players.note: Love to see Jhonny starting off with a bang — 4/5 buy at $29, up nearly 100% since. Four doubles, a homer, a SB. Hitting .519 with 2 HR, 3 SB, .407 ISO, 268 wRC+ in Single-A (30 PA). Hard to keep him at a buy now that he's doubled — more hold range. Could see more steam when he moves to High-A.

players.name: Chase Harlan
players.note: Surprising the market hasn't reacted more. Was a 4/5 rated buy at $17 — still a buy at current price. Big power potential, teenage prospect in a franchise that sells well. .217 ISO and a 23.3% walk rate (nearly double last season). Small sample but great start.

players.name: Taitn Gray
players.note: 4/5 with a base price of $12 — currently up over 250%. Two HR last week after a double and triple in opening weekend. Hitting .370 with .333 ISO, 202 wRC+. Switch-hitting 18-year-old on fire in Single-A. Signed for under $1M in the third round. Consider cashing a portion if you have a stash — 250% in two weeks is wild.

players.name: Josiah Hartshorn
players.note: Gave Hartshorn a 3/5 at $17 due to multiple high school injuries. Up over 100%. Gone deep, stolen a pair of bases, drawn TEN walks in 42 PA while only striking out once. Swing is very Bryce Harper-esque. Not sure I'd buy much higher but the upside might be worth it.

players.name: Nathan Flewelling
players.note: 5/5 rated buy on the Rays sheet at $12 — nearly tripled. Still in buy range under $30 given top 60 ranking. First 18-year-old in 20+ years to get 300+ PA in Single-A with 20%+ walk rate. More aggressive early this year leading to 2 HR in 24 PA (hit only 6 in 461 PA last year). One of the youngest Bowman hitters in all of High-A. Power surge coming.

players.name: George Lombard Jr.
players.note: Hold on my Yankees sheet at $150 as 28th ranked prospect. Hard not to go up when you're hot as a Yankee. Never surpassed 9 HR or .146 ISO in any season — already gone deep twice with only 4 Ks in 32 PA. Could hit $300 by debut. With Dax Kilby ranked higher at under $100, I'd personally go that route if I were a Yankees fan.

players.name: David McCabe
players.note: Sneakily productive bat since 2022 — 6'3" switch-hitter with plus power. 139 wRC+ in 2023, down year in 2024 due to injury, bounced back with 132 wRC+ last year. Back in AA this year where he's crushing it but is 2+ years older than average. Expect him in AAA soon if he keeps hitting. Age limits his Bowman appeal.

players.name: Samuel Zavala
players.note: 4/5 on White Sox sheet. Price oddly showing down due to redemption/sparse sales (only 2 base auto sales this calendar year per ProspectPulse). Hobby darling in 2023, fell off in 2024. Bounced back with 122 wRC+ as 20-year-old in A+ last year. Two years younger than average in AA. Already gone deep twice with 177 wRC+ in 36 PA. Still solid upside for how cheap he is.

players.name: Blake Burke
players.note: Knew he had massive power — 16 HR/.161 ISO in 567 PA last year with surprising .292 BA. Did not buy. He has now hit SIX homers in his first 43 PA at AA. Strikeouts up, contact down, but the huge power we knew was in the tank is out. Wouldn't be surprised if he hits 30 HR this year. Tip of the cap to those stashing him — likely up 200% soon.

players.name: Anderson De Los Santos
players.note: Back-to-back great weeks in AA. Swing rate down 11%, drawing 10 walks in 31 PA. Added a homer, three doubles, and a SB. Drastic improvements from '24 to '25 so a leap is possible. Want to see more before buying — put a pin in it.

players.name: A.J. Ewing
players.note: Made one of the biggest hobby ranking jumps from end of last season — now 23rd. First said 'buy' at $9 exactly one year ago — up nearly 600%. Double plus speed (70 SB last year), plus defense in CF, great contact. Part of the reason he was 3/5 at $50 is below average power. But the other tools may be enough to sustain the price.

players.name: Charles McAdoo
players.note: Had him as 3/5 — may upgrade to buy. Price going down feels disrespectful. 24 years old is playing a role. But 17 HR/21 SB in 2024, 16 HR/34 SB in 2025. Hitting .325 with a HR, 4 doubles, a triple, and SB in first 47 PA. Swing rate down 7.5% leading to nearly 6% more walks, striking out 8.6% less. Great bat getting very little love — price trending down makes no sense.

players.name: Esmerlyn Valdez
players.note: 4/5 buy on Pirates sheet — biggest Hot Sheet win last year. First 'buy' call at $7, went over 1,000% by end of season at $80+ in the AFL. Price got cut in half since November which felt crazy. In 59 PA: 3 HR, 25.4% walk rate, 18.6% K rate, .256 ISO, 170 wRC+. Saw this card hit $90 once before. One of the better power bats in AAA, will almost certainly debut this year.

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: Not sure what can be said about this kid that hasn't been said before. Struck out 15 of 25 hitters faced (60%) while walking only one across two starts. Best high school pitcher I've seen in six years of ranking — not particularly close. Only one prospect with the type of stuff that could generate Skenes-level buzz prior to debuting and it's Seth Hernandez.

players.name: Jesus Tillero
players.note: Name to watch. Dominant in DSL debut at 17 with 1.47 ERA in 10 starts. Two starts this year: 5 IP, 2 H, 8 K followed by 6 IP, 2 H, 5 K — yet to allow a run. Command looks improved, swing and miss up, young for the level, and he's a Dodger. Could be a sneaky hobby arm if he keeps it up. Already stashed a few personally.

players.name: JB Middleton
players.note: Getting close to stamping as a buy. Liked him out of Southern Miss — 10-1, 2.31 ERA, 10.42 K/9, 2.14 BB/9, second best WHIP in all of D-I over 105.1 innings. Concern is smaller frame and proving starter workload. Rockies pitcher discount keeping prices low but with a couple more strong starts will likely crack top 200 and probably be a buy under $10.

players.name: Malachi Witherspoon
players.note: First buy at this level and has now doubled since team sheet. Concern was never stuff — potentially three plus pitches — but control. Through two starts (8 IP) has walked one while throwing 66 of 107 pitches (61.7%) for strikes. Command looks much better than expected. Now at $15 he's in hold range until he proves it longer or against better competition.

players.name: Gage Wood
players.note: Electric start. Between two starts: 7.1 IP, 3 H, 1 R, 2 BB, 15 K (57.7% of batters). Concern is smaller at 6'0" and never threw more than 40.1 innings in any college season. 0.57 FIP shows how unhittable he's been. First round pick, $3M bonus, threw a no-hitter in CWS. Phillies need to move him to High-A — he's clearly not going to be tested here.

players.name: Tanner Franklin
players.note: Unreal start to professional career — highest High-A pitcher on the sheet in consecutive weeks. Through 6.2 IP: 3 H, 0 R, 16 K of 28 batters (57.1%). Only concern is 26 of 27 appearances at Tennessee came in relief and early walk rates were terrifying, but much more accurate at Knoxville. Cardinals deploying as starter. Could be another Chaim Bloom masterclass. Wait for hype to cool — like him around $20, $30+ is steep.

players.name: JT Quinn
players.note: Wasn't even in top 200 on Orioles sheet — now 101st, showing how high you can shoot with a strong debut. Tied for most K's of any Bowman pitcher in High-A last week — 10 K in 4.2 IP, 2 H, 0 BB, 0 R. Two extremely strong pitches (fastball, slider) but command has been shaky and reliever risk is real. Control has been good early though. Don't think this is a bad price to get in at.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: Broke the news in Discord that no Red Sox prospect drew more rave reviews in camp. Velocity sitting 95-97 mph — significant bump from low 90's at LSU. Secondary pitches are filthy. Dev staff source said he 'might be first one from that group to get to Double-A'. Quite a rise the last month or two — at this price I don't know that I'm buying anymore.

players.name: Steven Echavarria
players.note: Very sneaky buy — got first round money ($3M) as a high school senior with 99 mph fastball and plus slider. 6.55 ERA debut, 4.59 ERA last year but was 18 and 19 at the time. Only pitcher to start 25 games at High-A at age 19 or younger last year. Still 2+ years younger than average pitcher at this level. Cold weather prep arms often develop slower. Fun cheaper stash for the upside.

players.name: Tyler Bremner
players.note: 4/5 buy on Angels sheet at $30 — up close to 50% since. Legit arm despite the 'can you believe they passed on Anderson' narrative. Surrendered hits to just 2 of 25 hitters (.095 AVG) while striking out 10 (40%). Imagine a few more starts before he moves to Double-A — and Triple-A this year feels likely. Angels may let him climb every level and reach the MLB this year. Solid grab.

players.name: Kash Mayfield
players.note: 5/5 rated buy — fascinated that price hasn't moved more. 6'4" lefty hasn't allowed a SINGLE HIT in first 7 innings at High-A (two years younger than average at this level). 7 IP, 0 H, 0 R, 5 BB, 8 K. Walks are an issue but he's so hard to hit it barely matters. Last year only three pitchers age 20 or under threw 60+ IP with K/9 over 13 — White, King, and Mayfield (Kash's walk rate was 3% lower than both). Big breakout coming. Market is off on him.

players.name: Jordy Vargas
players.note: Hasn't done much recently to inspire Bowman hope, but impressive in DSL and CPX early on. Missed all of 2024, returned last year with extremely high K rate but walking 16%+ of batters — doing again this year. Opponents have had sub-70% contact rate in three consecutive seasons. Feels like a reliever profile but we'll keep watching just in case.

players.name: Joseph Dzierwa
players.note: Got people buzzing with impressive Spring Training into debut — 6 IP, 1 H, 0 R, 9 K. Coming out of Michigan St. I had him more as a strike thrower than high K guy which kept him in hold range on Orioles sheet. This start showed more of what I expected — threw strikes, limited damage, but only struck out a few. Good upside but base auto was $7 on Orioles sheet, still up almost 200% from there so more of a hold.

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: Perfect example of small samples shifting rankings — first two starts so good it rocketed him to #1. Note: Thomas White making a rehab start in Single-A affected the formula, will normalize within a week or two. Went from 5th to top after consecutive scoreless starts — 9 IP, 5 H, 17 K. Doing so in AA is an aggressive assignment even out of college. Don't envision him falling outside top 3-4 anytime soon. As the biggest name college pitcher there was never a chance to get in early — makes his price a hold.

players.name: Richard Gallardo
players.note: Two different $1 pitchers turned in back-to-back strong AA appearances to start the year with Gallardo being one. Professional debut back in 2019 as a 17-year-old but has struggled to stay healthy — only 18 IP in 2024, missed all of last season. Everything in his career statistics leads me to believe this hot start is noise and not news.

players.name: Adam Seminaris
players.note: Being over 27 and still in Double-A is not great for Bowman value. Actually had productive seasons and coming off best year — 3.02 ERA in 125.1 IP in AA with the Mariners. Command pitcher with low walk and K rates. K/9 is an impressive 12.66 this year but was 7.54 last year and I'm not sure I believe it. Too old to move up much.

players.name: JJ Goss
players.note: Was a decent name when the Rays selected him 36th overall in 2019 but hasn't done much professionally. Solid ERA last year but K/9 under 7. Even this year opening with back-to-back solid outings his K/9 is still under 7 and he's walked too many. Don't see much here.

players.name: Khal Stephen
players.note: 4/5 buy on Guardians sheet — love seeing him on here twice. Could fall off if I add a WHIP qualifier since he gave up 7 hits last week and 4 walks the week prior. Those walks improved this week but still too many hits. Strikeouts are up though — exactly what we want from him since low swing-and-miss was keeping this price in check. Contact rates down almost 7% early on vs last year. Not worried about walks since command is a strength. Watch the K's going up.

players.name: Alex Clemmey
players.note: Pulled me back and forth during team buy sheets — originally 3/5 hold at ~$15. Was the only pitcher who made more than five starts in Double-A last year age 19 or younger. Currently four years younger than average AA pitcher was last year. 6'6" lefty with double plus fastball and really good curveball. 3.47 ERA, 10.49 K/9 at age 19 last year. BUT 5.63 BB/9 and no great third pitch. Concern he's being groomed as a high leverage reliever. Price has inexplicably gone down — if you can get the base auto at $10 it's worth the hold for the upside.

players.name: Hagen Smith
players.note: Entering 2025 was one of the more exciting hobby pitchers but ranking slipped due to command struggles — 6.66 BB/9 in AA last year (17.6% walk rate). Through three starts this year the White Sox version we all expected when they drafted him 5th overall out of Arkansas. 14 K in 9 IP and only 3 walks of 37 batters (8.1%). Though I have Schultz ranked 2 spots higher, Smith is worth grabbing since his time will likely come this year as well.

players.name: JR Ritchie
players.note: 4/5 buy on team sheets — was $38 at time of article, up almost 50% since. Made two starts last week — 12.2 IP, 3 H, 1 R, 12 K combined. At this point it's inevitable we see Ritchie get called up. Still think we see more Fuentes at big league level first but the Braves rotation could use help. Still not a terrible buy since call up is coming soon, but based on ranking I don't see a ton of value at this price. Hold what you've got though.

players.name: Noah Schultz
players.note: Was in the same boat as Smith — big hobby name before stats fell off. Similar walk issues (5.55 BB/9 in 73 IP last year). Something the White Sox put in the water this offseason — he's arguably been the best pitcher in AAA since the start of the season. 3 appearances: 3-0, 1.29 ERA, 12.21 K/9, 1.29 BB/9. Facing 47 batters — .089 BA, 40.4% K rate. Gross. Set to make his major league debut tonight. Wishing him all the best!

players.name: Sean Sullivan
players.note: Put some respect on Sean Sullivan's name! 4/5 buy on Rockies sheet — may be the most productive pitcher in all of the minor leagues you've never heard of. Consecutive seasons in 2024 and 2025 with 100+ IP and ERA under 3.00. Nobody cares in Bowman because he throws ~90 mph and doesn't post big K numbers. But he's incredibly effective. Was the only pitcher other than Ritchie who made two starts last week and still qualified. Now in AAA and will probably debut this season. 70 grade command gives him a solid floor as a back-end starter — more than you'll find for $5 elsewhere.

players.name: Tanner McDougal
players.note: The only one of the three White Sox pitchers I made a buy on their team sheet — name of the game is value. Made massive strides last year, drastically improved walk rates with three plus offerings: fastball sitting 100 mph, two huge breaking pitches. In 15 IP this year: 2.40 ERA, two 8-strikeout games in three starts. Hold him through the MLB call up. Not as big a name as the other two, might not get the initial buzz, but I'd argue he has the best chance of the three to blow people away with his stuff. Still a good buy.

players.name: Brody Hopkins
players.note: 5/5 buy for the Rays — long felt like he's incredibly slept on with some of the best stuff at the minor league level. Walk concerns have crept up again — 5 walks in 5 innings last week. Even with that though ERA under 2.00 through 14 innings because opponents batting just .191. As he gets going the walks will come down. Capable of rattling off a 10 K game at any moment — great pitcher to target at this price. Didn't start pitching seriously until spring of his final college season (three years ago) and already inside my top 25 non-debuted pitchers. Huge ceiling.

players.name: Yeremy Cabrera
players.note: One of the hottest hitters in Single-A this week — two homers, a triple, two doubles, six stolen bases, and seven walks. .640 OBP. 20% BB rate, .362 ISO, 214 wRC+ in 60 PA. BABIP is sky-high and contact rates still aren't great, but a player with his tools shouldn't be this cheap. Still a buy. High-A promotion likely soon.

players.name: Caden Bodine
players.note: Hit .556 with a .636 OBP and struck out only once all week. 89.6% contact rate, 3.2% K rate in 63 PA this season — his bat-to-ball skills are the real deal. 60 grade hit tool. Hobby ceiling questions remain for a hit-over-power catcher. Already a buy in my opinion. Needs to be in High-A or Double-A now.

players.name: JoJo Parker
players.note: Made him my #2 chase in 2025 Bowman Draft behind Eli Willits. Through 61 PA as a pro: .298 BA, 2 HR, 6 SB, 19.7% BB, 21.3% K, .255 ISO, 186 wRC+. Selective, not chasing, drawing walks, hitting for power and speed. Small sample but there isn't really a flaw in his offensive data yet. Could be the real deal.

players.name: Emil Morales
players.note: Third straight year where BABIP luck seems to be on his side — .404 in CPX, .425 in A last year, .457 in A this year. The power projections for the teenager are off the charts and .262 ISO at age 19 is what sells. Still think he's more of a .250 hitter long-term but he smashes the baseball. Big time upside, plays for a franchise whose prospects pop in the market.

players.name: Rainiel Rodriguez
players.note: The craziest stat when doing these sheets is that dark green age highlight — youngest hitter with a Bowman auto at the entire High-A level. What he's done there against players years older is remarkable. Kept OPS over 1.000 without a homer — over .500 OBP with five doubles. .280 ISO, 192 wRC+, 1.43 BB/K on a 16.1% walk rate and 11.3% K rate. Forget the position. This bat is insane. Still a buy.

players.name: Lonnie White Jr.
players.note: Blast from the past. At one point I was a huge Lonnie White Jr. fan — made nice profits when he tore it up early in 2023. Back in that Florida League season he may have been the best athlete in all of minor league baseball. Former multi-sport athlete committed to Penn State. Injuries have derailed him every year. Until he stays healthy and produces at a higher level, watching from afar. Glad to see him back.

players.name: Nathan Flewelling
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Nothing makes me happier. Last year walked in 20.4% of 461 PA and hit 6 HR all year — gave me big Roman Anthony vibes. Hoped he'd get more aggressive in High-A and the power would take off. He has not disappointed. Walking nearly 8% less but already 4 HR in 47 PA with a .366 ISO. Hardest part is deciding whether to sell some pieces. Hobby rankings say this price should still be higher. Flewelling to the moon.

players.name: Caleb Bonemer
players.note: Strange sales — seen under $60 and sold at $100 ask. ProspectPulse average $70, still an easy buy there. Top 10 non-debuted hitter for me. .385 ISO, 171 wRC+ are pretty ridiculous. Only flag is 30% K rate and low contact early — calling it a yellow flag. Still a buy. Was under $20 when I first recommended him.

players.name: Danny Serretti
players.note: Contact-over-power switch-hitter who had an outstanding professional debut in 2022 — 177 wRC+ across three levels. Nothing of note since. Never had an ISO over .117 in a 200+ PA season but this year it's .450 with 4 HR in 13 games. Hard to believe it's real. Even if the power increase is legit he's about to turn 26 in Double-A — the path to hobby relevance is murky unless he's promoted to Triple-A immediately and keeps mashing.

players.name: Franklin Arias
players.note: Nobody had Franklin Arias 3-HR week on their bingo card — he only hit 8 all of last year. Sub-8% K rate at Double-A as a 20-year-old isn't surprising given the 60 grade hit tool. Any power increase here is massive. Roman Anthony has debuted, Marcelo Mayer has debuted, Kristian Campbell has debuted — Arias is essentially the only exciting young hitter left in Boston's system for hobby fans to target. No surprise the base auto jumped 40%+ this week.

players.name: Alex Binelas
players.note: Long road since the Brewers drafted him in 2021 — now his third franchise. Hit .206 with 25 HR in 2022, then failed to hit more than 10 HR in each of the past two seasons while improving his average. This year both are clicking: .459 ISO with 5 HR in 47 PA. Best version of him we've seen. But as a 26-year-old in Double-A it will take a sustained crazy stat line to get real hobby motion.

players.name: Cayden Wallace
players.note: Showed up on several hot sheets last year and I kept thinking he might be figuring it out — but season-long lines were never spectacular, going hot and cold. Off to a 3 HR, 3 SB, 174 wRC+ start this year. Former second round pick of the Royals. A bit old for the level. Expect a Triple-A promotion soon, but even then needs an extended run there for me to have real interest.

players.name: Kendall George
players.note: One of the most electric men in the minors. Some may remember his 100 SB season last year — hit .295 with more walks than strikeouts. Hobby never gave him much love due to no power. Now hitting .408 with more walks than K's and 11 SB in 12 games at Double-A. Closest thing to Chandler Simpson left in the minors and he plays in a big-market org. Might take time but I think he goes up eventually.

players.name: Anderson De Los Santos
players.note: 3 weeks in a row and his cards are going DOWN? That's the beauty in finding prospects others aren't looking for. Age-appropriate hitter at Double-A with 1.000+ OPS in three straight weeks. .324 BA, .265 ISO, 184 wRC+. Swing rate down almost 11%, walking in 27.1% of PA. BB/K jumped from 0.66 last year to 1.30 this year. Wildly low entry point. Already want to pin him as a potential hobby sleeper.

players.name: Jesus Made
players.note: Not sure there's anything to add that you don't already know. An absolute freak. Nearly five years younger than the average hitter at this level and still too good for it. Him and LDV are in a league of their own. Hard to recommend buying at this price but whoever is the #1 prospect entering Spring Training next year tends to get pumped — happened to Holliday, Anthony, and Konnor Griffin. If he doesn't debut and graduate, Made could be a $500+ base auto.

players.name: Brock Rodden
players.note: When healthy a sneakily good bat. Last full season in 2024: 14 HR/29 SB, 116 wRC+. In 2025 before injury: .293 BA, 5 HR, 16 SB in 178 PA with 138 wRC+. Small switch-hitting infielder with plus speed, .160 ISO range throughout career. Aggressive swinger who doesn't walk much — BB/K not pretty. Solid producer when on the field but as a soon-to-be 26-year-old doesn't do much for me from a hobby standpoint.

players.name: Ryan Waldschmidt
players.note: 5/5 rated buy on his team sheet — the first one I did this offseason. His price is up since but I think it keeps going. Above average hit, power, AND speed — the power is probably plus. wRC+ at every stop: Single-A 143, High-A 141, Double-A 143, Triple-A 154. Hard to be better than this guy has been and yet he still doesn't get the respect he deserves. Should already be a $100 auto. My gut says called up before the All-Star break.

players.name: Michael Lombardi
players.note: Would buy now.

players.name: Ethan Pecko
players.note: A Pecko truther through and through. Scored a rehab start in Single-A after thoracic outlet syndrome — no surgery required and looks back on track. Made him a buy on the Astros sheet because he was drastically underpriced for his performance level and proximity to an MLB debut. Houston's rotation is dropping like flies and I still think we could see him this year.

players.name: Riley Quick
players.note: Would buy now.

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Best pitcher coming out of high school that I've seen in 6+ years of following prospects for Bowman. No hits allowed and 8 K's over 5 scoreless innings. We've never really seen a non-debuted pitcher do these kinds of numbers this far from an MLB debut. He's essentially the pitcher version of Konnor Griffin. Conventional wisdom says there's a ceiling but he may just be so good he's in a market of his own. This kid is the real deal.

players.name: Mason McGwire
players.note: Yes, there's a relation — Mark's son. One of the best minor league weeks we saw: 7 scoreless with 10 K's allowing only 2 hits across two appearances. Didn't pitch at all last year and when healthy in 2024 half his appearances came in relief where he struggled with command. Putting him in players to watch in case drastic improvements were made during his time off, but based on what I've seen I don't see much reason to buy in yet.

players.name: Gage Wood
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Another scoreless outing drops his ERA on the year to 0.79 with a K/9 over 15. Interesting to see the price drop — my suspicion is $60 might be the ceiling for a base auto on a college pitcher still in Single-A. He was too good to be there two starts ago. Love the continued dominance but hard to buy at this price until he replicates it at the next level.

players.name: Landon Harmon
players.note: Consecutive hot sheet appearances after only three starts. Best start yet — 5 innings, 2 hits, 0 walks, 5 K's. Struggled with command in his first two outings but made the correction. Teammate Miguel Sime Jr. was my Prospect of the Week but Harmon is ranked higher and is currently half the price. While everyone is freaking out about Sime (rightfully so) I'd probably pivot and buy Harmon at the friendlier entry point.

players.name: Hiro Wyatt
players.note: Stays in the sleepers section for now. Pedigree coming out of high school with a $1.5M signing bonus from the Royals but has been just okay in his first two pro seasons. A command-over-stuff pitcher so not super exciting. Any prolonged success this year could sway me — he's dirt cheap.

players.name: Mavis Graves
players.note: Maybe a buy? Most intriguing 'is this something?' start of the season. 6'6" lefty the Phillies signed out of high school for under $250k in 2022. Strong 2024 in Single-A (3.64 ERA, 12.54 K/9). Across 7 innings this year: 3 hits, 1 ER, 14 K's in 26 batters faced — 53.8% K rate, 18.00 K/9. Need to see more but moving him into the 'yeah, this might be something' portion of my rankings.

players.name: Johnny King
players.note: Particularly special — we're from the same hometown and I was posting clips of him as a 2024 Bowman Draft sleeper when he was one of the cheapest players in the entire product. Story similar to Mayfield: even when command is shaky it almost doesn't matter because he's so unhittable. Only three pitchers age 20 or younger had a K/9 over 13.00 over 60+ innings last year — Thomas White, Kash Mayfield, and Johnny King. Dominant at a young age with wild strikeout numbers is a beautiful recipe. Still a buy.

players.name: Kash Mayfield
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Wondered how many great starts it would take before people started buying and the answer was three — base auto nearly doubled after striking out 8 over 5 scoreless. Gave up his FIRST HIT OF THE YEAR in that start. On the season: 12 IP, 1 H, 0 ER, 5 BB, 16 SO (12.00 K/9). Made him a 5/5 buy on the Padres sheet and he's making me look like I knew what I was talking about. Biggest thing was the zero walks in the last start. Probably still a buy — I'd stop around $40 for now.

players.name: Cam Caminiti
players.note: Not cheap but still a buy. One of only two Bowman pitchers at this level who are still teenagers (along with King). Was a buy on the Braves sheet and might look even better than expected. Atlanta knows how to develop pitchers — Strider, Schwellenbach, and soon Fuentes, Ritchie, and Murphy. Caminiti got over $1M more to sign than any of those. Most pedigree of any arm they've signed in years. 3.5 years younger than the average High-A pitcher last year. Opponents hitting .212 with a 33.9% K rate against him. I think this is a top 10 pitching prospect in baseball.

players.name: Chase Shores
players.note: Wanted to see him pitch professionally before jumping to conclusions but I think I've seen enough. Two starts and already walking only 2 of 27 batters faced. Missed a bunch of time at LSU and command was shaky when he returned but that hasn't been the case as a pro. Monster on the mound at 6'8", touches triple digits. Angels let him go 5 innings and throw 65 pitches in just his second pro appearance — giving him every chance to start. High-A hitters batting .080 with 63.5% contact rate against him. A name to stash.

players.name: JT Quinn
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Coming around on Quinn as a buy. D-I pitcher in Single-A so wouldn't go crazy but worth grabbing something. Scouting report at Georgia was great stuff with big reliever risk. Not only has the stuff looked as advertised (14.79 K/9 in first three starts) but the Orioles have let him throw 60+ pitches in all three starts — set on letting him roll as a starter. Command has been the opposite of an issue: 1.93 BB/9, walking only 3 of 51 batters faced. Ready to see it in High-A.

players.name: Bryce Meccage
players.note: Had Meccage as a 4/5 buy on the Brewers sheet. Still not super excited about the control — two straight scoreless starts but walked 7 in 7.2 innings. Good at limiting damage and it's an aggressive assignment for his age, but needs to stop walking so many guys. Still like the upside as a big frame pitcher with good stuff. Walk rate is not sustainable for a starter.

players.name: Jordy Vargas
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Vargas is going to make me pay attention. Best start yet: 6 IP, 2 H, 0 ER, 1 BB, 7 K. Command struggles in the past so the lone walk was nice to see. My only issue is that he's been extremely lucky — 1.29 ERA comes with a 4.01 FIP and 4.44 xFIP, opposing hitters have just a .107 BABIP against him, and he's stranded 93.8% of baserunners which isn't sustainable. Officially putting him on watch but not yet convinced it's for real.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Have to tip the cap to Andrew Parker from SoxProspects — when he told me earlier this spring that Eyanson might be better than Kyson Witherspoon I thought it was an overreaction, but he hasn't looked wrong. Not only filthy stuff (42.9% K rate) but hasn't issued a walk all year. Incredible. Price has tripled in the last few months though. Inside my top 30 but not a price I can get behind right now. If he moves to Double-A and stays ridiculous we can talk about a $100+ base auto. I'd cash in some of what you have.

players.name: Tyler Bremner
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Another buy from the team sheets we're steadily making green on — was $30 at the time and keeps ticking up. Now inside my top 15 non-debuted pitchers and cracking the top 10 is in the realm of possibility. So many people gave the Angels flack for this pick but I think he's the real deal. 0.77 ERA through three starts, struck out 45.5% of the 44 hitters he's faced including 10 in his last start alone. His changeup might be one of my favorite pitches in all of the minor leagues. Promotion to Double-A coming soon and it's very much deserved.

players.name: Justin Lamkin
players.note: Don't hate a buy. Had Lamkin as a hold on the Royals sheet because I loved watching him at Texas A&M but thought he was more of a command pitcher that wouldn't generate whiffs professionally. The big lefty creates deception with funky arm action but I was unsure if his stuff was good enough. So far not an issue — 1.54 ERA, 39.1% K rate through three starts. Some BABIP luck and 3.84 FIP suggests possible regression, but his 13.89 K/9 and 60.0% contact rate tell me he's missing WAY more bats than expected. Under $10 I'm all about snagging a few.

players.name: Nazier Mule
players.note: The fastball/slider combo has always been nasty but throughout his career he's pitched himself into jams with below-average control. Walked one in his first appearance but three walks in 3.1 innings most recently — though he limited the damage. Good news: K's are up, 11.05 K/9 in first two starts is encouraging and his 11.8% walk rate is actually a massive improvement from the 18%+ in his previous two seasons. Trending right but too small a sample — need to see more.

players.name: Adam Seminaris
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Nothing like one of the hottest starts to the season and your autograph goes down from $3. Much of this is age — 27 in Double-A with no top 30 Phillies prospect status. But these starts have been really good with 6+ K's in all three. Surprisingly not ready to call this nothing. Had decent numbers last year but always a plus command/blah stuff pitcher. This year his K rate has jumped from 20.2% to 34.4% and K/9 is up by more than 5. Need to see it in Triple-A for it to matter, but if the stuff has truly ticked up he might not be the worst $2 pitcher.

players.name: Khal Stephen
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Breaking my brain. Has always been a command pitcher — last year across three levels had a 1.75 BB/9 and walked only 4.9% of hitters. Issue was not a big strikeout guy. This year K's are up, contact rates against are down 6%, but he's walked 20% of batters faced. Last start: no hits allowed but walked 5 in 5 innings. Since his track record even back to college shows he fills the zone I'm betting this walk rate corrects itself. Top 60 pitcher under $20 — still a solid buy.

players.name: Sandy Gaston
players.note: Great start but unfortunately he's a reliever — and not 'reliever risk,' he's actually a reliever only. Seven appearances this season with no starts. There is a path to being electric enough as a reliever to be hobby relevant and Gaston does have a really good fastball, but I'm not sure there's much of a ceiling here.

players.name: Matt Wilkinson
players.note: Could technically be considered three weeks in a row — qualified last week making two separate starts which is impressive. Second start of the week was ridiculous: no-hit through 5 innings with 6 K's against the same lineup he'd already faced. Extremely encouraging because Wilkinson had a dominant 2024 (1.90 ERA, 13.20 K/9, 2.81 BB/9 over 24 starts) before struggling last year. This year he looks like that 2024 version again. Inclined to believe 2025 was an off year and this is for real. I'm a buyer at this price.

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Anderson has been nearly untouchable — only one run over 14 innings. Mixing pitches beautifully, 41.5% K rate, 7.5% walk rate, 60.6% contact rate against through three starts. Assigning a college pitcher to Double-A to start his pro career is aggressive but he may already be ready for Triple-A. Not ready to say he's better than Thomas White or Robby Snelling, but we're probably flipping a coin. In terms of value though you can probably find more elsewhere given he's the most expensive pitcher not named Seth Hernandez by a decent margin.

players.name: Jaron DeBerry
players.note: Want to like DeBerry but can't understand his prices. They were this high when I did the Brewers sheet and they're staying there. Great pitcher but at the end of the day he's a command-over-stuff pitcher who might never strikeout enough hitters to have a huge hobby ceiling. Should climb the Brewers system with a solid floor as a middle-to-back rotation arm — totally fine buy at $10 and under but I don't understand this one at $20.

players.name: Herick Hernandez
players.note: Last week was in my sleeper section and went back out and did it again. Good: fanned 9 in 7.2 IP over two starts, sitting at 13.94 K/9, 31.4% K rate and 64.6% contact rate against. Bad: walked 7 in that same stretch and failed to make it out of the second inning in his last start. Would have been removed next week if I add a WHIP qualifier. ERA still under 2.00 because he's not easy to hit, but eventually walking this many batters will bite him — his 4.82 FIP agrees. Good stuff but needs to clean things up.

players.name: Zach Thornton
players.note: Was a hold on the Mets sheet — extremely effective command pitcher but was over $10 and doesn't strike out many hitters. More of the same through two starts: 2.61 ERA, BB/9 under 2.75, but K/9 under 9. Not a bad buy because there's something to be said about consistently keeping an ERA under 3.00 without spectacular stuff — will almost certainly pitch his way into a big league rotation. But if you're chasing big price increases from dominant outings he's not the guy. Great pitcher, still a bit slept on.

players.name: Dax Fulton
players.note: Made his case for Prospect of the Week striking out 10 over 6 scoreless innings. The issue: high highs and low lows — gave up 4+ ER in both starts prior. K rate is up considerably from last year which is great for a guy who struggles with command at times, but he's been very hittable over the past few years and didn't make it out of the first inning in his season debut. Marlins also have Snelling and White ahead of him. Very cheap sleeper but don't see much more right now.

players.name: Robby Snelling
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Probably put up the biggest fight for Prospect of the Week: 6 scoreless innings, 2 hits, 1 walk, 9 K's. These starts feel expected at this point — his market is finally taking notice after being slept on all of last season. Base auto was around $50 when I made him a buy on the Marlins sheet. This man has nothing left to prove in Triple-A. In 4 starts this year: 1.89 ERA, 41.9% K rate. Not bad for a guy once considered a command-over-stuff pitcher when drafted. Can't wait to see him pitch in Miami.

players.name: JR Ritchie
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! The man can't be stopped. In 5 Triple-A starts this year: 3-1, 0.99 ERA. Doubt he cracks my top 10 because he's never been the type to rack up enough K's to make people go crazy but he's a fantastic hold — the Braves are calling him up soon, probably before the All-Star break. If you want to buy and hope for a price spike on a strong MLB debut go for it, but for my rankings he's now in hold territory at this price.

players.name: Hagen Smith
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! White Sox have a trio of Triple-A arms mowing hitters down and we already saw Noah Schultz get called up with his card price spiking. When the day comes that Smith gets called on, same could happen. Priced almost the same as Ritchie but ranked 6 spots higher — more likely to grab one of his. The difference is the K upside, that's what makes cards go boom at debut. Plagued by walks last year but through 4 starts has cut his walk rate nearly in half while increasing his K rate to 36.5%. Should see him up in the somewhat near future.

players.name: Thomas White
players.note: Three straight Marlins pitchers in Triple-A — those Charlotte Knights hitters ran into a buzzsaw. The price jump is honestly funny. Was a buy all offseason around $50, came back from an oblique strain rehab start in Single-A and the price didn't budge. Then he twirls 4 innings of 2-hit ball with 8 K's back in Triple-A and everyone collectively goes 'oh yeah, Thomas White' and goes back to buying. Still a good price — could blindly pick him, Kade Anderson, or Robby Snelling and be happy. That's how close they are, yet White is about half the price of the other two. Pumped to see him pitch in Miami and even with the missed time I'd be surprised if we're far from that.

players.name: Leo De Vries
players.note: The margin between Leo De Vries and Jesus Made is now razor thin, I wouldn't be surprised if we saw them start to swap weekly depending on who is playing better

players.name: Rainiel Rodriguez
players.note: I think Rainiel Rodriguez is still a buy under $100 — ignore the catcher bias, I think this bat could be special

players.name: Aidan Miller
players.note: Was $100 during Spring Training but has fallen since he hasn't played due to a back injury. He has resumed swinging so maybe not a bad idea to snipe his auctions while he's off the field

players.name: Caleb Bonemer
players.note: Being $70 still doesn't make sense to me — his base auto should be $100 pretty easily by now

players.name: Ryan Waldschmidt
players.note: I think we see Ryan Waldschmidt called up in the next month or two

players.name: Ryan Clifford
players.note: Started slow but has now homered in 4 of his last 5 games

players.name: Franklin Arias
players.note: Hitting 6 HR in 13 games after hitting 8 all of last season feels crazy — not sure the power uptick will remain but if so he could continue to move quickly

players.name: Theo Gillen
players.note: Theo Gillen is the man, that's all

players.name: Juneiker Caceres
players.note: Slow start but he's picking it back up — having 2 HR already after only hitting 4 last year is worth noting. If his power increases his cards still have a ton of room to go up. Currently running a contact rate over 90% at age 18 in Single-A

players.name: Bryce Rainer
players.note: I felt like Bryce Rainer looked lost early on this year and I know people are excited about the promotion to High-A but I think that had more to do with them wanting Jordan Yost to get SS reps in Single-A. I'm not worried about Rainer yet but I'm not giving much weight to the promotion since it didn't feel earned

players.name: Justin Gonzales
players.note: Saw some early graphics floating around for 2026 Bowman rankings with Justin Gonzales missing from the top 10 — if he's not in the top 3 most expensive 1st autos upon release I'd be shocked. If that's the case be ready to grab him wherever you can

players.name: JoJo Parker
players.note: JoJo Parker looks like the real deal

players.name: Josuar Gonzalez
players.note: Don't worry about the drop in Josuar Gonzalez's rankings — the lack of 2026 stats dropped his production ranking but once he returns it will correct

players.name: Nathan Flewelling
players.note: Nathan Flewelling is the man, that's all

players.name: Roldy Brito
players.note: Roldy Brito and Juan Sanchez (TOR) will likely be top 5 hitter chases for me in 2026 Bowman. Brito could end up being a strong buy since many will view him as a backup chase to Ethan Holliday and most people paying up for Colorado in breaks will be willing to part with his stuff

players.name: Cam Collier
players.note: Not sure if it's prospect fatigue at this point but Cam Collier having an auto sell under $20 is crazy to me — still very high upside and already has 3 HR and a .221 ISO in Double-A this year

players.name: Braylon Payne
players.note: Autographs selling recently under $10 feels criminal — 4 HR & 6 SB already this year in High-A at 19, should easily be over $20

players.name: Yairo Padilla
players.note: On the 7-day IL with a shoulder strain — no injury updates which is par for the course in MiLB but worth stashing while he's out

players.name: Luis Lara
players.note: Wild to see the climb since the start of the year — the bat has always been legit but only hit 2 HR last year in 600+ PA. This year already has 3 HR at age 21 in Triple-A. $30 is not a cheap base auto but he has only base and no color so it should add more value to the base

players.name: Andrew Fischer
players.note: Don't panic — this is a typical recent draft pick big shift. Will be a top 10 chase for me in 2026 Bowman and probably closer to top 5

players.name: Abimelec Ortiz
players.note: Can't be letting these autos go for $6 — Nationals should have him up in the next couple of months and that first MLB homer is going to get the people going

players.name: Ethan Holliday
players.note: With the amount of Ethan Holliday advertising Topps has done and the fact that he's Jackson's brother I'm fully prepared for him to outsell Edward Florentino early on. On player profile alone he'd be outside my top 5 hitters in this product but since we're hunting for resale value and I know what type of premium his cards will command he'll be closer to the top 3 in my rankings

players.name: Deniel Ortiz
players.note: I don't hear much about Deniel Ortiz in prospect circles but he looked unreal last season — will be watching to see how he looks in Double-A the next couple weeks but could end up being one of my favorite sleepers in the new release

players.name: James Tibbs III
players.note: Everybody wants to freak out about James Tibbs III and his 10 HR but his base auto being $100 is a sell for me — between the bad in-zone contact rates and Dodgers inability to give prospects regular playing time in the MLB it will be hard for him to keep this hype afloat

players.name: Dillon Lewis
players.note: Could be a nice 2026 Bowman sleeper — very quietly went 22 HR & 26 SB last year but the checklist says he'll be in Yankees uniform and is now on the Marlins which could kill his price

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.note: No panicking on 2025 draftees! Nothing wrong with Neyens, Hammond, LaViollete, Carlson, or Pierce — just typical things we see when I start factoring in stats for newer players

players.name: Jadher Areinamo
players.note: Only hitting .172 with a 38.7% K rate since returning this year but the 3 HR in 7 games are way more impressive for a player whose contact skills are consistently plus. The batting average will correct and if the power stays he could fly up

players.name: Edgar Montero
players.note: Keep an eye on Edgar Montero and Daniel Pierce these next couple weeks — I think both could end up as top 10 hitter chases for me in 2026 Bowman

players.name: Daniel Pierce
players.note: Keep an eye on Edgar Montero and Daniel Pierce these next couple weeks — I think both could end up as top 10 hitter chases for me in 2026 Bowman

players.name: Taitn Gray
players.note: Big time up arrow right now

players.name: Samuel Zavala
players.note: Big time up arrow right now

players.name: Yeremy Cabrera
players.note: Big time up arrow right now

players.name: Josh Owens
players.note: Played in an extended spring training game last week where he played both ways — hitting a 426 ft. HR and also throwing 95 mph on the mound. It appears the Rangers will continue to let him do both for now which gives his autographs a considerably higher ceiling

players.name: Cole Mathis
players.note: Was a 2024 Bowman Draft sleeper for a lot of people but wasn't healthy for much of 2025. Hit 7 HR in 14 games to start this year and was immediately promoted from A to A+. To be fair he's a 2024 college bat so crushing in A is to be expected but I do think his 55 hit and 55-60 power is a great combo under $15

players.name: Wyatt Sanford
players.note: Few players on the 2026 Bowman checklist have done more in the last month to increase hobby value — 175 wRC+ with 5 HR & 7 SB. Great name to file away because I don't expect him to be a big chase (for now) and think he has great upside

players.name: Kyle Lodise
players.note: Jumped wayyyy up the charts despite batting under .200 this year — breaking the rankings model by batting .190 because he has a 34.3% walk rate and 152 wRC+. Hasn't hit a single homer but enough doubles and triples to keep his ISO over .140. Very weird player but the analytics side wants to love him

players.name: Sean Keys
players.note: Sean Keys might just be the man, that is all

players.name: Victor Figueroa
players.note: Few players on the 2026 Bowman checklist have done more in the last month to increase hobby value — 218 wRC+ and 6 HR. Great name to file away because I don't expect him to be a big chase (for now) and think he has great upside

players.name: Anthony Huezo
players.note: Was one of my 3/5 holds on the Astros sheet I shouted out to watch early on and he has not disappointed. If that sheet came out today I'd probably make him a 4. Since his price hasn't changed I don't hate this as a buy. Could be plus power and above average speed. Last year had 8 HR and 18 SB at age 19 with a 139 wRC+, then went and played professionally in Australia where he slashed .340/.443/.588 with 6 HR in 30 games. Already has 3 HR and 9 SB this year with a .306 ISO. He's 20 so not young for this level and his contact rates are not the best (that's being nice), but for under $10 the power/speed makes him a decent target.

players.name: Anyelo Marquez
players.note: A touch older than I'd prefer for this level but not as ready to move him up in the rankings as I am with Huezo because the tools aren't as good. Contact over power hurts his card ceiling, but after hitting 4 HR in 191 PA last year he's already matched that in 76 PA this season. Worth putting a pin in — if the game power has genuinely increased he could be a solid stash with a safe floor, but need to see the HRs continue over a longer period before I'm interested.

players.name: Yasser Mercedes
players.note: When I talk about prospect pedigree this is a prime example. You can be a nobody and get hot for months and cards won't budge, but if you USED to be a big hobby name people remember much quicker and are willing to buy back in. I'd love to buy into this but tough considering Mercedes has been on my hometown Fort Myers Single-A team for three seasons. Happy to see him playing better but 10 good games isn't enough to erase how badly I was burned on his cards years ago. Maybe if he got promoted and crushed in High-A I'd consider — but nothing for now.

players.name: Cam Maldonado
players.note: This was my bad — Maldonado should have made last week's list but was left off due to my error because his cards say 'Cameron Maldonado' and it made him not populate in my rankings. Few have been hotter to start the year: 7 HR and 8 SB in his first 17 games with a .364 ISO and 169 wRC+. Contact rate over 80%, strikeout rate barely over 15%. Stat line alone is gorgeous, but 22.5 is pretty old for this level. Due for a promotion right now but he needs to get moving — not sure I can buy at this price yet.

players.name: Cooper Flemming
players.note: Was a buy on the Rays sheet which may turn out to be the organization that brings us the most money this year with increases to Flewelling, Gillen, and Taitn Gray already. What we didn't know about Flemming coming out of high school was if he'd have enough power — but if this season is any indication there might be plenty of it in the 6'3" teenager. Hitting .333 with 3 HR, 5 SB, .222 ISO, and a contact rate over 82% in his first 84 PA as a professional. I was already high on him but I don't think I was high enough. Grab something of his to stash.

players.name: Caden Bodine
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! My views on Bodine haven't changed much since last week. As a real life baseball player I actually like his profile quite a bit but ranking him in terms of hobby ceiling is tricky. Incredible bat-to-ball skills and basically allergic to striking out — 2.3% strikeout rate. His 187 wRC+ is the highest of any Bowman hitter still in Single-A which is impressive, but being a 22-year-old catcher with possibly below average power gives me pause. Don't love him, don't hate him. Need him up a level and hitting for power against better pitching for me to believe at this price.

players.name: Robert Arias
players.note: Love when the cheap under $10 buys on the team sheets show up early. Was a 4/5 on the Guardians sheet at $6 and on his way to tripling since then. One of the best contact hitters you'll find for his age — 14.6% walk rate to just 11.1% strikeout rate last year at age 18, and stole 29 bases in 46 games. My hobby scouting report: because everything else is so good all it would take to make the card double or more is to see a little power. After hitting 2 HR in 198 PA last year he's already hit 3 in 78 PA this year, and yet again has more walks than strikeouts. Major up arrows for me on Arias.

players.name: Lucas Ramirez
players.note: I don't know that any prospect benefited more from the WBC than Lucas Ramirez whose cards went nuclear due to his strong performance. I don't mean to be a hater but I'm not sure how long you can capture that hype if you're only a decent prospect. Since WBC stats don't factor into my rankings and I go strictly off minor league games this price feels insane. The 'he's Manny Ramirez's son' will fade eventually unless he can consistently produce. He is off to a good start but there are pretty glaring signs of regression to come in his approach, BABIP, and contact rates. I would have already sold everything I had if I had any.

players.name: Braylon Payne
players.note: Insert the Anchorman 'boy, that escalated quickly' meme. Been saying Payne under $10 feels crazy and just like that he's up over 250% in a week. Life comes at you fast. What's crazy is that I still have questions about the swing mechanics producing consistent fly balls but when you're the second youngest player on this list for the level and hit 4 HR in one week I guess I'll shut up. Incredible athlete and the raw power I've always felt was in the tank is showing its face. Walks are up and strikeouts are down from last year. Lot of up arrows. He could move up further in my first big in-season rankings update but I have the target price at about $35 so I'm probably holding after that big jump.

players.name: Yophery Rodriguez
players.note: After crushing the ball with Milwaukee, Rodriguez struggled a bit after the trade to Boston last year but was running some low BABIPs which led me to believe he was a bit unlucky. Still like the profile quite a bit, especially if he could consistently find power. He's done so this year with 5 HR in his first 17 games — the same amount he hit in 104 games last year. Contact is good, speed is really good (though he oddly hasn't stolen a base this year), so keep an eye on that power because he could get some serious helium if he keeps this up. Even with the 55% price increase he's not a bad buy at $14 since he's playing for a team with such a strong hobby fanbase now.

players.name: Lonnie White Jr.
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! If you are looking for the ultimate dice roll, Lonnie White Jr. may be one of the best athletes in minor league baseball. Unfortunately he's often injured and now in High-A for the third consecutive year because of the time he's missed. Since he could put up ridiculous HR/SB numbers if he stayed healthy for once it almost makes him worthy of a snag at this price, but until I see it in Double-A or better it's hard to invest much in a prospect his age.

players.name: Mike Sirota
players.note: Very few prospects had as dominant of a 60 game run as the one Sirota was on last year prior to his injury. He has picked up right where he left off and is once again looking like the prospect I thought he could be when I was scooping cheap autographs of his in 2024 Bowman Draft. Not often you get plus power and speed from a guy who is also a solid contact hitter and Sirota truly has one of the best packages of hobby tools you're going to find. He turns 23 in June and is still in High-A — my guess is he gets promoted very soon because he's way too good for this level. Even with the age adjustments I put the expected base auto value at around $70 so there's a little room here still.

players.name: Nathan Flewelling
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! I'm not sure it gets better than this. If you had told me one year ago that the best card in my collection today would be of Nathan Flewelling I would have assumed I lost half of my cards in a house fire. Instead he's just been the most consistently hot hitter of any prospect with a Bowman autograph. I've been toying with a formula for buy ratings and price targets — it's still a work in progress but I have the expected value on this base autograph at about $49 currently so even with the over 250% increase since I released the Rays sheet I still think this should be a touch higher. Flewelling to the moon.

players.name: Kaeden Kent
players.note: Didn't give Kent much of a look in 2025 Bowman Draft because I wasn't under the impression he had any above average tools, and he still might not, but there's a path to relevance if you're decent at everything — which he may be — and it doesn't hurt that he's a Yankee. Putting him on the official players to watch list because we know how crazy this price could go if New York fans decide he's a guy they like. I just haven't seen enough in the power department to move him up a ton in my rankings yet.

players.name: Josh Adamczewski
players.note: Was a buy for me at $27 on the Brewers sheet and he's up about 55% since then — not a bad start. Now inside my top 70 non-debuted hitters and the card market has reacted accordingly. When you put any of his career stats in a per PA sample he is arguably one of the best minor league hitters — the only issue is that last year's 308 PA were the most he's ever had in a season. In those he hit .320 with 5 HR and a 155 wRC+ and this year he's already matched that HR total in his first 62 PA. Seems like the Brewers just consistently find great under the radar bats. I wouldn't be surprised if Adamczewski was in my top 50 by the end of the year.

players.name: Ronny Cruz
players.note: I don't know that I've ever seen a universally unranked prospect come out of nowhere and get as much public hype in a one month span as Cruz has. Everywhere I look on Twitter it's Ronny Cruz — lofty player comps, scouts talking about how much they love him, people saying 'I told you so.' There's still time for him to move up in my rankings but for where I have him this price increase feels crazy. We saw Braylon Payne go up 200%+ but he's inside my top 100 and seemed severely underpriced to me. Cruz doesn't. People will point to the quick promotion to High-A but as a counterpoint that expedited move may have been because their Single-A roster is overflowing with infielders in Willits, Fien, and Dickerson. I'm not saying Cruz won't be legit, because he might be, but he has an aggressive swing rate and very low contact rates (61.3%). I may be way off here, but this price increase feels like a slight overreaction.

players.name: Caleb Bonemer
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! That formula I'm working on has the expected value on a Bonemer base autograph at around $150 — that's how drastically underpriced he is. He does have random $100 sales pop up and I think you're going to start seeing way more of them, but this average staying at $70 feels criminal. Already 7 HR and a .392 ISO in 20 games at High-A as a 20-year-old. I know he's a White Sox prospect but the lack of respect is astounding. Top 10 hobby name in my opinion and should be priced there.

players.name: Alex Binelas
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Do you know how hard it's gotta be to have a .531 ISO and 186 wRC+ over a span of three weeks and not see your base autograph budge from $2? To be fair you're not going to get hobby attention in Double-A when you're nearly 26. With that being said I don't know how long you can hit like this without seeing it move. I'm sure he'll be in Triple-A soon and it's hard for me to say a prospect this age is a buy at any level, but also it'd be hard to go down from here.

players.name: Jonah Cox
players.note: Another edition of 'too old to be here' but Cox is 24 which is better than some of the 26s we've seen on here. Last year he had 10 HR and 58 SB making him one of only five prospects in all of baseball to hit those marks. The speed is double plus but the power is below average — however his 3 HR in 18 games to start this year has his ISO sitting 100 points higher than it was last year. There's BABIP luck here but hard to argue with a 205 wRC+. He already has 12 SB and could legitimately go 15 HR/50 SB which would be insane for a $3 autograph even at age 24. Don't love it, but don't hate it.

players.name: Sean Keys
players.note: Take a bow Mr. Dahl from ProspectPulse. For those who don't know, Keys was one of his favorite sleepers entering this season as there was a ton of underlying data that suggested his 2025 season was much better than the surface stats showed. This year he's off to a ridiculous start, batting .338 with 9 HR through 17 games. Those 9 HR are second in all of the minor leagues to James Tibbs III who has nearly 50 more PA than Keys this season. I recommended Keys a few times when he hopped up on hot sheets last year because I've always been intrigued by this bat, but now that he's up over $20 I think it puts him in more of a hold range.

players.name: Franklin Arias
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! We thought the Arias power might be a fluke but he hit 4 more this past week and it may be time to start recognizing it. The market already has and his base autograph has quickly doubled since I made him a buy on the Red Sox sheet at around $60 earlier this spring. Part of me still leans in the direction of this power increase not being sustainable and his ISO which currently sits at .463 probably normalizes to under .200 by the end of the year. Even then it's a massive improvement from what we've seen from him in the past. Stock is way up but so is the price — not sure I'm buying any higher than this right now.

players.name: Anderson De Los Santos
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Last week I said De Los Santos may need to prove it some more even after three straight appearances and all he did was go out and do it again. There are hot starts I'm willing to look past because a player is too old for the level or has something in their underlying data that concerns me — but I have nothing on this one. Now he is running a high BABIP so his .340 AVG is going to come back down, but that's ok. In 70 PA: 3 HR, 22.9% BB, 20% K, .283 ISO, and 186 wRC+. Power up, walks up, contact up, strikeouts down. It's only been a month but I've seen everything I need to see. I'm down to give it a shot.

players.name: Sabin Ceballos
players.note: As a Braves fan I was sad to see Ceballos go when he was traded to the Giants back in 2024. He's got a very strange profile — good contact rates but not much in the way of power or speed, which makes it tough to be relevant in this hobby. Numbers didn't pop last year with a 102 wRC+ but his 82% contact rate and 7.3% SwStr% give him a fairly safe floor. After hitting only 6 HR in 420 PA last year he already has 4 this year and his .239 ISO is more than double what it was last season. Could be nothing but with such a safe floor it's not the worst play.

players.name: Danny Serretti
players.note: 3 weeks in a row and price going down is crazy — but again, you can't be 26 in Double-A and expect people to dump money into your cards. What's crazy is that I don't necessarily think this is a fluke. I think the hit tool is good, the approach is much improved, and for the first time in his career he's showing good pop. Unfortunately this age is a bit of a dagger into the buying value.

players.name: Jace Bohrofen
players.note: Actually thought this was a sneaky pick when the Jays selected him in the 6th round out of Arkansas back in 2023 and to be honest he's had a sneaky professional career — 181 wRC+ in his debut, then marks of 130 and 106 in two full seasons. Contact skills aren't great but he makes up for that with above average power and solid speed. Already at 6 HR and 4 SB but also has a 31.7% strikeout rate — that's just who he is. Positives and negatives but nothing really moves the needle for me.

players.name: Junior Franco
players.note: Since he hasn't played many full seasons I can't get much of a read on Franco. I've seen some good, I've seen some bad. One consistent thing is his ability to put the bat on the ball — posts contact rates around 80% pretty regularly. Never hit for much power but his two homers, five doubles, and one triple this year put him at a .210 ISO which is about 50 points higher than it was last year. To get there though he's sacrificed some contact with strikeouts almost doubling. Too soon to tell if this is anything worth monitoring.

players.name: Andy Perez
players.note: This isn't the first time Perez has started hot — I once scooped a bunch of cheap autos of his on COMC to flip when people caught on. Unfortunately that hot start didn't last and he's never put up a wRC+ over 100 in any full season. His contact rates are almost always over 80% but his swing rates are almost always over 60% which is EXTREMELY aggressive. I'm always thrown off by guys who swing at everything and are able to put the bat on it because eventually good pitching will take advantage of that. He's drawn one single walk in 80 PA this year and I think his inability to be selective will stop him from sustaining much success over a full season.

players.name: Travis Bazzana
players.note: Congrats to Mr. Bazzana who will make his last hot sheet — it was announced while I was writing this that he is being called up. Much deserved and it was only a matter of time because he's been tearing the cover off the ball for weeks. His price couldn't really have dropped by 30% and the explanation is that there were some outlier sales on the high side that temporarily spiked his average prior to last week's article. The $175 range is more standard for where we've seen him priced and it will be interesting to see what his call-up bump may look like. Best of luck to him in Cleveland!

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.note: I always have a soft spot for Morales because a lot of people were chasing him when 2024 Bowman came out and I pulled a true gold auto of his from my personal box that I ripped live on stream — a fun moment. Unfortunately much of his hobby appeal was the big power we expected when he was drafted out of Miami but it never really materialized. He's never hit more than 15 HR or had an ISO over .165 in any of his professional seasons. He's a player you can hold past his MLB debut because he can be streaky and you never know when that raw power will show up, but now that he's up around $10 I'm not actively buying.

players.name: Ivan Johnson
players.note: Good tools but Johnson is the oldest player on this list by over a full year. For a player this cheap his career has actually been pretty productive but I don't see much that leads me to believe we should be buying anything at the moment. If he continues this success over a span of a couple of months then we can talk.

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Ridiculous stuff from Hernandez to start his professional career. Through 4 starts he's 2-0 with a 0.53 ERA, 16.94 K/9, and 2.65 BB/9 across 17 innings. It's common early on that pitchers who have kept runners from crossing the plate will see big splits between their ERA and FIP suggesting they've been a bit lucky — but Hernandez's 1.04 FIP says he's straight up dominating. Opposing hitters have an almost comical 49.1% contact rate against him. He's struck out 53.3% of the batters he's faced and has allowed one extra-base hit after facing 60 batters. Probably the best pitcher we've seen come out of high school in the last 10+ years.

players.name: Hyun-Seok Jang
players.note: Stuff has never been a question for Jang — four different pitches which have graded out as above average or better at times, but the command has never been super sharp. Back in 2024 at age 20 he had a very impressive 16.69 K/9 but along with that came a 6.63 BB/9. Due to injuries he's now 22 and still in Single-A. There's upside because of the stuff and organization but he's never thrown more than 40.2 innings in a professional season. Also his autographs aren't terribly cheap which is common in Korean and Japanese prospects — tough entry price for an unproven player.

players.name: Riley Quick
players.note: Last week in the $10 & Under Sleepers section I put Riley Quick followed by a 'buy now' note — and that's because as a pitcher for my hometown Fort Myers team I've gotten a couple good looks at Quick and I think he could be a guy. Already ranked him as a top 12 pitcher chase in 2025 Bowman Draft and yet he's looked even better than I expected. The Twins are easing him in with no more than 3 innings in any appearance, but in 8 innings opponents have one hit in 28 tries while striking out 46.4% of the time. Even with the slight price increase I think he's still a buy.

players.name: Blake Wolters
players.note: Very interesting name to see pop up here. Wolters was thought to have one of the higher ceilings of any prep arm in the 2023 draft class — a multi-sport athlete who pumped 99 mph as a teenager. The Royals went way over slot and signed him for $2.8 million in the second round. Unfortunately as the story goes with many prep arms it didn't quite come together in his first two seasons. Now in his third consecutive season in Single-A he's finding more success, especially with the strikeouts where his K% is up about 6.5% from last year. Still think there's good upside because of the pedigree but need to see him continue to miss bats, and a promotion wouldn't hurt either.

players.name: Mason Morris
players.note: When I decided to add the WHIP qualifier to knock off pitchers who are walking too many batters, Morris did just enough to stay under that threshold last week despite walking 3 batters in his outing. The stuff is very good but the command is iffy. Though he dramatically improved his walk rates in his last year at Ole Miss he also worked exclusively as a reliever. He has the frame to develop into a starter but that would require refinement of a third and fourth pitch along with limiting his walks which are already over 20% this year. Will track that development but nothing yet.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! The life of being a Red Sox prospect — you start playing well and the eyeballs on your cards go up exponentially. When I did my team sheets shortly after 2025 Bowman Draft, the top two pitcher prices in the system were Kyson Witherspoon at $60 and Anthony Eyanson at $21. Over the last two weeks Witherspoon's base auto is averaging $35 and Eyanson's is over $80. Can't talk about Eyanson without shouting out Andrew Parker from Sox Prospects who let us know very early on that this might happen. Not that I don't believe in Eyanson but this price is pretty wild — since many of you got in at 25% of the current value I don't mind selling some pieces and taking your money. Not often you can 4x less than a month into the season.

players.name: Marcus Phillips
players.note: Feels strange to see a Red Sox prospect go down in price after back-to-back solid outings but when your teammate is Anthony Eyanson you don't get as much public love as you should. Turned in 3.1 hitless innings his last time out with five strikeouts, however he did walk four batters. Control seems to come and go — didn't make it out of the first inning in his first career appearance due to three walks, settled down walking only one in consecutive appearances after that, then struggled to find the zone again last week. On the plus side hasn't been easy to hit, allowing only two hits over his past seven innings while striking out twelve. Still think there could be some reliever risk here but working in Boston's pitching lab should help. Since we've seen what happened to his teammate's cards after a few good starts, I might be willing to buy this one and hope it clicks.

players.name: Johnny King
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! If King ends up being a top pitching prospect in baseball I may take one of my bigger victory laps — he was basically the pitcher version of Nathan Flewelling for me in 2024 Bowman Draft and I talked often on Twitter about him being a fantastic sleeper. Three hitless innings with three walks and four strikeouts last week. King is the youngest pitcher on this list at the High-A level. This might just end up being the Thomas White mold where a pitcher walks what looks like too many batters but because he's so hard to hit and has such incredibly good strikeout stuff it doesn't matter. King is still only 19 and will be until the end of July. The average High-A hitter is more than 22 years old. They're batting .114 off of him so far this year. Crazy.

players.name: Justin Campbell
players.note: One of my favorite prospect stories this year — Campbell made his professional debut earlier this month after being drafted in the first round all the way back in 2022. Can't be easy to shake off the rust when you haven't thrown in a real game for four years but he's been one of the most dominant pitchers we've seen this year.
