In 13.1 innings across 5 starts: 0.68 ERA, 37.5% K rate, 4.2% walk rate. Not uncommon for command to be one of the last things to come back after these types of injuries — but Campbell's command has been very impressive early on. However his card prices are flying up and we have to consider that because of the missed time he's now 25 and in High-A. I don't think it's a fluke but this price is already pretty high for where I'd rank him. Still awesome to see.

players.name: Justin Lamkin
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! If there's a pitcher this week that makes me think 'this is what hot sheets are for' it's Lamkin — making his third consecutive appearance without seeing hardly any reaction from the card market. Over four starts he's allowed a total of two earned runs (1.02 ERA) while striking out 12.23 hitters per 9 innings. Opponents are batting .153 off the awkward lefty and have just a 64.9% contact rate against him. I wasn't positive his stuff would play up enough against professionals to rack up strikeouts but he now has 6+ K's in all three starts in which he went more than three innings. I think he's worth a stash.

players.name: Braylon Doughty
players.note: Had a few nice starts to begin the year but the strikeout numbers weren't as high as I was hoping. He fixed that in his last start — after allowing a solo HR in the first inning he blanked his opponents for the remainder and finished the 5-inning start with that lone earned run and 8 K's while not walking a single batter. Through four starts this year: 1.88 ERA, 8.79 K/9, 1.26 BB/9. He's young for the level, mixes pitches better than arguably anybody his age, and doesn't issue walks. Hobby ceiling will depend on how high he can get those strikeout rates but I still think he's a buy at this price. Let's hope what we saw last week in the K department is a trend that will continue.

players.name: Tyler Bremner
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! We're almost there — creeping up on 100% gains since Bremner was a $30 buy on my Angels sheet and at this rate it looks like we'll get there pretty soon. Can't say enough about how good he's looked. Now sporting a 1.08 ERA, 13.50 K/9, and 2.70 BB/9 over his first 16.2 innings. His 39.7% K rate and 7.9% walk rate are just about identical to what we saw each year from him in college. Gets plenty of swing-and-miss while also not issuing many free passes. Felt he was very slept on in 2025 Bowman Draft and now he's showing why. Almost time to see him in Double-A.

players.name: Brody Brecht
players.note: Way back on the Rockies sheet I said if you're going to buy an arm for upside in their organization it's this one, and early on this year he's shown us why. A ridiculously good 15.63 K/9 — striking out 44% of the batters he's faced. His 3.55 ERA comes with a 1.73 FIP suggesting he's been even better than the stats show. Two issues: not exactly young for the level and very iffy control. Control did look in check last week when he threw a hitless 4 innings with 7 strikeouts and only walked one. He'll go as far as the improvements to his command will take him. Opponents are hitting .114 and he's going to continue to post crazy strikeout numbers thanks to his electric stuff — cards are a pretty solid hold.

players.name: Anderson Brito
players.note: Turning in a 10 K start and seeing your autograph price virtually stay the same feels crazy. I feel, as I've felt for some time, that Brito is one of the most slept on pitchers in the minors — that's why he was a 5/5 for me on the Rays sheet. Technically as my 30th ranked non-debuted pitcher with a base autograph under $20 he's still a 5/5 buy for me. Command issues in the past but they're not that bad — his 13.4% walk rate last year is down to 6.3% so far this year. On top of that his strikeout rate is also up. Even with a solid 3.68 ERA he's been unlucky — opponents have a .405 BABIP while his FIP is only 2.02. Have always loved Brito. Still love Brito.

players.name: Bryce Meccage
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Another player the WHIP qualifier would have weeded out in the past due to walks, but his two walks over five innings last week was quite an improvement from prior starts. Something tells me the Brewers unlock something here. For a cold weather prep arm who has already reached High-A in his second season he's on a pretty aggressive track and though the K & BB numbers aren't great I do think he has the stuff and makeup to get there. Could be a slow burn but at $10 and under I think he's a good long-term hold.

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! After his first two starts I had a disclaimer that since the sample of innings was small it wouldn't be surprising to see him slide back down — he apparently had other plans because he continues to just mow down hitters. After his most recent outing striking out 8 while only allowing one hit over 4.2 innings, I find it hard to argue against him being the #1 pitching prospect in baseball. Over his first 18.2 professional innings: 0.48 ERA, 30 K's, only 4 walks — a 38.2% K-BB ratio. Video game stuff. Anderson is showing why many expected him to be the first pitcher off the board in last year's draft.

players.name: Matt Wilkinson
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Last week I said I was in on buying 'Tugboat' and he didn't make me look bad — throwing 5.1 hitless innings with 7 K's which gets even crazier when you realize that the last time he pitched prior to that he led his team to a combined no-hitter. That's right, in his last two starts Wilkinson has thrown 10.1 HITLESS innings. His 2024 season was one of the best we've seen in awhile before he struggled in 2025. Whatever was wrong he fixed it, and having back-to-back hitless starts is crazy. Buy him up. All aboard the tugboat.

players.name: Jamie Arnold
players.note: More of the same from Arnold as this 2025 draft class has looked absolutely outrageous early on this season. Though he started the year outside my top 15 pitchers he's well inside the top 10 now and creeping up on top 5 — however the top 5 feel so locked into place it may be impossible to crack until one of them debuts. Arnold's showing that he was worthy of being the 11th overall pick with an ERA under 3.00 and a 34.4% strikeout rate in Double-A. His funky arm slot is especially devastating to left-handed hitters who are currently batting under .200 against him. Love what I've seen and I don't dislike him as a buy but he's in more of a hold range for me at this price.

players.name: Zach Thornton
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Eventually I'll have to make him a buy right? I've said it since the Mets sheet this offseason — he's extremely productive but as a command-over-stuff pitcher he's not overly exciting. I may be coming around on him though. He's a Mets prospect which means his cards could blow up at any moment if he has a start that gets any sort of public attention. He threw 72.2 innings last year with an ERA under 2.00 which feels impossible in today's game. This year he looks just as effective. Maybe it doesn't happen until he reaches Triple-A but I'm starting to find it hard to believe you can pitch this well in this franchise and not see your autograph go up. Not a bad player to hold and one of the safer floors you'll find at this price.

players.name: Ethan Pecko
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! After making two rehab starts in Single-A, Pecko returned to Triple-A and proved he's just as effective there — striking out 6 over 3 scoreless innings. Made him a 5/5 on the Astros buy sheet when he was under $10 because I've felt for awhile like he is one of the most slept on arms in Bowman. Unfortunately he had a scary injury to start the year but appears to be back and better than ever. The Astros rotation has already lost a few starters to injury and might need to make some moves. My guess is that they don't want to rush Pecko and the fact that he's only throwing 3 innings per start means they're likely ramping him back up. I do still think he debuts this year — makes him a great buy and hold since he's one of the cheapest of my top 40 pitchers along with Anderson Brito, who we know I also love. Good stash here.

players.name: Thomas White
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Running out of good things to say about Thomas White. Was my #1 pitching prospect for a long time and in my heart he still may be even though the formula has dropped him down a few spots. He's the cheapest pitcher in my top 5 with the four above him all priced a decent amount over $100. I still think that when it comes to pitchers the high you are chasing is a guy getting called up, striking out 7-8 MLB hitters, and his cards going to the moon — the Jacob Misiorowski special. We hoped it would happen with George Klassen but weren't so lucky. Of the pitchers who have yet to debut that have the best chance of replicating Miz's success in their debut I still think it's White.

players.name: Dylan File
players.note: Talk about a fascinating career path. As a 21st round pick in 2017 by the Brewers out of Dixie St., File was a pretty decent arm in the minor leagues during the pre-COVID era. After reaching Triple-A in 2021 he was there all of 2022 before leaving the MLB to go play in Korea for the 2023 season. After only one season he returned and has since had minor league stints with the Diamondbacks in 2024, Mariners in 2025, and now Tigers in 2026. Will be a cool story if he gets the chance to make his MLB debut after that journey but he's about to turn 30 and doesn't strike anybody out so I don't see much reason to buy anything.

players.name: Mitch Bratt
players.note: Not sure what's in the water in Triple-A this year but no lists are chalked full of my preseason buys more than the Triple-A pitcher hot sheets. It's been a mixed bag for Bratt — basically alternating between really strong outings and ones where he gives up a few runs — but despite that his ERA for the season remains under 3.00. With some of the best command of any pitcher in the minors he had a 1.54 BB/9 last year while also striking out more than 10 per 9 innings. Of the 216 qualified arms last year at every minor league level only one had a walk rate under 5% and a strikeout rate over 26% — and it was Bratt. His K's are down this year but the 5 in 4.1 innings last week puts him back on the right track. Because his command and pitchability are so good he has a rock solid floor as an MLB starter which is more than you can say about most prospects with an autograph this cheap.

players.name: Quinn Mathews
players.note: Another win for the buy sheets. The struggles Mathews faced last year were due to the ball that the Triple-A/MLB levels use — he was not able to adjust to the change after being promoted from Double-A. Even in interviews he cited how much it messed with his spin and we saw his walk rate balloon. Two weeks ago he walked 6 batters in 4.1 innings. Added the WHIP qualifier to knock those types of performances off the hot sheet but he came back last week and only issued one walk. Good news is his strikeouts are up quite a bit and his autograph price continues to climb. I'm not sure how you pitch at the MLB level until you figure this out which makes me a bit scared. Hopefully last week's outing was a sign of good things to come — still only cautiously optimistic.

players.name: Robby Snelling
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! White's teammate Snelling is a player I've been high on for awhile and even last year I had them neck and neck for the #1 and #2 spots despite Snelling getting way less love from most outlets. Well, that gap has closed and now everybody is aware of Snelling's dominance at the upper minor league levels. Between the start of this season and last year he's now thrown nearly 90 innings at Triple-A and has an ERA under 2.00 there. Starting to wonder what the Marlins are waiting for. If they're trying to win (remains to be seen) I think we see both of these guys before the All-Star break — but now that the market has caught up on his prices I'd be in hold mode waiting for that debut.

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.note: Another player who could move up on my re-rank — hard not to be impressed with the 5 HR and 7 SB in his first 20 games. The only downside is he has a 36.3% strikeout rate, kind of fitting the profile I expected for him coming out of the draft. Might strike out a lot but the power might be the best of any prep hitter in last year's class so the hobby will continue to pump him up. Be cautious because he's running a very high BABIP and with the low contact skills (67.6%) his average will likely come back down in the near future, but if you're buying you're buying the power and it looks for real. He's a hold for me at this price.

players.name: Cesar Quintas
players.note: I love getting in at the ground floor on very cheap prospects so I'd love to say that I see something here, but Quintas is now 23 years old and playing in Single-A for the third consecutive year. It would take way more than a few hot weeks before I had any interest here.

players.name: Cooper Flemming
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! When I saw this price I thought it was a mistake but nope — on May 1st somebody went and bought about ten base autographs at full ask at $40-45 and drove this thing through the roof. I was fully prepared to come on here and tell you about how Chris Clegg from Dynasty Dugout said he was the best player he saw on the field this week in Charleston and how I'll likely move up Flemming quite a bit in my re-rank — and those are still true — but this price will have to settle back down before I recommend buying because this is crazy! When I labeled him as a 4/5 buy on my Rays sheet his autograph was $7 so congrats to anyone who grabbed some fun color.

players.name: Jack Gurevitch
players.note: I won't say this is nothing but I need to see more. Gurevitch is old for the level and has a 30% strikeout rate — not ideal. The power however might be really solid. His last year at University of San Diego he hit .371 with 17 HR in only 56 games while striking out just 15.5% of the time. In his pro debut last year the hit tool looked shaky and none of that power showed up. This year the hit tool still looks shaky but the power is what we expected with 5 HR and a .281 ISO early on. Still need to see the contact improve and would like to see it up a level, but will put a pin in him.

players.name: Anibal Salas
players.note: This is a 'could be something' to watch going forward. Salas had a great DSL debut but when he came to the states he struggled in the CPX and had to repeat the level. This year everything is trending in the right direction — walk rate is up 5%, ISO is up from .166 to .234, and his contact rate is 13% higher than last year's. Still too early to get a good read but seeing both contact and ISO spike that much makes him worth keeping an eye on.

players.name: Byron Chourio
players.note: As a member of my hometown Fort Myers Mighty Mussels I'd love to say I've seen improvements worth buying but I'm not sold. Numbers look much better than last year but the underlying data is mostly the same. He was unlucky last year on the BABIP side and now he's a bit lucky this year — that 100 point gap is making up a lot of the production. Contact is still good as it's always been but there's not much in the other areas that leads me to believe a breakout is coming.

players.name: Mike Sirota
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Our hitting Prospect of the Week had one of the most ridiculous weeks we've seen yet this year with an OPS over 2.000 and a 3-HR day. One of my favorite targets in 2024 Bowman Draft the upside has always been big for Sirota and I still don't think we've seen the best of him yet. Even on the homers he hit last week not a single one looked like he got all of the barrel — his hands and bat speed are just fantastic. Can't imagine we see him much longer in High-A as this promotion should be coming in the next few weeks. In my opinion he's a much, much better hobby prospect than James Tibbs III so this base autograph getting to $100+ if/when he gets hot at the upper levels isn't out of the question.

players.name: Caleb Bonemer
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Justice for Caleb. I yelled on here last week about the disrespect that his base autograph was still somehow averaging $70 and he goes out and has a 4-HR week and shoots it up over $100. My target values actually went up even more and I still think he's deserving of being a $150+ base autograph. Not sure if it's the people afraid to collect White Sox prospects or what but I think whenever MLB Pipeline or Baseball America releases their updated rankings he's going to move up quite a bit and that will likely trigger a price increase. Formula says he's worth holding until that happens but I first labeled him as a buy last year under $20 so if you've 5x'd your money I wouldn't blame you for selling since I did the same thing.

players.name: Freili Encarnacion
players.note: On the flip side of what I said with Kent, when a prospect for the Yankees or Red Sox gets hot and gets absolutely no attention then I'm much more likely to take a stab. I'm not going to tell you that I love Encarnacion but for what he is and who he plays for this is not a bad buy at all. Last year he had 18 HR & 11 SB with a .190 ISO and 111 wRC+ but he's an extremely aggressive swinger. This year it's looked much better — 13.6% walk rate more than 8% higher than last year, already hit 5 HR with a .298 ISO. While he's batting just .212 his BABIP is crazy low at .225 and despite that still has a 127 wRC+. Age appropriate for the level, good power, on the Red Sox, and $2? You could do worse.

players.name: Felnin Celesten
players.note: Talk about a name you love to see. During the 2023 international signing period few prospects got more buzz than Celesten who was ranked second in the class behind Ethan Salas — a potential 5-tool switch-hitting shortstop who signed for $4.7 million. Unfortunately he battled injuries and didn't play at all in his signing year, and while he posted impressive numbers in his pro debut the following year it was also cut short. Last year he was merely average across the board and his stock fell big time, but through 108 PA this year the approach improvements have been massive. Walk rate is up 6% and strikeouts are down 4%, causing his BB/K to move from 0.41 to 0.81. Since there hasn't been enough production for me to rank him higher he's a hold at this price, but if you like to roll the dice on untapped potential there is still a ton of it here.

players.name: Kaeden Kent
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Life of a Yankees prospect. I say that I want to see more before I make any judgments and by the time he strings a few good weeks together his price has doubled. Kent has looked great so far and it shouldn't come as a shock if he ends up being ranked when I do my re-rank but I don't anticipate it being high enough to warrant buying this over $20. Really like what I've seen so far but as goes the story with many New York prospects he'll probably never be at a price point I see a ton of value in.

players.name: Cal Conley
players.note: As a Braves fan I want to say I see something here but not much swaying me yet. Conley had a nice season back in 2022 with 16 HR and 36 SB, but his production fell off an absolute cliff after that. Love to see him bouncing back but this isn't a large enough sample of good to do anything for me. I would need to see it last a little bit longer and carry into Triple-A for it to get near my radar.

players.name: Damon Keith
players.note: I actually didn't hate this pick at all when the Dodgers drafted him and thought he could be a really solid Bowman deep sleeper because of his ability to hit for power and steal bases. He showed some of that in 2024 with 17 HR and 13 SB, finishing the year with a 138 wRC+ in Double-A. Unfortunately that was his age 24 season and the following year almost all of his stats backed up on him. Now with the Brewers he looks fantastic to start the year — strikeout rate 10% lower than last year's to go with his .371 ISO. Who would be surprised if the Brewers took a guy people had given up on and found something? It's kind of what they do. Worth watching because the tools are so good but the age is a killer here for Bowman — that's not to say it can't go up though.

players.name: Jonah Cox
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Another player who is a bit old for the level but keeps on hitting — last week had three triples and one strikeout. Not sure I've seen that. His story is still the same as I mentioned last week: a very interesting hold at under $10 because I think there's a legitimate chance he could have a 15 HR/50 SB season while reaching Triple-A. It's going to take some time before anyone starts giving him props since he's an older prospect — that does limit the upside a bit since you're betting on him continuing this torrid pace — but if his power gains keep up he could be a sneaky player even with the age considered.

players.name: Ethan Salas
players.note: Over a year ago one of my first Substack articles was my quest to find the hobby's favorite tool. Was it age, power, speed, organization? What I found was that really the answer is pedigree. It's why the prices on #1 draft picks and top international signings are always inflated. There may not be a better example here. Ethan Salas was deemed by many to be a top 10 prospect when he was 17. When 2023 Bowman Chrome came out his base autograph sold for $400. After an underwhelming 2024 and a 2025 where he was injured almost the entire year this card was $48 on my Padres sheet a little over a month ago. One hot sheet and you go from $48 to $72. One more and you're now $132. This is what happens when you're a name.

players.name: Danny Serretti
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Alright, four weeks and I'm paying attention. Serretti was moved up and played a few games at Triple-A last week then came back to Double-A and even with the shuffling was able to qualify pretty easily. Still not sure what the promotion/demotion was about but I'm coming around on this being a hitter. His FanGraphs page thus far is gorgeous: 5 HR, 3 SB, 20% BB, 16.8% K, .342 ISO, and 199 wRC+. As a switch-hitter he's looked impressive lefty and righty with multiple homers, as many walks as strikeouts, and a .350+ AVG from both sides of the plate. This year there are two hitters in the minors with 90+ PA, an ISO over .300, wRC+ over 185, AND a SwStr% under 8.5% — Franklin Arias and Danny Serretti. Being 26 in Double-A is a hobby death sentence so it's hard for me to say he's a buy, but this is very impressive stuff.

players.name: Xavier Isaac
players.note: Now here's a price increase you love to see. Honestly Isaac under $30 never made much sense to me and it blows my mind that he was ever selling that low. After needing brain surgery 'Big Pookie' is back and better than ever. His strikeout rate is near 40% and the contact rates are terrifying, but he's also very patient with a 25.6% walk rate and he absolutely mashes — hitting 7 HR with a .391 ISO this year. Will he ever make consistent enough contact to be a regular major leaguer? Who knows. But with 80 grade raw power he's going to generate plenty of hype as a prospect before we find that out, and that's really what this is all about. I think 30 HR is in play this year if he stays healthy.

players.name: Bryan Rincon
players.note: As someone who once loved Rincon as a sleeper, this is great to see. Back in 2023 at age 19 Rincon had 8 HR and 27 SB while reaching High-A — approach was really strong with a 0.89 BB/K as was the contact rate over 80%. He was one of my 'if he grows into power' type prospects. Sadly the following two seasons were both big disappointments. His walk rate is up from last year and strikeouts are down 8% showing an approach that looks much more like the old version of him. He also has 4 HR and a .221 ISO — never hit more than 8 in a season. Put a pin in him. This could be a very, very sneaky 10 HR & 40 SB season.

players.name: Mac Horvath
players.note: Horvath came over from the Orioles in the Zach Eflin deal and is sort of a super utility player that has seen time all over the infield and outfield. 13 HR/35 SB in 2024 followed by 16 HR/41 SB last year is a pretty strong combo for a player you hear little about. He doesn't have base autos so I used a multiplier from his color but he doesn't exactly sell well. Likely has average power and plus speed but the hobby has never really cared about him up to this point despite some decent seasons — hard to tell if they ever will. Your typical Rays bat that is just quietly solid.

players.name: Raudi Rodriguez
players.note: Few prospects improved their stock in the AFL last year than Rodriguez who hit .433 there showing that his Single-A breakout wasn't a fluke. The knock on him last year was that he was 21 in A ball, but after that strong fall showing the Angels opted to have him skip A+ and put him straight into Double-A. Early on he's looked like he belongs here — hitting .282 with 3 HR, 11 SB, 20% BB, 17.3% K, and 136 wRC+. The power hasn't shown up much yet but he had 14 HR last year with a .189 ISO and is projected for plus raw power to go with above average speed. Now that he's at a more age appropriate level and still looks legit I'd be more willing to grab something of his.

players.name: Ricardo Olivar
players.note: Olivar was a sleeper of mine in years past and he's a great example of how little respect you get when you're old for the level you're at (and a catcher). He rattles off 10+ HR & 10+ SB seasons, always with contact rates close to 80%, always with a solid batting average, and nobody cares. His 2022, 2023, and 2024 wRC+ marks were 179, 138, and 139. This year it's 142. It's what he does. Sure he's a 24-year-old catcher in Double-A but the man can hit. Unfortunately it's never really translated to hobby success.

players.name: Jace Avina
players.note: I liked Avina as a buy this offseason as his hitting data last year looked like it was the most well-rounded we had seen up to that point in his career. This year however we've seen the old Avina — batting .200 with a 37.4% strikeout rate but has 7 HR and a .289 ISO. Yankees fans are excited about the power as his price has nearly tripled since my article where he was $6, but I don't think this version of him is sustainable. Then again chicks dig the long ball so if he hits 20+ HR as a Yankees prospect maybe this thing keeps going up. In his defense he's running a low BABIP and the batting average should trend up but the approach and contact seem to have taken a step back early on. If the price is going up though I guess it works.

players.name: Brett Bateman
players.note: Great approach, phenomenal bat-to-ball skills, but almost no power. Between 2024 and 2025 he hit a combined 3 HR in almost 900 PA. Good player and I don't doubt his ability to hit for average but without any power to show for it I'm not sure how he goes about getting a ton of buzz. Cubs fans pay up for their prospects but he's not a top name and it will be really hard for him to find consistent playing time if and when he does get called up. Not sure I see much here at the moment.

players.name: A.J. Ewing
players.note: Ah, to be a Mets prospect. You get hot, you earn a promotion from Double-A to Triple-A, you play well your first week, and cards go through the roof. Wish I could say that I was surprised since this is not uncommon to see with prospects in an organization like this. Ewing was a big win on last year's hot sheets as I first signaled him as a buy when his base autograph was $7 and you could get refractor autos under $10 on COMC. Those days are long gone and so is his buying value. He could end up in the Mets outfield at some point this season which makes him a fun one to hold to see if these fans overreact again when he gets called up, but if I'm being honest I'd have a hard time not cashing out this profit, especially since he's not a power hitter.

players.name: Jacob Gonzalez
players.note: Back to the pedigree I mentioned with Salas — for most prospects if you had the professional career up to this point that Gonzalez has had and you got hot for a few weeks your base autograph probably wouldn't sniff $20. But when you're a first round pick you are forgiven much quicker. I actually love the adjustments we've seen from Gonzalez and though it will remain to be seen if he can keep up this power increase the approach in general looks a lot better. I'd be stoked if I was a Sox fan or had something of his but since he hadn't shown much up until this year I'd have a hard time buying in now. Definitely trending in the right direction though.

players.name: Kemp Alderman
players.note: Last year Alderman had 22 HR, 22 SB, a walk rate under 10%, .197 ISO and 135 wRC+. This year he has 5 HR, 4 SB, a walk rate under 10%, .189 ISO, and 135 wRC+. Gotta give it to him he's consistent. He was a buy for me on the Marlins sheet because even as an aggressive swinger who won't draw many walks he puts up really good HR and SB totals and projects for double plus power. I still think there's more juice in this price — he's now inside my top 100 hobby hitters which may be surprising since most people who aren't Marlins fans probably don't hear much about him. He should debut this year and his power ceiling is still really solid for the price.

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Great to see YoYo showing off the power with a multi-homer week bringing him to 5 on the year to go along with his .330 average. As a disclaimer his BABIP is over .400 and his contact rate is barely 70% so that average is going to come down, but this is a great start for him. If I had to guess the Nationals call him up within the next month or two and because of that he's kind of a fun hold — though he's the type of player I would hold past his debut. His days of generating big time buzz on the call-up date may be over but he's a streaky hitter with great raw power so if he came out hot it could be fun.

players.name: Eddys Leonard
players.note: Was shocked when I saw that Leonard hasn't debuted as I could have sworn he got close three years ago. At some point he'll probably make it up with the Brewers as a backup infielder but we've seen enough of him in his career to know what he is. Solid bat but no real above average tools so I'm not sure I'm buying the hot start.

players.name: Ivan Johnson
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Have the same feelings as last week. I actually really like the tools but 27 is not an age you want to be in Bowman for a non-debuted prospect. With that being said for $2 I'd consider taking a stab here. Johnson's hitting .308 with 6 HR, 7 SB, and 168 wRC+ at the highest minor league level. This leads me to believe that at some point he probably gets called up and seeing your price go up from a couple bucks if you make it to the show feels like a pretty safe bet. Players like this I'll go to COMC and just buy a stack of base autographs for a couple bucks and immediately relist them for $10. Not sure I'd go big personally though.

players.name: Henry Bolte
players.note: Since my rankings weigh the tools that are hobby relevant I've pretty consistently been the high man on Bolte who is in my opinion one of the best athletes in all of the minor leagues. While he's had some scary high strikeout rates in the past they've been in check this year and he's currently batting .305 with 7 HR and 13 SB. Throughout the course of a full season I really think he could get to 20 HR/50 SB, especially with what looks like an improved approach and contact this year. But hard to believe the A's wouldn't call him up before that happened. Sadly he was a redemption autograph and his base are extremely short printed with only one confirmed sale in the past month at $180. His colors don't sell that crazy — a blue wave auto selling the other day for barely over $200. If you're going to buy him get some color because that seems like the way to go.

players.name: Mason Morris
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! We can officially put Morris on the names to watch list. The downside is that walks still aren't where you want to see them — after issuing three in his last start his walk rate is over 18% for the season. Since he keeps making the list and getting out of jams he's worth keeping an eye on, especially since the Reds seem committed to making him a starter after he was exclusively a reliever in college. But there's been some BABIP luck and he's not generating enough swing-and-miss.

players.name: Blake Wolters
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Good pedigree here as a prep arm who was considered by many to have the best ceiling in his draft class leading to an almost $3 million signing bonus. He's been better his third time around in Single-A but even with three solid outings in a row the pitch data isn't that great. As is the story with Morris, Wolters is still walking too many hitters and allowing too much contact — the low BABIP will likely catch up to him. Still worth watching but not a buy for me.

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! The kid is unreal. Even with this string of dominant performances he seems to have reached his peak at the moment. On the April 14th hot sheet his average base autograph was $233 and after making it three consecutive weeks after that we haven't seen the average get above $240. That probably means that until he's promoted and/or MLB Pipeline and Baseball America catapults him in their rankings this one might not have much more room to move. He deserves every bit of the love he's gotten but this would be a tough point to try to get in at.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! When I do my full re-rank I suspect that Eyanson will be even higher — top 15 is not out of the question. Not many have looked as dominant early on and he's one of only three pitchers who have made my list in five consecutive starts to begin the season, with the others being my #1 and #2 pitchers. In mid-February I wrote in the Discord for people to buy him because of the reports I had heard from those who cover the Red Sox prospects saying he might be better than Kyson Witherspoon. His average base autograph then was $12 so anyone who bought is officially up over 700%. What a ride!

players.name: Boston Bateman
players.note: Would buy now.

players.name: Riley Quick
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! After making only three starts in Single-A they decided they had seen enough and gave him a quick promotion to High-A where he did not disappoint in his first start there — 4 innings of 1 hit ball, no runs, 5 K's. Quick's season line looks fake: 0.00 ERA, 13.50 K/9, 2.25 BB/9, .054 batting average against, 55.6% opponent contact rate. It's only been 12 innings but perhaps 12 of the most dominant innings we've seen in the minors this year. I've always been a fan putting him in my top 12 pitchers list from 2025 Bowman Draft and labeling him a buy at $7 on the Twins sheet. Selfishly I think he'll keep going up.

players.name: J.D. Thompson
players.note: Would buy now.

players.name: Johnny King
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! The kid just keeps doing what he does — missing bats. Once again he's the youngest pitcher to make the hot sheet at this level and his stuff has looked incredible. Through his first 5 starts he now sports a 0.63 ERA with 13.81 strikeouts per 9 innings. His walk rate is high but I've made this comparison before — he's not all that unlike Thomas White. You'll live with the walk numbers because he's borderline unhittable, with a .104 batting average against him which is not only the lowest of any pitcher under 20 who has thrown 10+ innings, it's more than 20 points better than the next lowest. At this rate he could end up a top 10 non-debuted hobby pitcher by the end of the season.

players.name: Joseph Dzierwa
players.note: Another name I expect to move up some spots in my re-rank — wouldn't be surprised if he cracks the top 100. The 6'8" left-hander has looked very solid to start his pro career and now has a 2.33 ERA over his first 27 innings. He mixes pitches well and throws strikes with an impressive 6.7% walk rate. From a hobby perspective though I need him to miss more bats — there's a long list of really effective pitchers who don't get hobby love because they strike out a few batters a game. We've seen Dzierwa throw two 9-K outings already but he's also had two 3-K starts. A pitching profile I'd love at around $10 but I don't think I can get there at $20 unless the stuff starts to trend up.

players.name: Taylor Dollard
players.note: Dollard is off to a nice start to the season but he's a command over stuff pitcher who struck out 17.5% of the hitters he faced last year and allowed a contact rate over 80%. Both of those numbers have improved this season but he's now 27 and by far the oldest pitcher on this High-A list. Not sure there's much to see here.

players.name: Justin Lamkin
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Two weeks ago I said I don't mind a buy at $8 and then when he showed up again for the third time last week at $9 I said this is worth buying. He hasn't made me look dumb yet — firing off 5.2 innings with 8 K's allowing two runs. Considering the questions I had about him coming out of college were if the stuff would play, it does not look to be an issue and his 12.34 K/9 through five professional starts is very, very encouraging for a big lefty with plus command. I've got quite a few green arrows next to Justin Lamkin's name and think this may have been a really strong find by the Royals.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: A very interesting sleeper I'm officially going to be watching the next couple of weeks but not buying yet. Snead was a reliever at Tennessee who touched 100 mph with his fastball but the Angels drafted him with every intention of making him a starter. So far that experiment has looked good. Through 17.1 innings he has a 5.19 ERA but opponent's BABIP is nearly .400 and his 3.22 FIP and 3.41 xFIP tell us he's been better. Command was thought to be a potential issue but his walk rate is currently under 8%. If that continues all we'd really need to see is the refinement of his secondary pitches and he could end up being a very sneaky starting pitching prospect.

players.name: Walter Ford
players.note: Two in a row for Ford who is one of the younger pitchers on this list at High-A, but the K/9 being under 6 in his last start isn't an outlier. He's been a fantastic command pitcher with walk rates under 6% in each of his past three seasons counting this one. However his contact rates against hover in the 75-80% range and strikeout rates are often under 20%. Solid floor but hard to envision a ton of hobby upside due to the lack of K's.

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! My #1 hobby pitching prospect continues to show why he is in that top spot with his fifth consecutive week on the hot sheet. What's funny is that entering this year I didn't think anybody could do much of anything to pass Thomas White and Robby Snelling as my 1 and 2 and yet a month into the season two 2025 draftees have already overtaken them. Can't say enough good things about Kade — this looks like the real deal. Five starts, 0.37 ERA, 14.05 K/9, 1.48 BB/9. No notes. He's a stud.

players.name: Matt Wilkinson
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! I said I was in on 'Tugboat' as a buy last week and he ran it back with another fantastic start. He'll likely move up quite a bit in my re-rank and I still think if you can get his base autograph under $20 he's a solid player to have some cards of. He really seems to have regained that 2024 form when he looked like he was on his way to being a top 100 prospect prior to the struggles in 2025. I'm a believer in the bounce back.

players.name: Drew Beam
players.note: Feels like maybe a few bad comps or auctions for this thing to drop like this but it is possible that nobody is watching his cards. Unfortunately even after a couple strong starts I don't see anything here. He pitches to contact so his swing-and-miss rates are very low and he hardly strikes anybody out. Not overly exciting.

players.name: Michael Morales
players.note: Kind of the same story with Beam above — results have been okay but he's been lucky with BABIP so far. His ERA will likely regress, he allows too much contact, and on top of not missing enough bats the walk rates aren't that great either. Nothing for now.

players.name: Gary Gill Hill
players.note: If I'm adding a buy at this level this is the one I'd be most tempted by. Hill was a 3 for me on the Rays sheet but he did get a writeup because I was so on the fence with him. What held me back is that he's not a big strikeout pitcher — and that's still true — but the Rays really like him and are promoting him pretty aggressively. He's the youngest pitcher on this entire list and last week he made two starts, one in High-A and the other in Double-A after a mid-week promotion. His command is really good, likely a 60 grade, so the ceiling on his autographs will come down to if he ever has good enough stuff to have an exciting K rate. As a 21-year-old already in Double-A for a franchise who is great at developing pitchers it's not the worst floor for an autograph this cheap.

players.name: Jagger Haynes
players.note: I'm not sure what's going on at this level but the pitchers definitely have a type. Haynes has eerily similar advanced pitching numbers as the previously mentioned Beam and Morales. Decent arm but doesn't miss a ton of bats so the strikeout numbers are never super exciting. Nothing personal — it's just not my type of pitching prospect.

players.name: Richard Gallardo
players.note: Almost in that same boat except the difference is that he has been a strike throwing machine compared to the others. He also allows contact at almost an 80% clip and hardly strikes anybody out but he's more effective thanks to a very low walk rate — under 5% last year and under 6% this year. In 5 starts he's 2-0 with a 1.57 ERA and 1.96 BB/9 which is amazing but he's striking out less than 6 batters per 9 innings. Effective arm but it's not for me. Then again the floor is pretty safe due to the plus command and at $1 how does it go down?

players.name: Henry Williams
players.note: Opponent contact rate 80%. Strikeout rate under 17%. Walk rate close to 10%. Nothing spectacular — has just been solid for a couple of weeks. Not my type.

players.name: Robby Snelling
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Do you ever get sick of seeing this name? I sure don't — he just keeps on dealing. Since his autograph is short printed he often goes weeks without a sale which is what makes it look like his average is going down as it can revert to older comps. What's exciting is that we might be able to assume some big news here soon. With Miami DFA'ing Chris Paddack that leaves a hole in the rotation and the Marlins writers have already announced that the most likely options to start in his place are Braxton Garrett and Robby Snelling. I'd feel good about the chances of Robby Snelling getting called up to make his MLB debut this Friday.

players.name: David Sandlin
players.note: Given their proximity to the MLB you're probably fine buying any of these guys now.

players.name: Dylan File
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Same story as last week — File is a really cool story but as a pitcher who is nearly 30 and doesn't really strike anybody out his hobby ceiling is pretty limited.

players.name: Miguel Ullola
players.note: Given their proximity to the MLB you're probably fine buying any of these guys now.

players.name: Quinn Mathews
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Not sure this price could have gone down this much but likely the same story as Snelling where his base autographs don't sell frequently so if a couple weeks go by without any sales it reverts to the 30 day average and can sometimes get wonky. If you're finding Mathews at $30 I think you have to buy him. Still not sure what to make of his issues with the Triple-A baseball — some starts it looks like the problems are behind him and others he's all over the place. Still think there's really good upside and he'll almost definitely make his MLB debut this year, likely in the first half of the season.

players.name: Mitch Bratt
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! My guy. Love me some Mitch Bratt. He didn't have the strikeouts working early in his first couple of starts so it was great to see him turn in a solid outing with a K/9 over 10. At this point I have to accept that he's never going to get the love he deserves but remains one of the most underrated pitchers in the minors. Don't love to see opponent contact rates up so much this year but keeping an ERA under 3.00 in the extremely hitter friendly Pacific Coast League is quite impressive. Another one whose debut could come in the next couple of months.

players.name: Beck Way
players.note: Going through the numbers on Way's appearances and I almost got really excited. Sure he's older but 5-1 with a 3.54 ERA, 2.32 FIP, 12.84 K/9, and 2.66 BB/9 is really, really good. And then I remembered that he's exclusively a reliever and has been for years. Dagger to my heart. Still massive improvements from what he showed last year, especially in the swing-and-miss department, but not being a starter makes me out on him.

players.name: Luis Perales
players.note: Given their proximity to the MLB you're probably fine buying any of these guys now.

players.name: Thomas White
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Imagine being a Triple-A hitter and having to face both of these guys in the same week — has to be brutal. Although Snelling is likely to be up first because the start of White's season was delayed due to an oblique strain, I still think we see both of them in the near future. I've said it before and I'll say it again: I still think White is a buy at this price and has $100+ upside because of his ability to generate whiffs. With pitchers your dream is a guy getting called up and striking out 7-8 hitters in his debut to make his cards go to the moon — and White has that type of stuff. Can't wait to see the both of them in South Florida soon.

players.name: Johan De Los Santos
players.note: I've mentioned how great Johan De Los Santos's bat-to-ball skills are but I may have underestimated them myself — he has a 0.0% SwStr% through 24 PA meaning that of the first 57 pitches he's seen in the states he hasn't swung and missed at a single one of them. Update: he just hit his first career HR too.

players.name: Steele Hall
players.note: Steele Hall is arguably the most electric name we've been waiting to see professionally and since much of what determines his hobby ceiling is how much game power he'll get to it's great to see him go deep already.

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! In terms of consecutive appearances on the sheet Neyens is the hottest Bowman hitter in Single-A currently. He was a buy for me on the Astros team sheet at $36 so another hot week or two and we're going to be closing in on an early double up. The report on Neyens was that you buy him because he has the best raw power in his class for prep hitters and we've seen that this year with 6 HR and a .247 ISO in his first 25 career games. He's now a top 100 prospect for me and will likely see another decent jump in the coming weeks but even with that this price is probably in a hold range for me now. He's been almost too patient with a 30.3% swing rate so he's drawing more walks than I expected but the contact still isn't great and his K rate is over 30%. For real though I love Neyens but not sure I'd jump in for the first time at this price.

players.name: Myles Naylor
players.note: Great to see the third Naylor brother getting going. The projection is good here as an infielder with a good frame who should have plus raw power but we hadn't seen a ton of it prior to this year. After posting a .122 ISO last year that number currently stands at .202 which is a massive jump, and so is his batting average which is up nearly 100 points. However he has a 37.1% strikeout rate and both his .444 BABIP and 62% contact rate scream regression. Nevertheless it's great to see his power trending up in such a big way but the contact questions are going to keep him off my radar for now.

players.name: Felnin Celesten
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Last week I wasn't ready to sound the alarm for the Celesten breakout season being real yet but he's definitely got my hand on the button now after batting .500 with two more homers. Though my ranking doesn't give him much respect you have to remember that it weighs more than one season's worth of data and up until this year he had played through so many injuries he never really lived up to his potential. My only issues remaining are that he's got a high BABIP and the ground ball rate still needs to improve but everything else is much better. Walks up 5%, strikeouts down 4%, ISO up 75 points. He's starting to feel like the Celesten we were hoping to see when he was a high profile signing back in 2023. His hobby ceiling is massive and this base autograph still hasn't gotten back to the price it was at when he first came to the states, so if he keeps hitting like this there's plenty of room for it to go up more.

players.name: Devin Fitz-Gerald
players.note: Trending towards being one of our best team sheet finds not named Nathan Flewelling, Fitz-Gerald was a buy on the Nationals sheet at $14 only one month ago and is now up close to 200% as he continues to swing a hot bat. In that span he's moved himself from 120th in my hobby rankings to knocking on the doorstep of the top 50. He was one of my favorite holds in 2025 Bowman Chrome because he was hurt when the product came out and nobody seemed to want his cards. Now the switch-hitting infielder is batting .310 with 6 HR, 10 SB, .283 ISO, 168 wRC+, and as many walks as strikeouts as a 20-year-old in High-A. Contact rates over 80%. SwStr% under 9%. Park factors suggest he's actually been UN-lucky. Feels wrong to buy in given how much his price is up but I wouldn't be shocked if he kept going at this point.

players.name: Ramon Ramirez
players.note: Grand Salami is going to love this one as I convinced everyone back in 2024 Bowman that of the cheaper players to chase Ramon Ramirez was one of the sneaky best hitters. He still hasn't gotten his hobby love but he has gone up a few bucks in the last week and would still be rated a buy at this new price for me. Ramirez, who won't turn 21 until next month, is hitting .305 with 6 HR, .238 ISO, and 133 wRC+ this year in High-A. His contact rates are also up for the fourth consecutive season. Might not ever get a ton of hobby love as a catcher but the dude can swing it.

players.name: Jaime Ferrer
players.note: Usually when I see the guys that are older for the level show up I can chalk it up as them not really being worth a watch but this stat line is absolutely worth putting a pin in for $3. Last season Ferrer hit .216 with 5 HR, 6.2% BB, 22.5% K, .122 ISO, and 82 wRC+. This year those numbers look like this: .293 AVG, 9 HR, 17.1% BB, 21.4% K, .326 ISO, and 172 wRC+. Has almost doubled his HR total in one third of the plate appearances. Walks are up eleven percent, ISO is up 200 points, wRC+ has more than doubled, oh and he's striking out less? I know he's 23 but man this line is a work of art. Not that I'm buying, but also I'm not saying it's nothing.

players.name: Luis Suisbel
players.note: Suisbel made a number of hot sheets last year and he's just not a guy I've ever been able to get a good read on. Had a 150 wRC+ in 2023 but since then the stats bounce around. Hit .276 with 15 HR in 2024, then hit .211 with 23 HR last year. The contact rates swing back and forth — always worth keeping tabs on because of the power but nothing really stands out this year as being different.

players.name: Mike Sirota
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Last week's Prospect of the Week stays scorching hot and makes his fourth consecutive sheet — and that promotion to Double-A feels like it should be coming any day. Sirota is hitting .333 with 7 HR, 7 SB, .333 ISO, 195 wRC+ and has as many walks as strikeouts. He's moved inside my top 20 non-debuted hitting prospects and nothing we've seen suggests that he's going to slow down any time soon. For where I have him ranked presently this base autograph is about where it should be but as a believer in this offensive skillset I have zero doubt in my mind that he will end up being a $100+ base autograph guy down the road. Considering he's a Dodger I'm honestly surprised he's not there already.

players.name: Charles Davalan
players.note: There must have been some auctions that went low because it looks like some people have been scooping these base autographs at prices under where they were selling last week. I think it's time we have a conversation about Davalan. I think he's legit. He was a prime 'if only he had power' prospect coming out of the draft with a plus hit tool and plus speed but I didn't expect there to be this much this early. He's hitting .304 with 6 HR and 8 SB already with a .223 ISO and 148 wRC+. It doesn't look like that average is trending toward much regression either as Davalan has just a 12.4% strikeout rate and a contact rate north of 84%. As much as it pains me to say this I think the Dodgers might have found another guy.

players.name: Malcolm Moore
players.note: Moore has had a really solid start to the season after struggling a bit last year. His contact rates were solid last year but he had some bad BABIP luck which has normalized this year helping him raise his batting average by over 60 points early on. The hit tool is decent and so is the power but none of the tools are really plus and he's a catcher so the hobby might not get excited for him. He was however a first round pick who the Rangers gave $3 million to in 2024 so there is a bit of pedigree on his side if you're looking for a positive way to spin his hobby ceiling. As of now it's not for me though.

players.name: Ricardo Olivar
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Like I said last week, this dude hits and hits and nobody cares. We have further proof after he batted .350 with three more homers and two more stolen bases last week and his card price didn't even budge a dollar. As of this morning Olivar is the 104th ranked hitting prospect according to Scout the Statline's Peak Projections and being a nearly top 100 hitter under $10 is wild. Of the 21 prospects who have 10+ HR this year his 17.9% K rate is not only the lowest but nobody else is even under 20%. It's a shame that the Bowman people don't find him exciting but Ricardo Olivar rakes.

players.name: Aeverson Arteaga
players.note: This name pinged my radar as one I remembered from back in 2022 as he had a productive first couple of years and was a fairly popular Bowman sleeper at the time. Since then he hasn't done much and I haven't heard his name in card circles in years. Looks like he's off to a hot start this season but despite his average being up over 100 points from last year his contact rates are down big, and the 200 point gap in his BABIP may be the culprit. Hard to know for sure but might be more luck than anything at this point.

players.name: Jonah Cox
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! How does he keep doing it?! Cox's first appearance on the hot sheet his base autograph was $2 and in a month since then he's gone up 850%. This is a prime example of why I love the cheap under the radar guys. I said it on one of the hot sheets a few weeks back that part of what could help this autograph despite him being old for the level was that it looked like the power was coming up in a big way and it didn't seem out of the question that he could put together a 15 HR/50 SB season. After another homer and two more stolen bases last week he's up to 4 HR/18 SB in 28 games. Be warned the BABIP is near .500 which is insane so he's not going to keep batting anywhere near .421 but the power increase from last year seems legit. At a $20 base auto being up almost 1,000% in a month I'd probably bail but that's up to you!

players.name: Tyler Hardman
players.note: Hardman had a decent season last year with 20 HR and 12 SB with a 119 wRC+ in Double-A — unfortunately for his Bowman values he was 26 and now he's a year older and at the same level. Still think the power is good and while he's not speedy he's opportunistic on the base paths and should continue his string of 20+ HR/10+ SB seasons, but unfortunately he's in need of a promotion to Triple-A and would need to keep up the hot start there to get much hobby traction.

players.name: Seaver King
players.note: Not sure what they put in the water out there but King has been a different hitter since we saw him in the Arizona Fall League last year. During the regular season he looked pretty lost at the plate and I had all but chalked him up to being a speedy defender with a bat that wasn't exciting for Bowman. After he hit .359 with a 1.031 OPS in the AFL he officially went on my watch list and all of the improvements we saw there have shown up early this season as well. Biggest thing is the approach — he's swinging at 9% fewer pitches this year and has raised his walk rate from 5.8% to 13.9%. His ISO was under .100 last year and today for 2026 it's over .250. Been a great turnaround to watch and he has up arrows in my rankings, but the market has adjusted and he's probably still a hold for me right now.

players.name: Ralphy Velazquez
players.note: Everyone knows we love Ralphy around here and he was a 5/5 rated buy at $42 on my Guardians sheet. Up quite a bit since then and he keeps on hitting. Biggest thing for him this year has been the patience — his walk rate which was under 10% last year is over 14%. Along with that his strikeouts are all the way down to 16.9%. I still think most people think of him as this big bruising power hitting first baseman, but Velazquez is currently batting .308 to go with his .192 ISO. This is a professional hitter. Still think he's slept on.

players.name: Xavier Isaac
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Three straight weeks for 'Big Pookie' as he drew five walks during the week and added yet another HR to his total. Nothing has changed from last week. His contact rates are still terrifying as are the strikeout rates but the power is so good that it's going to continue to support a card price this high. Isaac has stepped up to the plate 109 times this season — walked 27 times (24.8%), struck out 43 times (39.4%), and had an extra-base hit 11 times (10.1%). Truly a three outcome player, and his ability to crank XBH has led to a .358 ISO but his contact rates are under 60%. Baffling player but at the end of the day there aren't many prospects with 80 grade raw power so as long as he keeps hitting at a 30 HR per season pace his cards should still go up.

players.name: Henry Bolte
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Who else but this week's Prospect of the Week. Bolte put together one of the most ridiculous weeks we've seen all year with 5 HR and 4 SB while batting .556. Unfortunately his base auto was extremely short printed so the lack of sales are what swings his average auto price in big directions. I know that a few of you out there grabbed some color and should be rewarded nicely because not only is he the hottest Triple-A hitter in the world right now but he also just got called up earlier today. It's showtime!

players.name: Eddys Leonard
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Are the Brewers really going to make me like Leonard? Of course he's 25 so the market isn't going to react much when he has good weeks but this makes three in a row and for the season he's hitting .345 with 6 HR. My only issue with Leonard's cards are that when he gets called up it's probably going to be a short stint or as infield depth and he doesn't profile as someone that Milwaukee is going to hand over the keys to a position to. Really nice season but not sure I can make anything of it.

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! A couple of weeks ago I said that he probably wasn't worth a buy but you could hold him past his MLB debut in case he got hot — but he's hot now, and his prices are going down? Feels odd. He's a player with good pedigree who was a pretty big Bowman name back in 2024 but he never really put it all together the way people expected. I'd argue though that he looks better this season than we've seen him at any other point in his professional career and realistically he could get called up at any minute. With a base autograph around $10 I don't think he's a terrible buy given how close he is to the show. Could be a good opportunity for a quick flip.

players.name: Carson Taylor
players.note: This is tough because Taylor missed basically all of 2025 but the last time we saw him healthy in 2024 he very sneakily had a 140 wRC+ in Triple-A with the Phillies where he hit .279 with 16 HR. Unfortunately it's two years later, he's still in Triple-A, and he's about to turn 27. I actually don't hate his bat and think that when he does get a shot in the majors he'll probably be an okay platoon hitter, but with his age I don't think you'll see any buzz when he does get the call so he's nothing more than a dice roll in hopes that when he hits the MLB he's equally as hot.

players.name: Johnny Slawinski
players.note: Slawinski struggled in his first outing but turned it around last week firing off four scoreless innings with 6 K's. One of my favorite under the radar arms from 2025 Bowman Draft.

players.name: Aaron Watson
players.note: Even more under the radar in the same product is Aaron Watson who I've actually had ranked higher since release and his base auto was $5 up until last week. Still think he's a solid stash and the 6'5" right-hander has allowed 1 ER across 8 professional innings striking out 12.

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! Seth needs to chill because I'm running out of shades of dark orange to use for my color coding. Last week I said it might be hard for this price to go up anymore unless he saw a promotion and that's exactly what happened. That means this is Hernandez's last week on the Single-A sheet and to continue this ridiculous run he'll have to replicate his success at the High-A level. It's hard to imagine him struggling though because he's been almost untouchable since making his professional debut. He has officially overtaken Kade Anderson as the #1 pitcher in my hobby rankings. Can't wait to see him up a level this week.

players.name: Jacob Morrison
players.note: Morrison was delayed in making his professional debut but has now turned in back-to-back scoreless outings. The 6'8" right-hander was very solid last year at Coastal Carolina but he's more of a command over stuff guy presently so it remains to be seen if he'll strike out enough professional hitters to generate a ton of hobby buzz. Despite that his base auto is still on the rise as I think everyone seems to be excited that he's back and looking good. Like the upside especially with an organization that seems like they don't miss but until I see more I'm not sure I can get to this price.

players.name: Jeter Martinez
players.note: Martinez is a righty with a big frame and even bigger fastball who signed with the Mariners originally back in 2023. He has a plus fastball and plus slider which help him rack up strikeouts — 8 of them alone in his last start. Unfortunately the one thing that's kept Martinez from being a top starting pitching prospect is his command which he's struggled with in the past and it doesn't look much better this year. He's been great with a 3.72 ERA and 10.24 K/9 but he's also walked 16.1% of the hitters he's faced. I really want to like him and do think from a hobby perspective there's a lot to like, especially considering he's still only 20, but I'd need to see the control get a little better.

players.name: Blake Wolters
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! After three weeks of me saying that I don't believe the improvements are real I'm starting to wonder if we should be paying attention to this. The pedigree is great here as a prep pitcher with extremely high upside who signed for $2.8 million back in 2023. After me knocking him for his command he went out and threw 5.2 innings with 2 walks and 9 K's. The only thing keeping him from getting a 'buy' stamp is that opponents' BABIP is still under .200 and his 1.65 ERA comes with a 5.04 FIP suggesting he may regress in a big way. He's inching closer to getting me on board but I'm still not quite there. Love what I've seen compared to last year though.

players.name: Mason Morris
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! It seems like Wolters and Morris have been paired together all season as they both keep showing up at $5 and I keep finding reasons not to buy them. Morris also has been extremely lucky in the BABIP department and has FIPs and xFIPs that say his ERA could blow up soon. He's also not striking out as many batters as I'd like to feel confident in his cards going up in price and despite me adding a WHIP qualifier to the hot sheet he keeps barely skating by walking four batters each start. Nothing for me still but worth monitoring.

players.name: Brock Porter
players.note: Great pedigree here with Porter who was a 4th round pick out of high school in 2022 and signed for $3.7 million. He's a 6'4" righty with great stuff but iffy control. While he's gotten off to a great start this year with a 2.40 ERA and 12 strikeouts per 9 innings his walk rate is about 17%. Oh, and there's that thing where he hasn't started a game since 2024 because the Rangers shifted him full-time to a reliever last year. That alone kills much of his hobby ceiling and while electric relievers can sell, it's not for me.

players.name: Justin Lamkin
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! This appears to be a fun find for the hot sheet — Lamkin was around $7 when I said we could probably go ahead and buy because he's a big lefty with good command who we weren't sure would have strikeout stuff but his ability to miss bats early on made him more exciting than I originally anticipated. Not only have his autographs tripled in price but they announced today that he's getting promoted to Double-A. I wouldn't be surprised if we get a nice little bump from that but after that I'd at least consider selling. Not that I don't trust Lamkin to keep climbing but he still hasn't quite cracked my top 100 pitchers and he's already selling where I'd put a top 30 or 40 arm. Probably a hold for me now — if this price gets to $30 I'd probably sell.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Even with the price doubling I think we're going to want to grab a piece of Snead, and after I watched his start last week I actually went and bought a true blue auto for around $50 plus shipping. When I say he looked unhittable I mean he didn't allow a hit. He didn't even allow a walk. 6 perfect innings with 6 K's. After looking like walks could be an issue for him in college where he was a reliever they have been anything but — his walk rate has dropped to 6.4%. I still think the secondary pitches need work as the Angels continue to develop him as a starter but he throws gas and the control looks much better than expected. For under $10 I'm in on that alone in hopes that he will continue to improve as a professional.

players.name: Joseph Dzierwa
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! At the end of the week I'll release my first full re-rank for pitching prospects and as a teaser, Dzierwa has moved up 50+ spots and presently sits at 65th. I've grown to love watching him pitch despite making him a hold because I didn't think he'd post good enough strikeout numbers to be a big hobby name. He does still have starts here and there where he only strikes out 3 or so hitters but he's missing more bats than I expected. In two starts last week he struck out 15 hitters over 8.2 innings and now has a 11.10 K/9 to go with a 2.27 BB/9. Few pitchers have looked more dominant than him through the first month of the season. Hard to pay this entry price even with his huge move up my rankings, still trying to fight my FOMO.

players.name: Joe Whitman
players.note: Prospect of the Week still slept on!

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! It feels unfair that you can go out and dominate for the sixth consecutive week and lose your spot as my #1 pitching prospect but hard to argue with what Seth Hernandez has done. They're both ridiculous though and I wouldn't blame anyone for having Anderson at the top because they will probably trade places throughout the season for me. His stats this year look fake: 0.60 ERA, 14.10 K/9, and 1.50 BB/9. Of the 106 batters he's faced he has struck out 47 of them (44.3%) and walked only 5 (4.7%). Absurd stuff. Deserves every dollar of the price at this point.

players.name: Cade Smith
players.note: Last year was a strong one for Smith who had a 2.50 ERA across three levels at age 23, finishing in High-A. This year he got the move up to Double-A and has looked solid early on but nothing really pops. Even last year with that good ERA the strikeout numbers never really wow'd you and when that's the case I'd like to see really, really good walk rates so I can at least see a good amount of separation in the K-BB% but those were kind of eh as well. He gets results but I haven't really seen anything that excites me.

players.name: Connor Staine
players.note: Staine posts more exciting strikeout numbers but he also walks more batters, with a BB/9 that is currently over 6. The stuff looks pretty solid for a guy with a $1 autograph and he's missed a good amount of bats with a 65.4% contact rate and .174 batting average against him — both really good. But he gets himself into trouble with walks and then when he does give up one of those hits they produce runs because the bases are never clear. Intriguing for $1 but needs to improve the command before I'm interested.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! With Kade I almost said I've never seen a K-BB% bordering on 40% until I realized that Eyanson's actually is 40% — with a 44.7% strikeout rate and 4.7% walk rate through his first 24.1 innings as a professional. He earned a promotion to Double-A and he just keeps on dealing. It's obviously nothing major but interesting to see him and Anderson both go down a few dollars in the midst of this run, it's almost as if everyone expects it now and there's nothing they can do to get more hype. With my re-rank coming this week Eyanson will move from the mid-20's to inside my top 15 as he's been probably the biggest prospect riser in all of Bowman so far this season.

players.name: Liam Doyle
players.note: There were a couple of high first round pick pitchers who struggled early on this year and Doyle was one of them, but he looks to have turned it around with consecutive strong starts. While I'm certainly less worried I'm still worried. The biggest green flag has been the command with a solid 7.6% walk rate, but the most surprising thing to me has been the strikeouts. Though his 11.14 K/9 is solid his 28.3% strikeout rate feels a touch lower than I expected after he struck out more than 40% of the hitters he faced last year at Tennessee. He has been unlucky with BABIP so the ERA should get better, but opponents are hitting .294 off him this year and his lack of a great third or fourth pitch seems to be his Achilles' heel. Still think there's fantastic upside hence why he's a top 30 pitcher for me, but a $50 base autograph is extremely steep for a pitcher I haven't been overly impressed with yet.

players.name: Matt Wilkinson
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! Not often you'll see a player get traded while they're on a run of five consecutive hot sheets but 'Tugboat' was moved this past weekend to the Giants in the Patrick Bailey trade. While you hate to see him leave Cleveland who seems to be crushing it with pitching development lately, it should be good for his cards as you've now opened a brand new pool of buyers and the Giants do have a stronger hobby fanbase in general I'd say. I liked him as a buy around $15 and still don't hate him at a touch over $20 especially if the Giants fans are looking to buy him up after his first start there.

players.name: Jacob Miller
players.note: Miller has been a good workhorse for the Marlins the last two years throwing 114+ innings in both of them but the stats have just never really popped. ERA is ok. Strikeout rates are ok. Walk rates are ok. There's still time for things to change and there's decent pedigree here as a 2nd round high school selection with a $1.7 million signing bonus in 2022, but since he's debuted I haven't really seen anything in the pitch data that has made me want to rush out and buy his cards.

players.name: Ethan Pecko
players.note: Criminal he's still $10 — would buy him now. After making two rehab starts in Single-A, Pecko returned to Triple-A and proved he's just as effective there. Made him a 5/5 on the Astros buy sheet when he was under $10 because I've felt for awhile like he is one of the most slept on arms in Bowman. I do still think he debuts this year which makes him a great buy and hold since he's one of the cheapest of my top 40 pitchers. Good stash here.

players.name: Adisyn Coffey
players.note: Solid arm, good strikeout stuff, but Coffey is now 27 and is as much of a reliever as you can be — with only one career start in five professional seasons. Unfortunately that's just not a recipe that will get your cards sold.

players.name: Mitch Bratt
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Four weeks in a row and the price goes down — the Mitch Bratt disrespect! After struggling to strike batters out in his first few starts the 7 in 5 innings last week was solid and he's lowered his ERA to 2.48 in the extremely hitter friendly Pacific Coast League which is not easy to do. BABIP's have been low and his FIP and xFIP are a touch over 4.00 so there is concern that a regression start is coming but hopefully before that time comes we see the Diamondbacks call on him to make his MLB debut as he's very likely the 'next man up' when they decide to dip down into Triple-A for a starter. He's been one of my favorites to watch for a couple of years now and while the hobby has decided he's not electric enough to sell for more than $20 I'm still holding in case that first call-up start is solid.

players.name: Yovanny Rodriguez
players.note: Sneaky good bat.

players.name: Jose Castro
players.note: Very interesting name to watch here. Any player for the Yankees can pop at any moment in Bowman and the tools here are solid for a few bucks. The 6'2" Castro hit 6 HR and added 20 SB last year in the DSL and we've seen the power and speed early on in the states too. Only issue here is that Castro missed all of 2024 and then repeated the DSL when he returned in 2025 so he's making his stateside debut in the CPX at 20. He's dominating but he's far too old for his level for Bowman. Not a terrible look for the price but needs a promotion quickly if he's going to get any hobby respect.

players.name: Corey Cousin
players.note: I put Cousin in my sleeper section last week because he does interest me quite a bit. We should have plenty of time to watch him progress before deciding if it's worth a buy because he's not a top 30 Royals prospect and doesn't have much name recognition as an 18th round pick out of high school in 2024. When Baseball America did their report card for that draft class they named Cousin the 'Fastest Runner' of the KC picks. He missed all of last year with injury and has looked great early on in the CPX not only showing off that speed but also some power with a .267 ISO in 39 PA. Need to see more but he could sneak up on people.

players.name: Jhonayker Ugarte
players.note: My favorite of the group.

players.name: Joswa Lugo
players.note: Lugo has more name recognition than most players in the CPX because he's a top 10 prospect for the Angels who was a $2.3 million signing. Really, really good tools — possibly plus power and speed — but his contact rates have been pretty bad because he's extremely chase prone. Love the tools because you don't get many 6'3" teenage shortstops with this power/speed potential under $20 but he's never going to reach that full power potential if he doesn't improve his pitch recognition. Very fun lottery ticket but even then this price is probably a tad high for me.

players.name: Chase Harlan
players.note: I'll start moving him as much as I can in the rankings but the improvements we've seen to Harlan's approach could be big time. Many people will look at the 2 HR this year and be disappointed but one of my favorite spots in prospecting is when guys who have absolutely no question about their power start correcting other things. Harlan has always profiled as a huge power bat with hit tool concerns. He's swinging at 11% fewer pitches this year and he's raised his BB/K from 0.54 to 1.11. Walks are up 9%, strikeouts are down 3.5%, and his swinging strike rate is under 10% after being over 14% in Single-A last year. Do not worry about the power because it's absolutely there — him improving everything else is a huge green flag for me.

players.name: JD Dix
players.note: This is the moment we've all been waiting for. Dix was one of the better 'if that power shows up' prospects in the 2024 draft class. Last year he hit 2 HR and had 28 SB in 408 PA with a .109 ISO. This year his walk rate, strikeout rate, and contact rate are almost mirror images of last year but he has 6 HR and 12 SB in 145 PA which gives him a .203 ISO. His .229 average is likely keeping people away but his BABIP is 135 points lower than it was last year so I think we see it climb as the law of averages works itself out. What's really important is that we wanted to see power from the 6'2" switch-hitter and it's here. He's a buy all day at this price.

players.name: Johan De Los Santos
players.note: I know we love us some JDLS but man you guys are wild. Within 2 minutes of me getting the notification that he hit his first career HR it was followed by a flurry of eBay notifications saying 'sorry this got away.' Then he gets moved up to Single-A and immediately hits another. While I do still think this is a bit of an overreaction because I don't expect that power to continue, it's hard to argue with buying him because of how unreal his bat-to-ball skills and speed both are. Still love him but now that his cards have doubled this is a hold for me — I'd have a hard time paying $30+ for his base auto. Hope he continues to go to the moon for you all though!

players.name: Malcolm Moore
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Moore was in serious consideration for Prospect of the Week with his 4-HR week where he hit .520. Last week I mentioned how good the pedigree is as a first round pick with a $3 million signing bonus but I never really thought that the tools were much more than average. Looks like maybe the joke's on me because through 127 PA he's hitting .318 with 6 HR, .255 ISO, and 151 wRC+. There's a chance this price is long gone because his base autograph was a redemption so the sales don't roll in as frequently as some players but if he's still trading this cheap I'd be more than ok with grabbing a piece or two.

players.name: Zander Darby
