players.note: Between Darby and Jonah Cox I'm not sure what the Giants put in the water out there in Arizona during spring but these guys look different. Now Darby is running a BABIP near .500 so his .355 average is absolutely going to come back down to earth, but the power increase has been noticeable. After hitting 6 HR all of last year he already has 5 this year improving his ISO by nearly 100 points. Despite that his contact rates are actually down a little and his BB/K has been cut in half as he's been more aggressive. Definitely putting a pin in him but with being old for the level and running such a high BABIP I'm not personally buying it yet.

players.name: Won-Bin Cho
players.note: If you've been around Bowman for a few years you may remember Cho. I actually had a PSA 10 atomic auto of him a few years ago and he was a popular sleeper as a teenage prospect from Korea with plus power projections. He reached High-A at 20 but never really took off like we hoped and here he is two years later at the same level. The good news is that the power we heard so much about as a teenager has shown up. After hitting 7 HR with a .109 ISO last year he's matched that HR total in about one third of the plate appearances raising his ISO all the way to .254. He moves well too and after stealing 26 bags last year he has 14 already this year and is currently on a 21 HR/42 SB 100-game pace. It's probably not realistic to expect him to keep this up especially since the contact rates don't look great, but I could see him getting a slight boost since he was a name in the past.

players.name: Alfredo Duno
players.note: No surprise here — Duno has been one of my favorite prospect bats for some time now and is in my top 20 non-debuted hitters. There aren't many hitters who consistently put up these type of results. Really good approach and even better power. Homered in three consecutive games last week and it feels like he's hitting his stride. On my 2025 Reds sheet I made him a buy at $25 but his stock has really taken off in the last year. Still love him and think the offensive potential is very high but it's tough to buy a C/DH this expensive. As a counterpoint this bat could be special so he really pulls me in both directions in terms of how high his auto could go.

players.name: Devin Fitz-Gerald
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! The man who needs no introduction. I'm not sure there's a prospect getting more public love currently than DFG and he has earned every bit of it. Back in November when I was on Substack I wrote an article of players to stash in the offseason and one was Fitz-Gerald at $7 so that one worked out a little bit! When I do my next re-rank I would imagine that he moves up even further and could be pushing the top 25-30, but even then this autograph price would be a tough buy for me. Not that it won't keep going up, but buying a player who is up 750% isn't really my style. Shoutout to everyone who held up to this point — if you have multiples it might not be a bad time to take some profits on a couple and hold the remaining ones as a free roll.

players.name: Aaron Walton
players.note: Tough one here. I actually like Walton quite a bit and I don't think his hot start is noise — I think he's a solid bat. Had 14 HR/19 SB last year at Arizona with a sub-14% strikeout rate which led to a selection with a Comp B pick at the end of round two where the Guardians signed him for a little over $1 million. He's 6'4" and clocks plus run times to go with tremendous bat speed. There are mixed reviews on how much power that will translate to because there are a lot of moving parts in his swing but he's currently hitting .315 with 8 HR, 11 SB, and a .277 ISO in High-A. Think he's a sneaky one to watch but with his autograph already up near $20 I wouldn't say I love the value.

players.name: Yasser Mercedes
players.note: Insert the Grand Theft Auto 'ahhh sh*t, here we go again' GIF. There are few players I've both made and lost money on as often as Mercedes in the last few years. He's one of the original players that made me stop trusting DSL prospects after he dominated there only to come to the states and struggle for YEARS once he got above the rookie levels. He played for the Twins Single-A team near me in three consecutive seasons which is never a good sign. The tools are fantastic and even last year he had 11 HR/36 SB despite hitting .199 with an 87 wRC+. Don't know what clicked this offseason but he has been unreal. Since he has pedigree in the hobby as a former top name and has such great tools I can't blame anybody for taking a dive and hoping this is for real because if it is this card could move quickly, but I'd also tread carefully.

players.name: Jhonny Severino
players.note: After the 2024 season it looked like Severino could be a really sneaky prospect name as he went 16 HR/16 SB at age 19 but the following year he struggled what felt like all year. This year has been some good — his power seems to be back with 7 HR already and an ISO over .200 and the average is up — but even after the consecutive hot weeks his wRC+ is under 90. Tools are good but he's an extremely aggressive swinger and the iffy approach keeps him from being consistent so him going on these hot streaks isn't uncommon. Nothing for me yet unless we were to see some real improvements to his chase rates.

players.name: Tony Blanco Jr.
players.note: Everyone's favorite roller coaster of a prospect. I joked in an article one time that he is a never ending cycle of buys and sells if you want to try to ride the wave. He's 6'7" and realistically probably won't ever have a strikeout percentage under 30% in the minors but he also hits the ball harder than anybody who isn't in the MLB (and most players who are). Because of this he's never really a bad buy because each time he hits a ball 120 mph he breaks the internet and his price doubles, and then he gets cold and they dip back down, and then he does it again. Blanco is a hard player to trust but there's no denying that his 99th percentile MaxEV makes him fun.

players.name: Ralphy Velazquez
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! This will be the last week on the Double-A sheet since it was just announced that Velazquez is on his way to Triple-A. Very much deserved too. Has long been one of my favorite hitting prospects as many of you know. One of the most slept on power bats in baseball and he's pretty firmly inside my top 15 hitters now. Unlike Isaac, these contact skills are not bad, and Ralphy's .248 ISO comes with a strikeout rate under 19%. Just a ridiculous combination. Even though he's still only 20 I don't suspect that Triple-A pitching will give him trouble at all and at this point you have to wonder if we could see him down the stretch for Cleveland later this year.

players.name: Chris Suero
players.note: Last week someone asked for a list of players who were due for positive regression and Suero was one of the names that stuck out most to me because he was not only getting extremely unlucky but also hitting for power, with a .250 ISO and .200 BABIP going into last week's games. After a 2 HR/3 SB week those season numbers are starting to look better and although he's still batting .204 he has a 130 wRC+ thanks to his .276 ISO and 18.6% walk rate. No secret I've always liked Suero. He's an odd player as a catcher with plus power and speed but he might go 20 HR/30 SB this year as a Mets prospect and I find it hard to believe his card price wouldn't go up if that happened.

players.name: Jonah Cox
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! This is getting out of control. Part of me still thinks this comes crashing back down to reality. Just look at the stat line last week — he hit .417 with 0 walks and 7 strikeouts. Everything he puts in play is finding a hole. His BABIP is damn near .500. Such a good story though as a guy who started with a $2 autograph on his first hot sheet but it appears the market doesn't want to go much higher on him. Can't say I blame them being that he's almost 25 and could regress soon. Still think that 15 HR/50 SB season is on the table though!

players.name: Brooks Brannon
players.note: Last week Brannon was on the sleeper list and he crushed it again last week seeing his autograph price double. Andrew Parker from SoxProspects.com has been taking questions on Boston prospects in our Discord. He said Brannon looked fantastic this spring and was expecting the breakout even earlier this season. Still not a big enough sample to crack my hobby rankings but being a Red Sox prospect with a .475 ISO in Double-A and having an autograph under $10 doesn't feel like a terrible buy.

players.name: Dylan Campbell
players.note: Campbell has pretty solid power and speed with 14 HR/33 SB last year but he doesn't hit for much average and none of the tools are overly exciting. Even with the consecutive strong weeks his wRC+ is only 84 and it hasn't been higher than 105 in any of his professional seasons. Don't see much here right now.

players.name: Xavier Isaac
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Part of me thinks the no change in autograph price has to do with Isaac being a redemption and not having a ton of base autos listed for sale so they don't move as often. The clips of him this last week have been comical — there's a slow-mo I watched of his new 2-strike approach where he essentially doesn't use his lower body, gets wide no stride and swings for contact and even with that he hits pop flies that carry over the fence. At this point if you're going to buy him you have to accept who he is. Arguably the best raw power in all of minor league baseball but he's always going to have wildly low contact rates and strike out in 30%+ of his at-bats. My head tells me this could still go higher though.

players.name: Seaver King
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! As is the story with Ralphy above, King is another one who is on his way to Triple-A with a promotion that was announced today. I gotta give him props here. I was totally out on King after the 2025 season because his approach at the plate did not seem like something that would lead to success but ever since he appeared in the AFL he's been on fire. Nothing about his offensive game looks the same as what we saw last year and we might have to start recognizing that this is a legit bat. Even with the move up in my rankings though his price is up drastically since last year so he's still more of a hold for me than a buy, but shoutout to anyone who was a believer and was on his cards early!

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! When are we going to see YoYo get the call?! Crazy that you can make five consecutive hot sheets while being in Triple-A on the doorstep of the MLB and still be under $20. I stand by what I said last week — I don't think he's a bad player to stash since that debut is probably coming soon and I do think this is the best version of Morales that we've seen since he was drafted, but now that he's nearly doubled since last week this is probably my stopping point for buying. Hope we see him up soon though.

players.name: Cooper Ingle
players.note: I screamed from the rooftops for years and years and years that Ingle's autograph which was under $10 for what felt like forever was undervalued. Finally he's started to get some love as he's been crushing the ball in Triple-A this year and we saw that autograph get near $40. Unfortunately he had a short IL stint and then the wind really got taken out of the sails of his cards when the Guardians traded for Patrick Bailey in a move that seemed like it blocked Ingle. Love the player but not sure I'm buying at this price.

players.name: Aaron Sabato
players.note: Clear out those shoeboxes if you collected Bowman cards in 2021 — I guarantee you've got some Sabato's stashed away. He was actually a pretty big chase back then as a first round pick with good power but his minor league career just never took off the way many expected. After hitting 23 HR last year he seems to have bounced back nicely and he's on a 30+ HR pace this year. This would be a very deep sleeper option since his name has recognition — you could hope that he gets called up and starts his MLB career hot — but as a 27-year-old hitter who hasn't debuted the hot weeks don't do too much for me.

players.name: Johnny Slawinski
players.note: Typical rookie levels. We saw a price jump when the CPX started because people got excited to see a player take the field for the first time professionally but then his price dips down even though he's playing well. I think I'm a buyer on Slawinski under $15. Said it in my 2025 Bowman Draft preview but I think the upside here is great and some of the scouting report coming out of high school was that as a multi-sport athlete he's extremely athletic and should be able to repeat his delivery well enough to throw consistent strikes. That may have been an understatement. Through 12 innings to start his career he's stuck out 16 batters and walked.... ZERO. Like what I've seen so far.

players.name: Aaron Watson
players.note: Seemed I was higher than anybody on Watson for 2025 Bowman Draft and as long as he's hovering in that $10 range I think he's worth buying for the upside alone. There aren't many 6'5" pitchers who come out of high school with plus command but that's the calling card here. The question was as he grew into his frame if the stuff would tick up enough from where he saw it as a prep for him to be a legit arm. Across his first three professional starts opponents have a 59.3% contact rate against him and he's induced a swinging strike percentage of 21.6%. That's really strong for a 19-year-old with his frame and ability to locate his pitches. He's a top 100 pitcher for me.

players.name: Jeter Martinez
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! One of these days Martinez may make it out of the sleepers category and into the "time to buy this guy" range but I'm not quite there yet. Still think he looks much better early on this year than he did last season and the hobby upside is tempting for a younger 6'4" pitcher with his stuff, but the walks are still an issue. Much better last time out with only one in six innings but would need to see it continue for a couple more starts.

players.name: Malachi Witherspoon
players.note: Nobody seemed to be after these autographs when they were $9 on the Tigers buy sheet and I mentioned that I thought he was worth a buy for a couple of reasons. One was that the stuff was never really a question but he struggled with control at Oklahoma. He got behind often in counts and then had to serve up strikes which were hit hard. I know it's Single-A hitters and he's a pitcher from a big college so it's hard to get too excited about him dominating but I'd look at his 5.6% walk rate as a bigger green flag than anything else. If he's improved his ability to harness all of his pitches he could rise up the rankings quickly, unfortunately I need to see it in High-A before I can bump him much more and now that he's up to $15 I'm probably holding until I see that.

players.name: Michael Lombardi
players.note: We all know about my love for Lombardi so seeing him make a second straight appearance is music to my ears. Fascinating as a two-way player who was a closer in college but the Royals selected with the intention of stretching him into a starter. There's still work to do with the command but his ability to miss bats is absolutely not question as I'm going to go ahead and stamp his curveball as one of my favorite offerings in the minor leagues. Normally the 5.61 BB/9 would scare me off but like I've said in the past with Jacob Misiorowski, Thomas White, Johnny King, etc. I'll live with a few walks a game if you're unhittable and Lombardi has been. Opponents are hitting .187 off him this year and of the 109 hitters who have stepped up to face him he's struck out 47 of them (43.1%). That alone should help his card market steadily climb as he works on improving the other aspects.

players.name: Kendry Chourio
players.note: My #1A pitcher chase

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: 7 weeks in a row! Do I even need to keep writing about him? Best prep pitcher I've seen in the last 10 years blah blah gets promoted to a level where he's more than 3 years younger than his average competitor and doesn't allow a single hit over his first 5 innings there. Kid is unreal. If you're buying his cards you're banking on the fact that he is in such a league of his own that he's going to continue to shatter what we thought was possible for the price point on non-debuted prospects. I would have said Konnor Griffin couldn't get much higher than a $400-500 base auto before his debut and he got over $800. With pitchers I'd normally say $150 is where I'd stop even for my #1 spot but as with Konnor the rules don't apply to Seth because he's a freak. Sadly I don't own any but I'm excited to see how high this thing can get.

players.name: Blake Wolters
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! Four straight weeks on the Single-A sheet and I kept not wanting to commit because he's older for the level and was still walking too many batters, the Royals promote him to High-A and he turns in one of his best starts yet. At this point I've got to say go in if you're a believer. It's still risky because Wolters looked very average in his first two professional seasons but as I've mentioned in past articles there is some good pedigree here. You don't give a $2.8 million signing bonus to a high school pitcher if you don't think there's upside and while up to this point we hadn't seen it materialize there's no denying that he looks much better this year. I'm not fully sold but for $7 I think there's plenty of ceiling.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Last week was a great time to get his true blue auto in the mail because he went out and did it again, of course not a no-hitter this time around but still strong. I've mentioned that I like him as a buy under $10 but even up at $14 now I don't think the value is bad. There are often growing pains when it comes to converting relievers to starters but Snead has looked fantastic in his professional debut, most importantly with his command where his walks per 9 innings is down below 2.00 after another start where he didn't issue any. At this point he's the refinement of a third/fourth pitch away from being a solid starting pitching prospect but with a plus fastball and improved control he's off to a great start.

players.name: Joseph Dzierwa
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! One of the biggest risers in last week's update to the pitching prospect rankings was Dzierwa who keeps on climbing as he gets closer to cracking my top 50. It was announced that he'll be making the move up to Double-A this week so that should definitely help his chances if he continues to dominate there. He's probably surprised me the most of any pitcher from last year's class outside of maybe Anthony Eyanson. I always say don't give in to FOMO and unfortunately his prices took off in a hurry so I don't know that I'll ever get a piece. Maybe in the unlikely event that he spins a gem in his AA debut and this price stays under $30 I'll give him a look but he's a hold for me right now.

players.name: Brock Porter
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Three straight weeks of dominant relief appearances for Porter whose ERA now sits under 2.00 for the year. Unfortunately the days of him being tried out as a starter are over and it looks like his role in the organization will be that of a high leverage reliever. Love seeing him continue to crush it but relief pitchers are kind of a tough sell in Bowman so I'm not sure there's much we can do with it at the moment.

players.name: Kash Mayfield
players.note: Spoiler alert: Kash is going to be the pitching "Prospect of the Week". His average base autograph price dropping after two straight scoreless outings doesn't make much sense to me but here we are. What if I told you that in 7 starts this season Mayfield has given up 0 earned runs in 5 of them. Not only that but in ALL 5 OF THEM he didn't allow more than a single hit. High-A hitters are batting .097 against him this year with a 64% contact rate and 32.7% strikeout rate. He's no doubt had some BABIP luck and his 1.52 ERA comes with a 3.41 FIP but even that is solid for what he's doing. Not sure what it will take for him to start getting more hobby love maybe a promotion or a move into MLB Pipeline's top 100 but the way he's throwing both of them could happen this year.

players.name: Tanner Franklin
players.note: Franklin came out of nowhere at the start of this year and fired off some dominant outings and saw his autograph price double from about $15 to over $30. It seems some of that excitement has faded and his price is starting to come back down even though he's doing a lot of the same things. Now that he's moved all the way up to inside my top 30 and his price is simultaneously losing steam I actually don't hate a play on his autographs if they're sitting in the low $20's. The command is by no means elite but it looks much improved from last year and the 6'5" righty is still missing as many bats as ever. Wouldn't be surprised if a move to AA was in the near future.

players.name: Mavis Graves
players.note: The MiLB's Free Game of the Day last Friday was Seth Hernandez's High-A debut but people tuning in may have been surprised to see him get locked into a duel with Graves who for the record was facing a much, much tougher lineup of the two in that game. Even with that tall task Graves showed up with 10 K's over 5 innings allowing 1 earned run. He's been popping up on hot sheets all season and we've been trying to figure out if he's for real but it's hard not to think the answer is yes. The 6'6" left-hander struggled with command last year and I know it's only been 7 starts but few pitchers have seen the type of improvement across the board that he has. His walk rate is down 5%, his strikeout rate is up 16% (!!), and contact rates against him are down to 57% which is crazy low. Of the 855 pitchers who have thrown 20+ innings in the minors this year there are the only 4 with a K-BB% over 34.5%: Anthony Eyanson, Seth Hernandez, Kade Anderson, Mavis Graves. Start up the hype train.

players.name: Koen Moreno
players.note: Couple of strong starts in a row for Moreno but the season long line isn't doing anything for me and there's nothing in the swing-and-miss or command department that really blows me away. Can't say that I see much here.

players.name: Dasan Hill
players.note: My #5 pitcher chase

players.name: Matt Wilkinson
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! I will say that I assumed after being traded to a new team if Tugboat came out and dazzled that the Giants fans would buy him up but this price seems to be moving pretty slowly. Even with six consecutive weeks on the sheet we've only seen his base autograph go from $13 to $22 and that increase feels light. Some people could have concerns over the long-term ceiling since his stature isn't one that typically plays well with starting pitchers but I still think he's been dominant enough for this thing to get more juice. On my next re-rank he'll almost certainly crack the top 100, especially if he keeps pitching this well, but I am surprised the market isn't moving faster on him. Still think he's a strong hold.

players.name: Jacob Miller
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Miller is starting to grow on me since the Marlins do well with pitchers and he has been a reliable arm that is on pace for 110+ innings for the third consecutive year but he's never been a big strikeout guy and that kind of kills the ceiling on his cards for Bowman. Still not a bad sleeper because he's been effective in his career but his secondary pitchers are better than his fastball and the lack of swing-and-miss probably stops him from being a huge name in the hobby.

players.name: Adam Seminaris
players.note: I'm really, really close to calling Seminaris a sleeper it's just so tough because you know how Bowman people are going to look at a 27-year-old arm in AA but he's looked much better this year. Has always had plus command so the 2.50 BB/9 is no surprise but his strikeouts have always been in kind of a boring range at 20% and this year have improved to 27.5%. I still don't think there is enough strikeout type stuff in the tank for a prospect his age to see much love but he's definitely worth putting in a pin in with how well he's throwing.

players.name: Ryan Sloan
players.note: Friend of the program Ryan Sloan makes it in consecutive weeks! Ryan was one of our big finds last year as I moved him up inside my top 25 and started labeling him as one of the best pitcher buys when his base autograph was under $20. His stock has gone up quite a bit since then as has his ranking which is now inside my top 5. He's also the youngest Bowman pitcher at the AA level and he uses three plus pitches with great command to shut opposing hitters down. Don't be fooled by the 4.94 ERA he's had some bad BABIP luck and both his FIP and xFIP are a full run lower as he's improved his contact rates from last year even with the move up in competition. Excited to see him keep doing it and would venture to say this won't be his last hot sheet appearance.

players.name: Joe Whitman
players.note: Bowman people being haters of crafty lefties is such a shame but even with that Whitman is a buy all day at $5. Our reigning 'Prospect of the Week' has now turned in three consecutive scoreless starts with 20 strikeouts in 16 innings. The command has always been great but the stuff has definitely taken a step forward this year. Contact rates against him are down 5% from last year, strikeout rates have gone from 24.2% to 31.8%, AND his walks are down. Since he's not overpowering maybe he's a guy whose base autograph tops out around $20 by the time he debuts kind of what we're seeing with Mitch Bratt but if you had some deeper color that would still be a 4x if it happened. Don't think that's a reach at all.

players.name: Victor Lizarraga
players.note: When it comes to $1-2 guys I'm always looking for something that jumps out in terms of improvements they made or something about them that I think could lead to Bowman value but sometimes it looks like nothing more than a few good starts strung together. The latter is the case here, not sure I see much with Lizarraga that would be a signal to buy.

players.name: Dylan MacLean
players.note: There's more to MacLean though who does have some things about him that I like. Actually had a really productive season last year in High-A with a 3.34 ERA. He's a lefty with basically average stuff and good command which we know is the pitching profile that Bowman people love to hate on. Walks are good as they always have been for him but the ability to miss bats has improved a touch, with a K/9 that is about a full strikeout higher than last year. It's still not a super exciting number though and while I do think he looks solid it's more floor over ceiling.

players.name: Jonathan Santucci
players.note: Santucci's start to the season has been a little bit tougher than last year's but he's bounced back nicely. After struggling to find the zone and walking 6 batters three starts ago he has settled down and has only walked one over 11.1 innings in his past two starts. Slider is the out pitch here and it's really, really good with really late snap he tunnels it very well with his fastball. As long as those command issues from earlier this year are behind him I think the upside is really good here in terms of Bowman value. He's in my top 25 and any arm in a Mets uniform with a strikeout rate over 30% is one that could pop at any moment. We're probably only a few more good starts in AA away from potentially seeing a promotion to AAA and I'd think that should give a nice little bump too.

players.name: Gage Stanifer
players.note: My #11 pitcher chase

players.name: Eddy Yean
players.note: You may recognize Yean's name because he's pretty regularly atop the velocity charts that go out in the Bowman Brew every morning. He throws gas but he's also exclusively a reliever so that kind of kills much of the fun.

players.name: Gage Jump
players.note: My #4 pitcher chase

players.name: Luis Perales
players.note: Such a frustrating player but the numbers continue to love him for the price

players.name: Max Clark
players.action: Many of the 2.0’s will have a reasonable explanation for why their base autograph price is inflated so I’ll explain those. Obviously there can be other factors at play that will make my formula not like their autograph price but it doesn’t necessarily mean their value is terrible. Max Clark for example has an extremely short printed autograph and the low supply leads to a higher price point. Doesn’t mean I hate his cards there’s just not a way to make the formula differentiate that.

players.name: George Lombard Jr.
players.action: No explanation here other than Yankees tax. Even for a Yankees SS prospect his cards are drastically overvalued.

players.name: Justin Gonzales
players.action: New release pricing. Love Gonzales but this is steep.

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.action: New release + he’s a Holliday = will likely never be a price that I like

players.name: Charlie Condon
players.action: Will probably debut soon but has just been okay so far in AAA, price helped by being such a big college name but doesn’t play for an organization that will help his value much when he’s called up and hasn’t been consistent enough for me since being drafted to be $100+

players.name: Ethan Salas
players.action: Tough one, I want to believe in the bounce back season and I do to some degree that’s why he’s moved up so many spots in my rankings since the start of the year, but his price has also more than tripled because of his hobby pedigree. It’s just not for me

players.name: Ching-Hsien Ko
players.action: Redemption base autograph and is extremely short printed so that’s driven the price up, nothing against him

players.name: Yairo Padilla
players.action: Was given quite a large deduction for not having played yet this year and still ranked this high. Last I heard his shoulder injury wasn’t expected to be that serious so hopefully he randomly shows up in a lineup one day, you know how those minor league injury updates are

players.name: Yolfran Castillo
players.action: I’m actually still a believer long-term in Cam but the fact of the matter is that recent results are weighted heavily in the new rankings format and since returning from that hand injury last year he’s never quite been the same, wouldn’t panic on him yet

players.name: Felnin Celesten
players.action: He’ll keep moving up the rankings as he continues to improve this year but much like Ethan Salas his pedigree causes his cards to go up faster than even these rankings can account for. As with many of the players that the formula will rank 2.0, the ceiling is very, very high but you’re taking on more risk buying a player this expensive with a limited track record

players.name: Tyson Lewis
players.action: He’s a big hobby name because the tools will be incredible if they all click but I still have major approach/contact concerns for an autograph this expensive. Like I said with Celesten the price is high because the good ceiling presents the possibility of a huge payday, but no doubt a risky entry point

players.name: Tony Blanco Jr.
players.action: The deduction for his auto being a non-1st drops this into the lowest buy range, electric power but you have to wonder how sustainable his offensive production is with the massive swing-and-miss numbers

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.action: Love that he’s getting respect as I’ve been shouting him out on hot sheets for five or so consecutive weeks but when those started this card was $6. Even two weeks ago when I said he was a solid stash for a call-up he was still at $11 on average. Despite not even getting the call yet the numbers would say it’s time to sell at $25

players.name: Jadher Areinamo
players.action: This feels like a mistake, looks like a few slipped through the cracks for a buck or two and drove this average down. Even with the price correction for his auto being a non-1st he is drastically underpriced

players.name: Termarr Johnson
players.action: Base autographs are redemptions and short printed, that along with the pedigree of being a high draft pick has kept his autographs higher than they probably should be

players.name: Josuar Gonzalez
players.note: Buy Rating: 2.8/5.0 HOLD | Expected Base Auto: $74 | Love me some Josuar but as the buy ratings suggest the market is pretty spot on with him. I do think that as he's promoted to Single-A and continues to play well this should very easily get over $100 with his pedigree of being a #1 international signing, but for where he's at now this price seems to fit.

players.name: Cristian Arguelles
players.note: Definitely a name to watch but he's a player I've always been on the fence with. Production is out of this world right now and the patience, contact, and power he's shown make him a decent grab for under $20. The only issues are that he repeated the DSL which I never like to see and even with his outrageous statistical season the second time around he had some extreme BABIP luck which he's having again in the CPX this year. Nothing against him at all and think the upside is good but I need some numbers to normalize before I can really get a read on him.

players.name: Aidan West
players.note: 4.9/5.0 Strong BUY | Expected Base Auto: $13.60

players.name: Brady Ebel
players.note: 4.8/5.0 Strong BUY | Expected Base Auto: $20.80

players.name: Hans Montero
players.note: Ah, the life of a Yankees prospect. Have a 3-HR game and watch your cards go up 500%. Definitely looks better this year but he's 22 and this is his third consecutive season in Single-A. Not exactly a vote of confidence. Worth watching but nothing for me right now.

players.name: Hayden Alvarez
players.note: Buy Rating: 3.5/5.0 HOLD but lean BUY | Expected Base Auto: $28.40 | He was in the buy range when the Sunday article came out but his price has come up a few dollars after another strong week. Alvarez is a 6'3" teenager with good bat-to-ball skills and great speed. Many in the organization think he'll grow into more power as he adds strength to his frame and if that's true he could be a big time helium name, although there is a chance that 'aha moment' for the hobby isn't until next year. He's already doubled his HR total from last year though so that's a good start. Good long-term hold.

players.name: Kellon Lindsey
players.note: Buy Rating: 3.3/5.0 HOLD | I think maybe some people did a little buying Sunday night after those rankings came out because this was $13 on average when I looked yesterday and now it's up to $20. Look, we haven't seen enough from Lindsey professionally to say he's going to be a good prospect, and he currently has more BABIP luck than probably any other prospect in baseball so the ridiculous average you're seeing will come crashing back down. But at the end of the day this is a first round pick, $3.3 million bonus, prep shortstop, with double plus speed, who plays for the Dodgers. That alone gives him a higher ceiling than most for this price. There's risk but in my opinion the reward outweighs it at the moment.

players.name: Blaine Bullard
players.note: 5.0/5.0 Strongest BUY | Expected Base Auto: $28

players.name: Truitt Madonna
players.note: Possibly a name to watch from 2026 Bowman. Wasn't on many radars but the Padres are pretty sneaky when it comes to finding talent late. Madonna is a 6'2" catcher with plus power projections who also sees time at first base and DH. There hasn't been enough good for him to climb up a ton in my rankings but he's a name worth monitoring as the season goes on.

players.name: Jake Munroe
players.note: 5.0/5.0 Strongest BUY | Expected Base Auto: $16.20

players.name: Dean Curley
players.note: Buy Rating: 3.5/5.0 HOLD but lean BUY | Expected Base Auto: $15.20 | Curley has officially cracked the new top 200 after consecutive strong weeks. There's passive and then there's whatever Dean Curley is doing. He currently owns a 26.3% swing rate which would make Emmanuel Rodriguez look aggressive. That's led to an almost 30% walk rate and .497 OBP which is extremely impressive. When he does swing he's doing so at the pitches he wants and he's driving them, with a .200 ISO and 160 wRC+ in High-A. He'll have to start swinging a little more because I don't think 26.3% is realistic to keep up over the course of a full season but his bat has looked fantastic when he does swing it. He's moved up quite a bit for me recently and still think he's a solid grab around $10.

players.name: Murf Gray
players.note: Buy Rating: 2.3/5.0 HOLD but lean SELL | Expected Base Auto: $27.40 | This one stings because I want to love Murf Gray, and I do, but the market has also loved him ever since his cards came out. With the massive jumps that are possible in the new rankings system he's gone from outside my top 200 to almost inside my top 100 but even with that a $40 base autograph is a little steep. Got promoted to High-A and hit 3 more HR in his first week there. He'll keep moving up as high as the numbers will allow and I feel like I'm probably already higher on him than most people, apparently just not the Bowman people.

players.name: Braylin Tavera
players.note: Tavera has always been a very interesting hobby player with good power and speed projections but questionable swing decisions. The power has jumped in a big way this year with 6 HR in 33 games after hitting just 7 all of last year, raising his ISO by 75 points. Unfortunately with that his already high 30.5% K rate has gotten even higher at 36.7%. He is what he is. Great hobby tools, not great contact. Not my usual target but I'd be lying if I said there wasn't upside for $3.

players.name: Malcolm Moore
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Another week where Malcolm Moore mashes adding a couple more homers to his total. I'm starting to believe that maybe this breakout is real but I've talked about in the past how his base autographs don't sell a ton because they were redemptions. Though the base autograph price will show as if it's not moving much we're probably very unlikely to get one for $10 since his last Speckle /299 went for $45 and Sapphire autos are around $50. Great season but looking at the sales of his color autos they're more in a hold range for me than buy.

players.name: Alfredo Duno
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Buy Rating: 3.7/5.0 HOLD but lean BUY | Expected Base Auto: $100 | When I updated the new rankings Duno was one of the biggest movers up to the now 11th best non-debuted hitting prospect for the hobby. Back in 2025 when I did my Reds buy sheet he was a buy for me at around $25 but those days are long gone. I still lean towards a buy with him because I do think he should be a $100 base autograph guy, but if you do your buying and selling on eBay that's not a huge profit window after losing about 13% on fees. Still think we'll see him hit triple digits though.

players.name: Charles Davalan
players.note: 4.6/5.0 Strong BUY | Expected Base Auto: $50.80

players.name: Jared Jones
players.note: 2026 Bowman name — the other Pirates Jared Jones. Must be confusing. Even FanGraphs has pitcher Jared Jones for his headshot. Hitter Jared Jones has double plus power and is off to a great start but the approach is not great. He's looked much better this year than last but he's striking out over 30%, contact rate under 70%, and his .487 BABIP says the average will come down. It's tough because power is the tool you want in Bowman but I think it might be the only one he has.

players.name: Quinn McDaniel
players.note: Blast from the past. I was flipping McDaniel base autos on COMC when he was a Giants prospect years ago. Showed some promise with a 13 HR/40 SB season in 2024 but then kind of fell off. Was playing Indy ball until the Twins scooped him and put him in Single-A a couple of weeks ago. He played one week there before a promotion to High-A and here he is again on the hot sheet twice in as many tries. Fun to see but too small of a sample to move much.

players.name: Josh Adamczewski
players.note: Buy Rating: 2.7/5.0 HOLD | Expected Base Auto: $58.80 | I was shouting out to buy Adamczewski on hot sheets last year at $7 so it feels crazy to me that his prices have come up this much. Sadly I don't have anything of his anymore. He's a prospect that I love and can't say enough good things about. Think the Brewers found a legit one here, but even with a move to inside my top 40 hitters he's priced slightly above my target for that spot.

players.name: Sam Petersen
players.note: 5.0/5.0 Strongest BUY | Expected Base Auto: $23

players.name: Thayron Liranzo
players.note: 4.6/5.0 Strong BUY | Expected Base Auto: $16.40

players.name: Kyle DeBarge
players.note: 5.0/5.0 Strongest BUY | Expected Base Auto: $15.40

players.name: Romeo Sanabria
players.note: There might not be a more consistent prospect than Sanabria who comes in every year and bats .260 with a .135 ISO and 120-ish wRC+. Unfortunately being a contact over power first baseman is not a profile that's ever sold in Bowman. I actually think he's a solid bat and he's produced at every level they've assigned him to as a professional, it's just not a very hype set of skills as far as the hobby is concerned.

players.name: Jonah Cox
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! Buy Rating: 2.0/5.0 SELL | Expected Base Auto: $10.30 | Here I get all excited to talk about the insane season Cox is having with another appearance and another increase to his autograph price only for my new formula to rain on my parade by giving him the lowest buy rating. To be fair, even with the massive jumps in scoring he still barely made the top 250 which is where a $10 autograph should be. Don't get me wrong he's still going to have a much, much better year than we all expected but there's regression coming eventually. If he was still $10 I'd say he's worth buying and hoping he continues this ridiculous run but he's up nearly 1,000% this season so it's hard to disagree with the buy ratings saying he's a sell.

players.name: Ruben Ibarra
players.note: You'd think you would have heard this name considering Ibarra hit 21 HR last year with a 136 wRC+. Sadly though he's a catcher, and not just a catcher but an older catcher. Good power but he just turned 27 and this is his third consecutive season in Double-A. That makes it tough to get the people going.

players.name: Tavian Josenberger
players.note: Josenberger is kind of a funky prospect that card people aren't sure what to do with and honestly neither am I. Bat-to-ball skills are good but he doesn't hit for much power. Speed is great and back in 2024 he stole 50 bases in just 86 games. Despite the good walk rates and contact though he still never manages to hit for good average, and the consistently low BABIPs each year probably point towards the contact he's making not being great quality. Still could be solid if some power pops.

players.name: Ryan Clifford
players.note: 4.6/5.0 Strong BUY | Expected Base Auto: $55.60

players.name: Payton Eeles
players.note: One of my favorite prospect stories — Eeles signed with the Twins in 2024 for $500. I only remember that because we pulled signing bonuses for the 2025 Bowman cheat sheet and I thought his was a mistake. That year he went from Single-A all the way to Triple-A with 12 HR, 41 SB, and 154 wRC+ combined at three levels. The power output for the 5'5" Eeles seemed to end there though and his ISO was just .071 last year and is under .100 again this year. Great approach, great contact, great speed — just such a good 'hustle' guy — sadly just not a profile that sells without power, especially at age 26. Still love watching him though personally.

players.name: Aaron Sabato
players.note: The year of Sabato continues? Now has 10 HR and a .368 ISO but the days of him being a hobby name seem to be gone because the prices have moved basically not at all. I suppose there's the hope that you grab something for a couple bucks, the Twins call him up, and he launches a few early homers. Definitely not out of the realm of possibility but also tough to bet on.

players.name: Hendry Mendez
players.note: Buy Rating: 2.6/5.0 HOLD | Expected Base Auto: $17.30 | Breaks my heart that the market caught on to Mendez. Well, not really because I had cards of his and then sold them but this is a guy who was a $2 base autograph on my 2025 team sheets prior to last season. He's basically cut from the same cloth as Sam Antonacci. Always had ridiculous contact rates and approach but hadn't hit for any power until he did and then his cards went up. He's still only 22 in AAA and is currently batting .313 with a .200 ISO and sub-17% strikeout rate. Love the player but in order for this to go up much more he'd have to sustain this power for longer since it hasn't really shown up prior to this season. Not impossible though and still a hell of a floor if it doesn't.

players.name: Yohandy Morales
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! Buy Rating: 2.2/5.0 Lean towards SELL | Expected Base Auto: $15.30 | Two players get the distinction of making six sheets in a row and the buying formula says 'nah'. As someone who is a notorious seller of hype though it is kind of doing what I intended. Morales was $6 on the first hot sheet so his price has now quadrupled in the last month and a half. Great to see him get hot and the call-up is likely coming soon but at this price he's probably a sell.

players.name: Seaver King
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Buy Rating: 3.2/5.0 HOLD | Expected Base Auto: $40.40 | Very few players have made bigger moves up my rankings sheet in 2026 than King who was outside the top 200 to start the year and has officially cracked the top 75. Can't say enough about how much better his entire offensive process looks compared to last year. Now that he's up in AAA we will see if another hot week could shoot him up high enough to make him a buy but as of right now he's only a couple bucks under where I'd expect him to be. The Bowman market is inefficient but every now and then it reacts to certain players in a very efficient manner, I think it's been pretty spot on with King.

players.name: Dean Livingston
players.note: Less pedigree coming out of high school than Slawinski but I had Livingston as a sleeper in 2025 Bowman Draft and based on what we've seen so far I think you have to like a buy at around $7. Tons of untapped potential in this arm since he didn't really start pitching as a starter until his senior year last season. As he adds strength I wouldn't be surprised if he got up to triple digit velocity and he's been almost unhittable in his first 12 innings as a pro inducing a 20.9% swinging strike percentage. Very sneaky grab.

players.name: Briggs McKenzie
players.note: Don't hate a buy — McKenzie is ranked the highest of the 2025 Bowman Draft prep arms group and has solid upside.

players.name: Matthew Fisher
players.note: Don't hate a buy — $10 or less prep arm with solid upside from 2025 Bowman Draft.

players.name: Sadbiel Delzine
players.note: I want to love Delzine but you'll notice that the other pitchers on this list that we've seen in a limited capacity are around $10 and after another strong start last week Delzine's closer to $20. Not super surprising since he's 6'5", the youngest player on this list by almost a year, and a Red Sox prospect. Few hobby fanbases overreact to a small sample more than those Boston faithful. Tremendous upside but for 9 DSL innings and 12 CPX innings this price is steep.

players.name: Johnny Slawinski
players.note: Pretty shocking he hasn't gone up yet but it is the CPX. It often takes the public longer to catch on to prospects playing well at the rookie levels due to the lack of video clips, data, and just eyeballs in general. Slawinski is already showing around 18" of IVB on his fastball and has yet to walk a single batter in his first 17 professional innings. I like him as a buy.

players.name: AJ Russell
players.note: Probably the best stash as he's now moved around my top 50 range and is still under $15. Big frame pitchers with electric fastballs move the needle more than anything in Bowman and Russell might be one of the sneakier ones. His 4.20 ERA in Single-A comes with a 2.06 FIP which suggests he's been more dominant than the stat sheet might indicate and his 14.40 K/9 there would certainly back that up.

players.name: Michael Lombardi
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! As one of the OG believers, it would bring me joy if we continue to see this trio of 2025 draft pitchers for the Royals in Lombardi, Lamkin, and Millar take off. All three of them were $7 or cheaper on the Royals sheet so the first two have already nearly tripled. Even though Lamkin is now up to Double-A and continues to look great I'm still higher on Lombardi. Not only was he a two-way player in college but when he did pitch he was a closer who threw primarily two pitches. Much of his development early on will be working on command, stretching him out, refining his secondary offerings — things that Lamkin already had going for him as a starter in college. Still think that Lombardi's stuff is better and has a higher ceiling, it might just take more time.

players.name: Kash Mayfield
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Kash was my only Padres buy this offseason getting a perfect 5/5 rating at $12 which he'll likely triple after a couple more strong starts. Honestly I'm surprised it hasn't gone up more than it has. Not only is he young for the level but opponents are batting .101 off of him this year as he's given up 2 or fewer HITS in 6 of his 8 starts. There's been some BABIP luck so his 1.30 ERA isn't going to hold but hitters have a 63.2% contact rate against the lefty and everything points towards him being a future top 10 pitching prospect.

players.name: Boston Bateman
players.note: Looks noticeably low for where he's ranked — a good grab at this price.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! Five weeks in a row and your price goes down feels insane. With the release of a new Bowman product though it's not uncommon to see players from past releases level out because there's so much attention on the new names. Wouldn't make this mistake here as I called Snead as a solid buy when he was under $10. After a rankings update he's now inside my top 75 and climbing. I still thought he'd miss a few more bats but the control has been MUCH better than expected as the former college reliever has now issued ZERO walks in his last three starts over 18 innings. Definitely trending up.

players.name: Cade Kuehler
players.note: I love me a Braves pitcher but unfortunately it's always hard to be a big name in Bowman when you aren't a strikeout guy. He's been extremely effective this year but it's been thanks to an improvement in his command. Fine for real life baseball, not super exciting for cards.

players.name: Braylon Doughty
players.note: Many of you know I've always loved Doughty, one of my favorite pitchers there is. These last couple of starts have been big green flags for me. He mixes pitches and locates them better than arguably any other pitcher his age — the question for Bowman was always going to be if his stuff would be good enough to post great strikeout numbers as he moved up levels. Last week he struck out 8 over 5 innings and though it's not included on this sheet he pitched last night and struck out 9 in 4.2 innings. His K/9 was in a 'not exciting for Bowman' range after his first few starts but is now up to 11.30 to go along with a 2.48 BB/9 and 3.03 ERA. Quietly just a really, really good pitcher who hasn't gotten the love he deserves yet. Value buy — looks noticeably low for where he's ranked.

players.name: Brock Porter
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Same story as last week. It's a shame because I really like Porter but he operates exclusively as a reliever and that's just not a path to much hobby relevance as a prospect.

players.name: JT Quinn
players.note: Looks noticeably low for where he's ranked — a good grab at this price.

players.name: Tanner Franklin
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! It's funny watching the Bowman market work. Franklin was around $17 on the Cardinals sheet, started the year with a few really strong starts and immediately doubled, and now he's crashing back down to his original price despite turning in three strong outings in a row. The 6'5" right-hander has now allowed 2 or fewer runs in 7 of his 9 starts this year including his last 4 in a row. Now that his prices have settled back down I don't hate stashing him for around $20.

players.name: Joe Whitman
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! We've now seen four consecutive gems (two were in one week), including being named Prospect of the Week, and Joe Whitman is still $7. The hobby's hate for crafty lefties has gone too far. It would be one thing if he was a low ERA, low walk rate guy who didn't strike anybody out but his K/9 this year is up to 11.37 after striking out 7 or more hitters in 3 of his last 4 starts. He's missing way more bats this year, getting weaker contact, AND walking fewer batters. This is a top 100 pitcher for me all day. Value buy — Joe Whitman at $7 is criminal!

players.name: Khal Stephen
players.note: Stephen is having a bit of a funky year. He's a pitcher I've always liked and at the end of last year my hopes were that if he could improve his strikeout rates he could be a really nice hobby arm. One of the better command pitchers you'll find — he had a 1.97 BB/9 at Mississippi St. followed by a 1.75 BB/9 in his professional debut where he climbed three different levels. This year that walks per 9 is up at 4.15 which is strange for him but he has settled down recently. Unfortunately the strikeouts that I hoped would tick up haven't. Still think there's upside but if he doesn't start missing more bats I don't know how much this price has to go up.

players.name: Adam Serwinowski
players.note: Good value in being under $10 and inside my top 100. Numbers still like him quite a bit.

players.name: Jamie Arnold
players.note: Was $50 entering the season but prices have cooled off after a couple rough outings — still inside my top 10 arms and worth a look.

players.name: Alex Clemmey
players.note: It feels like Clemmey has been a hold for me for years. He'll go out and have an 11 K start that nearly ropes me all the way in and then he'll go back out and walk 6 batters and get hit around. I've never really gotten a good read on him and that's why he's remained around the same ranking since last year. He is however extremely young for the level which is a huge plus and his strikeout rates are up from last year, but so are his walks. I think the upside is still really good at this price for the 6'6" left-hander but the more his command backs up the more I worry he could end up as a high leverage reliever. Still plenty of time though.

players.name: Adam Seminaris
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! The underlying numbers for Seminaris are actually really nice, as they have been all year, the issue is that he's 27 and has been pitching in Double-A since 2023. I do think that the Phillies will promote him to Triple-A soon and it will be very much deserved but given the age and fact that he's a command pitcher I'm not sure it will move the prices much.

players.name: Victor Lizarraga
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Somehow defying the odds by continuing to make it despite his season long line not looking good in the ERA, K, or BB departments. I'm not buying that this is anything.

players.name: Dylan MacLean
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! MacLean's start to the 2026 season has been much more encouraging so I'm not ready to say that it's nothing but most of his effectiveness comes from his command and ability to generate weak contact. None of the pitches really pop and he doesn't strike out a ton of hitters. Good arm but not a hobby exciting one.

players.name: Jacob Miller
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Four weeks in a row and losing 60% of your value is pretty crazy work but welcome to the card world if you aren't a big name prospect. As I've said before Miller is a great innings eater but doesn't strike many batters out so he doesn't really sell.

players.name: Gage Stanifer
players.note: The new rankings system loves Stanifer who has moved up almost 50 spots. He does have great stuff including a fantastic slider and when he's on he's on, making him very capable of racking up strikeouts. The downside is that in a two week span this year he's had a 9 K game and a 6 BB game. There could be some reliever risk if the command doesn't improve but this is a guy who had a 2.86 ERA while striking out 35.5% of the hitters he faced combined across three levels last year. If you believe in the stuff, and the Jays pitcher development (which has improved), he could be a fun player to stash for $10.

players.name: Beck Way
players.note: One of the better turnaround seasons we've seen in Triple-A and the numbers for the year are really impressive especially the huge increase in strikeouts, unfortunately he's a reliever only which is a dagger.

players.name: Gage Jump
players.note: This week's Prospect of the Week didn't even have time to get that award or get a hot sheet write-up before he was called upon to make his MLB debut. Have loved watching the success the last couple of years but unfortunately now that he has debuted he will be removed from the rankings list. So long old friend.

players.name: Mitch Bratt
players.note: I'll never let the hobby win its disrespect for crafty lefties. Still love Mitch Bratt and can't help it. Seeing his price go down after what he's accomplished in his minor league career feels crazy.

players.name: Wei-En Lin
players.action: SELL — Not really fair here because his base autograph is a redemption and seems to be very short printed. Nothing against him but the high price due to short supply throws the formula off.

players.name: Luis Perales
players.action: Strongest BUY — Tough one, wouldn't be surprised if he continues to slip more as he struggles but the formula has always liked Perales because the stuff is really good, he's just not missing nearly as many bats this year.

players.name: Alejandro Rosario
players.action: Strongest BUY — Even with the deduction for players who haven't played in 2026 he's still top 100. If you're someone who doesn't mind a cheap stash on an injured pitcher he's not a bad long-term hold, just tough since we don't really know what his timeline looks like.

players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Price Last Week: $17 | Price This Week: $26 (+52.9%)

players.note: Price Last Week: $7 | Price This Week: $9 (+28.6%)
