players.note: Price Last Week: $20 | Price This Week: $23 (+15%)

players.name: Blaze Jordan
players.note: Price Last Week: $56 | Price This Week: $48 (-14.3%)

players.name: Kemp Alderman
players.action: Strong BUY — Unfortunately injured so as he misses time his ranking will drop, you can probably wait on this one.

players.name: Hyun-Seok Jang
players.note: Jang’s ERA for the year isn’t pretty but the FIP and xFIP are lower so he should trend back in the right direction. His most notable improvement this year is the command as he’s cut his walk rate in half from 18.3% to 8.9% while keeping the strikeout numbers about the same. Could end up being a really nice prospect with the way the control is trending but this is his third year seeing time in Single-A and with the additional market of international buyers his autographs have always been too steep for me.

players.name: Alex Santos II
players.note: Another strong week for Santos and the strikeout numbers look much better this year but the Astros moved him to the bullpen and he’s worked exclusively as a reliever this year which kind of kills any of our excitement.

players.name: Dean Livingston
players.note: Buy Range: $6 - 4.3/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $9.40

players.name: Jaxon Wiggins
players.note: Wiggins is ranked 38th but let’s not forget he was a fringe top 10 pitcher for me entering this year before he was hit with the injury bug. He’s climbing his way back and after firing off back-to-back strong starts we have to like the odds of this price returning to that $50 range it was at in the spring. Unfortunately his rehab assignment has him pitching two levels down from where he finished last year which hurts part of his hobby ranking, but if he gets back to AAA and keeps this pace up he’ll probably find himself back in my top 25.

players.name: Gabriel Hughes
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! I may have been first to the Gabriel Hughes party a few weeks ago when I realized that many of his pitching metrics looked drastically improved from last year. That continues to be the case after another nearly spotless start and he now owns a 10.62 K/9 and 2.43 BB/9 in the EXTREMELY hitter friendly Pacific Coast League. Unfortunately as I’ve said in the past the pitching conditions won’t get much easier when he’s called up to the Rockies. I do think he deserves to see some gains on his autograph price so I’d be tempted to buy because under the hood his stuff this year looks solid, but knowing what awaits him at the next level makes it tough.

players.name: Adam Serwinowski
players.note: Great to see Serwinowski staying hot and congrats to anyone who bought when this base autograph dipped down near $6 earlier this year when I signaled him as a buy. The only thing keeping him from climbing higher than he has is the walk rates, and the iffy command combined with the fact that he has two plus grade pitches makes you wonder if the Dodgers convert him to a reliever in the future. Still tremendous upside especially in this organization but at $15 I’m holding.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: Buy Range: $7 - 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy). Expected Value - $19.40

players.name: Robinson Ortiz
players.note: Fun arm who had a very legit season last year with the Dodgers but he’s a reliever. The good news is that we could potentially see him called up in the near future but buying a relief pitcher and hoping he wow’s in his debut is a tough ask.

players.name: JT Quinn
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Quinn has been a buy on numerous articles in the past but his target price now sits dead even with his actual price which makes him a hold. It’s not impossible though that when I do my next big re-rank he winds up closer to 70th and that makes him a buy at this price but I’ll wait to see how that shakes out. One of the biggest surprises for me so far in the 2025 class and I’ve been so impressed with what I’ve seen he’s gone from outside of my top 150 pitchers prior to the season to now top 80. Keep on holding.

players.name: Jamie Arnold
players.note: Buy Range: $31 - 4.0/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $47.50

players.name: Gage Ziehl
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! I had a feeling that after weeks and weeks of no movement there would come a day where a handful people said, “alright, I’m in” and bought his cards, and it looks like that came last week as his base autograph more than doubled. As I’ve said for about all of his six week hot streak, if he can consistently come out with 6-7 K starts he should have great upside at this price as a 70 grade command pitcher, and we’ve seen it at times this year. But then we also get these 3 strikeout starts sprinkled in. Either way he’s been very effective these last two months after a slow start and I really do think the Boston pitching lab could make something out of this, rankings be damned.

players.name: Gage Stanifer
players.note: Well, well, well. If it isn’t our first 5/5 on the hot sheet. The amount of people sleeping on Stanifer is crazy especially considering he got his autograph in the newest Bowman release and it’s already under $10. I think the people are wrong. He pitched at three different levels last year and finished with a 2.86 ERA and 35.5% strikeout rate. The start of this year was rough for him, with a 7.71 ERA in April and 16 walks to 27 strikeouts. He followed that with a 1.37 ERA in May and then a 3.28 ERA in June where he walked only 9 batters in 5 starts compared to 33 K’s. There’s still a touch of reliever risk because the control gets away from him at times but this is way, way too live of an arm to be under $10.

players.name: Jacob Bresnahan
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! I said it last week but this kid’s sneaky. The control isn’t necessarily a red flag but maybe a yellow one as he does struggle to locate at times, but not last week, walking only 1 in 6 innings while striking out 7. Think there’s good upside here at $10 but for where I have him ranked the formula says that price is pretty fair. If you’re a believer I’m good with a buy here but the market seems to be spot on.

players.name: Kyson Witherspoon
players.note: Double dose of the Witherspoon twins on today’s hot sheet. Another guy who was top 10 for me before the year but I think the season that Anthony Eyanson is having is what more people expected from Kyson Witherspoon. Everyone really bailed after the slow start to the year but he seems to have turned it around as of late which is huge. After posting a 7.13 ERA in April he got that down to 4.00 in May and now 3.38 in June. He’s climbing back up my rankings as quickly as each start will allow but let’s remember that this was just a 1st round pick by one of the strongest fanbases in the hobby. I’d almost be tempted to buy if anything.

players.name: Ethan Pecko
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Now that the Astros have called up Miguel Ullola to join their bullpen it feels like we should be getting closer to Pecko getting his crack in a rotation that has a -5.2 WAR this year, 29th out of 30 teams. His prices have already doubled since I made him a 5/5 buy this offseason at $6 but he has remained a 5/5 or close to it for the past few months as well. I know a couple of you got into red autos and some other deep color early and cashed out for really nice gains so congratulations to you. If you don’t have anything I still don’t think it’s too late to grab a piece and hope for a solid debut if you’re into that kind of thing.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: After the first month of the season the Eyanson-mania hit an all time high and this base autograph got up to $100 at its peak. Since then he’s been promoted to AA, continued to look really good, yet lost about 40% of that value. The only yellow flag is that his K’s have dropped quite a bit and his walks are up so you’d like to see him correct that, but even with that his ERA in 7 starts at this level is 1.48. When his autograph price exploded I accepted the fact that I’d probably never own one because it got so blown out of proportion. Where it’s at now though makes it almost worth hopping in and trying to catch a second wave.

players.name: Ryan Sloan
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! While everyone fights over whether Seth Hernandez or Kade Anderson is #1 let’s not gloss over what our friend Ryan Sloan is doing in AA this year. The youngest pitcher at the entire level (4.3 years younger than average) posted an ERA under 4.00 in consecutive months and his 11.37 K/9 and 1.89 BB/9 on the season are both fantastic. If Anderson’s base autograph is $175+ then Sloan’s should be much, much closer to $100, and as I’ve said in the past I think he has a higher ceiling as an MLB starter than Anderson does too.

players.name: Seth Hernandez
players.note: As we’ve been saying all year Seth is breaking the ceiling of what we thought autographs of non-debuted pitchers could reach so while the formula thinks he’s overvalued it’s tough to say for sure. People have disagreed with me and said Kade Anderson is their #1 pitching prospect and the argument for it is fair, but Hernandez’s upside especially in Bowman is quite a bit higher. There’s only one Paul Skenes but if anybody in the minors has the stuff to replicate that craze it’s definitely Hernandez.

players.name: Johnny King
players.note: Buy Range: $26 - 4.8/5.0 (Strong Buy). Expected Value - $48.75

players.name: Bryce Cunningham
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Another one where my target price is right on the nose. Cunningham continues to pitch well and being an underrated Yankees prospect is nearly impossible which makes me want to buy him for when that day comes that their fans get excited and pump his cards. My only issue is that he’s a changeup dominant righty and doesn’t miss a ton of bats. Like him but don’t love him, but buying in hopes that the Yankees tax kicks in later isn’t the worst strategy.

players.name: Boston Bateman
players.note: Bateman was a buy for me on the Orioles sheet at $8 and honestly I’m surprised this hasn’t gone up more, but if you got some color then you’ve almost doubled your money so hard to complain. There’s probably still some reliever risk in the 6’8” left-hander and the overall walk numbers are up a touch from last year but his strikeout rate is up 4.7% too and he’s mowing down hitters at a level where he’s 2.5 years younger than the average pitcher. If he can show down the stretch an improved ability to throw strikes it would drastically move up his ceiling, either way he’s a top 100 pitcher for me.

players.name: Malachi Witherspoon
players.note: The numbers don’t like the price on Witherspoon but since it’s so low I don’t think it’s actually worth selling right now and you’re better off waiting to see if he pops later this year. His swing-and-miss numbers look great and the command has been a pleasant surprise for me as well, the only issue is that when he does get hit he gets hit hard, something that happened to him in college as well. Still think the bones are solid here and the 3.58 xFIP says his 5.12 ERA has been unlucky. Not sure I’m buying necessarily but I’d definitely hold what I have.

players.name: Hunter Patteson
players.note: Hard not to root for a fellow UCF Knight, my alma mater, but Patteson is a typical crafty lefty who has posted low walk rates but also low strikeout rates the last two seasons. Sadly just not the type of pitcher that the hobby is after.

players.name: Michael Kennedy
players.note: Undersized lefty who strikes out less than 9 hitters per 9 innings. I really want to love him because his age 19 season with the Pirates was fantastic but since the move to Cleveland the strikeout rate is down in a big way. Tough to get the Bowman people moving for a 5 inning start with 1-2 K’s and he’s had a handful of those already this season. Probably going to be a nice arm for the Guards, just not sure it works for what we do.

players.name: Quinn Mathews
players.note: 5 weeks in a row! If it isn’t public enemy number one. Mathews made it all the way up to my 15th ranked pitcher before the wheels fell off and he couldn’t find the zone for a month. Then he fell down the rankings, then threw consecutive 6 inning starts with only 1 walk each, got my hopes up, and then back to walking everybody. I said a couple weeks ago I’ve thrown my hands up because I just can’t seem to get on the right side of his ups and downs. Still think you hold because the Cardinals should call him up soon and with a strong debut this price could jump up considerably, but it’s hard for me to trust him a ton.

players.name: Sabier Marte
players.note: Nothing new for me here. Marte’s upside as a 6’5” pitcher in the Yankees system does interest me a bit and his 5.64 ERA comes with a 3.93 FIP so he has been pitching better than the box scores may indicate, but due to injuries he’s 22 and still hasn’t pitched above rookie ball. Would need to see something at the next level to consider buying.

players.name: Adler Cecil
players.note: Big 6’4” left-hander who has been mowing down hitters so far this year with a 41% strikeout rate, unfortunately as with Marte he missed all of last year so he’s yet to pitch above the rookie levels. His last start was by far his best, striking out 10 batters over 5 innings, but again until we see him face better hitters I don’t think we can do much.

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! We get it man, you’re legit. For those of you counting this is now 12 out of 13 weeks that Kade has made the hot sheet. If you’re wondering why he hasn’t been promoted yet I don’t think he will, and it’s probably more likely that if Seattle were to call him up they’d pull him straight from AA. The only block in the road is that their rotation is already stacked. Will be interesting to see how they find a way to work him in but it becomes more clear every week that he’s just too good to be in the minors.

players.name: Cam Caminiti
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! This feels like maybe there were some outlier sales because I wouldn’t expect Braves fans to let this price fall below $40. If you can find him under $40 I like him as a buy because what he’s shown recently as one of the youngest pitchers in High-A has been really impressive. I know Briggs McKenzie is the shiny new toy and his price is surging (and I love him too) but for me Caminiti’s ceiling is much higher so if they get into the same ballpark of price this is where I’d be buying.

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.note: Buy Range: $39 - 4.1/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $59.60

players.name: Charlie Condon
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Condon came in hot with a 3 HR week and at this point we’ve got to be wondering when that trip to Denver is coming. I’m not sure how the Rockies could wait more than a couple of weeks. Since Charlie has so much pedigree as a top draft pick and is known for his massive power I do think there’s a chance that when he debuts this base autograph pushes closer to $125 but that day could come at any moment so this is about the time where I’d shift into ‘get ready to sell’ mode and start drafting my listings. Will be an exciting day when it comes.

players.name: Bryce Rainer
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Sometimes the numbers say you should sell but this is another case of one we should ignore. Rainer’s ranking slipped a ton early on this year because his new swing looked like it was going to be a nightmare. However, since then he has quieted the hand load and has been demolishing the baseball. He was $90+ on the Tigers buy sheet and let’s not forget that when 2024 Bowman Draft came out him and Konnor Griffin were basically a coin flip for a lot of people including myself. After a .643 OPS in April that autograph price was nearly cut in half and got down into the $50’s but he’s hit 6 HR with an OPS over 1.000 this month and he’s almost gained all of that value back. If he continues to look like the Bryce Rainer we hoped to see prior to this season his ranking will shoot back up and his card value should continue to do so as well.

players.name: Fernando Cruz
players.note: Cruz was a big name coming out of the 2024 international class but he struggled in his DSL debut and then again even more in the CPX the following year. There’s great power and speed upside and most of the numbers are much improved his second time through the CPX but there are still some red flags in the contact. High upside but he’s a gamble.

players.name: Brailyn Antunez
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Antunez has been a buy in past articles when he was $6-7 and now that he’s doubled the formula says he’s a hold though it does still point to him being a tad undervalued. He’s been scorching hot the last few weeks and if you’re going to take a chance on an 18-year-old prospect with really loud tools this is still a solid option. Approach and K’s are a concern but the power/speed here is really, really good.

players.name: BJ Murray Jr.
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Another no base autographs guy like Mike Boeve. I touched on Murray last week but it’s the same story. No real red flags. Contact looks great and power is up, what more could you want to see? He’s now 26 and the fact that card people didn’t take notice of him after his 20 HR/20 SB season last year means they might not ever. Your best bet (if you did want to buy) is grabbing some cheap color and hoping that whenever he does get called up he starts hot because the Cubs fans will shoot your prices up when that happens. On the flip side their AAA roster is pretty stacked with guys who they don’t have an opening for on the big league club so it’s hard to know how long you’d be waiting.

players.name: Fenwick Trimble
players.note: Buy Range: $8 - 4.4/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $12.70

players.name: Sean Keys
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Technically Sean Keys shouldn’t be on here because prospects are removed from my rankings when they make their MLB debut but he qualified, and we love him, so he gets his last shoutout. Keys was a 5/5 rated buy the last three times he was mentioned in articles, including both of the last two hot sheets where he was $20. Congrats to everyone who bought something nice because your money doubled up quickly. It’s been a great run Sean Keys and thank you for the memories!

players.name: Gavin Kilen
players.note: Buy Range: $19 - 4.0/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $28.80

players.name: Nick Becker
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! As I said last week I liked Becker when he was drafted which is what has kept him ranked ahead of some of these other CPX names that I have a little less faith in. He’s striking out more than I had anticipated but he still checks a ton of hobby boxes and has really good upside. At this price though I’d probably want to see it in Single-A before I felt comfortable buying much. Definitely trending in the right direction though.

players.name: Brent Iredale
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Yet another great looking week for Iredale who went deep twice but for me the green flag was the 7 BB: 5 K because the approach and contact are a bigger question mark than the power. Trending in the right direction but as I said last week, 23 in Single-A won’t move the card market much.

players.name: Dean Curley
players.note: Buy Range: $6 - 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy). Expected Value - $15.70

players.name: Mike Boeve
players.note: Boeve doesn’t have any base autos but I’ll still go ahead and add him because he does have plenty of color autos out there. He was actually one of my favorite sleepers back in 2024 because all the guy did was hit. You ready for a stat line? That year between A+ & AA, Boeve hit .338 with a 159 wRC+, posting an 84.6% contact rate and 6.2% SwStr%. Unfortunately he’s battled some injuries since then and when he was on the field last year all of those numbers fell off pretty hard. It looks like he’s trending back towards that version of himself but he’s now 24 and in AA for the third year in a row. I actually think the bat is nice and wouldn’t be surprised if he finishes the year (health permitting) with a very impressive stat line, I’m just not sure if the card people will care.

players.name: Mairoshendrick Martinus
players.note: Just a player I’ve never known what to do with. Has always been extremely streaky. Fantastic tools with 7 HR & 21 SB already but he’s back in Single-A at 21 after seeing time in High-A last year and looking solid for a couple of weeks. Not sure if the Dodgers just didn’t have room to keep him there or what. Has improved his swing-and-miss tremendously since his time in rookie ball but we need to see him face better pitching.

players.name: Luke Dickerson
players.note: Buy Range: $13 - 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy). Expected Value - $28

players.name: Ethan Anderson
players.note: Anderson hasn’t moved up enough to get into my top 250 but let the record show that I really like this bat and always have, as he was featured as a sleeper for me on many articles last year. Unfortunately he hit for almost no power last season (4 HR), but that has changed this year more than tripling his power output to 15 HR, raising his ISO from .090 to .245. Another win for the juiced balls theory. It’s not common for a C/1B prospect to be hit over power but his contact skills are really strong so the increase in power makes him a very intriguing bat. Keep an eye on him.

players.name: Eduardo Quintero
players.note: Buy Range: $60 - 4.1/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $92.50

players.name: JoJo Parker
players.note: Big move this week for Parker who goes up 10+ spots and is on the verge of entering our top 20. Hard to argue with that as he made an adjustment in his load and swing mechanics that seems to have worked because he is mashing. I see him live a good amount and will still stick to my original assessment from the 2025 Bowman Draft writeup that he might have my favorite package of offensive tools in the class after Eli Willits. Sadly $80 isn’t cheap so it’s a tough one to buy too heavily unless you think he’s a future top 10 prospect but for what it’s worth I’m a believer.

players.name: Gabriel Davalillo
players.note: Buy Range: $12 - 4.4/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $20.80

players.name: Demetrio Crisantes
players.note: Hopefully this price still exists after Crisantes hit for the cycle yesterday, but if it doesn’t I will tell you that you should have bought last week when he was a buy on here! He was also a buy on my preseason Diamondbacks sheet despite being on the shelf. After a fantastic 2024 that didn’t get nearly enough attention his 2025 was cut short and everyone seemed to forget about him. I’ve long been a fan just need him to stay healthy, and now that he has he’ll probably start getting that respect in the hobby that he’s deserved. Think if you’re still seeing $30 base autos he’s a buy. Love what we’ve seen so far since he returned from injury.

players.name: Matt Fraizer
players.note: What you probably don’t realize is that Fraizer had a minor league season where he hit .306 with 23 HR and 15 SB between A+ & AA. Unfortunately that was in 2021 and he’s struggled to replicate that success since. He’s now 28-years-old which makes him too old for the Bowman people, even if he were to get hot, but seeing him perform well early on with a new team is a step in the right direction.

players.name: Seong-Jun Kim
players.note: Still haven’t figured out a way to adjust the rankings for these two-way players like Kim, Owens, Morii, etc. so it always puts them lower than they should be. The bat has looked good so far in his CPX debut so with the combination of Texas letting him develop on both sides and the international buyers he brings his hobby ceiling is huge. Until we see more we still have to assume this price is more hype than anything, but I’d actually argue that’s good for his cards because when players with this type of hype struggle their prices don’t drop as quickly as your average prospect.

players.name: Druw Jones
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! This is the ultimate ‘Undertaker sitting up in his coffin’ GIF. Is Druw Jones alive? I would have said no until I watched him hit a 480 foot homer yesterday. That’s 4-8-0. Unfortunately it was only his 3rd HR of the year and his K rate is currently over 30% so I can only get so excited. The good news is that he’ll continue to climb levels and will reach the MLB with his glove alone, and because he’s such a good athlete there’s always a chance things will click with the bat as well. He was the #2 overall pick for a reason after all. I see the argument for wanting to gamble on a guy like him especially since his base autograph was once about $400 and is now under $20, but I’m not sure I’m ready to be hurt again.

players.name: Cristian Arguelles
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! I’d be tempted to ignore the ratings here and continue to hold. When I sit down and do my next big re-rank in a couple weeks I’ll move Arguelles up but he’s kind of stuck for now because there’s a performance score that helps them climb in between and he’s nearly maxed out on it for the rookie levels. I do think that this is an offensive profile that will work at the next level and I don’t expect him to falter when that move to Single-A comes, but he needs to get there first and this price is already pretty steep.

players.name: Handelfry Encarnacion
players.note: Names you love to see. Everyone knows I’m a big Handelfry guy so him having consecutive weeks with an OPS over 1.000 is great news. Even with the price increase he remains a buy for me at $15 since I have his target closer to $25. He has yet to get much public love but after starting the year slow hitting under .200 with a .656 OPS in April, Encarnacion has hit .270+ in May and June with an OPS of .916 and .815. Last year he had 5 HR/6 SB and in fewer games this season he’s at 8 HR/17 SB. Everything seems to be going in the right direction.

players.name: Alessander De La Cruz
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! The hobby rankings shown and buy ratings only go through 250 but I can tell you that ALDC moved inside my top 300 this week and as I said last week I don’t think he’s a bad flier for how cheap he is. He’s not exactly young for the level since the Rockies had him repeat both the DSL & CPX which is a downer but hopefully they’ll put him in Single-A soon because it’s very much deserved.

players.name: Nick Lorusso
players.note: Another ‘probably too old for the hobby to care’, Lorusso is going on 26 and is repeating the same level he was at last year. Much of the approach, contact, etc. looks similar but the power is way way up. After hitting 7 HR in 112 games last year he’s already gone deep 13 times in 61 games this season, nearly doubling his ISO from .127 to .249. Love to see that but still not sure it’s enough to make the Bowman people get up.

players.name: Yohairo Cuevas
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Great to see him staying hot but some of his qualifying time for the previous hot sheets was spent in Single-A which isn’t where you want to be at almost 23. I believe I said it last week but this is the second year in a row he’s looked great when he’s in A but struggles when he’s in A+. This hot week is a step in the right direction but it’s still nothing for me.

players.name: Devin Taylor
players.note: Sometimes guys don’t hit for power but if you know it’s there then you have to trust it’ll show up. That’s where we’re at with Taylor, who hit an Indiana school record 54 HR in three collegiate seasons. This year his .164 ISO is decent but not what you’d expect from a power bat, but unlike many power bats his hit tool is strong as well. He walked more than he struck out in his college career and this year between A+ & AA he’s hitting .305 with a 16.2% walk rate, 10 HR, and 10 SB. Once his power that we know is in the tank starts to pop I think he ends the year as a top 100 prospect for a lot of people. And that could be coming sooner rather than later because after having a 116 wRC+ and .144 ISO in A+ he’s got a 144 wRC+ and .219 ISO since his promotion to AA. I believe in his bat.

players.name: Kemp Alderman
players.note: Buy Range: $20 - 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy). Expected Value - $42.80

players.name: Welbyn Francisca
players.note: Last year some of our favorite Guardians prospects like Jaison Chourio and Welbyn Francisca struggled, seeing their stock fall off, but both have bounced back in a big way in 2026. Welbyn’s always been a great bat-to-ball hitter but the power was nonexistent last year with 3 HR and a .073 ISO in 428 PA. This year he’s already doubled that to 6 long balls in only 98 PA raising his ISO to .250. I’ll spare you my theory about how juiced the baseballs are this year but either way it’s great for us with his Bowman cards. The only red flag is that to get to this power he’s sacrificed quite a bit of contact and his overall rates are down 10%. Still think he’s a great hold.

players.name: Kane Kepley
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! How Kepley lost value on his autographs this past week is a mystery. Probably just a few auctions that slipped through the cracks and ended low. This hitting approach is incredible, and the speed is great as well. Last week he had a .444 OBP thanks to 5 walks, added 3 more stolen bases to get him to 39 on the year, and though the power is his only below average tool he had two doubles, a triple, and homer as well. No doubt slept on for the lack of power but even with that considered he’s almost a top 60 hitter for me. He has a chance to be the North side of Chicago’s own Sam Antonacci, and I think that as he climbs minor league levels they’re going to grow to love him.

players.name: Owen Carey
players.note: Buy Range: $16 - 4.0/5.0 (Buy). Expected Value - $24

players.name: Oswaldo Osorio
players.note: Also 21 and still stuck in Single-A with Martinus, however his contact rates haven’t improved nearly as much. While the power is good he’s a tad old for the level and he strikes out a ton. Nothing for me right now. If you were going to take a chance on one of them popping since Dodgers prospects tend to do that, I’d go with Martinus before Osorio personally.

players.name: Brock Rodden
players.note: Rodden had a sneaky good season in AA last year and the move to AAA has not been tough on him as he’s already doubled his HR total and raised his ISO 60 points while cutting down his strikeouts by nearly 7%. Great improvements but as a speedy switch-hitter with a good glove and below average power it’s not a profile I expect people to go crazy for. Very productive but better baseball player in real life than he is for the hobby.

players.name: Andrew Fischer
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! On one hand every time Fischer hits more bombs and shows up yet again on the hot sheet I feel like an idiot because my rankings still think he’s overpriced. What makes me feel like less of an idiot is the fact that he’s playing out of his mind and his autograph prices aren’t really going up, which does make me think I’m right. The regression hasn’t hit yet, and I hope it never does, because this run he’s on is incredible to watch, but seeing as though he HAS to put up this level up production to keep his autograph at $100 tells me that once he’s not doing that it’s going to go down. As I’ve said before, I buy when I think there’s 50% gains on the table and it’s hard for me to picture him being a $150 type guy.

players.name: Rainiel Rodriguez
players.note: Buy Range: $94 - 4.8/5.0 (Strong Buy). Expected Value - $180

players.name: Eddie Rynders
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! No respect! Of course it’s not uncommon for cheaper players like this to fluctuate a couple bucks each week but this time it’s down after his third straight appearance. It wasn’t the most exciting hot week since he hit .222 and struck out 9 times, but his .391 OBP and 2 more homers didn’t hurt. Still don’t think we can do much with this. Rynders is up to 8 HR in the same amount of PA that he only went deep once in last year, raising his ISO from .067 to .204, but to get to that power he’s sacrificing a lot of contact and has seen his strikeout rate go from 25% to 44.5%. Love to see the power showing up but he’s got to find a way to balance the two.

players.name: Ivan Luciano
players.note: Listen, I’ve never hated Luciano who was one of my very deep sleepers in 2024 Bowman Draft. He stood out at the combine that year with great performances with the glove and bat in the showcase games. Great approach and barrel control but likely below average power. Obviously a catcher with below average power is not a recipe for hobby success, but he has improved his ISO from .103 last year to .151 this year while also dropping his strikeout rate and improving his contact rate to over 81%. Not sure I love the ceiling but not a bad floor for a few bucks.

players.name: Brody Hopkins
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $17, Buy Rating 4.7/5.0 (Strong Buy), Expected Value $31.50. No separate write-up.

players.name: Riley Quick
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $14, Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy), Expected Value $38. No separate write-up.

players.name: Sheng-En Lin
players.note: Shifting fully to pitcher-only after being a two-way prospect. Up-and-down season but best start of the year last time out (5 IP scoreless, 0 BB, season-high 8 K). Price now leans on pitching + international market alone; not interested at this price yet.

players.name: Henry Lalane
players.note: Price jump to $43 (+186.7%) is real, not a data error — Yankees hype plus consecutive Baseball America Hot Sheet appearances. Dominant 7-start run, climbed 90 spots into the top 100 (#96). Still 22 in Single-A for a third year, lefty leaning on a changeup that plays up at this level — $43 is around my 9th-10th ranked pitcher price, don't see him getting that high. Consider selling.

players.name: Luis Perales
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $6, Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy), Expected Value $14.20. No separate write-up.

players.name: Taylor Dollard
players.note: Two strong starts in a row but hard to get excited — he's 27 and in A+ (tough Everett park, though). Plus-command, limited swing-and-miss. Price flat at $2.

players.name: Dean Livingston
players.note: Sleeper pick back in January at $7. Better than expected pro debut — 2.72 ERA after moving up to A ball at 19, price still at $7. Great frame, projects to a triple-digit fastball down the line. Buy Rating 4.2/5.0, Expected Value $11.20 — solid upside play, in Buy Range.

players.name: Antoine Kelly
players.note: 0.71 ERA over 8 AAA appearances since the Dodgers-to-Cubs move, but he's a reliever, which kills the hobby excitement despite the results. Price up to $10 (+25%).

players.name: Aiden May
players.note: Efficient 2.63 ERA pro debut last year but FIP/xFIP and a .175 BABIP suggest heavy luck. Command improved this year but strikeouts down — price likely stays put ($3) unless that changes. Worth watching given the Marlins' player-development reputation.

players.name: Cam Caminiti
players.note: 4 weeks in a row. Price back up to $50 (+31.6%) after last week's dip; ERA trending the right way by month (5.63 Apr, 4.64 May, 2.65 Jun, 0.00 so far Jul). Formula reads 'lean sell' (2.4/5.0) due to early-season struggles, but still the highest-upside arm in the Braves system, Expected Value $36 — ignore the sell signal.

players.name: Jacob Bresnahan
players.note: 4 weeks in a row, price flat at $10. Like him overall but command isn't great and he really only has two plus pitches — some reliever risk. Buy Rating 2.9/5.0 (Hold but overvalued), Expected Value $9.46; target price has sat around $10 for months.

players.name: Luis De Leon
players.note: Price crashed to $6 (-71.4%) — chalk it up to bad auctions, not a real market shift; shouldn't be under $10 as a top-50 arm. Wildly inconsistent (3.26 ERA May, 8.15 June incl. one 10-ER blowup, but also a 5-IP no-hitter and most recently 1H/9K over 5.2 IP) — 5.37 ERA masks a 3.90 xFIP. Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy), Expected Value $24.50. In Buy Range.

players.name: Ethan Dorchies
players.note: Extremely young for A+ at 19 (younger than Cam Caminiti), a 10th-round underslot Brewers signee with a 2.74 ERA over 82 IP last year as an 18-year-old. Stats haven't popped yet and he allows a lot of contact, but Buy Rating 4.6/5.0 (Strong Buy), Expected Value $7.12 at $4 — good shot on a projectable 6'5" teen arm. In Buy Range.

players.name: Kendry Chourio
players.note: First pitcher since Eury Perez (2021) to throw High-A innings in his age-18 season — 3.78 ERA, 9.18 K/9, 1.62 BB/9 across 3 starts, 4.9 years younger than average with elite sub-5% walk rates at every stop. K/9 under 10 is the only real knock for top-10 hobby status. Buy Rating 4.1/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $50 at $32 (-20%). In Buy Range.

players.name: Nate Snead
players.note: Back-to-back strong starts after a rough patch in June. Converted college reliever the Angels pushed aggressively to A+ then AA after 7 dominant starts — control has been great (1.73 BB/9 combined) though he doesn't miss many bats (7.98 K/9) despite triple-digit velo. Buy Rating 4.8/5.0 (Strong Buy), Expected Value $17 at $9. In Buy Range.

players.name: Gage Ziehl
players.note: 7 weeks in a row; price back to $5 (-44.4%) — buy some. Not in my top 150, but out-performed Kade Anderson in back-to-back weeks and punched out 8 last start. Plus command mutes upside (occasional 2-3 K starts) but floor looks strong.

players.name: Michael Lombardi
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $10, Buy Rating 4.2/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $15.80. No separate write-up.

players.name: Alex Clemmey
players.note: Last week's $35 print was a data blip (one bad-title PSA 10 sale), now corrected to $17 (-51.4%). Big 6'6" young lefty for the level but struggles with location — gets hit when he finds the zone, high walk rate, limited bat-missing; profile risk skews reliever. Buy Rating 2.0/5.0 (Consider Selling), Expected Value $8.08.

players.name: Jonathan Santucci
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $21, Buy Rating 4.2/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $34. No separate write-up.

players.name: Boston Bateman
players.note: 3 weeks in a row; price down to $12 (-20%) even as he's set to jump ~20 spots to inside my top 80 on Friday's re-rank. 6'8" lefty with good strikeout stuff, part of a quietly strong Orioles pitching development effort. Buy Rating 3.4/5.0 (Hold but undervalued), Expected Value $14.60.

players.name: Matthew Fisher
players.note: Another 2025 prep-arm sleeper, now trailing Livingston in my rankings but fine either way at $5-6. Getting more strikeouts than Livingston with a five-pitch mix and good offspeed spin. Buy Rating 3.8/5.0 (Lean Buy), Expected Value $8.50 — cheap flier.

players.name: Cade Obermueller
players.note: Dominant since a delayed pro debut: 2.70 ERA and 35.6% K rate over 7 Single-A starts. Need to see the college-arm jump hold at A+ (Zach Root comp) before fully buying in, but nothing suggests he'll struggle there. Buy Rating 3.5/5.0 (Lean Buy), Expected Value $8.86.

players.name: Seojun Moon
players.note: Nice outing but control still an issue — walked 3 in 4 IP, BB/9 at 6.0 on the year, unsustainable for a starter. Just 19 with real upside; international market drives the price, fine with it but not in love.

players.name: Kade Anderson
players.note: 7 weeks in a row (13 of 14 Hot Sheets) — arguably the best minor league pitching season watched in 6+ years. Price up to $195 (+9.6%) despite Buy Rating 2.3/5.0 (Lean Sell), Expected Value $125 — him and Seth Hernandez have broken the target-price model; Mariners likely keep him off the hitter-friendly AAA PCL squad, raising call-up odds. Too expensive for me despite the talent.

players.name: Zach Root
players.note: Buy even before last night's 6 IP/1H/0ER/2BB/11K gem topped the Bowman Brew — this $11 price (-35.3%) may not last. Target price ~$19, ranked 56th (pre-last night). Not entirely sure how he's doing what he's doing, but plays for one of MLB's best teams. Buy Rating 4.4/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $18.80. In Buy Range.

players.name: Quinn Mathews
players.note: 6 weeks in a row — my 'Bowman arch nemesis,' ranking has swung from 15th to ~50th. Just posted a 2.05 ERA in June and a scoreless-walk start in July, but don't fully trust the newfound command yet. Buy Rating 2.3/5.0 (Lean Sell), Expected Value $21 at $32 (-8.6%) — hold if you own him for the eventual call-up, not buying right now.

players.name: Mason Morris
players.note: Converted college reliever who can miss bats, but walk rate still too high despite recent improvement (back-to-back Hot Sheet appearances). Liked the profile (similar to Michael Lombardi) but not missing enough bats yet. No action for now.

players.name: Bryce Cunningham
players.note: 4 weeks in a row; price up to $14 (+40%) on Yankees hype after another effective start. Fastball doesn't stand out and sub-9 K/9 as a changeup-first righty, but results keep him around 95-100 in my rankings. Buy Rating 2.4/5.0 (Lean Sell), Expected Value $9.94 — hard to buy over $10.

players.name: Michael Kennedy
players.note: 3 weeks in a row despite being an undersized, low-strikeout lefty — struck out 6 last time out. Price down to $1 (-50%). Could be a nice long-term arm given Cleveland's pitching development track record, but not much hobby excitement here.

players.name: Ryan Sloan
players.note: 4 weeks in a row; price up to $82 (+6.5%). The $100 gap to Kade Anderson doesn't make sense — 4.6 years younger than average for Double-A (biggest age gap other than Chourio), 6'5" frame, one of only two Bowman arms with 50+ IP, K/9 over 11, and BB/9 under 2 (the other is Anderson). Buy Rating 3.4/5.0 (Hold but undervalued), Expected Value $100.

players.name: Johnny Slawinski
players.note: 10 CPX starts: 3.30 ERA, 13.21 K/9, 2.33 BB/9 — about maxed out my rookie-level rankings (#59) yet formula still says undervalued. Like the profile; could keep climbing if he repeats this in Single-A.

players.name: Anthony Eyanson
players.note: 3 weeks in a row; price up to $69 (+9.5%) after striking out 7 last outing (K's had cooled since the AA move). Bounces between #4-5 for me with Karson Milbrandt (no Bowman auto); cheaper than target price even after running to $100 earlier this year. Buy Rating 3.2/5.0 (Hold but undervalued), Expected Value $75.

players.name: Adam Seminaris
players.note: 4 weeks in a row; price flat at $3. Now a 2.62 ERA, 10.71 K/9, 2.05 BB/9 season with K rate up to ~30% from 20% last year. Huge downside is he's 27 in a level he first reached in 2022 — no good explanation why he's still there, but the age will keep Bowman interest low.

players.name: Yohairo Cuevas
players.note: 4 weeks in a row — a strange player to peg: split time between A and A+ last year (crushed A, struggled A+) and it's the same story this year (171 wRC+ in A vs. 72 wRC+ in A+, 1.632 OPS this stretch). Back-to-back hot weeks here make you wonder if something's clicking; not a big name but a .205 ISO gives him room to grow. Price flat at $2, a bit more interested than before.

players.name: Peyton Graham
players.note: Tools have always been strong (2nd-round 2022 Oklahoma pick) but injuries limited him until last year; now further improved — .303 average, 4 HR, K rate under 20%, 45 SB in 65 games (1.607 OPS). Price up to $5 (+66.7%). Nice season, but at 25 in AA the hobby likely won't bite unless he repeats this in AAA soon.

players.name: Hiverson Lopez
players.note: After struggling badly in the DSL last year, everything has flipped this time — walks doubled, strikeouts down 7%, ISO up 200 points (1.556 OPS). Price up to $4 (+33.3%). Catcher repeating the DSL caps the excitement, but worth a pin.

players.name: Charlie Condon
players.note: 4 weeks in a row; price up to $111 (+19.4%) after his 4th straight hot week (3 HR this time), rebounding from the $80s earlier this year (1.524 OPS). MLB debut feels close — fine with selling here, especially over $100, given the James Tibbs III risk (gets hot, doesn't get called up, price falls). Buy Rating 2.0/5.0 (Consider Selling), Expected Value $52 — could hold for the call-up but wouldn't be shocked if it just sits $110-125.

players.name: Jaron Elkins
players.note: Price up to $12 (+50%) purely on Dodgers-prospect hype (1.488 OPS). 2023 prep pick whose K rate has dropped from 35.1% (2024) to 29.7% (last year) to 24.7% this year while walks rose and power exploded (+100 ISO points, 11 HR/25 SB in 54 games). Still 21 and in Single-A though, and contact needs to hold at A+. Watching from the sidelines for now.

players.name: Dakota Jordan
players.note: Cheapest hitter on either Futures Game roster (fun dark-horse angle), price up to $17 (+13.3%). Loud tools — 15 HR/15 SB already — but a bad-hit-tool profile as an aggressive, low-walk college hitter that worries me for the upper levels (1.462 OPS). Buy Rating 2.3/5.0 (Lean Sell), Expected Value $11.04 — not my type of profile even though the tools are fun.

players.name: Andrew Fischer
players.note: 7 weeks in a row with an OPS over 1.000 (currently 1.450) — one of the most impressive Hot Sheet runs ever, yet price has barely moved across the last 4 sheets ($100/$103/$100/$99). Likely close to his peak and a cold streak will hit the price hard; a great player but not a hobby profile that sustains much over $100. Buy Rating 2.0/5.0 (Consider Selling), Expected Value $44.

players.name: Roldy Brito
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $34, Buy Rating 4.4/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $58. No separate write-up.

players.name: Franklin Arias
players.note: Two more homers this week, price down to $131 (-8.4%) despite continuing to outperform. Made him a buy on the Red Sox sheet this offseason at $65 — up 100%+ since. Only concern at $130+ is power sustainability, which I can't confirm at this price even though I love the player. Buy Rating 2.5/5.0 (Hold but overvalued), Expected Value $97.50.

players.name: Eduardo Quintero
players.note: Price up to $62 (+3.3%) as power returns — 4 HR in the last 35 days after just 2 in April+May combined (1.333 OPS). Contact rates are better than ever; was around $100 in March and nothing suggests he isn't as good as advertised. Top-15 prospect for me. Buy Rating 4.5/5.0 (Strong Buy), Expected Value $110. In Buy Range.

players.name: Won-Bin Cho
players.note: Check your old shoebox' alert — a popular 2022 sleeper name (plus power projections, viral BP clips) who never performed in the U.S. until now. At 22 between A+ and AA: 15 HR, 23 SB, .275 ISO, 135 wRC+ (1.331 OPS) — and just 10 games into AA has 7 HR (.583 ISO). Price exploded to $23 (+228.6%) before there was time to react; would've been a buy near $15 but the jump makes it tough to chase now.

players.name: BJ Murray Jr.
players.note: 4 weeks in a row, red hot again (1.291 OPS) but no base autographs exist for him — color only. 26 and stuck in AAA on a team without a great track record finding playing time for prospects, so hard to know what to do with the improvement. Price data N/A both weeks.

players.name: Owen Carey
players.note: Braves' 15th-round 2024 pick, a 'lite' version of teammate Eric Hartman — good hit tool, good (if lesser) speed, previously modest power. Missed a chunk of this year hurt but power is climbing fast: .087 ISO in A ball last year (4 HR/525 PA) to .202 in A+ this year (5 HR/137 PA) as a teenager (1.283 OPS). Price up to $17 (+6.3%). Buy Rating 3.3/5.0 (Hold but undervalued), Expected Value $19.47 — sneaky bat under $20.

players.name: Devin Taylor
players.note: 3 weeks in a row; flagged last week as too cheap under $20 and he answered with a 4-HR week. 8 HR in 24 games since the AA promotion (.286 ISO over 109 PA) after 6 HR in 57 games at A+ (1.273 OPS). Was a top-10 hitter to chase in the 2025 Bowman Draft class for a reason. Price up to $24 (+33.3%). Buy Rating 3.8/5.0 (Lean Buy), Expected Value $33.67.

players.name: Kavares Tears
players.note: Power was respectable but unspectacular in his pro debut (.159 ISO, 13 HR/107 G); this year it's exploded to .282 ISO on 12 HR in half the at-bats (1.218 OPS). Still a lot of swing-and-miss, not usually my type for a college bat, but the power alone is worth watching. Price down to $6 (-25%).

players.name: Yasser Mercedes
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $10, Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy), Expected Value $21.80. No separate write-up.

players.name: Jesus Baez
players.note: #2 on my 'Unlucky Hitters Due to Bounce Back' piece, and he delivered — 4 HR in 5 games right after (1.214 OPS). Only 19 prospects age 22-or-under have 200+ PA and an ISO over .270 this year, and his 16.6% K rate is the lone one under 20% — far better contact than the other big-power names. Price up to $19 (+90%). Buy Rating 2.3/5.0 (Lean Sell), Expected Value $12 — a hold after buying opportunities under $8 a few weeks ago.

players.name: Angel Genao
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $37, Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy). No separate write-up.

players.name: Breyson Guedez
players.note: 2026 Bowman sleeper who, like Juan Sanchez and teammate Edgar Montero, jumped straight from DSL to Single-A — a tough assignment. Approach needs work but he's only 18 and struck out in under 10% of PA in last year's DSL (1.206 OPS). Buy Rating 3.7/5.0 (Lean Buy), Expected Value $11.52 at $9 — fine as a cheap long-term sleeper stash.

players.name: Cooper Flemming
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $25, Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy), Expected Value $51. No separate write-up.

players.name: Josh Caron
players.note: Featured in my 'most improved hitters' piece — much better numbers this year (average .197→.261, ISO .134→.283, 15 HR in 70 fewer PA than last year's 9, already 15 HR/15 SB by early July) yet his card value is down ~50% from last year (1.175 OPS). 31.5% K rate is the concern, but no real reason for the price decline given the performance. Price flat at $3.

players.name: Nathan Flewelling
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $39, Buy Rating 4.4/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $66. No separate write-up.

players.name: Will Bush
players.note: Power-first C/1B with a solid offensive career, but nothing that looks like it will move the Bowman market (1.131 OPS). Probably a bit slept on among Astros prospects, but not an active buy right now. Price flat at $5.

players.name: Marcus Lee Sang
players.note: Capable of solid HR/SB combos (10+/10+ three straight years, 2022-2024), but the approach isn't great and he's 25 in AA (1.109 OPS) — hard to see much hobby interest. Price flat at $2.

players.name: Handelfry Encarnacion
players.note: 3 weeks in a row; price up to $22 (+46.7%). Joins Josue De Paula as the only qualified prospects at any level/age with 10+ HR, 15+ SB, sub-20% K rate, and BB/K over 0.85 (1.085 OPS) — no standout tool but does everything well, power trending up (.133 ISO last year → .177 this year). Top-3 in my own share count among 2026 Bowman names. Buy Rating 2.8/5.0 (Hold but overvalued), Expected Value $19.73 — long-term play.

players.name: Fernando Cruz
players.note: 3 weeks in a row; price flat at $10. Dreamy tools for a Cubs teen prospect (1.078 OPS) but the payoff depends on quality of contact, which has improved but isn't great yet — more lottery ticket than real buy until the hit tool catches up.

players.name: Maykel Coret
players.note: Of the DSL repeaters, this is the one worth a flier — was a notable international signee who didn't play poorly last year, hence the Rays kept him there. Struggling with contact now (1.074 OPS) so still just a lottery ticket, but a 6'4" teen with plus power/speed projection in a strong development org. Price up to $6 (+20%).

players.name: Alessander De La Cruz
players.note: 5 weeks in a row; officially cracked my top 200 hitters. Price up to $12 (+71.4%) from $5 as early CPX success looks legit (1.071 OPS). Buy Rating 3.2/5.0 (Hold but undervalued), Expected Value $13.70 — expect a Single-A move soon with room to climb further if he keeps producing.

players.name: Ethan Anderson
players.note: 3 weeks in a row; a hit-over-power C/1B who was never going to get much hobby love, but the '-over-power' label is fading fast — 17 HR and a .250 ISO one year after being under .100 (1.066 OPS). Odd profile for the hobby but a solid player regardless. Price down to $13 (-18.8%).

players.name: Xavier Neyens
players.note: Posted a wild 1.065 OPS week driven almost entirely by walks — .167 average on 2 hits but a .565 OBP off 11 walks (2 hits were a double and a HR). Price up to $43 (+10.3%). Risk is the Bowman market has never quite known how to value this profile, but the raw power makes it hard to pass. Buy Rating 3.9/5.0 (Lean Buy), Expected Value $61.33.

players.name: Bryan Rincon
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $11, Buy Rating 5.0/5.0 (Strongest Buy), Expected Value $24.80. No separate write-up.

players.name: Sam Petersen
players.note: Buy Range only this week: $14, Buy Rating 4.0/5.0 (Buy), Expected Value $20.80. No separate write-up.

players.name: Michael Arroyo
players.note: Last AA Hot Sheet appearance — being promoted to AAA alongside teammate Lazaro Montes. Was in my top 30 hitters at a $20 base auto when I started my hobby rankings last year; has more than doubled since but target price is still $10 above where he trades (1.040 OPS). Smaller frame leads people to underrate his power, but production has been elite at every stop back to age-17 DSL ball. Price down to $43 (-4.4%). Buy Rating 3.6/5.0 (Lean Buy), Expected Value $56.

players.name: Branden Boissiere
players.note: Hard to give much weight to these back-to-back weeks — he's on a rehab assignment and the first hot week came in the CPX (1.040 OPS). Production was up last year and he started hot in AA before the injury, but at 26 the market has little room to move. Price flat at $3.

players.name: Mike Sirota
players.note: One of my top-5 most undervalued names from the 2024 Bowman Draft release (alongside Sam Antonacci and Nathan Flewelling); sold my own shares last year after a big run-up but would hold if I still had them. Tools in this org profile for a $100 base auto, and I think he gets there by year-end (1.016 OPS). Currently riding a 68-game on-base streak, extended yesterday with a HR. Price up to $92 (+15%). Buy Rating 2.8/5.0 (Hold but overvalued), Expected Value $84 — unreal production, no notes.

players.name: Brent Iredale
players.note: 4 weeks in a row; price up to $10 (+42.9%). Still mashing (.246 ISO, 1.013 OPS) but as an almost-23-year-old in Single-A, needs to prove it against better competition before I give it real weight.

players.name: Antonio Anderson
players.note: 6'2" switch-hitter with above-average power projection at just $5 (down 20% this week) is a fine price point, especially as a Red Sox prospect (1.006 OPS). Already matched last year's HR total in 200 fewer PA, walks up 3.4%, strikeouts down 7%, contact rates up 4% in a shortened 41-game season. Trending the right way but hasn't done enough since being drafted to be a buy yet.

players.name: Milan Tolentino
players.note: Quiet 20 HR/20 SB breakout in AAA last year after showing little power before, though strikeout rate climbed over 30% to get there; same story this year (10 HR/10 SB already, K rate still 30%+, 1.000 OPS). Could make noise on a call-up, but with how many good under-the-radar Guardians prospects exist, not the direction I'd go. Price flat at $11.

players.name: Cristian Arguelles
players.note: 1.333 OPS. Took a while to bring Arguelles into the top 200 given distrust of rookie ball stats, but underlying data is really, really good - brought him WAY up once trusted. Even so, hard to go over $25 for a Complex League hitter, so not actively buying at this price despite really liking the bat.

players.name: Jaeden Calderon
players.note: 1.299 OPS. Odd player - played well in 2023 DSL debut but Phillies had him repeat the level anyway, posting wRC+ of 146 and 147 across those two years. Stateside debut last year was injury-shortened (12 games). Sent to Single-A this year but struggled (.138 in 151 PA), demoted back to CPX. Looks great again vs. rookie pitching, but no success proven past that level, and turns 21 in a couple months - tough to get behind.

players.name: Abdias De La Cruz
players.note: 1.045 OPS. Signed in 2022 with above-average future grades on raw power, speed, and fielding - a fun dart throw. Now in his 5th pro season and still just that. Power is up this year and contact rates have steadily improved for four straight years, but the 6'3" tools-y outfielder remains a developmental project.

players.name: Ichiro Cano
players.note: 1.434 OPS. Bonus points for the name alone. Solid contact hitter across all three stops (DSL, CPX, A) but that's the only real positive - doesn't hit many homers, doesn't steal many bases. Productive, but not exciting enough for the hobby.

players.name: Ivan Luciano
players.note: 1.238 OPS. Catcher with below-average power isn't the hobby dream, but this feels like a risk-free floor at $3. 2nd rounder out of high school in 2024, impressed in draft showcases. Good approach (0.75 BB/K), good bat-to-ball (81.1% contact, 19.4% K), and power ticking up (.164 ISO this year vs .103 last year). Not hobby exciting, but a solid player.

players.name: Jaron Elkins
players.note: 1.110 OPS. 4 weeks in a row! Up 50% again on the Dodgers-prospect hot streak. Still have contact questions - .340 average comes with a .422 BABIP, though BABIP has been .375+ for three straight years over 1,000+ PA. 13 HR/29 SB; 100-point ISO jump and big BB/K improvement are green flags, but as a Dodgers prospect prices get steep fast - already too rich unless this continues at High-A.

players.name: Joendry Vargas
players.note: 1.175 OPS. Stock has fallen hard from being a legit 'Vargas or Emil Morales' debate. Dominated DSL/CPX but struggled in first taste of Single-A while battling injuries; back there again. K rate down over 10 points (30.4% to 19.5%), contact up from 65.1% to 77%. 6'3" SS with plus power projections, but swing decisions still aggressive/impatient, limiting power access. Not ranked currently, but a tempting buy-low given he was a top-10 org prospect two years ago.

players.name: John Wimmer
players.note: 2.161 OPS. Great year in Single-A - .333 with a 154 wRC+ and 3 more HR this weekend, but only 25 games. ISO jumped to .284 after failing to top .115 in his first two seasons - very small sample. 2023 HS draft pick, now 21 and repeating A ball; would need to sustain this over a few months for Bowman buyers to take notice.

players.name: Kevyn Castillo
players.note: 1.176 OPS. Third straight season in Single-A - first two cut short (~200 PA each) with .292 and .285 averages aided by extreme BABIP luck. This year contact looks great, K rate down to 18.0% for the third straight year, with 11 HR and 18 SB. Price unlikely to get juice unless he replicates this at the next level - Angels need to promote him.

players.name: Blake Mitchell
players.note: 1.667 OPS. Profile like Emmanuel Rodriguez/Ryan Clifford - power, OBP, and wRC+, but strikes out a lot and hits for low average, a profile the hobby has never known what to do with. 17 HR, 18 SB, 23.7% BB, .423 OBP, .249 ISO, 137 wRC+, but .238 average, 33.7% K rate, and a 59.7% contact rate. Side with the analytics (wOBA/wRC+ are most predictive of offensive success) but hard to get a following with these splits.

players.name: Casey Cook
players.note: 1.114 OPS. Shoutout even though his first hot week came in the Complex. 3rd rounder out of UNC in 2023 showed solid contact (78.6%) and speed (29 SB) last year in A+, but only 6 HR in 493 PA (.089 ISO). Since returning this year, 3 HR in first 9 games - great start but small sample (36 PA). Deep, deep sleeper for now.

players.name: Easton Carmichael
players.note: 1.092 OPS. Whole Greensboro team has been hot lately, Carmichael included. Hitting .310 with 16 HR, 11 SB, .220 ISO, 117 wRC+, despite some scouts seeing him as a glove-over-bat catcher. Moving up the rankings toward the top 300. Active collector/trader on Twitter.

players.name: Ethan Frey
players.note: 1.069 OPS. Featured in 'Top 10 Under $10' article - now clear he was only that cheap because people didn't realize he was returning from injury. Autos have more than doubled since coming back. Slept-on power potential and sneaky athleticism; hopeful these two hot weeks signal he's fully healthy and catching fire.

players.name: Felnin Celesten
players.note: 1.167 OPS. 'Not seeing value' is misleading - he's shown he can be a $100 base auto prospect. One of the best international tools (5 above-average grades) but delayed by early injuries. Posted 156 wRC+/.216 ISO in 32 games in 2024 CPX despite an alarming 64.9% ground ball rate (4.85 GB/FB). Improved for the third straight year - ISO now .220 vs .102 last year. High-A Everett's small park is a factor, but the improvements are real; can't rank him higher right now though.

players.name: Sammy Stafura
players.note: 1.610 OPS. 3 weeks in a row! 3 more HR last week (16 total in 53 games) plus 17 SB. One of the tools-iest 2023 draft athletes but hadn't accessed his projected power until now - nearly tripled HR total from last year in 300 fewer PA, ISO up from .139 to .297. Contact rate dropped below 70% for the first time, a slight worry, but counting stats are good enough for the card people. Moving up rankings but price is moving faster.

players.name: Wehiwa Aloy
players.note: 1.458 OPS. Top-100 hitter in the rankings, landed at a spot where he was red hot at 2026 Bowman release, hovered near $100 before falling to current price. Like the raw power, some approach concerns. Missing the 'recipe' ingredients for a big-name college bat (similar knock as on Andrew Fischer). Orioles fans may be inflating this given no Nate George right now; worried this has too much room to fall once he cools off.

players.name: Brandon Compton
players.note: 1.462 OPS. 3 weeks in a row! On an absolute heater - 3 HR in 185 PA (Apr-May) vs. 17 HR in 157 PA since June. Same issue as Blake Mitchell - even with 20+ HR, .400+ OBP, and great wRC+, a 35% K rate scares people off. Walks over 20% too (analytics dream, likely why the Marlins liked him), but low contact means low average. Expected this to have moved up more given the power surge.

players.name: Dylan Dreiling
players.note: 1.288 OPS. Sneaky name, just got his first Dreiling in a stack sale. Hovering $10-12 for weeks with a lot to like at this entry point - above-average power and speed, batting .289 with 80.4% contact at AA. Age is neutral. Among Bowman prospects with 300+ PA, SwStr% under 8.5%, and ISO over .185, only Josue De Paula and Dylan Dreiling qualify (add Charles Davalan and Franklin Arias at 270+ PA). Solid offensive profile for a cheap price.

players.name: Leo De Vries
players.note: 1.290 OPS. Formula now has Eli Willits ranked ahead of De Vries at #3 - don't necessarily agree, think De Vries is more exciting than Jesus Made. Still slightly underpriced; should be a $250 base auto. Much more aggressive on the bases this year (32 SB vs 11 all of last year) while improving average from .255 to .292. Confident price goes higher before his MLB debut - wouldn't sell.

players.name: Matthew Wood
players.note: 1.343 OPS. 3 weeks in a row! One of the most rock-solid floors at this price, but being a 25-year-old catcher is unexciting to the hobby. Now has a 19.0% BB, 11.5% K, .239 ISO, 86.6% contact - crazy stats for the price, but probably not exciting enough to ever really take off.

players.name: Roc Riggio
players.note: 1.100 OPS. 3 weeks in a row! Does a lot right for hobby success including great power (.250 ISO for 2nd straight year), but trade from Yankees to Rockies isn't ideal for collectability and he's now 24 in AA - the age where Bowman buyers tend to lose interest. Like the bat, but team/age/platoon splits likely cap further love before his debut.

players.name: Zyhir Hope
players.note: 1.662 OPS. 3 weeks in a row! Will crack the top 20 next update, on an absolute heater in July (8 HR, 1.460 OPS). Doesn't get the respect he deserves sharing a field with Josue De Paula and Mike Sirota - the 'non-1st' autograph stigma scares Bowman buyers away. Ranking implies an $82 auto, but the non-1st deduction brings the target to ~$50 - slightly undervalued but priced fairly.

players.name: Jonathon Long
players.note: 1.429 OPS. 3 weeks in a row! Painful as someone who loved Long as a 2025 Bowman sleeper - but you can't account for a team sitting a player in AAA for 1,000+ PA. The formula moves players down the longer/older they sit without promotion, and nothing kills hype like being stuck. Ready for about a full year now; could probably start for half the teams in MLB, apparently just not the Cubs.

players.name: Josh Kasevich
players.note: 1.183 OPS. What he is: great average, great contact, solid defense - the type of player you want on your real-life club. Unfortunately 'good in real life' and 'exciting in Bowman' aren't the same. Batting .291 in AAA with a 10.9% K rate (crazy good), but just 3 HR and 4 SB in 91 games - a tough line to get card people excited about.

players.name: Johnny Slawinski
players.note: Wait for injury news, it was unclear if he was removed from this start for an injury or not.

players.name: David Davalillo
players.note: Rehab assignment.

players.name: Dean Livingston
players.note: 4 weeks in a row! Another start without a super exciting strikeout number for Livingston but regardless it's impressive to see him make four consecutive hot sheets in his first year out of high school, especially since he didn't start on the mound until his senior year. Long-term play. Great frame, great athlete, needs refinement on secondary pitches but scouts think the fastball could reach triple digits as he fills out. 2.55 ERA in his first 49.1 innings as a pro. Has had some BABIP luck that will likely regress since he hasn't missed many bats since his promotion from CPX to A, but this is a play on potential, so his early success only moves him up higher.

players.name: Riley Kelly
players.note: 6'5" RHP selected in the 4th round out of UC Irvine in 2025, shows promising spin rates on secondaries. Fastball may be only average - good shape but not much velocity. Last start was his best (season/career-high 11 K's); over his past two starts he's struck out 19 over 12.2 IP allowing only 1 ER, walking just 1 batter in each. Opponents have just a 67.1% contact rate, but when hit he gets hit hard - allowed 5+ ER in 4 of his last 9 starts. Hot right now but the tendency to follow a gem with a blow-up makes him tough to judge.

players.name: Trevor Harrison
players.note: Not loved by the rankings but a fan of Harrison as a big-frame prep arm with good stuff in a great org for pitcher development. Posted a 2.78 ERA between A & A+ at age 19 last year despite a mediocre 22.7% K rate. This year K rate is up to 25.9% (K/9 from 8.41 to 9.96), but he's been hit harder and ERA is up to 4.68. BABIP, Contact%, SwStr%, and ground ball rates are nearly identical to last year, but his HR/FB ratio has jumped from 2.9% to 20.3% (juiced ball effect). Looked much better since June 1st - not a bad flier for a couple bucks.

players.name: Jacob Bresnahan
players.note: 6 weeks in a row! After a 2.61 ERA in 93 IP last year, Bresnahan has a 2.92 ERA over 64.2 IP at High-A this year. Fired off his first 0-walk start of the season this weekend, striking out 7 in 5 IP. Rankings haven't caught on yet but recognition should be coming, especially if promoted before the season ends.

players.name: Chase Shores
players.note: On the edge of the top 150, worth considering at this price. 6'8" righty who can touch triple digits - question is whether secondaries and control are good enough to start. Had a 5-inning, 10-K start earlier this year but results have been mixed overall. Mainly a two-pitch pitcher with fringy command, concern he could end up in the pen, but exciting arm/upside regardless.

players.name: Tanner Franklin
players.note: Mixed bag - two dominant starts in early April sent his autograph over $30 (doubled from start of year), now back down to $15. Season line: 4.62 ERA in 17 starts, but that includes a 7.36 ERA in June sandwiched between 3.12 ERA in May and 3.38 ERA in July. 6'5" with an electric fastball - great combo for hobby hype. Inconsistent, but ceiling still strong; more tempted to buy now than when he was over $30.

players.name: Ty Floyd
players.note: Great just to see Floyd on the mound. Drafted 38th overall in 2023 (signed for $2M+) but didn't make pro debut until 2025 and has thrown less than 60 IP in his career. Potential here, but at 24 and without 30+ IP in a season since college, hard to have a ton of faith. Hopefully injuries are behind him.

players.name: Mason McGwire
players.note: Looked strong this past weekend; 2.89 ERA across A & A+ for the Cubs this year, earning a well-deserved Futures Game trip after missing all of 2025 with injury. Still pitching well since move to A+, but allowing 11.3% more contact and K rate down 12.1% since the promotion. Solid upside, but hard not to think card value is partly driven by being Mark McGwire's son. Getting close to cracking top 150 pitchers, but price is still more than double where it should be.

players.name: Braylon Doughty
players.note: 5.0/5.0 Strongest Buy. Firmly moving into top 10 pitchers after his last start. Youngest pitcher in AA not named Ryan Sloan, making hitters 5 years older look silly. In 4 starts since promotion, ERA is 5.00 but FIP is 1.98 over 18 IP - 2 of 4 outings were scoreless AND walk-less. Of 246 qualified pitching prospects, only 2 have a K/9 over 11.0 and BB/9 under 2.0: Kade Anderson and Braylon Doughty.

players.name: Gary Gill Hill
players.note: Effective but doesn't strike anyone out, so the hobby hasn't cared - until a 7-K line this weekend caught attention (only struck out 2 in each of the two starts prior, so don't expect this to be the norm). Young for the level with incredible command (1.54 BB/9), which is why the Rays keep promoting him. Maybe not a huge ceiling play, but the floor here is really strong.

players.name: Drew Beam
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Great three-start run - 3.15 ERA in July, though May and June ERAs were both over 8.00. Effective by mixing pitches and locating well, but without high strikeout numbers the Bowman crowd is unlikely to bite.

players.name: Jack Mahoney
players.note: 3 weeks in a row! Rockies pitching program producing more names than in past years. Now 6-1 with a 2.02 ERA across 12 starts / 58 IP. Ground ball rate way up (45.5% to 60.1%) - easier to succeed with a juiced ball keeping it on the ground. Strikeout rates still below the 'exciting' line, and being almost 25 in AA doesn't generate buzz, but a great turnaround from last year.

players.name: Quinn Mathews
players.note: 8 weeks in a row! Back in on Quinn Mathews. Was one of the first to rank him top 15 for pitchers before inconsistencies dropped him. After walking 11 over 14.1 IP in his last three June starts, walked only 3 in 19 IP during July. Always had front-of-rotation upside - went from A to AAA in his pro debut with a 2.76 ERA over 143.1 IP in 2024. Price has sat still for weeks because buying is tough; Cardinals fanbase could push this to $50 on call-up news if he has his 'A' stuff. Hold if you own any - he's been on fire lately.
